I'll deffinately come back in the near future.

Stopped in to pick up flowers at their florist as we went to visit a friend in the hospital. I love their flower section as it's always vibrant and fresh.  We were able to pick up what we needed for a very good price. The service in the store was excellent.

Traveling home from Orlando and the traffic was thick, so we pulled off at the exit after we saw the sign advertising Johnson's Barbeque, we followed the directions and almost missed it. Not to worry, we made a U-turn and parked in their lot.    It was a beautiful day, so we sat outside on the patio, Our server was prompt and we placed our order for Sweet tea (A must! It's perfection). While we were perusing the menu  a table near us got an order of Onion Ring, To be honest we hadn't considered apps, but the sight, the scent of them, that sold us. So we placed an order for them. And we weren't disappointed. They were HUGE, they were lightly battered, they were served hot and golden, They were absolutely delicious and their Ranch dressing was amazing.   Our mains: The husband got the 1/2 rack with the Cheese grits and the fried okra. He liked the okra as it's his favorite veg, and the cheese grits were served with bacon, how can you go wrong? The st. Louis styled ribs came out too and they were good, he said.   Me, I got the combo platter, 1/3rd rack ribs with brisket, sides of Mac & Cheese and Potato salad, The mac & cheese was to die for, the potato salad, meh, it didn't seem as if the potatoes were fully cooked. For me the ribs were on the dry side, and not terribly juicy and but the brisket was Yummmy.   One small aside: they have one bathroom stall for the women and one for men. If you plan to use it, be prepared to be greeted by a line outside waiting, no matter how quickly you go.

We attended 'The Haunted Tavern' at this location. It is the perfect location for such an atmospheric storytelling. With their theatrics and the building's known haunts, you have the absolute bet of everything.

I was desperate for a new color and new cut. My regular salon was closed, so I drove up 19, and saw this one on the sign. YES,  I quite literally picked this salon at random. I didn't read reviews and I didn't find out about the before hand. They simply were the first salon I came to.  I walked in, gave my name and told the gentleman (John) what I wanted. I spoke with the other stylist (Diana) and she said she'd take me as soon as she finished with her current clients. She was styling one, and letting the other finish his dye.  It wasn't much more than a half hour wait before I was welcomed to her chair.     She sat me down for a small consult, and I explained i wanted to change my color. I home dye but I always end up with my roots being one color, and the shaft/ends being a whole different shade.  She got her books and showed me a few different shades, we selected Rocket Red.  It looked great in the book; vibrant and warm.  The dying process was easy, Diana was lovely to talk to. We had similar styles in hair already, both of us having long, baby fine hair. She was previously a red head, so it was interesting to see someone with the same name with the same style.   Letting the dye sit, I leafed through magazines, taking note of the salon, it was very neat and up kept. Very modern. I learned that their staff often participates in hair shows.   When my hair was rinsed, we did the cut and though I asked for it to be shorter, slightly layered, my cut isn't dramatically different than it was before, but I'm not upset.  The color didn't turn out like it was in the book, but it is this LUSH rich auburn color that is stunning and will look fantastic for New Years.   The service aspect of the salon was top notch. Diana really went above and beyond while she worked on me. John, too seemed to truly care for his client.  Will I return? Yes, Yes I will.

We stopped in today around 3 pm for my mom's 78th birthday.  Having never been here, it was honestly a toss up between this eatery and one we were familiar with, so we opted for the new place, and we were very happy we did!  The eatery was quite empty, being that it was the end of their Brunch and regular dining time was about to resume.   The hostess was quite pleasant and seated us toward the back of the room and we were fine with that, given that we were the only people in the place.  Our server, Timmothy was friendly and very helpful when it came to telling us about the menu and the eatery itself.   We started with table side made guacamole, we were given a choice about what went in it from the ingredients there, so I went light on the cilantro and the jalepeño peppers, and when it was made it was FABULOUS. Seriously some of the best fresh Guac I've ever had.  We ate it all, literally scraping the bottom of the bowl and every last scrap of chips.  SO TASTY.   Our meals took a bit of time to come out, but I'm ok with that, after all I ordered the Short Ribs with the risotto and root veg medley, and BOY oh BOY that was so damn tasty! The risotto was the best!  Mom had the classic cut Prime Rib with the Sweet burbon mashed potatoes and green beans, The Niece had their burger and it was HUGE, even crushed, it needed to be cut in half to be eaten.  The husbeaste had their MeatLoaf and it was SO tasty. He had the regular Mashed Potatoes and green beans.  Everything was absolutely delicious, fresh made and succulent.   They brought out Mom a slice of cheese cake to celebrate her birthday with her.  That was very nice.   Will we be back? Yes.  The cost of the meal for the four of us, including my Espresso Martini, the Guac and the 4 entrees and soft drinks for the rest of the table was $160 including tip.

Culver's reminds me of a faster, but better Steak n'Shake.  I LOVE their butter burgers with bacon. I love the cheese curds, but I've yet to try the concretes. I will one day.   Through the drive through, there is always a little wait, but that's because the food is fresh as can be. Who's going to complain when everything is piping hot and juicy. Love me some Culver's

Yes, I drove an hour to some place YELP listed as hot and new. Yes, I took the Momster with me (I treated).   I haven't been down to the Tyrone area in -ages- Probably a decade or more, but this trip was worth it. Tom + Chee was damn good.  In fact, my check-in,  apparently inspired a few of my friends to go later that night and actually try a donut of theirs. Hehe.   Mom and I were surprised by their menu, it's extensive.  Since we didn't want to hold the line up, mom went with the classic: And chose 2 cheeses, Mozzerella and Cheddar on wheat with their soup of the day, Broccoli. Me, I chose their Roni Chee and the Chunky Tomato Soup, because I LOVE me some Tomato soup.   We were told that this is all hand made, no fryers, no microwaves, etc. and I tend to believe them, so we took our number and sat down at our tables with chairs that reminded me of being back in High School in Pasco County, and waited.   We had been given the wrong number, but the waitress found us, and our food was delivered.   The sandwiches and soups smelled great, they looked great and they were hot! The first thing I noticed? BUTTER! My sandwich had that great, grilled in butter taste. MMMMM Yes! Mom said that the Broccoli soup was good, but it was different, so I tasted it. To me, It was like they'd used Cauliflower as their thickener not cream. And if so. YAY! It's one of my favorite tricks.  She liked it.   Now the Roni Chee? We used to call that a hand pizza, and they did a fine job of it. I would have just added a few more pieces of pepperoni, other than that, this was a perfect visit.. Ok other than the HOUR drive, it was a perfect visit.   Bring one to Tarpon, Clearwater or Oldsmar!! Please!

Menchie's has been there a while, just outside of the Ice Rink. It replaced some fry joint and I'm glad it did!    I haven't stopped in for some unknown reason, but I did last night.. I had been at the mall with my paramour and I found myself craving something cold and sweet.  We made our way down to the first floor and saw the kiosk.  Since I hadn't visited before I asked a little bit about it and was told, its generally sold by weight, but Tuesday evenings it's all you can fit in the container for $5.  Not a bad buy when you see the size of the container.    The attendant offered us a few sample cups so we could try the flavours and once we decided what we wanted, we set to filling our cups. I got True Chocolate and Vanilla snow swirl, topped with Marshmallow, Chocolate fudge and Hot caramel, Omg That was HEAVEN.  My paramour went with NYC Cheese cake and Vanilla topped with Cheesecake bits and whipped cream.  This was such a total treat. YUM!

My first time into a Jimmy Johns, and I'm glad they have one in my neighborhood. I've heard the commercials, I've heard the hype of how fast they are. What I didn't know is where they skimped.  I ordered a BLT, and that's what I got, The bacon though? Cold.  Greasy, cold bacon is unappetizing. Sure it still tastes good, but it's not the same as hot, crispy bacon.   The store is bright, airy, clean and most importantly NEW.  They opened not long ago and they seem to be situated in a nice location. There are a LOT of employees, and they are efficient. They do get the job done very quickly. So I can't fualt them for any of that.

Shop local! This close to Christmas, I love being able to shop local, to support the local crafting community and of course seeing everyone out with their pups!   From Food trucks to crafters who make hand lathed bowls, where their profits actually go to homeless folks. There were so many different types of vendors! I found pendants that I loved, soaps, desserts, hand stamped bracelets to wonky looking dolls. If you can't find it here, you will probably find it the next time the event is open.   They are open every 2nd saturday from 10-4, though this time they were open 11-3, and had just had an all you can eat Pancake breakfast due to a 5K run at 8am! They really do a lot of involvement with the community at large.    Also, due to the location, there is a large presence of Scientology with the branding of a Human Rights organization.

I'm going to be upfront about my dislike of the parking situation in Down Town Tampa.  So when I got to the location, finding parking was hard! I ended up across the street at the parking structure for the Glazer Children's Museum, which was charging a singular priced parking due to Phantom Of the Opera going on at the Straz.   The walk to Anise wasn't bad, the lights were in my favor, and the scenery was nice with all the Christmas lights glowing in the early evening.  What I found distasteful, was the host- a young man in his early 20's, with light brown hair- wasn't paying attention to the door, he was head down over his phone, likely texting or checking Facebook. I had to speak up to get his attention. Only then did he let me know where my party was.    My party was that, a company Christmas party, about 25 people in attendance, drinks and appetizers provided by the venue. I have to admit, though I was a bit concerned over the offerings, I was actually quite happy with the flavours! We had curried chicken wings, curried deviled wings with lobster and vegitarian paninin.  All were delicious! I -LOVED- the deviled eggs, there was just something about them, they were TOTALLY off the chart.   The decor is amazing! I loved the bookcases in the bar area, the hydropinic greens in the lobby and the light fixtures that hung down from the high ceilings. This place has character! I can't wait to visit again, and am hoping that Anna will be my guide next time because I have a feeling I'd be out of my league!  Hats off to the Tender with the amazing dreads, Jarod(?) Sorry if I got the name wrong. He was really warm and friendly, totally LOVED his attitude!

Not sure why this Publix is marked so low.   I visited with a specific goal in mind, I needed 2 trays of holiday cookies for my Mom's nurses in the hospital. I knew the bakery would have just what i was looking for.  The kind the Alessi bakery ships in, Italian cookies with chocolate or jam, in festive colors and all with a hint of almond. They're so good   They had exactly what I was looking for, so I got the 2 trays, and a few other small things for mom. I was happy I was able to oblige her request and happy I was able to go in and out of this place without any issues.

On the way to get my hair re-colored at Tribeca, and I feel like my sugar is dropping. My fault entirely as I'd not eaten, so I pull in through the twin drive through and order a half/half iced tea and a caramel sundae.   Service was quick, order was correct and i was on my way in a mater of minutes. I am not a fan of Mcdonalds, but if you need to get an Iced tea. get on.

I'm so used to Kohl's having a certain format, that this store was odd to me. I stopped in because I had 2 $10 certificates that needed to be used by 8/2/15.    I was in a bit of a time constraint, so I just went over to the women's wear and pawed through the shirts. I found a slew of shirts I wanted, Ones I'd not seen at the local to me Store.   I finally spied a shirt I wanted,  a cute graphic tee with a bold pink flamingo ... alas it was only a size small.. and then I spied them, bright v-neck tees in royal blue, spring green, grey and turquoise... there were so many choices. Those were $11.99 each, I picked up 2! They ended up costing me $1.99 each! I loved it!

Since my car was parked near the JCPenney's I figured I'd take a look around. LOTS of sales going on. LOTS of things with bright red signs. I looked through some of the merchandise and saw that  a lot of it was current, much of it was decently made.  Everything looked pretty stylish, but on the first floor the racks were so close together, it was hard to manuever around.   The 2nd floor where the lingerie and plus wear wasn't much better. But at least you could get around a little better. Nice store over all.

BB&B is an amalgam of too much stuff in one large SQUARE store.  I came in to find ONE item, and walked out with something completely different! It saddens me that I paid full retail just because I didn't have any of thei coupons, but I did sign up to get them on my phone!

Just came back from a convention that was held at this particular Hotel.  Since they offered us a good rate and we sold out the hotel, I stayed here.   Check in was smooth, very little wait. The newly updated lobby is nice, very clean looking, very efficient. The staff is prompt and very friendly. Every person I got to interact with seemed genuinely pleasant. Every housekeeper smiled, every maintnence worker had no issue answering questions.   They've recently updated their bar and eatery too, both look like a million bucks too. Though in the bar, the prices were astronomical!  The rooms were clean, the rooms were spacious and the beds were comfortable. I loved the haircare products and the massage soaps. The coffee provided is delicious too!

New Taco Bell... It's a Taco Bell, but you still have to try them out to see how the service is. And on a rainy night on the edge of Pasco County, it wasn't bad at all. The window was polite, the service was quick and correct - that's the hardest thing to get with drive through, the correct order. I'd say i was really impressed.

Took my mom here for her 73rd birthday tonight.  Overall, the place is nice, if overly dark due to the heavy wood furnishing. The scent of fresh baked bread is heavenly.   We were seated 15 minutes after we arrived, which wasn't a terrible wait, but once sat, we waited another 7 minutes for the waitress to come and take our drink orders. It was busy so I can forgive that.    Our starter order was taken quickly, and drinks were brought to the whole party. When we placed our order, I made sure the waitress (Ashley) knew that it was Mom's birthday. She was glad we told her, because our starer was free. That was a nice touch, Thank you.     Our starters came out - the awesome blossom fried onion and an order of pigs in a blanket, they were all hot and crispy, and our salads came out too. The salads were either over dressed in the case of my Ceaser salad or the dressing on the side was horribly salted so that they were unpalatable.   Once the salads were picked up or tucked away for later in my case.  We waited for our entrees. Several times, our waitress came by to let us know that they'd be out "any moment".  Any moment turned out to be about 20 minutes later, leaving us to wonder if perhaps they either had to go to the store to get more Prime Rib or even new salmon.. In any case it was a long wait for the main courses.   When they did arrive, they were delicious, but given that we'd had to wait, the food we'd already eaten had begun to digest and we were no longer hungry.   All but one of our party ended up boxing most of their entree and taking it home.

I used to love the Lucky Dill at the old location. This new location.. It has it's issues. However the food is still Delish.  My favorite things are the Fried Green Tomatoes and the french onion soup! These two items make a meal for me every time I go.   Service is generally very good, but watch out for parking. Get there early if you want to make sure you get a spot.

I want to begin with, when you ask for mild, it should not cause your mouth to burn and your eyes to water. I have capsaicin allergies and this is why I asked for MILD Butter Chicken, but what I got was far from mild. My husband who does hot food said it was close in spice to his heat.  The flavor was good, but it wasn't worth a possible anaphylactic episode.   The Garlic Naan was delicious. Everyone else either ordered hot or Indian Hot, so I get there was likely a mix up, but it could have been very bad. As it was I ended up throwing up in the bathroom in order to prevent an issue.   I'm still.giving them a 3 star as the service was excellent and everyone else loved what they got.

There really is no other city like Tarpon Springs.   It is the Greek hub of the south. We are known for sponge diving and our delicious cuisine. We have a thriving antique center off Main Street and of course the Sponge Docks off Dodecanese blvd.   If you're looking for something interesting to do, make sure you check out one of the many art festivals, food festivals, night in the islands or concerts on the beach that the city sponsors. They seem to happen weekly in the summer time.  Tarpon is SUCH a great city. Oh! And don't forget to find the Tarpon Mermaid or the Iness Paintings.

Came to see about the Compassion Clinic that is at this same address. The people were all well informed and awesome. it's great to know that this is available and these people are here for those who need it.

Needed to fill the belly to fortify ourselves to face shopping the day before, the day before Christmas. The Philly cheese steaks are Ok. They are truly nothing to write home about, but they aren't terrible either. They were bready, but satisfying. I did really like the fries though.

I needed theme items for my trip to vegas. Who thought of doing a 1970's theme any way?  I didn't want disco, so I needed to go with Hippy. Where to get my costume supplies, well the ones I didn't make? That's right, Party City. There was one near mom's house and yes! They had what I was looking for, granted, it was on a top shelf, so I had to ask someone for help, and they did so without any qualms about it.   I may have ended up spending WAY more than I wanted to, but damned if the accessories I got (including a tambourine) didn't make my outfit ROCK!

I never even knew that there was a TD Bank here at this location, at the corner of Evan's road and US 19, until my brother decided he needed me to drop by there so he could pick up some cash after snagging him from the airport.   Their parking lot is large, for the office building it's located in, the grounds are well manicured and the people inside are friendly and polite.

What do haunters do while they wait for a tour to begin? They go to escape rooms. Why? Because a lot of haunts have escape rooms or are tied into the business some how.   This group graciously accepted our group of 4 and let us do their most creative puzzle and we put our heads together to solve the room. The time to beat was 38:23 or some place there abouts. The puzzle was pretty straight forward, but our methods weren't necessarily so.  Then again, not all of us had worked together before. STILL! We got out with 3 minutes to spare!  Of the 4 rooms this was their hardest, it was also their most detailed.  We were given a tour of the other rooms, and each of them were creative and adorable. I have to admit, I'd come and do each of them just to see how they are done and the outcomes.   Make your reservations, come and see the group down at Expedition Escape.
Just your average stop for gas. Pay at the pump, and the place was busy. No personal interaction with any living soul, just me and the gas pump.

Every so this place does a Ladies night with a theme... Last night was one of those nights. It was a Vintage Hollywood night. The idea was you and your Gal Pals dress in vintage looks and come in, enjoy a special 3 course meal for $25 each and $5 wine and $6 cocktails.   It's a great deal if you're familiar with their usual pricing.   Six of us came, six of us (in my group at least) dressed to the nines. From Pin up pretties, to a DisneyBent Glamour Witch, to Holly Go Lightly, Carrie from Sex in the city and the Black Widow, we all made our presence known. The LOOKS were all Fierce and Stunning. We were GLAMOROUS!  We had a cocktail or two at the bar, I have to say, try the LOVE Martini, it's Deliciously decadent.  The Cucumber martini looked pretty dang good too, let's be honest.   Once we were seated, that's when the fun started. If you've never eaten at a Melting pot, it's fondue style eating, that's pretty much, melted cheese and bread for your starter, a Meal that you cook in hot liquid and a chocolate fondue dessert. It's to die for.   So we had to choose 2 cheese styles, since we had 2 burners on our table - we chose the Alpine and the Bacon Jalapeno. Even with the extra jalapeno peppers added in, it wasn't too hot for me and trust me, we all enjoyed the cheese course.   Some of us opted for salads, I had the Ceaser, it was ok, the sweet nuts kind of threw me, with the savory dressing, but other wise it was tasty. The spinach salad looked good as did the Strawberry salad. All were visually pleasing.   Our main course - we used the court bullion as our cooking style. The special menu was a Chicken, Shrimp and terryaki steak, mushrooms, broccoli and other veggies all tossed into the pot. Once your meat was skewered, you simply put it into your hot liquid and wait 1.5-3 minutes depending on what it is. The shrimp of course cooked fastest.  When done, you could use one of six sauces to dip into and never ever eat from the fondue fork directly, those are hot! It doesn't look like a lot of food, but trust me, the length of time, the food you've already eaten and the talking you're doing, your tummy fills up fast.   Now the best part of the night.. Dessert. We opted for FLAMBÉ! for some reason the idea of something being set on fire really struck a chord with all six of us, and well. .ya, it's pretty! So we got the Turtle and another that both got lit on fire, mixed together and then we dunked all manner of tasty bits: Strawberries, pineapple, cocoa crusted marshmallows, pound cake, banana, and rice krispie treats into these bubbling pots of goodness.  By the time we were done, we were all groaning about how full we were, but we were all laughing and smiling. Bonding, that's what this kind of evening was about.   Would I go here again? HELL YES! Especially with these wonderful ladies!

Took mom to the Yankee Bean. I've seen it, but never ventured into the small space, so I thought that we should.  The place is TINY. 4 or 5 tables, a TV and a counter. You sit down and the waitress comes over, she covered the specials and let us peruse the menu.   When we did order, I ordered the Taco bean (I think that's what they were calling it) soup - which was basically a chili, and tasty, if bland. Both mom and I ordered the Mediteranian Wrap. Both of us found it tasty, but for two of us, with 2 wraps, 2 sodas and one bowl of soup, it ran $30.

This is not for the wooden rollercoaster that guarantees a trip to the Chiropractor. But rather GWAZI FIELD... The parade space where Busch Gardens holds it's concerts or other activities.   Tonight was part of the Summer Nights Concert Series featuring Pentatonix (PTX), if you've not heard of them, I'll wait while you look them up on Youtube.  *jeopard theme song plays*  Are you back, what did you think? Pretty amazing accapella group, right?  Now, imagine getting to see them live!  Well that's what I got to do.  The Gwazi field is set up so that there can be a large concert venue, Three large seating areas, enough benches for over 3000 people comfortably, 5000 if they pack them in. Tonight was seriously the first time i'd ever seen it packed so fully.    The sound and light show that they use is pretty phenomenal, if you ever get  a chance to see the Kenetics show, you'll understand why! They've put a lot of money into this improvement in the park, and it shows.  They even have beverage and food kiosks that look like little houses that line the walk way, which make getting your souviners, food and beverage very easy.  And 2 different sets of restrooms are close by.

Visited the Cheesecake factory with a friend who'd flown into town and let me choose where to go. I'm used to waiting up to an hour for seating, but at lunch, I was able to walk right in. Color me impressed! Granted, it was lunch, so that probably had something to do with it, but I digress... Service was excellent! Our waitress was chipper and cheerful and very helpful with ideas for what to order.   My friend and I perused the extensive menu while we chatted and caught up and then placed our orders. I ordered one of the lunch specials, a 1/2 sandwich a "cup" of soup and a salad. I didn't realize how much food that was going to be.  LORDY! There was a lot of food and that CUP of soup was really a bowl.  I wasn't able to eat all of it and ended up taking much of the food home with me.   My companion chose a meal of Salmon and asparagus which was both light and looked delicious. The meal was served quickly, along with some tantalizing fresh bread.  We really enjoyed everything that we tasted.    And because this is the Cheesecake factory, we did have to buy dessert, but not the namesake, we went with Tiramisu. Wow. i've not hat something so good outside of Tarpon, it really was 2nd to none. Yummy!

First time at Bar Louie at Countryside. A friend from out of town was visiting, so we opted for a place between us both.   Since we were catching up, we didn't order right away, but this didn't stop the waitress from asking us every 5 minutes if we were ready.  When we finally placed our orders, we chose the salmon sliders and the chicken taco plata.   The food came quickly, and over all, I'd say it was tasty, but with my order I got "Rice and beans". Needless to say, you can't to -everything- good.  The rice was hard and undercooked, the beans were overly spiced and inedible.   The tacos themselves were good, and the salmon sliders with Tots were tasty.  Eventually the wind started to build up and sadly our our door heater was out of propane so we were unable to get warm... we took ourselves inside.   Inside, we found that the ambient music was -too- loud to carry on conversations unless we practically yelled across the table.   We ended up ordering dessert, both of them that were listed on the menu, the Chocolate Cake and the Apple Whisky Cake. Both were absolute delicious - as was the coffee I ordered.   When we determined we wanted to pay the bill, our waitress who'd up till then, bothered us every 5-10 minutes was no where to be found.. Ah well.   Would I come back? Maybe. I'd certainly get the tots! YUM.

Today found the husband and I out  and about looking for a new place to nosh on this warm December Afternoon of Christmas shopping. We'd tried for a place in Ozona, only to find out they were closed.  The Dunedin Smokehouse was near enough so we motored our way down through the bike traffic - something was certainly going on in Dunedin to bring the bikers out, and snagged primo princess parking right up front.   Since the afternoon was mild, we sat outside and had a delightful waitress who took our order, she got everything right and even suggested that my Husbeast try one of the local brews from 7th Son, just down the street. It was a delectably light orange beer that even I could drink, and I don't drink beer!  Our meals were plentiful, I ordered the pork shoulder dinner, which was juicy, flavourful and rich. My two sides, potato salad and Gouda Mac & cheese were delectable. My Darling had the Porker, a lot of meat, with sausage, ribs and pulled pork and two sides, his were some greens sauteed in bacon and of course the Mac & Cheese. I'm not sure that I could justify the $1.50 up charge for the M&C for both of us again in the future, but it certainly was a tasty plate.  He managed to finish his, I took over half of mine home.   The service was quick, efficient and always on par. I think the only time we had any "issue" was in the time seating to having our order taken. About 7 minutes passed because Our waitress wasn't on the floor just yet and the other waitress was talking/kabitzing with another table whom she seemed very familiar with.   Over all, the visit was a good one. We enjoyed ourselves and will most certainly return.

I popped in to JC Penney's to see the Sephora location. I wanted to see what was going to be on clearance. Nothing caught my eye, so I ended up taking a walk through the isles.   While there, I happened to notice that there were boxed jewelry sets on sale for 40-75% off. This is pretty good! Especially since I'm enjoying wearing pendants these days. I managed to pick up several marcasite sets with pendants and earrings for less than $12.00 each. These were door-busters for the day after Christmas and Saturday. I'm glad I got what I got!  The rest of the store was in turmoil with returns, but the register that I came to was pretty quick, and the cashier, Pat, was really personable and friendly.

If you come here, make sure that you don't park in the wrong area. Much of this is NOT public parking, Much of it is for Deeman's landing and those who live here. Otherwise, there is a circle of parking at the end, about 20 spaces in total, that are geared towards the public. You can park here, but watch out for those who are space hogs or don't understand how to park in a semi circle.   The monument here, for St. Petersburg's fallen Police Officers is quite lovely, if sobering, The view of the (Now defunct) Pier is quite incredible, and of course there is Albert Whitted Airfield, so you can see planes taking off and landing every so often.  It's a good place to sit and watch the wild life or just take a load off and listen to the lapping of the waves on the break water.

Met a friend here today for lunch.   Let me be honest, I was trepidatious. I am not vegan, I don't know anything about eating Raw, and I didn't know what to expect.   From the moment I walked in, I was pleasantly surprised. First, it smelled REALLY good. I mean REALLY good! 2nd, I was asked if this was my first time, and since it was, they offered me samples of their smoothie of the day, an Orangecicle one that was tasty, and then samples of their veggie pate's that they use in their food.    I do have a food allergy, so after clarifying which ones I could eat - the ones without the hot peppers (only their chili has it) We were good to go!  The faux eggs and faux re-fried bean paste were both absolutely delicious.  My friend and I opted for their today's specials and we were RAWKED to the core. The food tasted clean and fresh as it's all made in house. The strawberry lemonaide was neither too tart or sweet and was refreshing to boot.   For desert we had the key lime Cheeze cake which was absolutely yumm-ola! I would certainly recommend this place if you're in the area. It's THAT good.

I love stopping in TJ Maxx, but the reason I come is to see if they have any Argan Oil cleansing mousse. I'm addicted! That stuff cleans like nothing else. Sadly of all the locations I've been to lately, NONE of them have had it.   This location is nice, quite neat and well kept. I was not impressed with their beauty and makeup section, as it wasn't laid out like i'm used to but over all, a good, sound store.

I was lucky enough to experience ESP during the daytime while on the Legendary Haunt Tour. We were able to see about half of Terror Behind the Walls with the lights up and hear about how they transform this historic site into a haunt in about 90 minutes.   This is such an incredible site, wether or not it was being used as a haunt. I know I could wile away a complete day here, exploring every nook and cranny. The echos of the past seem to scream through the hallways. The sounds are clear, if only in the imagination.

Since i'm following a low carb diet, eating out is a challenge.  I wanted something that I didn't cook for a change! I was out at Target on 54 & Little road, and decided, I'm going to try Chili's, since they have a "Lighter Side menu".  The husbeast, the bestie and I were seated without any preamble and waited only a few minutes for our waitress to come by and offer us our drinks, which we quickly placed.  For dinner, each of us chose something off the Lighter Side, I got the Grilled Chicken Salad, the bestie got the Talipa, but opted to have the rice subbed out for more broccoli, and all the sauces on the side, and the Husbeast got the shrimp tacos.    Everything came out just as we ordered. Sauces that were ordered on the side, came on the side. Substitutions that were asked for, were made. This impressed me because honestly, this usually gets screwed up.  And all the food off this special menu was very tasty.   The only reason I'm only giving 3 stars is because the service was -s-l-o-w-.  We wanted to cash out, but there was one waitress who was just chatting with a couple at the end of her station for over 20 minutes, and the manager had to come and cut her off.  Our waitress delivered our check, and then disappeared for over 8 minutes.  We were on some what of a schedule so this set us back considerably when we already had the money set to go.

Yep, I found another one. Why? A friend needed a new bra!   Here's a hint for all the women who might come across this: If you gain/lose more than 20 pounds, it's time to get re-fitted in your bra. I guarantee that you're NOT what you were before.    Since I can usually visually size very well, I took my friend over to Ross, and found a few different styles for her to try on. One thing I HATE about Ross is that their lingerie sections are horribly kept. It doesn't matter which one I visit, the bras are disgusting. They are never in order, they are always messed up, Finding a size is like an easter egg hunt. GOOD LUCK!   But we did find a few of the sizes I suggested - I generally suggest two, different band/cup combo's because Go up a band, go down a cup, is kind of how it works. And you HAVE to try them on. Well, after 3 different ones, we found one that she liked and it was only $6.99 +tax.   After that, I looked around and saw nothing I either didn't already have or nothing I wanted. Heck, I even played personal shopper for a complete stranger. Yes, life is fun when you have very few inhibitions.   Ross is great when you need something and you just don't know what!

I haven't been in a Pier 1 in AGES. I now know why. I WANT EVERYTHING!!!  They have everything that I could ever desire to decorate a home, a hundred homes. From earth tones to peacock brights. Whether I want something that's sedate or something that's absolutely,ridiculously, out of this world covered with bling!    I love their book cases, their futons and rugs. They have some of the best statuary and dishes I've had the pleasure of seeing.   Truly, if you want decorator pieces with friendly service, come visit Pier 1.

Popped in to get myself a diet coke since I was on the way home, and found out that they had a few of the Disney Collection items in their Cosmetics Area. I wound up getting the villain's hair ties and a Maleficent make up bag. I hope they get the Elf Sets in soon!  The check out girl was awesome, she certianly knows her clients by name and cares for each one of them!

DRAG QUEEN BINGO!  Need I say more? Traila Parks and Natasha Richards host this weekly event, and let me tell you, it is not for the prudish. These "girls" really do pull out all the stops to make it a fun night to be had.   If you win in one of the early games, you get to spin the prize wheel which can net you anything from a "Tea bagging" to drinks on the house. We won one game and spun the wheel only to win long island ice teas!  There were some awesome drink specials on Skittles and starbusts, and while they sound delicious, I didn't have any. Some beers were very cheap as well.  It was a fun evening and I look forward to becoming a regular.   There is a drawback though... because it is a bar, there is smoking allowed on the inside. If you're not a smoker, you need to be aware of this in advance.

This mall quite frankly scares me. It's old, It's out of date and the parking lot is just.. yeah. I came here for one particular store.. and found it, but had to drive all the way to the back, because I didn't want to park at the front of the mall. It's either time for a face lift, or time for this mall to be given last rights.

I don't usually stop into pet supply stores, but today, my cat fountain failed me (or so I thought) so I needed to replace the unit, since i never seem to be able to get just the little bubbler that runs them.   Pet Smart had quite the selection to choose from and since I have their loyalty card, I was able to get it for $69 vs the $94 it was marked.   I also took a few minutes to commune with the felines up for adoption, to look at the Herps and the birds.   The biggest draw back? The stink of the reptile cages. It hit me hard when I came in today.

Usually I love a Dillards. I go because they have a large collection of bras in my size and their women's clothing (Especially clearance) is always a fine selection.   On this visit, I went to check out the annual clearance of bras, and while there in the lingerie department, the store associates were too busy kabitzing about another employee to bother and see if I needed help (I didn't, I knew what I was looking for) I got to hear some interesting gossip though!  Also while there, as I was browsing through the (horribly disorganized) clearance bin, I was approached by the Estee Lauder sales girl, she asked if I used their make up, I don't, but she offered me a trial of their base. I took the card, but didn't take her up on the sample,I'm a MAC girl all the way.   When I finally decided to try on the bounty of clearance bras, I asked for a room to try things on and was just waved on into the trial room. Only after 25 minutes did I come out with my choices, to find the sales girl on the phone, supposedly checking on something, but the conversation I overheard was purely personal. To her credit, she did hang up and put through my sale.    I won't be back to the Countryside Dillards.

I've been waiting for this place to open. It's tucked away in the back corner of a shopping center that has a couple of great places to eat already, so this looks like it will be a great addition.  Upon entering, you're greeted with a great quirky atmosphere. Reclaimed woods from an old barn lines the walls, old oak on the floor. Edison lamps hang from the ceilings, along with some some "Steam Punk-esque" type of fixtures that give the place something more than a Hipster vibe, quirky but chic.   It wasn't busy when we arrived at 9pm, but the place still had a good crowd as the husbeastie and I were sat at a cozy table for two near the window. We got acquainted with their "Playful Summer Menu" and noticed that there were some really interesting options on the menu. Items like "French onion soup Rings", Meatloaf sliders and Baby Brats.  We were intigued by the onion rings so we chose them and I'm glad we did.. they were -SO- Good!  Our waitress was a delight, we asked her what was good and she made a few recommendations, basically spanning the menu, in the end the Husband chose the Craft burger with bacon and pork belly and I chose the Yippie Hippie salad with candied walnuts and cherries. Both were amazingly flavourful! The burger was so juicy! Cooked to a perfect medium rare, the bacon and pork belly added such depth of flavour that I couldn't help but want another bite.   The salad was served with an deliciously moist chicken breast, lots of juicy apple and candied walnuts that brought out the nuance of tastes.  I think that the dried cherries though.. wer e a bit of over kill.   For dessert we had a tough decision to make, it was either the flourless chocolate cake or the State fair puffs. In the end, the State fair puffs won out with their light and airy texture and the raspberry/greek yogurt sauce for dipping.  We left with really happy bellies. With this being only their second week, I'm certain that if they keep going in they way that they are currently trending they'll be a fixture in no time.  They are gonna be great!

This target is .. large and clean. The employees are always helpful and ready to go out of their way to find what you're looking for.   The layout is a bit different than my usual Target so i get a bit lost, but that's ok, that just means I'm up for an adventure every time I make my way through those great big doors!

Alright, my fellow yelper, Anna M always goes here, and since we were having a Girl's day, Lindsey and I decided this was the right place to have desert.   I honestly didn't know what to expect, but I was happy to see that parking was free before 5pm (We arrived shortly before 3:30) and Pi wasn't busy at all.   I ordered a Chocolate vanilla mousse cake, and a Luna hand crafted soda, with my yelp check in, I got a free macaron (a $2.22 value)  The soda was mixed right before my eyes, and it was incredibly good. Good enough that I got another one before we left. Light, tart and sweet, the flavors were spot on.  The macaron was flaky and almost as good as the ones I got in Vegas.  The Mousse cake was tasty as well, a bit heavy and since my belly has been fighting me, I was only able to eat a little bit, the rest resides now in my fridge for a later snack with some coffee.  The reason for 3 not 4 stars: One of the servers had severe B.O. I'm not talking light, I'm talking -STANK-. I noticed it when she delivered the drinks to the table beside us, and Lindsey noticed it when she delivered her handcrafted coffee to our table.  It is very off putting to eat or drink food when your olfactory senses are suddenly over whelmed with the RIPE scent of an unwashed body.

A clean Wawa, but once again, this wawa didn't have their pumps taped for security. This makes me fidgity in today's day and age. I don't understand why they don't offer this implied step to their patrons.   They did offer the cheapest gas at $1.99 in the area, the others around being $2.09 and $2.03. The pump was neat and the window cleaning station was half empty of towels as well as cleaning solution. Over all it's not the best impression.

If you want quirky, original gifts, this is going to be your place to stop. I was drawn in by the name alone, but the merchandise was amazingly top notch. They specialize in interior design and private events, and it shows! Every inch of this store is spotlessly set up. It is FLAWLESS.   If you want pillows that are reminiscent of old billboards/post cards welcoming you to St. Pete - that were custom made for the shop, you'll find them. If you want hand painted pillows that have the perfect sentiment for today, but may not be ... perfectly politically correct, they're here.   Heck, you'll even find some condoms, in cute little jars, that are imprinted with an "interesting" message.   Locally owned and operated, it's a great shop to visit & support!

This place has -everything-. What I was looking for was a pair of kitten heels (found them) but I ended up finding so much more.  I found a few shirts and some pants for my husband in their "Big & Tall" section. Some racy lingerie for myself - and for the husbeastie for Xmas.  I found some pretty bling for the Xmas party I'll be going to on Saturday, and all of it was reasonably priced too!   I will say that I did find some of the same items that I'd seen at Ross the other day, and their prices were slightly higher... and on other items, their prices were lower. I guess it's just a toss up.    The only complaint I really have is the attitude of their employees. I was looking through their shoes, and rather than move so I could look at the size I needed, As there are precious few size 11's available, their associate stood right in front of the ones I was going to look at, with a cart of inventory, and would NOT move. JUST sat there and looked at me as if daring me to move her.  I went around her.   The store is a bit disorganized, but any large discountery is going to be, it is the nature of the beast, you just have to dig for that bargain!

Stopped in to get Coffee and Donuts for the haunt crew. It's always a good thing to bring those you work with a treat. I also picked up my lunch, sadly the tuna salad was rancid, and just didn't smell right so that ended up getting tossed.  The donuts though, those were a hit.

Stopped in here for lunch with an ex-beau.  Their food is good. I got the pulled pork with sides of loaded potato salad and green beans. All of it was so good, except the potato salad, it was TOO heavy on the ranch/sour cream.   In any case, stop and get you some Holy hog. You'll thank me.

Sometimes you just need coffee. I'd much prefer to give my money to a mom and pop coffee joint, but honestly, $bux will have to do. The service was excellent, the product was perfect. and the company was great.

After an amazing event, I headed down to Ybor to catch my friend Jenny do a show at the Lion's Den. Sadly for me, it was already over.  However, I was able to make my way up the stairs, (Where it's locate) and take a look around.  Inside, the Lion's Den is very inviting. Large comfy Couches, hard wood floors, and hookah! What else could be better?  I will say that it does need to be better marked, as it was very easy to walk past. The sign that hangs down over the door way either needs to have better lettering and lighting or there needs to be an arrow pointing UP!  For those who don't do stairs (And it's steep!) there's an elevator that carries a fair load of folks! Stop by and enjoy a good smoke and some conversation!

I stopped in after visiting my mom at the Hospital.   I wasn't even aware that NPR had a Beef's, but I'm glad they do. I sat at the bar, and the tender was awesome. She made sure my drink didn't go dry and took my order.  Once my order was placed, I watched a bit of TV on the monitors, before the wings were delivered to me, hot and fresh.   I opted for the Garlic parmesan wings, bone in and they were delicious! The skin was crispy, the seasoning was spot on and they were gone in a flash.   The eatery itself is neat and clean. I just can't get over the fact that this used to be a funeral home and a tea room.

Came in for my mom's 74th birthday. We told them when we arrived, thought they'd make note of it as we've seen them come and do a birthday song at the table...  Our waiter was personable, but clutzy. We arrived around 8pm and the restaurant was -not- busy. There were 2 other tables that were being served, one a large party, the other a couple.  Our waiter was handling one of them.   We placed our orders, starting with apps: The Scotty Thompson Bruchetta and the small calamari.  To his credit, the waiter brought both sauces.  When we placed our orders for our mains, even though it was Monday, we opted out of their specials, we wanted to try their new offerings, the pairs.  The husband opted to try the Chicken something with lasagne. Mom and I tried the chicken bryan with the pork tenderloins.  And my niece who often only eats burgers, had to have some help.  The waiter helped her make her decision.   When the food was delivered, the first thing I noticed was the size of the pork. These were so very VERY small, About 1" across Quite literally bite sized. The bacon that wrapped the pork was charred black. Not even delicately crisped, but absolutely burned.    The chicken Bryan was about half the portion you would get if you ordered a small order, but it was tasty as usual.  Mom ordered the steamed spinach and it was OILY as all get out, but my green beans were scrumptious.   The husband ordered his chicken/lasagne combo and was disappointed by his portion size as well. The lasagne was about 2" long by an inch wide. A taste or tease but hardly a portion. The chicken was little more than that as well.  And his spinach was the same, swimming in oil.    The niece liked her creamy tomato sauce dish. In the end, when the dessert was offered, we mentioned the birthday once more but it went over the head of the waiter once more. *shrug* Ah well, I do enjoy their food, but this location seems to be slipping..

A friend and I were looking for something to do - we didn't want the usual dinner and a movie, so he suggested Put Put Golf.  This was the only place that came to mind for both of us.   The Course is fun, challenging and honestly just nice looking. Sure there are some areas that need a bit of cleaning (the mummy for one) but over all, the treasure hunt, the spin a shot and the atmosphere of the place just add to the experience.   Bring the whole family, you'll have a blast. Bonus if it's over cast, as you'll not have a lot of people ahead or behind you.

I haven't been back since we did the Yelp Event here. I was THRILLED that I got the chance to come back on a whim.   I was asked if I'd been there before, when i said yes, they welcomed me back, made sure I had my VIP card, asked me if I had it on me, when I said no, they said it was ok, showed me the place in their book where I could text my phone number and that would automatically check me in, I just had to give a code to the waitress.   I was seated next to the kitchen, it was a very busy/distracting seat, but I got to see how fast the kitchen gets things in and out. I'd probably ask not to be sat there in the future, as I'm not a fan of fish odors and there were several.  However, I did order one of the lunch combos, a soup and salad for $8.99, of which I got a wedge salad and a crock of french onion soup. Both were exceedingly tasty.   Sad is that I did break a tooth.- not their fault in the least, I just know it happened there.

Stopped in tonight, and I will say that service is QUICK. So quick you don't even have time to check the menu before your waiter is there asking if you want an App.  OY! May I please have a moment to look?  Ok.. thanks.   Anyway.. Once I was able to look at the menu, I decided to order the edamame, and it was as I expected, though they did offer dipping spices, which were pretty tasty.  Our meals that were ordered were surprisingly large.. well my friends was anyway. I ordered off the 7 below 700 menu, I got the parmesan crusted steak, and while it was tasty, I wished they'd served the steak and salad on seperate plates. A bloody steak does not pair well with your bleu cheese salad dressing.   However, the shrimp and chicken fingers plate? The serving on that was GIGANTIC. 2/3rds of it ended coming home and becoming a meal for my friend's wife.  The shrimp and chicken were all very moist and flavourful.

The renovations they're doing to update the airport make it seem small, make it seem cluttered, but in truth, TIA is such a nice airport.  The staff is usually very friendly, there are lots of places to charge phones/tablets/what have you. There are lots of places to eat shops to hang out in. There is a LOT to do.

Stopped in tonight because I was craving Italian. Mind you, this is a new place and we weren't sure what they had so...  Backdraughts is a definite highlight to Main Street, Tarpon Springs. Their Wood Fired pizza oven makes the place cozy, the big bar is a nice asset as the tv is tucked back behind the topper and not an eye sore to all the other patrons.   The tables are spacious and there's nice tables outside for those who want to dine Alfresco - you know, for the few days a year when the mosquitoes aren't out to carry you away and the temps are bareable.   The service was Ok. A tad slow, but with only a few people inside it really wasn't bad.   The food... OMG.  We started with the house cut waffle fries with parmesan & garlic seasoning, they were THE BOMB! Lots of good seasoning and very crispy.  As for the pizza, we tried the White Hibiscus pizza. WOW. This is how I want a white pizza served. It was HEAPED with spinach, the fresh ricotta in literal scoops, a lovely Basalmic drizzle .. all of it was luscious and absolutely decadent.   We will be back.

Comfort food, that's what Bob Evans is.  A place where the older crowd comes , to have a decent meal at a decent price. The food is a bit above cafeteria food in flavor (though their soups are amazing) but you get enough to keep you fed and the prices are a good value, and they often put out coupons.

The Disney retail store in Country Side mall, is ...just like all Disney stores, chock full of Disney Merchandise. I came for one purpose alone.. To get my Annual Pass. I didn't want any hassle, I just wanted to get the pass and be on my way.  It was that simple.   I spoke to one cast member, she helped me quickly and I was able to get out of the store without much of an issue, other than over hearing one of the voice clips of Mickey admonishing Minnie to take it easy on the donuts, because they're fattening. *Shakes head* No need to fat shame women, there, Disney.

We stopped in at staples because we needed ink for our printer.   We spoke with one of the sales associates and he gave us a tip about how to clean printer heads and sold us an inexpensive ink cartridge. We used his tip and it worked! We still kept the printer cartridge that we bought, as a backup is necesary!

i remember when this place was the tops.   But that was back in the early 1990's. Fast Forward to 2013 and boy how the mighty have fallen. It was a derelict relic of the past.  Some flea markets are fun to dig through, this one was nothing but a sad shadow of what it used to be. So many empty stalls, so much malaise, that it seemed as if the whole place were looking for someone to pull the plug.  The one thing I noticed was the "Dollar Tree" mentality. There would be these large swaths of booths, all grouped together - a store if you will, of cheap imported merchandise, and they were in every section of the market.   They were selling the same things - exactly the same things. NO variety in item or price. It was really rather pathetic.

I've seen my friends check in here before, but tonight it was OUR turn.  I really didn't know what to expect, and the name is very exotic.. so I kind of crossed my fingers and jumped in.  When we arrived at almost 8pm there was a 20 minute wait to be seated, but once we were seated, our waitress (Kerry, I think) came over right away and took our drink orders. She was really friendly and personable. She answered all our questions and let us know what to expect since it was our first visit.     For our starters we ordered the pork and plantains, which turned out to be a really tasty combination. I'm not very adventurous in my food choices, I usually leave that up to the Husband, but tonight, those flavours combined nicely, The smoky pulled pork, the slightly sweet plantain, the sweet with heat of the mango salsa and the bbq sauce made for some really good bites. And the cilantro crema? REALLY tasty.  Since it was Burrito night  - They have a special every night of the week - the husband ordered a chicken burrito, it wasn't anything fancy but the flvours were all good. I ordered one of their Zinzaladas, a chicken one.  For me, the red adobo sauce was a touch too sweet, but when I added some of the left over cilantro crema.. well that just made it all the better.   What really made this a 5 star visit though? It was the fact that the manager came over and welcomed us to the place, he even gave us a voucher for a free appetizer the next time we come back. That was above and beyond in my book and shows that they actually care about what the customer thinks.  We will be back.

I LOVE the Spice and Tea exchange! When I get the chance, I stop in!  There is a blend that I absolutely can NOT go without, and if you want a suggestion.. try the Espresso Steak rub. I guarantee that you will thank me.  They have a customer reward program that is -so- worth it. Sotp in and visit, try their blends, you too, will become a faithful returning customer.

I should have checked the address when I wrote my other review.. So.. the review for that one goes here:      Not our first choice for dinner on this Saturday night, but since our first choice was SUPER busy, we decided to give this place a go.  There were 2 couples inside, one sitting and eating, the other waiting for their order to go.      We walked in, and took a moment to familiarize ourselves with the menu. I asked what was good, and got the standard answer of "everything" and then I was told what was popular, such as their Pulled Pork, pulled chicken and their greens.  Taking those things into consideration, I ordered the Pulled pork diner - 2 sides being the cole slaw and potato salad. The husbeast had the Pulled beef with Cole Slaw and french fries and my friend who was joining us had the sausage dinner with 2 sides of their greens.      Since it wasn't busy, we had the undivided attention, which pretty much included table service and everything. We asked for our sauce on the side, and it was given. There is no .. choice of sauces, it is only Daddy Mack's sauce, which is light, kind of sweet, with no tang. It's good but it's not Spectacular, and they will sell a 32ox bottle to you for $6.99.      The food was tasty, well the meat was. The Pulled Pork was tender, a bit on the dry side. The beef was flavorful and the smoked sausage was standard Keilbasa. As for the sides.. The fries were hands down the best thing we sampled. The cole slaw and potato salad were institutional - i'm not even kidding. They were store bought and getting close to ending their cycle of freshness. And the greens were Ok.      I'd come back, but not often.

The name has always made me giggle. It's a totally different euphsism, if you don't get it, I'm not explaining it to you.  Today though, I was on a girl date with my sister from another mister Lindsey From Lindsey goes Local and we decided ... WHY NOT.   I'm really glad we did! The owner calls it a "Girl Cave" and I can totally see why!  Inside it's an ecclectic mix of Vintage and New, of Fashion and trashion, of jewelry and fabulous fakes.  If you're looking for some dress up pieces, if you're looking for something to zuzsh up your burly-q outfit, if you're looking for an inexpensive corset (read not a heavy duty steel boned one) you're gonna find it here.   I ran across: Boas, gloves, costume jewelry, some nice pieces of decor, all manner of clothing, furs! and what have you, including to adorable puppies that were up for adoption. It was terribly hard to walk out without one of those sweet pups in my hands.  Each and every nook and cranny is filled with something that is both functional and fun. She has -everything- including a welcome smile and a glass of wine or a bottle of water for you as you shop.   Is this a place I'll be back to? YOU BETCHA!

Since the husbeast has a big trip next week to Washington DC, and his hands look kind of Raggedy, I thought it would be nice to start out the New Year with both of us getting Manicures.   He's never had one and I enjoy one so I thought I'd traipse us down to the place I found when I found Bayou Cleaners.  They were open, but busy, having given a couple of folks the day off for the new year.  That was OK for us, we didn't mind waiting. I was told to go choose a color and the husband was brought up to the table right away.   The nail tech worked diligently to make his nails look nice. She shaped and filed and buffed and even massaged his arms, using a technique that he thought only I used. *Heh! In your face!*    I got to wait a few minutes more after I decided that I wanted the Gel Manicure, it will last longer and not chip in a week. After all, my nails need to look good for Washington for me too.  I got Bill, he was very diligent in doing the nails, but I was slightly disappointed in the paint job. I loved the colors i chose, but the accent nails didn't get the coverage I felt they needed. However, I would come back and plan to, to get a pedicure.

I'm at that part of the year where I start looking for all new places to visit. Both my guys support this and so today the three of us spun the Yelp dial and found Christo's by accident.  We plugged in the address into the GPS and made our way, beating the Sunday Church crowds but apparently that in it's self wasn't enough, Sunday is a BUSY day with the regulars too.  And having eaten here now, I know why! Christo's is GOOD!  We were one of two groups of three waiting to be seated, but we didn't wait long, only about 10 minutes, once a table was cleared, we were seated, and our waitress was RIGHT there.  We all had coffee and water as our drinks.  She got that for us, while we perused the large menu.   The husbeastie was feeling brunchie, so he got himself the Monte Christo, but the beau and I were both feeling breakfast-y, so we both essentially got the same meal, the 2+2+2 (#16) but I got pumpkin pancakes where he got himself the french toast.   The food came out quickly and it was -delicious-! The eggs that we had on our platters were done to perfection and the cheese (Since we had that added on) was melted in. The pumpkin pancakes were dense but absolutely amazing, and the bacon was so yummy. I had a piece of the french toast and that too was so incredibly tasty.   The Monte Cristo sandwich was thick and a touch different than I've seen them done in the past, there was no grape jelly in it either, but the husbeastie liked his and the onion rings, that came as the side with it, were crispy and flavourful.   We all liked the food and the place was warm and friendly.

I stayed here for what was supposed to be an over night stay, but turned into 4 days. I have to say that I'm impressed. There were only one or two nurses/aids who didn't live up to their own level of care.   From the intake to the moment I left, I was well cared for. I felt comfortable and listened to (mostly) and I would stay here again if it were centrally located to me.    Their rooms on the post op wings are small but clean, and the nurses make sure you know that you can ring them. I'm the kind of patient that doesn't bother a nurse unless I absolutely NEED to. Apparently they appreciate that, but can forget about a patient like me. (it's happened in the past) However I do know how to be my own best advocate and learned to be one on this stay.

I attended 1001 Nights at Hip Expressions last night. Coincidentally it was also their 12th anniversary (YIP YIP).  This was my first visit to the location, because honestly I always thought it was "too far away" from my home in Tarpon. Turns out that it's actually closer than the place in Lutz.   The show was good, opening with "Kiss Kiss" by the school troupe the Hip Stars, lead by Johanna.  All I can say is that they were fantastic.  There were people who went to the school, and those who didn't, all who where there to entertain us and make us smile.   The space we were in was absolutely stunning. I'm now going to look into the different classes they offer and see what fits into my schedule.

Stopped in here with our bi-weekly gathering of the geeks, a group of 8 folks who like to eat together and talk, the place was chosen by one of our crew and reservations were made.  We took up one bank of their tables.    The place was filled with locals, and though not large, it was busy.  There was one waiter, and he was taking care of everything and everyone, and he got the job done!  Our drink orders and food orders were taken fast and efficiently.  When orders started coming out, they came out correctly.   Almost everyone ordered the handmade fresh rolls and those were so amazingly tasty with fresh mint and shrimp, they were to die for.  I ordered a broken rice dish with shrimp and pork and the husbeastie ordered a big bowl of Pho. Both were devoured! They were absolutely tasty and made fresh.  The broken rice dish I had had lots of shreded carrot and pickled cabbage, lettuce, mint and sprouts, it was filling and very crisp to the tongue.

Sweet tomatoes or Soup Plantation if you're west of the Mississippi is a fantastic place to eat when you tire of heavy meals and want something light and refreshing to nosh on.   I love the way they stagger their menus throughout the year so that each moth has a different theme. This month (June) is berry month and it's featured in the salads and in the breads. Trust me when I say it's delicious. Make sure you try the raspberry lemonade, all that's missing is the vodka.   So many different types of soup can be had! They usually manage to have my favorite - the chili or even a potato leak variety and that just makes me even MORE happy.  This, is, for sure, one of my go to places to eat.

I'm a Red Robin fan.  I admit it, I like them a lot. HOWEVER, I generally am a picky eater. I don't eat a lot of carbohydrates, so when I order something, I will ask for special requests... which is what I did when I stopped into this location with my friend Dani.  We arrived, we sat immediately and noticed that they'd done some recent remodeling. When we asked how long ago they'd done it, we were told a year ago.  We knew it'd been more recent than that, but I guess that was the time frame they were telling people. *shrug*  We both ordered something with a customization to it. My friend ordered the cobb salad, no tomatoes, dressing on the side. Me, I ordered the soup/salad combo, the southwestern salad, no jalapeno coins (Allergy) and dressing on the side.   Our food came.. for some reason, the salads were taking a -very- long time.  Anway, when they came, the soup was fantastic, but my salad was very.. very .. wet.  like soupy wet. A puddle at the bottom of the bowl also showed that there was dressing on it, as it wasn't clear fluid. I was sorely disappointed.   I called my waitress over and she apologized profusely, she took it back to the kitchen and immediately had the manager come over. He had them re-make the salad for me, and he also took it off the bill (something he didn't have to do at all, but I'm thankful he did.)  Over all, the Service was impeccable, but the food was just Meh.

We'd come into the plaza for Ice Cream, but that shop was over run with folks.  We walked until we found Westshore Pizza. The boyfriend and I decided that a slice and a soda would be a good lunch.   We both chose our slice - Pepperoni for me, Meat lovers for him, and a can of diet for both of us and selected our seats.   The pizza was heated up to the perfect temp and brought out to our table.  We enjoyed our time while we chatted and snacked.   Over all tasty pizza. The crust was light and crisp, the sauce was nice, and the cheese was the right amount of gooey!

Let me start by saying: I don't eat spicy food.   That my friends made a reservation for us here was daunting to me. I had no idea what would be on the menu, what I'd even be able to eat in a place that serves Indian food. But with an open mind, I decided to give it a try.   We arrived at our appointed time, our reserved table was ready. (they say on the website if you have a party bigger than 4, it's best to make reservations, this is because they are small, about 12-15 tables total) We were sat and given time to peruse the menu. My friends coached me through things and I ended up ordering Butter Chicken, mild as well as some garlic naan and a tandori salad.   The table got an assortment of dishes, some people ordered Indian Hot. When we said this, the Waitress looked at them incredulously, because there's no way they could want it, right?  But those in the party crazy enough, assured her that YES, they wanted it as hot as she could have it made. Clearly she didn't believe them, but hey, she did bring it out HOT.   The food was tasty, I enjoyed the texture and flavour of the butter chicken over the rice with peas. The Naan was absolutely amazing.  But the salad.. First of all I expected it before the meal, and yet.. I got it mid way through the meal, the Waitress kept promising it to me, saying  "just a minute on the salad" I am not sure if it was a back room communication issue or what have you, but when I got it, the chicken on it was exceedingly dry, but the lettuce was fresh as was the cucumber, and the tomatoes were almost white.   All of us (three couples) ordered dessert... it was terribly disappointing.  One couple ordered the Pistachio ice cream. It looked re-frozen. There was ntohing creamy about it.  Another couple ordered the rice pudding. They said it was Ok.   We ordered the "donuts" I think theyre called Galub.  Um.. they were pretty much re-fried dense stale doughballs soaked in rose syrup. They were not good at all.   While I would eat here again, I would not order dessert.

Walked in today, to find that one of the hair dressers was cleaning up a bottle of spilled nail laquer with some weak nail polish remover. She thought she was nearly done, sadly the color - an obnoxious yellow- was tracked across the floor.   They were able to take the husbeastie almost immediately and trim him up. The price was a bit more expensive than I thought it would be, $24.00 for a trim? Ok, that's something I wasn't expecting. Granted he has long hair, but they were mainly shaving the curlies at the hair line.. Meh.   We probably won't return.

Ended up at Portillos after spending the afternoon down in Brandon.  Friends of mine RAVE about this place because it's from Chicago, and the only other time I've tried to go here it was BUSY and the drive thru was packed as well.  So when I showed up on Sunday I was happy to not only secure a very close parking spot, There was only a line inside 1 deep, with an actual register that was open.   The registers are a bit odd, there are 5 of them, but the people tend to come up in a bunch and you cant get to them because people are blocking them. *shrug* When you do get to the register, it takes a few minutes to order what you want, THEN you move over to another spot and either sit down and wait for your number to be called or stand awkwardly and wait for the food.  I chose to stand. It was about 4 minutes for my order to come up.    I ordered a Chili dog, onion rings and a large diet coke.  The total was just under $10.  Over all, the taste was delicious, I loved the firm bite into skin of the hotdog, it wasn't something I was expecting, but every bite had that snap. The chili was good and the cheese was ok. The rings were delightful and Diet Coke is diet coke just about everywhere.   Over all, it was good food. I will say, that sitting outside in a period of 15 minutes we saw no less than 4 people come out and check the trashcans.

On our way to melbourne I asked the Husbeast if we could fuel up for our 3 hour drive with some caffine. He said sure. I asked for one of their Peppermint coca coffees and I was none to pleased with it. Very heavy on the mint, very light on the cocoa, light on the coffee, their mix was WAY off.   The service was good though, so there is that.

I came here to pick up a quick breakfast before a doctor's visit.  Instead I picked up donut holes for the office and a small thing of Donut fries for myself.    The drive through service was quick and thorough, but the food was meh. The donut fries had obviously been kept in a warmer of some kind and tasted of natural gas, and were thus unedible.

I like this place!  I've visited here many times, but the most recent time was when Hurricane Michael was buzzing through.    Many folks were out, enjoying the light rain and watching people fish off the piers.  There were no dogs in the dog park though so at least they were sensible.   The water was high, but no one was playing in the choppy waves. We just watched people tossing nets off the piers trying to catch what fish they might be able to.   There are plenty of parking spaces, nice restrooms available and trails through the mangroves here.  A lot to do on a nice day or even not so nice day if you're so inclined.

Bi-weekly Geek dinner with friends. Table for 8 and we were sat at 2 Four tops (which, when you pull chairs around is seating for 6) so we had to pull another table over.    We waited and waited for chip and salsa, but when we got it, it was tasty.   We ordered the Guac and their special guac, to nosh on before our meals, but it came out after our meals came to the table. (Harumph)   The food was tasty and filling, but nothing remarkable or memorable.

I was excited for this new place. NPR needed a nice place to go to, and this is right next to the casino boat.   The atmosphere outside is lovely with the tiki bars and fire pits and the white sand beach. There are even docks so that boaters can pull right in.  We opted to eat in the main building, everything faces the water so no biggie.  The only big deal is that at sunset, you will go blind.   There are no shades of any kind so the sun will be in your face no matter where you sit.   The menu seems nice enough and our waitress was super friendly and sweet. We started with iced teas and gator bites.  I wasn't impressed as they were terribly bland. They could have been chicken for all I could taste. I did like the addition of the garlic fried pickles to the basket, bit at $12.99, the appetizer was the same price as the average entree.   For our mains we had a friend grouper sandwich, which the husbeastie said was greasy, flavorless and that the lettuce tasted like it had some petroleum products on it.  He at the fish, but not the bun or lettuce/tomato set up that came with. The fries and Aztec slaw we're tasty.   I had their coconut rum chicken, it came with rice and a green bean medley. The breast was large and fried, and the coconut rum sauce was very tasty. The rice was very similar to Vigo Spanish rice and the bean medley was good. Over all not a bad choice.  The parking lot was ridiculously small and they only allow valet, which when you're leaving is kind of a joke. But still.. it was free or just the cost of a tip. We we're even parked right up front.   Will I come back. Maybe.

Great head shop in St. Pete.  Clean, the cashiers really listen to what you're looking for.  On Friday, the CBD items are 50% off.  Their glass selections are lovely and the incense is delightful.  I wish I lived closer so that I could visit more frequently.

Third of the Curv stores I've gotten to visit and it's just as fabulous. I think it's the darkest feeling of them all but It has a great selection of wonderful finds.   While I was looking through the dresses, I stumbled across a Bob Mackie designer shift IN MY SIZE! You can bet that I snapped that up for a fantastic price.   I saw Mod Cloth, Torrid, Ashley Stewart and Lane Bryant in the racks along with other names. There was a great selection of styles and colors, not just uniform black. NO ma'am, Curves are celebrated here and you can bring your fashion forward plus clothing here for trade on Mon, Wed and Saturdays.

I hadn't been to a Bahama Breeze in AGES, so when I saw one on SR56, I told the husbeastie we'd have to go. The opportunity presented itself when we were on the way home from our hamcation.   We stopped in on the way home from Orlando and were in before it was 3pm, so we were in for happy hour pricing - half price appetizers, lower price cocktails.  We ordered the beef empanadas and the husbeast ordered their drink of the month, which we were told was one thing, but when it was delivered to the table, was a completely different drink.  We were fine with that, but would have liked to have been told   The beef empanadas were absolutely delicious. I didn't need anything after that, I was done, I could have gone home happy right then, but I'd ordered more food, I'd gotten their fried chicken, and it was good, but those beef empanadas were so good, they over shadowed everything else.   When we got our bill, we didn't have happy hour pricing, we didn't get the $5 price on the empanada. And our waitress was taking forever to check on us and get back when when had a question. So we just paid the bill and decided we wont be back.

The other night I went out to dinner with my husband and 6 other friends. We arrived at prime time and had to wait. This was fine, the wait wasn't terribly long.  We were seated, and our orders were taken. The server was very pleasant and efficient, especially when having to deal with a large party.  When the orders were brought to us.. one of our parties was served a steak that was supposed to be Medium Rare. What he got was well done.  He capitulated on flagging the waiter down and asking for it to be redone.  In the end, he did just that.  The server apologized profusely and the steak was taken back, mean while the rest of us ate our food. 10 minutes later, the steak was returned, a new one, it looked and smelled amazing, but when he cut into it.. it was almost blue.. it was -that- rare.  Two times his steak was wrong. So third time's the charm. Of course my friend was worried that it was going to be spit on or something else, but when they brought it out the final time it was passable. He did end up taking much of it home because the rest of us were done.    The manager came over to the table to present the checks, he casually handed my friend a card for a free Appetizer, but there was no money taken off for the steak. It's not that he wanted it free, after all, he didn't even speak up on it, but if you mess up twice, there probably should be a bit more compensation for their trouble, especially when he didn't get to eat with the rest of us and was forced to watch us.   Not a good first impression at all.

I haven't had Lumpia since I was in Hawaii.   The food was ok, it wasn't the best, but it was good, hearty. I wish I hadn't have waited 25 minutes in line for it though.   The staff was polite and courteous, but over all, it's not the best I've ever had.

I don't know why I was there today, except it was done as a favor for family. My brother in law was recently injured and he couldn't leave the house, so he was looking for a particular item that was a Costco exclusive.    The parking area was FULL, we were parking at the VERY back of the parking lot. Given we were 3 days to Christmas this shouldn't surprise me, but it does.
