We made our way to the membership desk, a line 10 deep.  We began to fill out our paperwork, and when we finally made it to the desk, we asked if the item was in stock.   They were BUSY, the store was pretty well picked over, you could see that stock was dwindling.

Drive though.  Ordered a Happy Meal, with a coke and a large tea.  I got exactly that, with instead of the micro kids coke, an actual small coke for the Happy Meal. That was a nice treat.     They got the order right, absolutely no complaints.

While exploring places we've not been, while the husband has been on vacation, we decided to explore our own town.   We spent time on Main Street and stumbled across this tiny gem. That's not word play, but an actual observation. This place is small, tucked into the old infrastructure of the antique buildings and all that makes up Tarpon's down town.   It's got a great ambience and focuses on chocolate beers. Cool Niche! The husband grabbed himself a pint of something, and I simply enjoyed the atmosphere and chatted with 2 other folks and the bar tender.   I noticed that they have a Yoga class at 7:30pm on Thursdays for $10.00 and that nets you a beer too!  This month (January 2019) they'll be doing a beer and Ice cream pairing. Lots of community involvement, I like that!  Yes, the Hubby enjoyed his beer! We'd come back.

The Ritz, Ybor is a concert and party venue.   We held our annual Howl-O-Scream Season wrap up party, Screamers Ball there this year, and it was awesome. Great dance space, security, bar (With high priced drinks - 1 star) a live band, AMAZING air conditioning (Necessary as this was a costume party and it was still 90+ and humid as heck.) and of course it is right near one of the parking garages, so that was a HUGE plus.   We had a good party, a good time and we actually enjoyed ourselves

I don't usually have a reason to go into Walmart Neighborhood markets, but my Niece drove by and needed to grab something so, why not?  The store is large, like half of a super walmart with all the grocery needs you might have.  I really only spent a few minutes up in the front, looking for the restrooms (Small, but clean with 2 stalls for such a large store. )   Personally, I'm not a fan of their layout as I'm a Publix fan, but they're conveinent to the neighborhood and open 24 hours.

I stopped here after having a new crown placed in my mouth. I'd wanted Anthony's Pizza, but I was there at 11:00 am, and they didn't open until 11:30, so I took a chance on Pickles Plus.  I'm glad I did.   I was seated immediately and the waitress came over asking me what I'd like to drink. I ordered a Diet Coke.  After a few minutes she came over and I asked for a few suggestions. She told me her favorties and told me the specials of the day.  I thanked her and then placed an order for her favorite, the Cuban, but instead of chips, I upgraded to the potato salad.   I received a HUGE sandwich, on what looked like a half a loaf of pressed cuban bread. Stuffed with all the proper toppings, cut in half, with a huge helping of some of the best tasting potato salad I've ever had.  Needless to say, I left with half the sandwich to go.  The cuban is phenomenal!   I'll be back, that's for certain.   Oh, and as I was checking out, they had these HUGE brownies for $3.00 you can bet I bought one for snacking later.  SO GOOD!

So last Saturday, I had pain like I've never had before.  I thought it was just a strained muscle or really bad gas, but nothing was doing anything to make me feel better.  In the end, I woke my husband and had him drive me to the nearest ER.  This would be Helen Ellis Memorial Hospital (Which is now Florida Hospital North Pinellas)  There was absolutely NO wait time in the ER triage area. I was taken back immediately. The asked me what was wrong and I told them.  They did some small tests and figured out that I was right, I was having a bad case of a gall bladder attack.  Due to some elevated tests, they wanted to admit me for observation and eventually 4 different surgeries to fix me.  I experienced exquisite care in the hospital. Everyone was above board, everyone was very attentive. The doctors, the nurses and even Ryan in food service, They went beyond what they needed to.  I reccomend this hospital to everyone.   I hope that my future doesn't hold another 8 day stay in the future.. but should it, i'll go back there.

On the way home from Georgia, I made it nearly all the way home. I didn't want to push it too much further so I stopped on SR52 to fill my tank. The price was the same as it was everywhere else, but this location was very well lit, exceptionally clean and the bathroom was very neat.

I had my tire pop on the way to Tribeca Salons. It was raining, and they're literally next door, so with my stylists blessing, I ran my car next door and let them put a new tire on.   Though I have road hazard, I didn't know that at the time, so I paid for a brand new tire, and had them bag up my old tire to take it to the dealership, but Tires Plus took care of me just before closing. They were awesome.

Two Words: Snackin' Bacon.   I use this dunkin's drive through a lot, since they're on the way to most places. I've never had an order botched. They're very friendly when you chat with them and I always leave a tip.

This place came highly reccomended by friends, and I really wanted to like it, but I can't.   We stopped in while on Vacation and sat at one of the many tables in the dead center of the room. TBH I'm not sure how they ever have every seat full, there's not enough room with the way the tables are arranged.   Anyway, we sat and perused the menu, I looked at the special board and then the menu, The hubby chose the Chili mac and I opted for The Big Al, but I asked for mine with cheese and no mayo thinking that it should be easy to customise that order. (The Big Al is 2 BLT Sandwiches, and a bowl of Mac Salad for $11.95) The waitress took our order on some handheld device and came back to the table explaining that she couldn't customize the order the way I wanted (?) That she had to charge me for 2 BLT's separately and the bowl of Mac salad, so asking for no mayo, and add cheese, became $14.85 vs $11.95.  Three bucks for cheese? I don't think so.  I think the waitress needs to master her equipment better.   The food tasted good, I can't fault them that.

Why did we wait so long to try Costa's? I'm not sure. I was down to try something new in the neighborhood.    Being off Athens street, they are not on the main drag, but they have plenty of traffic, a side parking lot has cameras so they can tow you if you park there and don't patronize them.   Many tables outside make it so you can enjoy the lovely evening air or keep away from the crowds inside, but for us, we opted for the inside tables.  The waitress was friendly as she brought us our drinks and bread -oh delicious Greek bread! Such tender crust and yummy soft inside!   We ordered their tatziki with pita appetizer and it was good. Mild, lacking some of the garlic I'm used to, but good.  Our mains both came with either soup or salad, I opted for the Salad, and my mouth immediately started to water - it is now too, as I remember- the scent of the dressing was SO tasty, the feta and this pink stuff, I thought it was Anchovy on top, turned out it pickled garlic, my god.. SO GOOD!! The husbeast had the Avolemongelo soup, and it was some of the best we'd ever tasted.   Our mains came out and I ordered the Souvlaki platter with the lemon butter potatoes the husbeast ordered 1lb peel and eat shrimp with green beans.  My souvlaki was good, a touch dry, but the potatoes had such amazing flavor that I could not stop eating any of it. But I was stuffed so I ended up taking more than half of the food home.. all of it except the tomatoe slices, because they were delicious.   The husband's shrimp were jumbo and had lil legs still attached, so he had to de-shell them and he said they were tasty, but he too had too many of them and had to take about 1/3rd of them home.   We will CERTAINLY be back.

We'd originally gone to The Gulfview Square mall to see Yancy Street Comics, but much to our chagrin they weren't there.  It as only when we went to Books a Million, did we notice the new location for Yancy.   I am not a Comic Book Enthusiast, but my beau is, so we went inside.  There is SO MUCH in this store that is NOT comics that it was amusing to me.  Yes, they have your comics, but they also they have a lot of adjunct stuff.   Do you collect statues? They have them. How about posters? Yep those too. Stuffies, toys of all manner? Yeah they've got that stuff.

Popped into Cristaino's for lunch because I was hungry. It wasn't busy, there was one patron in side who seemed to be talking to herself. Come to find out she's a local character.   I got their lunch special: Two slices of cheese and a can of soda for $5. This was absolutely perfect for me, they heated up the slices and served them to me and it was delicious.  A bit warm on the inside, but that's fine too.  THe only reason I knocked off a star was because the toilet wouldn't drain.   Over all, food is good, service was fine. I'd come back in.

I've seen Fabletics offered on Facebook, I've even seen the recent TV spots, but what I never knew was they now have a physical presence in the International Mall.   On a whim, I stopped in and asked if they had plus sizes (I run a solid 16/18 depending and that's usually plus) when the sales lady looked me over and offered that I probably WASN'T their plus market but rather an XL or XXL based on their sizing.   Trusting her, I tried on their sizes and I am an XL (14/16 to them).  Their leggins are compression gear, well made and come in a lot of different styles and colors.  A bit more expensive than I was looking to pay, but with their loyalty program - free to sign up with, I got 2 pair for the price of one.   Stop in, you'll be impressed like I was.
Nice clean pumps, hand sanitizer is offered right there for you to use.   The location makes it easy to get into and out of when you're getting onto Racetrack Road.

My guy has a '10 Mustang that was giving him issues. He called Karl Flammer Ford for an appointment and was able to get one without issue.  They took care of him quickly.  When we were called to pick up the vehicle, the had him out in mere moments and his car is working just fine now. He will continue to go back.

The husbeast asked me to trust him and took me here... I was pleasantly surprised.  I was looking for BBQ that night and got the Cider Press cafe. I was not upset.   We were sat and the waitstaff was fast and friendly, arriving to take our drink orders. I ordered a Latte, and was asked what kind of milk. I hadn't ever put that much thought into it, so ordered a Coconut Milk latte. With that one decision, I think my next lattes in the future will all have to be coconut milk as it was SO good.   The husbeast started off our meals with buffalo bites, or Buffalo Cauliflower which I loved. I had their version of Shepards Pie - SO GOOD.  Though their mashed potatoes were dry and there was no Mushroom Gravy in mine as it says in their menu.  The husbeast had their garden Lasagne, he wasn't sure what to expect, but he liked it. It was very much like a Caprese salad.   Over all, a very good Vegan meal. I'd certainly try it again.

Went for a late lunch on a rainy afternoon, we'd been looking for a new place to try.   The inside is quite pretty, the menu was large, a vast display of different cuisine styles.  We started with the salt and pepper calamari which was delicious.   We both ordered lunch so we received soup, an egg roll and our mains. I got won ton soup, an egg roll and the Moo Goo Gai Pan,  everything was tasty, their soup was delectable.   Service was good, the tea was delicious and over all we'd come back.

The boyfriend wanted a smoothie, other than the smoothie place on 19 this was the only place I'd ever heard of.  They had one person running the fuel bar, and a line 5 folks deep. The wait was acceptable for things made fresh, but ti would help if there'd been at least one other person with the young man.

I visited a friend who was here before COVID lock down.   The hospital was quite nice, if large. Her room was private and she was being taken care of quite well.  I was impressed with the parking garage and the elevators and how well everthing was laid out.

Loved, Loved, LOVED me some Hillsborough River State Park. I had NO idea we had rapids in Florida, Now I do and I have photos of it to be sure.   Bring mosquito repellant, they're thick. Bring a camera, take pictures. Pick up any trash you see along the way as you shouldnt be leaving anything behind.   It's a long drive out there the way I came but it was totally worth it.   THere is a pool on site, I need to find out more about it, and it's wonderful. Will TOTALLY visit this place again and again.

Needed keys made, Ace was close by and since they're a local business the choice was easy.   The guy behind the key counter was busy re-screening something, but once he saw he had a customer, he put that down and helped us with our house keys.   It took literally minutes. We picked out 3 designer keys, ones that people would recognize for our home and he cut them while we waited.  Once they were handed to us, we looked through the store.  It's a nice store, filled with merchandise, not at all like a Big box hardware.  Nice and friendly, but not terribly busy.

I absolutely love the Dunedin Causeway, what a beautiful stretch of land between mainland and Honeymoon Island.   My friends visiting from Georgia really wanted to see the florida sunset so we popped on over here from dinner and caught the last of the summer sun as it dipped into the gulf.   A little water, a little sand and a dolphin in the water made the evening a greatly memorable one!

Drove here to see a friend who was visiting from Texas. It was Karaoke night so we sat ALL the way back at the back of the place. Our waiter brought us our waters or our food as we needed. It seemed to be a decent place.

Drive through order, Happy meal, coke no ice, Large Iced tea. No mistakes were made, order was fine, They still give out the baby fries with the happy meal and when you say extra fries you get two of those instead of a small fry. It's so cute!  Employees were friendly.

11 pm, I drove though to get myself an Iced tea. Since I had heard their commercials about their new Mozerella sticks at 3 for $1 I decided to try those. I wish I hadn't.  What I got was... revolting. The sticks weren't fried. I think they were microwaved. They were not at all crispy. The cheese had probably been melted at one time, but not now. They were pretty nasty in truth. The breading was limp and tasteless.. other than garlic. That was heavy. The cheese was like glue. I wasted a buck.   Their iced tea was old. I was a wasted trip.

I honestly haven't been to Sims park in AGES.  So when I went to go release some painted rocks to the wild, I was really amazed at how far it's come.  The old play ground has been demolished and moved, and is now AMAZING with state of the art flooring and play spaces.    They were putting down brand new sod yestereday, and adding new water lines to keep it alive.   The large screens that were up were showing up coming events, and that was pretty dang awesome! The Shaded spots were plentiful, the covered benches were nice. And now across Orange lake, they have some pretty walk ways and seating areas too.   New Port Richey city services has really done a great job making Sims Park a jewel in the city's crown.

I wanted to eat near the water, but the husbeast didn't want to go all the way to Clearwater, so I told him about this side of Dunedin. He wasn't sure - but when I pointed this place out, he'd already eaten here. He said we weren't dressed fancy enough for inside, but for outside, we were dressed just fine.   We had excellent seats, right on the deck next to the water - We should have considered this, that at 4pm on an early October Saturday, the sun was already in a downward arc and was blinding, but I got to hide behind a pillar and only took mild sun damage. The view though, Was incredible.   Our waitress was wonderful, She was from Hungary, was knowledgable about the menu and let us have a few minutes to decide what we wanted. We started out with ice tea, but those were old/skunky so I opted for a diet pepsi and the husband had water.   The husbeast had the gumbo and I had the French Onion soup and we both had the 1946 Salad.  Both of us were delighted with the food. The salads were huge and the soups were fresh made.  Neither of us were hungry when we left.    I did get to venture inside and it's quite Chi chi, the bathrooms are incredibly beautiful.

First time for visiting the iconic Krispy Kreme in Tampa. We used the Drive Thru (Covid and all), placed an order for a 3 pack, 2 hot glazed donuts and a fresh pumpkin spice cake donut. A whole milk and a vanilla frozen coffee.   The donuts were hit and fresh, though as driver I didn't get to eat mine until I was home and found it to absolutely decadent. The cake was moist and very nicely spiced.   The frozen vanilla latte was really good, not too sweet, and it hit the right spot on a hot October afternoon. The only issue was we had ordered a whole milk and got 2%. It wasn't a big enough issue to complain about, but something to note about accuracy in the order. We weren't upset. It got drunk.   I really wish we sti had a krispy kreme in Tarpon Springs. Going to Tampa isn't economical if I want hot donuts. We definitely will be back.

I popped up to the Tarpon Springs Library to see about getting my library card. After all, I've lived in the city for 4 years, you'd think I'd have one by now, but no.. I don't. SLACKER!  Anyway, after finding the LAST parking spot left, I made it up to the doors, passing a random homeless person with a cute daschund dog, and noted they were closed.   OF COURSE THEY WERE!!! It was Epiphany! Orthodox Christmas. No businesses were open in Down Town Tarpon, the Cross was due to be tossed in a mere hour. Ah well, I'll get my card another day.

I've been familiar with the Spartan Manor forever. I grew up with the family that ran it in my youth. Today, I was there to attend my Mom's annual investment group Christmas party.  The location was clean, except that there was the smell of wet dog.  The decor was what you'd expect for a wedding venue, large crystal chandeliers, 1980's carpeting, round tables and white cloths, and a small parquet dance floor.  The service was good, coffee and tea were constantly refilled. The food looked institutional, but tasted excellent: A 'Greek' salad, Lemon chicken, baked potato and carrots, dessert was white cake. Simple fare, but when your clients for the day were mostly over 70, bland is pretty much the way to go.

First visit was made ahead of time through the nurses at my Mom's rehab center. It was made more than a week a head of time.  When we arrived on the appointed day, there is a notice that our appointed doctor was not available, and that we'd be seeing one of his PA's. If this was an issue you could re-schedule.  Where's the courtesy in letting your clients know ahead of time? Their time is valuable too.  (This kind of thing is repeated frequently, sadly)  When we were finally called back into our room - it was more than a half hour later. This is after we were a half hour early. So by now we're here an hour.  Once in the room, the PA took the info from my mom, and made sure she'd get an Xray to see how the knee was healing. To his credit and the Xray tech's as well, they were both efficient and did their job without hesitation.   After at least 45 minutes, without anything to read in the office, and the ONLY THING in the very cramped lobby being male oriented magazines such as Golf, NBA or industry magazines, we were finally seen by one of the Residents. She was awesome and personable and the whole reason that this office gets a 2nd star.   We got our orders, got the approval to drive and to come back in 2 weeks, and while I won't be able to go back with my mom for the 2nd visit, I do hope they actually read these reviews and take into consideration how they're perceived. While I didn't have trouble with their staff, it's clear there's an issue.   My issue is that they lack the courtesy of notifying their patients about delays or even if the doctor that the patients are supposed to see isn't even going to be there and leave it on the patient-who's already made the trek to the office to either deal with it or re-schedule out at another time which is not at all good for anyone. That they are slow and don't really seem to give any care to the cost in time and comfort once the patient is in their office. It shows an over all lack of concern for anything but the all mighty dollar.

I broke my Addiction to Mc Donalds over 18 months ago, but I come back to them every so often because for a buck the 32 oz unsweet tea is a bargain.   The drive through here was terribly slow. We placed our order for 2 teas, it wasn't complicated, and the car before us had an order that seemed to take forever, but all in all it took just over 7 minutes to place the order and pick it up. 7 minutes for 2 teas? That's kind of sad.  That and the stink of oil that permeated the air was almost naseauting.
Went here for 'The Haunted Speak Easy" Event in February. It was awesome.  Who knew that this little old church had a hidden room, it stands that it's cool and creepy.

I had no idea this park existed. Hidden in the depths of a neighborhood, the Moccasin Lake Nature Park is just beautiful. The injured bird facility is wonderful for a learning camp. Though with Covid much of that has not been happening as of late.   The nature park revealed a surprise with a link to John Denver (RIP) to the local area. The shaded parkways, pathways, the bat house all have their own charm. I got to see some beautiful Florida wildlife, including bats, ducks, turtles and some Really nice sized alligators.   This has become one of favorite places.

Drive through, I was coming home from an evening out and needed a little sustenence so I opted to come here and grab their nuggets for the first time. I can tell you it wont be the last. Those were GOOD.   Love me some PDQ, glad we have one in our area now, but anywhere I find one, I visit.

Rise is totally one of my favorite dispensaries! They have a great staff, really friendly people and knowledgable too!   They're located in Pinellas Park/St. Pete, right near a McDonalds which, lets be honest, is KINDA brilliant. They carry all sorts of good strains, and are happy to answer any questions you might have.   I'm only beginning my education on why I smoke and take for my anxiety and fibro, but these people really know their Medical Weed.

What a delightful discovery! A friend took me here because he had fond memories. The last time he'd been there, they'd had "kitchen type chairs, and were a bit more homey" I was told, but walking in last night they've apparently undergone a renovation and they had a very nice look and feel.   Small and intimate, the eatery's first impression is the delicious scent of garlic and wonderful food.  We were sat by the owner, who was very friendly and grateful to have us in the place. Our waitress was wonderful, very attentive.  We ordered the gnocci with gorganzola cream sauce - and she didn't lie, it was to die for.   I ordered my standard meal from an Italian place, and that's Chicken Parmigiana, and my friend ordered a Chicken Francesce.   After we had our appetizer, out came the bread, served with oil and herbs. Yes, Other places (you know the ones I'm talking about) serve bread with oil, but they never give you enough of the herbs and spices.. this place offered a decadent mix of herbs and spices and there was plenty - not to mention the sauce that was left over from the Gnocci - SO DAMNED GOOD!  The Meals - since they weren't pasta centric, both came with a salad dressed with a creamy vinagrette, that was very tasty.  Then came our meals. Mine was a thin, lightly breaded chicken breast topped with slices of cheese - it could have either been fried a bit longer or the cheese could have been melted a touch longer, this is my only complaint, and a side of Rigatoni topped with their deliciously tart sauce. It was a phenomenal meal.   My Friend's meal was chicken breast, in a wine, lemon, butter sauce, topped with artichoke, capers, mushrooms and cocktail onions, and of course the side of pasta. He was a member of the clean plate club, so I'm guessing he loved it.  Will I come back? It's a long way to there, but it's totally worth the drive.   That and the owner personally seeing us out and shaking our hands as we left, that was an awesome touch!

I had to mail off some post Christmas presents.  When I arrived both associates were wearing their masks inappropriately. One as a chin guard, the other just covering their lips.   The one wearing as a chin guard.would cover his face when he had a client, but other wise was wearing bare face most of the time.  The other adjusted her mask, but pulled it down several times during our transaction to wipe her nose on the back of her hand, and then didn't use any kind of sanitation wipe.on her hands. Just gross any time if year, but with Covid, it's even grosser.  Packages were mailed, sent the shippers demeanor was ok, not entirely pleasant, but I imagine the day has been busy, the season has been stupidly so. They were at times abrupt and short as if customer service was an after thought, but the job got done.

I have passed by this shop for ages. Even back when it was in the Holiday Tower. Now they've moved across the street into a small, stand alone building right near Walgreens, so the beau and I stopped in, I'm REALLY glad we did.   Apparently this place is a hidden gems. Their prices are AMAZING and their selection is WOW!  They had everything the beau and I were looking for and less than we paid at the other stops we've been to in the past.  You can bet that we'll be frequenting this stop more and more.   They also have a cafe, which smells AMAZING.
I love Publix stores.   This location is much like the others. Clean and neat, well designed with the new floor plan, it's much more user friendly.

First Review of 2021! #3143  Really large Ace Hardware with a lot of useless space.  There's even a small division of the USPS located inside, that's useful.   We came today, to find museum wax, or something similar to make sure that our TV wouldn't fall off the new stand if our cats get rambunctious. We didn't find the Museum Wax, but did find gorilla tape, so that should do the job.    We had a nice time exploring the store, looking around to see what was there.  The place is neat in that its your every day hardware store, with a very female oriented gift shop plopped int the center of the store.   The first person we encountered seemed to be a hawker for a window/siding company who was offering a chance at a Ace gift card, if you listened to him. No one was stopping. I don't think any of the employees spoke with us at this point.   We found what we needed and made our way our without any issues and made our way to the check out, where they had three people on the registers. That was a pleasant check out experience.

The beau took me to the Gym to show me where he's working out.   He has the 24 hour access which is great. They seem to have a good selection of equipment, a large work out floor and a room for classes.    It's close and convienient to our needs.

Stopped in to Zydeco for Lunch on our way to my Brother in Laws. This is one of the Husbeast's favorite hangouts during the work week. He and his friends from work walk to this location and another a few times a week.   We were lucky and found parking right across the street.  The traffic in the city was somewhat heavy, but not unexpected, it was the city market and a few days before Xmas, but Zydeco wasn't terribly busy at all.  We were able to choose our seats and given menus right away.   We perused the menu and placed an order for a starter for the House tepenade, the husband ordered the gumbo and I ordered the braised beef poboy.  Everything came out and it was amazing. The flavours that were on our plates were complex and amazing.  I'd come back any time .

My friend took me to lunch after the museum and this was her choice. She's familiar with the owner and wanted to show off what he does. It was an AWESOME choice.   The ambiance is white table without being stiff and stuffy. Deep hues of Blue and rich browns make it relaxing as you look out over Tampa bay and Bayshore drive.    I expected notes of paint, and maybe if it were evening time, that's what you'd here, I don't know, but that's the vibe: chill and elegant.  The drinks were. Delicious, we had mimosas. And the food was decadent. I had their special picnic lunch and now know why people come JUST for the salad. The beef was amazing too.   My friend had herself the stuffed crab and could not stop raving about it!   We enjoyed ourselves with our waitress too! She was so much fun! I want to say her name was Ashlee, but I'm probably wrong. She had a great sense of humor and really loved her job.   This place is one of my new favorites in St. Pete!

It's that time of year again, time to get my annual Mammogram. Making the appointment was the hardest part of this experience, and the sole reason I didn't give 5 stars. I was on hold 15 minutes yesterday.   Today, I came in, was greeted within seconds, my information was taken and I was escorted back into a waiting room. Within 15 minutes I was taken into the Mammography room, shown what to change into, and then the Technician, Deborah did the Mammogram.   They're certainly not like they used to be. Modern technology has come a long way, and while yes, You're still squeezed and twisted, the table is no longer ice cold and the glass doesn't hurt nearly as much. All in all, the experience was a fine one. One that I, no doubt will make in 364 more days.

I am so glad I found Grill Fresh! The Hubs and I had decided to go to a different eatery when we saw GF and made a U-Turn. We've been back a handful of times since ( Ok, that's a lie, It's been weekly).  I love their bowl concept. I usually get their 5 bowl: 2 Bases, 2 Veggies, 1 protein and sauce. Their black rice is SO good, their pulled pork is absolutely decadent. Yeah I'm addicted.   The place is clean, the restroom is nice and neat.  I can't say I've ever had bad experience there, and I hope to continue that same trend as I go back again and again

I had to stop in to target on the way home from having lunch with a friend out in Land O Lakes.  This one, located on North Dale Mabry was the closest location.   A large store with a nice lay out, it had everything that I needed and then some. I was able to make a quick trip in and out.  I noticed at that point they were getting their Christmas stuffies out, and had some serious envy over the dragon and wolf. GIMMIE!

Let me say this first: I Like Cheesecake Factory, so it pains me not to give them something higher, but when you have a group of 7 people, and the hostess seating them gives attitude, it kind of colors the mood.    We were told our table was ready, so we marched our way up to the podium, a young woman grabbed menus and started to walk off, not saying anything to anyone, so we followed her. There was a general confusion about us because this didn't seem right.  When we got to the destination, I asked "We were supposed to follow you, yes?" She actually rolled her eyes and snapped. "We weren't quite ready for you yet!"  So I was about to have everyone turn around when she gave an exasperated sigh and said "Ya'll can stay now.. " and she moved off, shaking her weave.    Look, when you deal with the public, it helps to tell someone. "If you wait a moment, we'll seat you." Politeness works. Frankly this girl may have been having a bad day, but her attitude sucked.   Over all, the food was good, the service was spotty. We'd asked for more butter, it never came. A friend asked for the gluten free menu, and waited 15 minutes for it before the waitress had to be asked for it -again-. Another friend ordered two slices of a certain cheesecake, only one was delivered, it was -to go-.  She never came back with it. We ended up having to go to the case at the front of the place and letting them know the delima.   So the service was meh.

My mom is currently a resident at Madison Pointe. She is there to rehab from a car accident. I will say that I don't like seeing my mom in a nursing home. It scares me.  Aside from that, the location is clean, the food services are on time and the food seems to be edible. (I tasted a bite of my mom's chicken breast and it was dry, but I can forgive that when cooking for so many) While some of the PCT's (formerly CNA's) don't seem like they'd be able to do the required lifting and hefting, I have to trust that they know what they're doing.  Their gym/occupational therapy room is well appointed and staffed. From the day my mom was brought in until today (and continuing I'm sure) she's been getting regular therapy.   Yes, the facility is dated, but the beds are comfortable - even if they don't all match. The nurses seem to care, at least those that I've met. It's not an ideal place for me, but I could not have wished for better.

The beau took me to the Gym to show me where he's working out.   He has the 24 hour access which is great. They seem to have a good selection of equipment, floor weights, balls and mats as well as a nice floor plan that allows you to use it.   The only complaint is that they didn't have the ab machines he like the best.   They're close to home so it makes it easier for when he gets the gym bug.

I can't remember the last time I was here, it must have been some 20 years ago, but the park has changed some what, and so much for the better.    I was there with my guys and we walked and rocked the paths, hopefully leaving smiles behind.  The trails are nicely defined, and the old growth trees are beautiful to walk beneath, it helps to keep it cool in the heat of a Florida summer.   The pier used to go out to the depths of the water, but currently we're in a drought, so the table is low, the shoreline has receeded, letting the flora and fauna thrive.  This really is a gem in Pasco, Co.

I wasn't even aware that Mellow Mushroom was open on this side of the bay.  What struck me as unique is that the tree out front, a 1974 champion tree which has been lit with shifting lights to give it a psychedelic effect! It's really pretty.   The husbeast and I came down here to meet with a few of his geektastic friends and chill for a bit over food and beer. I didn't realize I was going to be the only spouse, but that's Ok, I had my phone, so while the guys caught up, I caught up on Facebook and took pictures for my Yelp review.   The location is clean. the first thing you notice when you come into the location, other than the giant yellow 'Steampunk' Mushroom outside is the Yellow Simpon's-esque Mushroom dude who greets you. He's -HUGE- and kind of scary looking!    Since we were a large group, we were settled in a very large booth, this wasn't good enough for the guys, but our waitress fixed this by pulling up a few chairs so that we could all look at one another. This worked better.   Apparently when you get computer genuises together, they have trouble ordering, so I placed an order for an appetizer of the Olive Tepanade cheese bread, so that we didn't camp at the table and annoy our waitstaff.  She was good, keeping everyone's drinks filled, as they chatted. FINALLY!! orders were placed and a selection of pizzas were ordered by several different folks, including myself.   I have to say that I'm not a huge fan of their pizzas, but they were all large, they were cooked well, and the food tasted fresh. I just didn't like the white pizza. I would have prefered it to have basil vs red onion. But that was my fault for not having them take off the red onion.  The service was excellent, and even though the night wasn't a busy one, we all enjoyed our time together.   The husbeast will get to know the staff pretty well, as his new job is right behind Mellow Mushroom!

Finally! After a busy weekend, the husbeastie and I got to have a birthday dinner. I didn't want the usual places we go, so I suggested Brio, since I'd never been. He agreed, and though it was the beginning of Dinner rush, we didn't wait long at all to be seated.  Our waiter, Chris, had a large section of folks to contend with, and handled it very well. We ordered an appetizer,  and it too about 30 minutes to come out, but we didn't seem to notice, uet the manager did. She came over and apologized, and let us know that it was on her. (Nice, since it didn't bother us at all)  No sooner did she let us know thst, than our entrees came out. The husbeast ordered lasagne and I ordered the Tuscan Pork Chops, the lasagne was good, the sauce flavorful and rich. The chops were a bit overcooked and thus dry, but the veggies were amazing as we're the potatoes.  I will certainly return.

I had to ship a piece of luggage that I borrowed back to the owner. First, I've NEVER Shipped luggage, so I had to get a box that fit, I might as well do it all in one stop.  The associate was helpful and professional, and in less than 5 minutes I was able to the luggage into the box and the item shipped. It wasn't cheap that's for sure, but at least It's insured and out the door and on it's way home.

Stopped in to pay a bill, and got sucked in because I saw a sweater I liked!  I love going through their sales racks, because you can find some phenomenal deals. They're carrying high end brands in their makeup departments, Mid range designers in the clothing departments and specialty items all over the stores.   Kohl's is truly a fun place to shop!

Stopped in here as my last food stop in New Orleans. My friend was driving me to the Airport and we were hungry.  Our waiter, Shawn, told us he wasn't supposed to be there, but he was an affable fellow. Except that we ordered coffee for two, and only got one coffee mug.  I asked for a 2nd cup twice. Finally I had to ask another server - that got me my cup. Our server was far more interested in chatting with a fellow server.   Out food came out quickly. It was done right, it was tasty and filled out bellies.

A new nail spa, they've only been open since just after Thanksgiving.  Inside, they're very chic. Very relaxing, and comfortable. Warm tones of orange, brown and stone, it looks upscale and high end. My reason for going there was to get my nails done for the Yelpies. Seems that Gel likes to peel off of me within a few days.  They asked if I wanted a powder manicure, I had no idea what they meant.. So, sure why not. I'd try it.  Well, I was in for an experience. First step was to remove the old polish, then to file and dremel down my nails, then came the application process. I'll save the details, but it really is a powder. A glitter really well.. several times this is done. It's very interesting and involved. In the end, it seems to be a more involved process than a normal paint manicure, but, my nails have never been shinier and it's been a few days, and there's no hint of chipping.   The technicians were all very polite and very friendly. I'll likely come back and see what they do for a pedicure with my itty bitty toe nails.  :)

OH MY WORD! Save me from myself.  This Sephora inside JCPenney, has apparently just recently opened, and according to the girl who helped me,Kimberly,  it is the largest in the district. It was simply BEAUTIFUL.   Yes, it's holiday shopping time, and all the holiday kits are out. My palms were literally sweating with the want to buy everything I saw. There were kits for eyes, kits for lips, special gifts with purchases. And of course the store was so CLEAN and neat.   The only thing that bothered me was that I watched a woman try something from a tube of mascara. Not use a disposable wand... UGH.. You don't know how many folks have done that, you don't know if someone has something, They supply doe foot applicators for lip gloss, They supply mascara wands and eye shadow applicators too, don't do this from the tube, EVER.   Will I shop here again? YES. Did I buy something? YES.. Of course I did. I could not resist.

Still new and working out the kinks. This is one of the harder DD's to get in and out of because of their location RIGHT in front of a mobile home park, adjacent to a Waffle house and some god forsaken construction.   The crew is somewhat in need of training, however it depends on who you get. I've gotten excellent service and I've gotten some absolute horrible stuff too. I mean when you order a caramel swirl coffee and get something pecan flavoured you kind of want to cry. And then sometmes you don't get your flavor at all... Le sigh.   Still when they're on the money, they're on the money.

Sometimes you just need an Iced Tea on your way to Orlando. Sometimes, McDonalds is about the only place you can get one quick. This one was acceptable as a hop on/hop off the interstate. The traffic was a pita to get thru. But the people were friendly and my order was done efficently and happily.

This is my Go To Target, It's on my way home from work, it's where I get my prescriptions filled.  Barbie in the Pharmacy is the best.   I find that the shelves are -always- being stocked, that the selection is usually pretty damned good (Except for plus women's clothing, what gives?) and that you can usually find just what you need. If you can't, just ask a helpful associate and they'll do what they can to locate it for you.  Their clearance items are usually pretty good too. Sometimes the hunt is part of the game! I love rooting through the makeup to find that perfect shade thats been discounted 50% off or more!

So... Today I went back to Island Way grill for -MY- birthday dinner. I was excited to go back, after all, back in August we'd had such a great experience.  Sadly it was not to be repeated.   We had made reservations and those were honored, thankfully, so there was no waiting.  We were sat easily, at first inside, but my mom, who's 73, complained of being cold, and our Waitress went to check to see if there was outdoor seating available, there was, and she escorted us to a table outside. Since she was essentially giving up a table, we tipped her.  She was warm and friendly, wishing me a Happy Birthday.   Once outside, the stink of cigar smoke invaded my nostrils. I can handle cigarettes, but cigars make me ill, I had to deal with it though, they're allowed to smoke them. *shrug*  I made a potty run and while I was gone, our waiter made his appearance and brought by water and only 2 glasses. My party made our drink order known, and when I came back, I thought he would have brought us another glass for water, but he never did.   Drinks were delivered, Apps orders taken and they came out -- too quickly. The 4 coconut shrimp were slightly cool and over cooked, The scallops were a mixed bag. They were flavourful but ... I don't know something was offish about them. Some were perfect but others had a different texture.  Perhaps NOT cooked all the way through?   Our mains order was placed, I specifically asked for mine to have double veg no rice as did my husband as we're on a carbohydrate restricted diet.   When they came to the table BOTH had rice with them *Facepalm* My Reef and Beef .. the reef - tempura shirmp was not crispy, it was slightly soggy as it had soaked up the vegi juices & the medium rare beef, was neither medium nor rare, trending towards the well done side of the index.  Sadly for fillet tips, this was the stringiest piece of beef I've had in ages.   Both the fish orders, Grouper & Salmon came out beautifully done and flavourful, if only it weren't for that damned rice.   We weren't checked on frequently and our teas soon ran dry.  When it was time to clear the plates, our waiter asked if we'd like to look at the dessert menu, I said no, there was birthday cake waiting at home for me. He shruged and brought us the check, no wishes for a happy birthday, nothing of the sort, it was as if courtesy just wasn't with John.  His attitude was very Laizè Faire.  I'm sad I didn't stick to tradition and go to Berns tonight.

Tonight saw me at Chili's with friends and their babe in arms.  We sat in the bar area since they offered free chips and salsa, which is always a bonus.   I have an issue with the bar area of most places, rather that those areas being conducive to conversation, they pump up the volume of what ever is going on - be it Sports, music or what have you, and it drowns out your availability to have a conversation with those you're sitting with.   They had one waiter and a helper in the bar area, and sadly a lot of patrons, so the service was a bit slow, and half way through our meal - around 8:30 pm one of the servers went home. That just made it harder on the waitress.    Beers were 2 for one, and my friends were indulging, myself, I stuck to diet coke.  My friend had a coupon for a free appetizer, so we indulged in chicken nachos, which were tasty.  Our meals, when we did order them were good, though I admit, that the lettuce in my salad was on the edge of going bad, it had -that- taste, but since I was already mostly full, It didn't really bother me terribly much.   Over all, it wasn't a bad experience, just not a stellar one.

Man, I hate giving poor reviews but when one is needed, I have to give one.   So after going to the Casino, Mom and I headed home by an unusual route. She wanted an Iced tea, so we went through the drive thru. We placed our order and drove up.  There was no greeting, no total given, just a hand thrust out the window. I put my money in said hand, and a few minutes later my change was literally thrown into my palm. No "Thank you, have a nice day" no "Here's your change, pull forward to the next window." And most importantly, NO RECEIPT.  At the next window, as I waited for my order, a part of it was handed out. The expiditer turned away, when he turned back he looked surprised to see us still there.. "Um, the rest of my order, please?" Oh.. yeah.. and he handed it out to me as well.   Again, no pleasantries, nothing to say "Come back again." nothing. Clearly this store needs re-training. Needs to know that even a smile at the window makes a difference.  I will NOT be back if I can help it.  This store is in need of something, perhaps new management - she was in her office near the drive thru, stuffing her face, and sucking down a drink.  - yes you could see her.  No it wasn't a good look.

I wanted wings, so the beau and I hit up Hooters. Why? because it was a lovely late winter/early spring day (3/4/17) And this particular place is right on the water. You can quite literally drive your boat up to it and debark into the resturaunt.   Open to the elements, there were a LOT of flying bees. No one was killing them (Thankfully) but they were kind of annoying.  The fried pickles were good, and the wings, we ordered Medium heat seemed to have absolutely NO heat to them at all. However they were tasty.   Our waitress, I don't remember her name, was pleasant but not terribly efficient. We waited a while on refills, to order and get our check.

Lovely historic old building, I Absolutely adore the history of Tampa and this little hipster place was no exception.   I was here to see WIT Improv, and the venue was small and cramped but it was like having WIT in my living room, complete with couches. It was very interpersonal, except for the drunks who couldn't be quiet and let the rest of us enjoy the show.   The food that came out - mostly heaping plates of nachos, looked fantastic. Good drink specials all night seemed to be being enjoyed by everyone. I hppe we'll all be coming back frequently to see WIT in the future.

Recently opened, but add another name to the high end grocery geared towards those consumers who are conscious about what they eat. Especially if they don't want their food to contain *Added hormones * Artificial colors & flavors * Antibiotics * HFC * Artificial Preservatives * Artificial fats & transfats * Artificial Sweeteners * Bleached or Bromated Flours.   The store is large, bright and well designed, with just about everything you could want, including tasting bars for Honey and a cheese. You can even sample off the olive bar,  this is useful if you're not totally sold on what the flavour might be.   Their selection is good, including their non food items such as health care and house cleaning supplies. All in all, it's a good addition to the healthfood/grocery stores like Whole Paycheck and Sprouts.

Here is a toss back to the 80's. Quite literally, I've not been to Ruth Eckerd hall since 1986, when I saw Andrew Lloyd Webber's CATS.    I was invited to see Alton Brown, and I jumped at the chance! The lobby is airy with a great brass staircase, it's a bit out dated, but it's still functional.  The seats are comfortable, they're spaced well and even have cup holders. That's important these days, when places sell beer and wine and let you take it into the auditorium!  The acoustics were awesome. There was no trouble seeing or hearing Alton at all! The lighting was excellent as well! I have to admit, I probably should come back to see other things at this venue!

I'd just come in from my weigh in, I wanted food, but I didn't want your typical stuff. I wanted to try something new, but I didn't want just -anything-.  I Pass Maloney's all the time, so i figured what the hell, and walked in.   The first thing I noticed was that it was dark. VERY Dark, but it's a pub, so that's to be expected. The table spacing is .. odd? They're high tops on wine barrels, but they're close together and that for me is a bit uncomfortable. I couldn't begin to explain that to you, but it was.  So I opted to sit at the bar.    The service was quick and friendly, the menu had a lot of options, at first, I thought I'd opt for their Shepard's pie, but then I saw the burgers and thought to myself what the heck, and got the bacon burger.  A huge half pound burger with Swiss and cheddar cheese and apple wood smoked bacon and a side of fries.  I ordered it medium and waited.   When it came to the table, it was perfectly cooked, the fries were seasoned with something that tasted like heaven in my mouth and that was all she wrote! I cut my burger in half, at the tomato by it's self, removed the onion from the set up and cast it aside like the vagabond it's meant to be and tucked into that thing like I hadn't eaten in a week. It was GOOD.   My meal, with drink cost about $11. I understand they do a burger deal on Wednesdays, but I was there on a Tuesday.

I hadn't been there in 7 years since I moved to Tarpon, but at the suggestion of my Date, we went there.   I was impressed with the renovation and as always the food was AMAZING. Always fresh, always tasty.  We had a new waiter and he was just learning, but he was good! Great potential.  Our order was two of the beef pho, and our drinks. My date had the Thai Tea and I had the Frenched Coffee (my favorite)   It didn't take long at all for the food to come out. We ate and conversed, getting to know more about each other. The food was perfect, even the jalapeno slices. ;)

Every 2nd Saturday of the month, the Honey Pot is host to Fetish Circuit in their upper floors. It's an interesting evening that caters to some of the harder players in the scene. You will find riggers, people into violet wand play, sensory deprivation, and of course corporal punishment.  It is NOT for the faint of heart.

I'm going to give them a 5 star review because the Tap House was very accommodating to us as we were celebrating a life well lived.  You see, a friend of ours, Holly, passed away 10/12. This was our way of toasting her, because it's HARD to get former and current Rennies together in any one place.   My friend Michelle had them hold tables for us, and they did, she got them to pretty much hold -all- the seats against 2 sides of the building for our party and we ended up filling up those seats. It's a good thing that we did too... since 90% of our party indulged in the tap. Even -I- had a glass to raise in toast.   The other patrons might have been annoyed, but some even joined us in raising a glass as we all laughed and shared story about our fallen friend.  The ale an cider was cold, the beer was decently priced (Unless you got that Zombie stuff, $12 a bottle? WTF?) and the company was quite comfortable.  If I find myself back down in the area, i'm certain I'll step in.

Today I had the pleasure of dining at the Island Way Grill. The location was chosen partially because it was a place I'd never been to, and to celebrate my mother's 72nd birthday.  Upon arriving, the scent of the place was amazing, the food could be smelled from the outside and it set my mouth to watering. Inside, my eyes were dazzled by the glass artworks everywhere.  As we sat, we were taken to a table that sat four and our waiter was incredibly efficient and personable.   Drink orders were taken, I tried one of the top shelf martinis, and lawdy! it was delicious, very smooth and tasty. Our starter of the wok grilled scallops was delicious, and our salads were fresh and lively to the palate. Our entrees came, and they too, were cooked to perfection. Or uncooked as the case may be in the evidence of Sushi Joe.    In the end, the bill was as we expected, for 4 of us it ran just under $150 +tip. So it wasn't terrible, but it certainly wasn't a night at Red Lobster. ;)  This is a place meant for celebration. A place to go to enjoy one's self and your company.

Christmas Eve, 7:45 pm Its clear that they wanted to go home, but they were still very happy, very friendly and very efficient.  We both got latte's I got the Peppermint mocha and the husbeast got the eggnog latte, and they were perfectly done. The crew chit chatted and smiled the whole time. Perhaps the most efficient Starbucks I've ever been in.

The movie theater is a nice place. It's clean, well kept and in general does a good job doing what it does - show movies.   The service though, is where it kind of lacks. Today, getting tickets for the "blue hair" showing of The Great Gatsby, I noticed that one sales woman had a line of about 5 people, there was another woman, holding a conversation in the window with one of her other co-workers, merrily chatting away, not bothering herself to help those who're backed up at the first woman's window.   The snack bar is a typical snack bar, and this is where movie theaters get you, the over priced half gallon sodas and tubs of pop corn that you end up dumping on the floor.  Though if you're lucky there's a promotion going on and you might get a bag of candy for only a dollar more.  For opening weekend, Gatsby was in one of the smaller theaters, and I can't say I was upset by that. There seemed to be plenty of seating. Only one party had to be broken up, and that was only because they wanted to sit in the stadium seating vs down on the floor.   With AMC, make sure you're a loyalty card customer, it earns you points towards admissions and free concessions.

Since I had to stop at the mall to pick up something I had engraved, I popped into the food court to pick up lunch.  I decided I wanted to get something different, and I wanted to get Greek. Enter Pita Grill Fresh, it's the first time I've tried it.  I ordered my typical meal, A Gyro, and it was OK. It wasn't the most fabulous food, I mean, I live in Tarpon. It was flavorful but .. eh.. I'd go again in a pinch, but it's not my favorite.

I really only did go into the lobby to cool down while at the Art Festival today. But what I saw, I liked. The collection of rocks beneath the stairs, all stood on end, fascinated me.   With the art festival going on, they had a Pay what you will kind of day. That makes it good for those who wouldn't normally be able to afford a visit.  Their bathrooms were large and -very- clean. The staff in the restroom were keeping on top of that task. I applaud them highly.

Do you know what a special kind of hell is?   A special kind of hell is going into a Halloween store a few days before Halloween.  This store was already showing the obvious signs of being picked over. The make-up section was beyond horrible in it's up keep. Their stockings were minimal, and the costumes. Well.. They were in some form of order, but you could tell that MANY of the packages had been previously opened and tried on, and then just SHOVED back into the packaging.   I came in to pick up the last of the accessories for my first planned Yelp-o-ween costume, and I managed to get 1 makeup stack, but I didn't get the rest of the items I wanted.  I ended up not wearing that costume in favour of wearing a more.. deliberate outfit.

I've wanted to go here for a while, but I've always been kind of ... well.. hesitant. Why? Well, it's kind of non-descript, located in a strip mall. I wasn't sure what to expect. I'm glad I finally went for a breakfast.   it's MUCH larger on the inside and many of the folks who go are OBVIOUSLY very much regulars and very much family. There's a lot of love here.   The food - I ordered Quiche. I LOVE quiche, and it was tasty. It came with a fruit bowl. I figured that this was going to be a bowl of canned fruit. I was -so- wrong. It was served in a small sundae bowl, but it was FAR from a small serving of fruit. HOLY COW. There were spears of pineapple, honeydew, cantaloupe, strawberries, kiwi, orange and blueberries. It was  lot of fruit. I also got 2 meats. I chose one of each a sausage patty and a strip of bacon. It was a LOT of food and it was incredibly inexpensive. Less than $8.00   The husband got himself a Mexican omelette, and he loved it. It had fresh avocado, lots of salsa and cheese, jalapeño and other spicy things, it also came with grits and cantaloupe and a choice of bread.. he chose a pancake.. and it was good.   The service was quick and good. We will be back!

One small note: Don't go here at noon on Saturday. The wait will be long. With that out of the way. GO HERE!     I'd seen the billboard on my way home from work the previous night, so last Saturday afternoon, I piled the husband into the car for our weekly sojurn to a new resturant to try.  Both of us enjoy hotdogs and this place promised to be a mecca of Hot Doggy Goodness!    It was during lunch rush and there was no seat to be had, so we chose to stand and wait for a while until a couple got up, taking their seat to wait for our food. I ordered the Chili dog, no onions, my husband ordered the polish sausage with hot kraut and we decided to get an order of chili cheese fries, and worried that they wouldn't be enough between us.   When the food came out, we were a bit surprised. Me by the size of the hot dog, it seemed to be swallowed up by the size of the bun, but they made up for it with the slathering on of the chili sauce. My husband said that the Polis Sausage was delicious, and the chili cheese fries were.. AMAZING! Their single order was enough for both of us and a gooey hot mess to eat. We loved them.  Less than $20.00 for the dogs, the fries and the drinks, and we included a 15% tip, so reasonable too! I recommend this place highly!

11:20 on Friday night and there is a line out the door. There are empty seats, but they aren't seating the people in them. Must not be enough servers on duty... 20 minute wait, the music is way too loud. My date doesn't want to wait and I don't blame him. We opt to cross our name off the list and find another place.

Tried to go to dinner here one night, but there was an hour wait. Opted to do lunch here and glad we did.  The first thing I noticed was how similar this place was to Grille One Nine in New Port Richey. Similar decor and similar menu. I'm guessing owned by people.   We ordered a bento box with tempura veggies, a seaweed salad and one of the Hawaii 5-0 rolls. Everything was tasty and delicious. For this lunch it was a bit pricey but nothing out of the ordinary.

We stopped in here entirely on a whim, and I'm REALLY glad we did.    From the outside, you wouldn't expect much, but stepping inside you get a whiff of that heady roasting meat aroma and you just know you're in for a treat!   The menu is on the wall, in chalk (makes it easy to correct when you run out of things) and in paper form for when you opt for table service, which we did.  Just know if you've got a budding artist, they offer chalk and challenge you to fra a pig. Have at it!   We sat and perused the menu while our waiter, English Dave came over and told us about the place. It's hockey themed, the son of the owners is a goalie (I think) for the Jr. lightning.  And when hockey plays, the  hours are longer.   I ordered the 2 meat combo with brisket and pulled pork. My sides we're their loaded potato salad and a cob of corn. My husband spied they were wing champs  ordered a dozen smoked wings. We got Mango sweet tea and peach unsweetened respectively.  When the drinks came, the peach was nice, but the Mango was HEAVEN.  The food came quickly, the wings? Yeah they earned their wing trophy. These were smoked and then flash fried. What ever seasoning is on them is perfect, no sauce is needed. They're great as is!  My brisket was melt in your mouth delicious, the pork was smoky and rich. The only small things I can even say is the potato salad needed more bacon to my taste, and the corn had been in water too long. But that's IT.   We've found our new bbq joint.

The menu is huge. If you want -something- it's probably there. They really need to concentrate on one thing to be good at it.   For Lunch, I ordered an endless soup and salad combo.  The soup I ordered was the Chicken Tortilla soup, the way it was delivered was interesting. A big bowl, with a few scraps of avacodo, little bits of chicken and tortillas, and the broth was added at the table. It was a nice presentation, but the only thing was, with the bowl being so large, the soup cooled off -very- quickly.  And the Ceaser salad was way over dressed.   Our waitress was very friendly and accomodating. :)

My friend and I grew tired of sitting and watching tourists, we didn't want burgers so we decided to look for food. The Beachcomber was across the street, so I pulled up my handy YELP app, and checked the reviews. Most were good, so I nodded, this would be a good place to go, even if I was a little daunted by the three dollar signs.   Walking in, the strains of piano music filled the air. The large Christmas tree in the cramped foyer glittered brightly and the hostess (and apparent owner) asked which side of the place we'd like to sit on - The lounge side or the restaurant side. I chose the restaurant.  We were lead to the dining room, where white linen table cloths and evergreen decor invited us to sit down.   Once seated, we were handed two menus and an extensive wine list. This was for the bottled wines, of which there are only just over 8,000.  (8000 wines? GOOD GOD!) I perused it for a moment, but I'm not a wine drinker so I opted to just look at the food menu. I was rather impressed. There were listings for everything from Surf & Turf, to Farm raised chicken to Chilean sea bass and even frog legs. Everything came with a soup or salad, a veg, a starch and of course everything started with their crudite platter.   Let's be honest, I've never been to a place where they bring out a serving tray that has cottage cheese, beets with horseradish, apple butter and corn salsa in it. I found it a bit odd, but hey, it's a signature thing, I guess. There were also rolls and crackers offered to us with fresh butter, cut from a stick, I'm guessing. The bread was good, but I didn't indulge in any of the sauces.   When the food came out, and it came out rather quickly: It started with a bowl of YUMMY cream of onion soup,and a bowl of Coleslaw - The soup was great, but the slaw was .. well, it was too wet. There was far too much mayo on it. I had a bite and returned it right away, I couldn't eat it at all.  The food though, was amazing.  My chicken was perfectly fried, lightly crispy with a side of delicious mashed potatoes and Broccoli.  My friend's meal was Chilean Sea bass on Risotto and broccoli, he said it was perfectly done.   Over all, this was a nice experience. I would come back. It appears to be the kind or place that takes reservations, though when we went, it accepted walk ups, according to the sign outside.

Original plans were to go to another place, but after checking out the reviews for that destination, I chose YoA based on what Yelp had to say.     While the rain poured down outside, we were escorted inside to a really neatly designed back wall area that looked like a whisky cask.  The only issue with this wall is that the sound reverberated/echoed off of it, making it much more amplified. NOT the best thing when you want to have a conversation with your date.   It took 10 minutes after we were seated for our drink orders to be taken. I can forgive that, based on the food we were served. Our starters were French Onion soup, Oysters and a shrimp chipolte flat bread: Everything was served quickly and all the flavors were so well developed.    When we got our mains, we had a nutty goat cheese salad and snapper. Serving sizes were pretty generous and the food was DAMN tasty. The Goat Cheese salad had the goat cheese medalions were lightly battered and deep fried, making it taste warm and melty. The dressing on the salad was glorious.   We even ordered dessert, Profiteroles and Creme Brulee! So rich and decadent. I couldn't finish mine at all.

I was truly pleasantly surprised by the Amarit Thai restaurant.  Inside the place is small, but richly appointed in reds and golds, the tables are comfortable and neatly spaced.  At 7:30 on Thursday, it was not terribly busy, so the meal was paced appropriately, nothing was rushed.   They do not have a huge or complex menu like some other places. A sheet with specials and then a simple menu, deconstructed with the meats and offerings.  We got our usual starters, for me that is Chicken Satay, the husbeast likes his Shrimp Tam Ka soup and of course fresh spring rolls.  Dinner itself was pork with broccoli and cashew for me done in mild and for the husbeast he got one of the sizzling shrimp plates done Thai hot.   Everything was super fresh, and I must note that the spring rolls were filled with layer and layer of lettuce vs others that are done with rice noodles and just a touch of lettuce.  They were tasty but not what I was expecting.  The Satay was tasty and done just right, and the husbeast said that while he'd asked for Thai Hot, it was more American Hot, and while that's ok for some, he prefers to cry when he eats his food. *grin*   Over all, I'd come back as I found it tasty and clean.

I'd heard about Love's from friends and made the attempt with the Husbeast to get down there for the brunch today. No luck!  We got there around 3:15 and it appears that we missed the brunch by 15 minutes. No worries, the hostess was a bit baffled by why we were there, but the Owner sat us and told us that they were serving the full menu until 4 pm.  Armed with the full menu, we were seated at a high top and perused the choices. We placed an order for a starter of Spin Dip and she hustled off to go place it.  After bringing our drinks and assuring us that our app would be out in just a little bit, the Owner came out once again and told us that they weren't doing very well with us today, but the Spin Dip wasn't available. Truth be told, they didn't order heavily for the weekend, due to the Holiday weekend and them typically not being busy. So we asked for a suggestion and were offered the Peanut butter Jalapeno poppers, which I declined due to allergies.   We asked for another and were told about the Brie Quesidilla, which we agreed to.  When that came out it was served with a side of corn salsa, which was as colorful as it was tasty. The quesidilla was tasty with the roasted veggies and the cheese, but it was on the greasy side as well.  And if we didn't act fast, the salsa's water content would have waterlogged the tortilla too.   Soon our Mains came out I ordered the fried chicken, something they're known for and got two sides with it, the cheese grits and fries. The husband got the fat italian burger.  When they came to the table everything was piping hot and smelled so good.  The fried chicken was crisp, light and tasty, the fries were quartered potatoes, deep fried and yummy, but the cheese grits, well they lacked something so they were left uneaten.  The Fat Italian burger looked delish and the Husbeastie said it was!  The hand formed burger was served with onions, peppers and italian sausage on a pretzel roll, with a side. The meat was top choice and really good. A decadent choice.   We will come back to try out their Sunday Brunch. I'm told that next week, in honor of Football Returning, they're going to have TV's and the NFL package, so that should really pack the seats!

I'm a huge fan of their salads. I absolutely love the crispy chicken salad, especially when you add on the almond slices and ranch dressing on the side.   The service through the drive through is always fast, very friendly and they always have a smile on their face. I enjoy the visit immensly. I really wish there was a PDQ near me in Tarpon as this location is the closet to me.

Since a friend from Texas was visiting, I figured that you can't visit Tampa without having Cuban food.   While the food was absolutely delicious and the service was amazing, the one thing I could not get over was the fact that as the place filled up with people, and the volume got louder, they increased the volume of the muzak. I just don't get that.  Our conversation went from ok to nearly having to lean in and scream at each other.

Family run, and busy the day before Thanksgiving, this is truly REALLY good pizza.  They clearly have their regulars and it's kinda cool to hear them address them by name. You know they care.   We ordered a dozen garlic knots and a large San's Specialty. The knots were good but could have used more garlic butter. But the sauce was delicious (To me. Mom thought it was too bitter.) The pizza was huge and loaded with toppings. But since we'd had 3 knots each (Yes I took home half a dozen) we could only eat 1 slice each!    The service was impeccable. I will come back again!

I'm a fan of this large format Publx.  They're well laid out, everything is neat and clean, and the employees are always helpful. The produce department is small, I wish it were a bit bigger. They carry organics and gluten free items. Their meat department is extensive and that makes me happy.   Overall, One of my favorite Publix in the area.

First, let me say that I was at LEAST passingly familiar with what a Spedini was. A lot of folks don't have that going for them. So when my friend suggested dinner last night, I suggested the place, I wanted a new place for a review, so I suggested THE GREAT SPIEDINI!  We walked in, and while the place is spare, the food smell was -awesome-!  There is a counter you can order at and there are tables. We asked what we were supposed to do, because it's not clear if it's order and sit, or sit and order. The girls were very helpful, you can do -either-. So we took a menu and sat.  A few minutes later, the owner came over and chatted with us, He was very warm, very friendly and thanked us for coming in.   He explained what a Speidini was - for those who don't know, it's grilled, skewered meat, marinated and served hot.  And if you've never tried it.. It's so good. I had a boyfriend in Connecticut who's mom introduced me to it.. But that's neither here nor there, it's just GOOD.  To me, they reminded me of the Greek Souvlaki, and they are similar.    Anyway, the owner made a few suggestions, explaining that you can have your Speidini a few ways either on Bread (hoagie roll), on a Whole Wheat wrap, or on lettuce leaves, depending on your level of health consciousness. ;) I liked that those options were available.  There were a slew of appetizers from your traditional guac and chips to the not so ordinary pork belly with blueberry bbq sauce.  Sides are separate and served in fairly large portions, but still pricy.  Now let's get onto the food review, shall we?  So as I said, my friend suggested we eat out, She was treating, so I chose the place, and she really liked that it was someplace she's not been a thousand times and not a traditional chain. That's something I like about places like this. YES, he has a few different places, but there not on every corner, yet somehow I hope we'll see more of them soon.  We started our meal with the Pork Belly with blueberry barbecue sauce on the side - I'm not a fan of sauced food, I think it hinders the flavours, but that's me, your millage may vary. When it came to the table it was presented beautifully, the sauce on the side with 7 succuletnly done large pieces of crispy, yet tender pork belly. Lots of meat and a nice portion of fat still clinging.  These were so good. It was a decadent little treat. I did try some of the Blueberry stuff with it and yes, it added good flavour! This is so a yes any time I come back.   Our mains were the Chicken Ceaser Salad and the Delux Chicken Spideni with a side of Cucumber salad.  The chicken ceaser was HUGE, two people could have eaten this easily. It was tossed with just the right amount of dressing, not too much, not too little, and a lot of good parmasean cheese. The croutons were generous and tasty, even if I don't eat them all too often and left them mostly behind. The chicken...OH THE CHICKEN! It was juciy and not over done.  The Deluxe Chicken Speidini was delicious! The hoagie roll was cut in half, the meat stuffed it's interior and the speidini sauce was soaked into the bread. Normally this would bother me, but it didn't make the bread a soggy mess, it was just tasty. It was so garlic-y, so.. NOMMY that it made me want to sop it up with every bite. The chicken was delicious too, no dried out disappointment here, just Om nom nomilicious!     The only mild disappointment was the cucumber salad. It didn't taste as fresh as it could have been. There was no -snap- to the cuke. It was as if it was a day old, not made that afternoon. I can't fault them for that, not at all. And it needed a pinch of salt. Once I added that, it sprang to life and made me happy.  All in all the meal was great, the service was wonderful and I know that this, being so close to work, will make me a very happy girl. ;)

We stopped here on Father's day.  The place was hopping, but we were sat immediately.  We took a minute to look over the menu and placed our orders, The mexican omlette for the husbeastie and French Toast for me.  It didn't take long for our food to get to us and when it came out it was delicious. Both of us cleaned our plates.  The only thing I'll note is that the ac was broken and our waitress was too enamoured with another table's child to pick up our order which was in the window for a good 5 minutes before another waitress brought it to us.  They don't hesitate package things up to go for you, and are happy to give you to go cups for your drinks as well. I'll certainly come back.

I love me a good bargain, and Ross is always the one place I can count on for that rush!  This particular Ross is pretty well organized, they're open until 10:30 most nights, and some nights until 11, so that gives me plenty of time to shop!   However since I'm a compulsive shopper, that means I can't leave the place without spending at -least- $50. Tonight was no exception. 3 dresses, 2 shirts and several new panties later, and my wardrobe has a lovely spring flare!

Every other week the husbeast and a few of his former co-workers get together, along with the wives for a catch up dinner. One of the foodie wives (NOT ME) selects the place and we all meet at the appointed time and eat. Tonight, this was our second choice. Our first choice didn't have any openings for our group nod nine until 8:30pm.  The Perogie Grill is an interesting place to say the least with its "Egyptian" decor and the Polish food. Our group came in in fits and starts but by 7 we were finally all together. Our waitress seemed... scattered? We placed our drink orders and it took 15 minutes for my iced tea to get to us. No, she didn't have many other tables.  When we placed our orders, they didn't all come out together either. One of our party's order was either taken incorrectly or forgotten all together, so when we all had our food, he had nothing and had to wait. The service was sloppy and rather poor. The waitress stepped on one of the wives foot 3 times.  The food though was consistently good. I had the pork schnitzel with 6 perogi- potato and cheddar, it was very food, but oily.  Something that a few hours later my stomach is not happy with... at all.  Over all, I don't think I'd return based on tonight's experience.

I adore Asia Nails! This is where I come -every- time I get my nails done. They have a very attentive staff, the girls always pay attention to detail when they're working on the hands and feet. I absolutely LOVE getting my pedicures done in their pedi-chairs.   Today I splurged! I don't usually get the Mani/pedi, and today, I didn't really get that, I got a Pedi/polish change, it took a little over an hour and a half for the service to be completed, but when they were done, I was SO happy, the color was JUST perfect and so neatly done.    I'll be coming back in a few weeks to get them re-done!

After a cold night doing some Emcee work, there could be nothing better than a hot bowl of hearty veg soup and a nice crisp salad! Stone Soup Cafe fit the bill perfectly.  The interior might be a bit dark but the food was fantastic. The service was perfect and friendly and over all, I would come back the next time I find myself in the heart of St. Petersberg.

Stopped here to fill up the car as we headed out to Orlando for my flight to Orlando.    The pumps were clean and neat.  We didn't go inside so I can't attest to the shop on the inside, but if it's like others it will be neat and tidy.

You really can't beat the sales that Kohl's has. I love walking into the place and finding their clearance area at 60-90% off.    i love that I can find jeans from different makers and try them all on. From Levis to JLo to Elle among a few of the brands that they offer.  There truly is something for anyone in their fashion departments. The have one of the best plus departments I've seen in a long time.   I see that they're also carrying high end make up these days too! This is great for someone like me!

A nice, clean healthfood store. I used to be able to buy the best organic cat nip here, but unfortunately they don't carry it any more.  They do, however, carry Aura Cacia oils, and that's a good thing.

I stopped by Alvin's Lounge because a friend of mine was preforming with the Gypsy band, Kafkasso. I wasn't aware that it was a "Special Event" night, so when I wandered in, I was a touch confused.  But the Owner, Alvin, greeted me asked my name and was very gracious.  I let him know I was there to support one of the dancers, and he was very happy to have me.  I pulled up a place at the bar - as all the seats otherwise were reserved due to a birthday party.
