I reserved another seat at the bar for the Mother of the dancer, and waited, while taking advantage of the $5 Vanilla Martini special - really nice.   When the rest of my party arrived, we took up the space we could at the bar, ordered our drinks and waited for the band to play... And play they did! They were Amazing!   I found out that there was a "long bar" menu, which had a nice selection on it. My friend ordered a meat & cheese plate, that was $13.00. I had no idea how they could charge that much for it. When it was simply a few slices of salami, some ham, some .. Bologna? we weren't sure. There were some nice cheeses, and then there were saltines. Yep, saltines. This plate wasn't worth the price they were charging for it.   I ordered a Ceasar salad, and it was good, the dressing was garliky and fresh, the cheese was yummy, but the croutons were peperidge farm. *chuckles* They were a fine side, but they didn't belong on the salad.   Over all, this is a great place to come, to drink and listen to some AWESOME music. To chill with your friends, but pass on the food.

I wanted to give this a good rating, because the food was Excellent, HOWEVER the service We received really dropped it down low.   We'd just finished with dance class and decided to catch a bite to eat with the whole crew. Since it was a nice night out, we opted to sit out on the front deck. The Bartender/waitress came out, offered us menu's, took our drink orders - the Harborrita (their signature Margarita 3 out of 5 people got one) and told us she'd be back with chips for the tables.   She came back with our drinks, but didn't bring my water (to go with my drink) nor did she ever come out with the chips she promised.  (Strike one) We all placed our orders and then sat about talking.  A little bit later and the food was delivered, and it was quite tasty, the pork tasted fresh (I had the pork topped taco salad, my friend had the beef soft taco, and another friend had mango salsa and chips)  We ate, but never once were we checked on.  Each of us sipped at our Harborritas, and arched our brows, they were -awful- strong. After a good 20 or so minutes of us having finished eating had passed and no one checking on us, one of our party went to find the waitress, she was no where to be found, He even went to check with the cook, and they didn't know where she was either. FINALLY she showed up and popped back to the bar.  (We have no idea where she went)  When she -FINALLY- asked if we were ready for our checks, she didn't even bother to ask if we wanted it split - we did. So one of us ran in and asked her to split it. She couldn't remember what went on which check (Um, didn;t you write things down in order?) When the checks were split, they were split wrong.  She couldn't fix it, so she had to find the manager or someone to help her out. Finally someone got the checks right, but since we didn't want to wait for her to come back out to us.. we went inside to pay the bills.. otherwise we might still be sitting out on the porch.   Clearly there's something going on if most of the recent reviews mention poor service.

Came in to this Bob Evans because the one near me closed.  I needed food before work and I was craving something quick and hearty.  The service was fast, friendly and overall the meal was good.   I enjoyed the $10.99 three course meal, which consisted of bottomless bread - with choice of soup or salad. A main course (which came with a side dish) and a dessert. Both the husbeastie and I chose the pot roast which was served over mashed potatoes with carrots and onions. It was rich and tasty. There was a salad and banana bread. And a dessert of a caramel sundae - which was unfortunately quite tasteless.

I love this place.   You can find the most esoteric items here. You can find Mikasa picture frames, you can find swarkovsky crystals and even Le Mystere bras. You can also find absolute dung - some of their make up is crap!  Though I did find China Glaze & OPI nailpolish in their isle.   This is a great place if you want to find some truly unique items.

Ross usually has a great selection of clothing at a decent price. They used to have a BIG selection of plus sized clothing, but that has started to dwindle. I don't get it. If we make up more than 1/2 the market, why do we not get that much of the racks? Eh.. what ever.   I found what I was looking for and more, I ended up with 4 tops, a pair of shoes and some lingerie. I'm quite happy with my purchases.

I'm leery of places that sell "low sugar ice cream" and the like due to them using artificial sweeteners, something that I'm sorely allergic to.  So I inquired and was told that this is NATURAL sugar.   One bite and I ws sold. MAN this stuff is good. It's creamy and hits the right buttons. It doesn't have the artificial bite of some frozen yogurts, and the nasty after taste of sugar free stuff, so it's Perfect!  My favorite flavors are the Chocolate Marshmallow and the Coconut. The coconut is AHHHHH-mazing.

It's a Ross. It's not the cleanest, it's not the most organized, but it has many of the things that I enjoy.  The hunt for bargains is part of the thrill when you go to a Ross. Sometimes You find some very good things, others you don't. It really is a toss up.  This one willfind me coming back to it on rare occasion though. If only to see what neat new things have arrived.

Not our first choice for dinner on this Saturday night, but since our first choice was SUPER busy, we decided to give this place a go.  There were 2 couples inside, one sitting and eating, the other waiting for their order to go.   We walked in, and took a moment to familiarize ourselves with the menu. I asked what was good, and got the standard answer of "everything" and then I was told what was popular, such as their Pulled Pork, pulled chicken and their greens.  Taking those things into consideration, I ordered the Pulled pork diner - 2 sides being the cole slaw and potato salad. The husbeast had the Pulled beef with Cole Slaw and french fries and my friend who was joining us had the sausage dinner with 2 sides of their greens.   Since it wasn't busy, we had the undivided attention, which pretty much included table service and everything. We asked for our sauce on the side, and it was given. There is no .. choice of sauces, it is only Daddy Mack's sauce, which is light, kind of sweet, with no tang. It's good but it's not Spectacular, and they will sell a 32ox bottle to you for $6.99.   The food was tasty, well the meat was. The Pulled Pork was tender, a bit on the dry side. The beef was flavorful and the smoked sausage was standard Keilbasa. As for the sides.. The fries were hands down the best thing we sampled. The cole slaw and potato salad were institutional - i'm not even kidding. They were store bought and getting close to ending their cycle of freshness. And the greens were Ok.   I'd come back, but not often.

The husbeast and I were looking for a new place to eat some BBQ at, and so I threw caution to the wind and spun the yelp spinner and it landed here on Chef Ken's smokehouse.     Not terribly far from our house, it took us 15 minutes to get there the way the roads are laid out. We appeared to be the only patrons there when we arrived.    They were low on pulled pork, but the husbeast and I both selected the brisket and our sides, Potato salad for me, slaw for him and we waited. The wait wasn't long, perhaps a five minutes at most and we were presented with Brisket sandwiches (We only ordered the meat.. so I don't know what happened there) which appeared to be heavily sauced, our side and our drink.    The bread was garlic and toasted, and pulled off to the side since I wasn't going to be eating it. But the meat was good. The sauce had a heat kick that was good and the potato salad was made with sweet relish, so not my favorite flavour combo, but not a bad one at all. The slaw was light and tasty.   We'd come back to try the pulled pork.

I came here because I was participating i Glorify Women, an expo that was said to feature a lot of things. The hotel confrence room we were in was small. There were tables set up with quite possibly every MLM except beach body or VI and thats because 2 others were there. There wwre vending tables that were reserved,but not taken.  We were told there would be a runway... There was not. The only presentations were us, our Belly dance school,and one makeup demo by one of the MLM groups. There were no talks,no speakers as promised.   So back to the hotel.. The room was small,water was only provided outside rather than inside and easily accessible. The room was warm. Overall it was meh.

Duffer's set up for us as one of the stops on the Legendary Haunt Tour. The had us as a buffet down in the pool hall portion of the bar.  They provided us a nice spread of Ceaser Salad, some potatoes, some steamed veggies and some Chicken Parmesan.   The waitresses were very quick to get the food set out and refilled quickly once it was emptied. They were fast to clear out plates and friendly as well. If I were in the area, I'd stop in again.

I'm surprised I didn't know about this place when I lived in Seminole Heights. Then again, it might not have been around then...   I came for the Monday Moonlight Market, a bohemian sort of idea where different artisans come and gather, food trucks and musicians too, and you can shop for that perfect unique item.  If you're looking for eclectic clothing, pure essential oil soaps, the odd bit or bobble of collected clothing/furniture.  Perhaps you're in the mood for a lamp that wears lingerie - trust me, they're adorable and would look great hanging above your pool table.   The food trucks are plentiful, the puppies are well trained - all their owners keep them on leashes, and if you're lucky, you might get to see the bunny from Hawaii at Filthy Farmgirl Soaps (Hawaiian Island Soaps).   I was impressed by the coffee vendor, their name escapes me at the moment, but the coffee had such a low acidic nature that it gave me no heartburn and tasted great! They even have sugarfree flavourings at no cost.  The girls were amazing.   Yes, I ended up buying things for Christmas, and I think I'll be coming back every time they have one of these things.  The ONLY drawback is the parking, it's a nightmare. So come early!

I had a chance to stop in here to pick up a few things to make a dinner with my Paramour.  We wanted fresh and good, and Whole Foods was right down the way, vs the Winn Dixie that was next door. I'm glad we stooped in, because I found exactly what I was looking for: Chopped veggies to make stirfry with, 2 beautiful boneless chicken breasts, and then we decided to peruse the rest of the store!  Oh my.. their olive bar is a treat! I found Olive tapanade, which is to DIE for. I ended up buying a small container since the items on the olive bar are $10.99 a pound, I got 1/2 a pound of the tepenade. I bought some parmasean and garlic fricos and then we took a trip to the Bakery. LAWDY! It was the promise land of sugary sweets.   I did notice that the prices were slightly higher here than they were at the Clearwater location, especially in the bakery. I'm not sure why, but I found that odd.

Dinner before I left for Scotland. I felt I should eat before I travel.  So we stopped at Codys.   The food was good, normal Fare. I had a small steak, with veg and a salad. Which is pretty good for $12.00. The husband had the same. We were able to eat for under $30. Service was pretty slow, but it I think that was because it hadn't been open that long (for the afternoon)

I wanted something different for lunch before I headed over to Down Town Tampa for my hair appointment, so I opted for Anthony's. I wanted pizza and this was going to be a good choice.   I'd gotten caught in the rain earlier that morning, so sitting outside was a nice choice, inside I would have been too cold. Sitting out side allowed me to warm up and start to dry out.  The waitress was very nice, she directed me to the lunch specials and gave me a few minutes to decide. When she came back, I opted for a single serve peperoni pizza and a diet coke.  The diet coke was bottle served - I asked about this and she said that her boss' philosophy is that it will always be the perfect coke that way, consistent quality. And I get that.  In a few minutes the pizza came out and it looked delicious, there was a bit of the tomato sauce bubbling up through the cheese and the ruby of the pepperonit just glistened.. and when I took a bite. YUM!  The only thing I can say about this place is that because it's coal fired, some of the crust may be over done for some people. NOT ME, I loved it, and I'll be back!

It's your typical McD's. Went through the drive through to get myself and the husbeast a $1.00 large Iced Tea.  Unsweet for the both of us, because sugar is a no-no.  There was a line, they're not fancy enough to have the double drive through, so there was a back up.  It was not unpleasant, but it was about 7 minutes of our time.  Nothing bad, just a wait. The iced teas were ice teas. Nothning spectacular.

Target! Far better than Wal-mart. The store is always clean, Always tidy, even on this Black Friday morning.  The staff was friendly and accommodating, the isles were wide and filled with new merchandise. There really was nothing to complain about.

This is my 2000th review!   The Escape Game was my first Escape Room, ever!  And it will not be my last one.   This was incredible fun! The puzzle we chose was "Nashville" and no, I won't be giving any secrets out. But let's just say, Pay attention to everything, Look for clues everywhere, and you'll get out.  We did it with 13 minutes to spare, and that says a lot about the team work used, considering it only took us 15 minutes to get out of the first room.   The event space is clean, neat and well designed. The story and theming is well done, something that is VERY important for a suspension of disbelief as you work through your puzzle and get to the bottom of the mystery scenario.   When you escape, you are Gifted with the black "I ESCAPED" bumper sticker.. A badge of honor among puzzle players. It made me happy!

As is our new Saturday tradition, My husband and i decided we'd try something new. Our first thought was to try a new Thai place on 19, but when we saw that it didn't open until 4, we motored over to Dunedin and tried out Cafe Alfresco.  He'd had the pleasure of going before, while it would be my first time.  It was the time between brunch and the dinner seating so the place was pretty dead. We were able to sit where ever we wanted, and the service was IMMEDIATE.  Our drink orders were taken and we were given a few minutes to peruse the menu and choose what was right for us.  When the waiter came back, drinks in hand as I updated Foursquare, and placed our apps orders, for what it's worth the Feta Alfresco and Creole Gumbo are made there on premise and absolutely DELICIOUS.  As I found out by updating my phone, I was entitled to a free pint of beer from Foursquare, the manager came over and let me know that even though they were trying to get off that program, he would still honour the freebie. Apparently, according to the manager, it's easy to get signed up, but in order to get off of their group, it takes a lot of work, something he's apparently not done?... Anyway...  When we placed our orders for our entrees my husband chose the curry and I decided to have their chicken sandwich. The curry was mild but had some exceptional flavour, and the chicken sandwich with fries was crisp and .. well, it lacked something. It was good, very filling, but there was just something missing from it. I would choose something the next time I visit.   One thing I don't understand is the need for TV's set to sports channels in every freaking eatery. Do we need to be subjected to that kind of "Entertainment" all the time? can't we just enjoy the company of our parties? This place had 2 TV's both tuned to some local sport's team's game, Frankly that was just not needed.   We will return, I will just not choose that same item next time.

Brand new shop, just opened up right before Thanksgiving in the Embassy Crossing Shopping plaza right off US 19.  The store is located closest to Olive Garden and is small but quite neat and very comfortable.   We stopped in because we know of the benefits of CBD oil. If you're unfamiliar with it, CBD has been targeted for use for Pain Management, anxiety, depression, migraines, nausea, addiction, insomnia and seizures.  CBD oil or Cannabidiol is a compound found in industrial hemp plants that offers numerous medicinal benefits without the psychoactive effects or the "high" you get with marijuana.  As someone who suffers with chronic migraines and fibro, I can honestly say, CBD is a game changer.   We stopped in and spoke with the woman who runs it. I regret I didn't get her name, but she's wonderfully stylish, happy to give you information, ready to explain the benefits and show you the products.  You can even try some, right there. They offer samples of the CBD oil dietary sample. A water soluble tincture that you take twice a day or as needed, it provides a calming effect quite quickly. We took the sample and It did work as they said, because Drive Time traffic on US 19 didn't bother me at all.   I also picked up a topical relief cream that I will use for myself, if it works as well as they say (And I've used a similar product in the past, that worked really well,) I'll offer it as an add on in my business.  Because I do believe in offering the best to those who come to me.   They offer a rewards program, sign up and you get $10 off when you spend $200, and it only goes up from there.

The husbeastie and I were looking for a new place to dine, so I drove us out to Thai Samurai. Why? Because we'd never been...   Entering, we were greeted with mouth watering scents! The place looks visually appealing and smelled great, so we couldn't wait to taste our food!  When we eat Thai, my husband -always, without fail - asks for Thai Hot.  Generally, the waitress looks at him and nods, but when he gets his food back, it's not that hot.  So we expressed to the waitress that the Thom Ka soup should be -extra super spicy hot- That Thai Hot was OK. I explained that I order Ghost Peppers for my husband to snack on.  She looked a little afraid but when the soup was brought out for him.. it was indeed -SOUPER SPICY!- It was the first time that he can remember the soup being actually thai hot.   The rest of the food was just as well done. His spicy dishes were spicy. My mild dishes were perfectly mild and just as tasty as I'd hoped they would be.   We will be back!

I decided to take Mom to lunch today, since my Birthday week was extended  -people just aren't booking massages while their kids are out of school, and I'm not complaining!   Anyway, I took her to this location and we were sat in the very front of the eatery. The first thing I noticed was this heavy odor in the location, like wet dog. It was very unappetizing.   When we were sat, the hostess was pulled aside by a waitress and told "Why are you sitting them there?!? Don't you know I was cut?" Ok, I get it, she wanted to go home, but you don't tell someone in front of guests that were just sat. Do that off the floor.  It took another 8 minutes before someone even greeted us, and another 3 for someone to come and take our simple drink orders.   We opted out of the apps today, I wasn't terribly hungry, and based on what I'd already seen, i wasn't sure what our experience was going to be like.   Anyway, we placed our orders, mom ordering the Maple glazed chicken and I ordered the shrimp/chicken meal.  They were delivered promptly, but I have to say I was disappointed in mine.  The shirmp scampi was delicious! It was the "Grilled" chicken I had an issue with.  I'm certain that when it came from the factory it might have been "Grilled" at some point, but today it was merely microwaved and tossed on the plate. The texture was rubbery and almost inedible. It was flavourless and over all just not right.   When we asked for a drink re-fill, we had to wait 10 minutes for that too. Needless to say, service was not prompt, nor was the food up to par. I'm kind of sad that I wanted to eat here after all.  The only good thing was seeing a friend I'd not seen in years.

Wow, this place was neat.    It's a consignment and antique type place.  I was kind of amused by it, at first, and then I just wanted to dig around and see what I could find. The last time I was at a place like this, I found a gorgeous, fully restored 1930's Nurses cloak made of wool for $40 and that was a great price. So I wanted to know what unique treasure awaited me here.   What I found was... interesting. The store is clean, neatly organized and each stall is for a particular vendor who may or may not be in residence. I saw a few who were, especially in their jewelry.    My niece likes it here because she thinks some of the items are haunted. I have to agree with her.  They probably are.   Things I found: Portraits, a standee of Justin Beiber, Guitars, OLD desktop units, countless beanie babies (only a buck! You know how expensive they were in their heyday), So many ornaments, Lots of a specific type of collectible teddies, 1960's dresses, Hats, gloves, some designer clothes in tiny sizes, a few wedding dresses, that though dated, were beautiful, hand made soap & baubles.   Over all, it's an ecclectic mess. Do you like a treasure? Do you like to hunt for something fun? This would be the place to do it.

Their AC wasn't working today. Air was blowing, yes, but it wasn't cool. The store was humid and almost uncomfortable.   That being said, the store is a riot of colors. It's one of the bigger CC's I've seen. Spread out over what used to be a Two Jay's foot print.  I suppose it's nice enough, but I have to admit that I prefer the one out at Wire Grass.   They do have all the jewlery you could ever need.. for any situation and any color scheme.. EXCEPT brooches or pins. Those, which they usually carry, don't exist right now. Go figure.

I'm not a mid day beach type of girl, not with red hair and pale skin, and yet....  1:30pm, 3/17/17 St. Paddy's day was absolutely beautiful! A slight breeze kissed the air, the sun was high in the sky and the temperature was about 74*. We're at mid season for Spring break and I honestly thought this place would be packed. Surprisingly, it was not.   The park was populated, but not overly so. The trails were nice, the wildlife was making appearances (Saw a deer and a gopher turtle) and the shells were in wild abundance. The water of the gulf was chilly at first but my feet readily got used to it.  With a blanket on the beach, the sugar sand made a wonderful place to chat with my sweetie as we watched other spring beach goers enjoy them selves either sunning or even braving the chill water.   This time of year it's not overly crowded, it's got restrooms and a few snack bars. The parking is plentiful and the sand is sugary white. Honestly it is a small sliver of paradise right outside of Dunedin.

Clean neat Racetrac out in lutz. A great place to stop for gas before you get to the interstate, and have to pay premium for fuel.    The pumps are brightly light at night, inside the store, the layout is functional and well done. There are sodas and pastries as well as all manner of snacks and what have you for you to pick and choose from.

On our drive back across the state, our tummies were grumbling. Thanksgiving dinner had been at 1 pm and now it was after 11.  It was time to eat.  The husbeast really wanted me to try this place out, it is near his work place and he thought that I'd like it.   When we got there, there was another group in the place, and another couple just arriving, but other than that, it was slow.  We were sat immediately, and our waitress was very friendly.  We placed our orders for Bacon Cheeseburgers and waited.  It wasn't but a moment before we were given a bowl of some of the best Cole Slaw I've eaten. We shared that and then our food was delivered.   My burger was cooked perfectly, the bacon was fresh, it hadn't been waiting all day and just warmed up by microwave, nope, it was fresh off the griddle. The only complaint I had was the onion rings were the prefab Oreida ones. Not hand breaded. Not that they advertise them as, but they were edible.  Over all, the the food was great and the service was fine!

I had a couple of friends who were in town. They wanted to know where we wanted to meet up. I told them, I had a car and could be anywhere, they chose HERE as the location to meet.  Great, I've not been to The Stone Soup Company since they were located in a different location down on 7th.   We parked out back and met them at the location, inside it was warm and inviting, the area was large, and we were one of 2 groups seated, but the upstairs Kava bar seemed to be hopping with all the people coming and going through the secret bookcase, (PSSST!!!by the way, you can find a flyer for a free shot of kava on many of their tables, take one and go upstairs) Once seated, our waitress, who's name I didn't get, got us waters for the table and gave us a few minutes to peruse the menu.   I must admit, I got a chuckle out of that read, there are a few political opinions on display, if you're not a little left leaning, you might be offended, or not, it just depends on your thought process.  That being said, the menu is extensive, the food is comprehensive and well thought out, so when the waitress came back over, we decided to place an order for the Cheesy Cuban Bread - after all, we're in Tampa, home of some of the best Cuban bread outside of Cuba.  We also placed our orders for our mains. My guy and I ordered the French onion soup, the Breakfast bowl and their version of Fish and chips.   We chatted and were happy when the Appetizer came out. Though many of us are on Carb restricted diet, we all broke that rule for that amazing bread. The cheese, garlic and cuban bread goodness was about to die for. It was crusty and gooey, all around heavenly.    Our waitress never let our water glasses go dry, she kept bringing out wine bottles filled with water, and finally the food. Everything was hot and fresh. The French Onion soup was a bit different in that it was garnished with those Durkee onion crisps you get during Thanksgiving, but it was tasty. The Breakfast bowl was supposed to have hash browns, but it had fries (Not a complaint, just an observation) and onions, the onions were warmed, but not at all cooked through-which I'd asked about and there were only 5 large pieces, which I could pick out, thankfully (not a fan of uncooked onions).  The fish and chips were surprisingly done well. Not huge planks of fish, but more like nuggets and they were good.   We got there around 8:10 pm, and finished around 9:10, we were the last to leave and it was clear they were ready for us to go, given by the staff just hanging out and looking at us.  While not rude, it was very obvious.

I signed up for PalmHarbor, Samantha Taylor Fitness at the turn of the year, after catching one of her seminars. I opted for the boot camp version over the personal training, price being the main factor.   The facility is new, placed in the former Shapes location with all new materials and all new equipment.  The boot camp classes are offered several times a day, 3-5 in the morning and a few in the evening as well, making it easy for everyone.   My favorite coach is Coach Kristy, she's really energetic, very positive and encouraging. She makes you know that you CAN do what she wants you to do, even though you think you're about to die. So far, my favorite class has been Boxing day.
I only use the ATM at this location.  The drive up lane was clear and I was able to access what I needed quickly.  When I have gone inside ages ago, It has always been busy and understaffed.

My first visit to Empamamas and I was blown away.  We came to Armature works because we were celebrating a friend going away, we chose Empamamas because we liked the selection.  We were made even happier by the idea that on that day, you got 2 Empanadas for $5 with fries and a soda it wasn't terribly expensive at all.   We both got the Tampagirl and the Cheeseburger in Paradise and we were not disappointed. The cheeseburger in paradise was ABSOLUTELY delicious!  My friend at the Tampagirl First and she swore that was her favorite. Either way, both were amazing and we'll be back.   Also, jazz up your fries with their Rosemary parmesan topping you won't be wasting your money, its the bomb!

We had a reservation for six folks, a few of us arrived early, not astoundingly so, but we were sat just before our time of 7:15. The last 2 party members arrived right on time.  The eatery was busy, it was the day after Valentine's day.   The service started off in an odd pacing. Drinks didn't come out together. The bottles of wine were delayed, beers didn't come and our server had to be reminded.  Apps were taken, but orders were not until after aps were eaten, which threw the spacing of the meal off. Our waiter seemed to disappear for long swaths of time.   The meal was ok, but the temperatures were -not-.  It seemed as if our food had sat in the holding window for a while as several of us had the same experience and had gotten the special for the day, which had been a 14 ounce peppercorn encrusted Strip steak with a peppercorn sauce, and all of us experienced the same thing. The sauce was cold, the steaks were cooling and though they tasted good, it was an odd sensation in the mouth to have warmish meat and a cold  sauce.  No, we didn't complain about it due to the wait we were already having with the service.   One of the members of our party asked for Pittsburgh style, I'm not sure if the eatery makes food in that vein, but she was pretty cheezed that hers wasn't "perfect". I'll take that with a grain of salt because I know nothing about that method of cooking.    All in all it took 2.5 hours for us to eat that evening, it normally never takes that long. We got a lot of talking done, so I suppose that isn't so bad, but the chairs at the tables are uncomfortable and sitting in them for that long wasn't the best for the evening.    I'll give the place another shot, but I am sorely disappointed. It was not a cheap night out for 2 people.

Went to dinner with my paramour after having dessert first over at William and Dean chocolates, since they are in the same strip mall.   There was no wait, we were sat at the back of the building in a large, comfortable booth and our waitress was with us immediately.  We ordered our drinks and perused the menu.  When she returned and our ice teas were in front of us, my beau ordered us their full stack of Onion Rings, and then we placed our orders for our mains. I opted for a crock of their French Onion Soup, and he went for the signature prime rib dinner.   We were started off with a big bowl of salad that comes with the meal, I asked for dressing on the side, it was mixed at the table and served to us on a plate, along with fresh yeast rolls with cinnamon butter & real butter.  When the onion rings came out, I knew I could only have one if I planned to eat my dinner. They were HUGE, coated with a delightful beer batter, the kind you find at state fairs.   When the mains came out, our waitress provided us a 2nd plate so that my guy could share the meat with me, which was really kind.  The soup was delectable and the steak and mashed potatoes were just what we asked for. It was delicious.  Generally I've found this chain to be hit or miss, This is most certainly a hit. We'll be back when we're in the area.   (Note to self, 1st review of 2019, #2614)

Saturday afternoon, around 2:30 pm.   Hank's is not terribly busy, but the sign on the door says they're going to be closed from the 2nd thru the 4th, and reopening on the 5th. You could TELL the employees did not want to be there.   We placed our orders: I ordered the 2 meat plate, pulled pork, ribs with sides of Green Beans and corn on the cob.  The husband ordered the back yard burger, with everything. His side was fries and an extra side of fried okra (He loves the stuff)  We got our drinks and sat down at the tables along the outside wall so we could watch the day go by.  The food takes a while to come up, there are apparently several orders before us and I blame it also on the burger the husbeast orders.   When it's delivered, it's without the okra. We mention this to the cashier/runner and she tells us "it'll be right up." And I hear her tell the guys in the window "There was supposed to be okra with that too."   We go about eating our food.  There is nothing special about the BBQ. The pulled pork was dry and not particularly flavorful, but it was plentiful and the ribs were tiny, but ok, they were served over two slices of white bread.  The husband's burger was cooked well (he asked for medium) and they forgot his mayo too.    He was quite literally done with his meal - and still no okra. Another girl was re-stocking the hot sauce bottles when I asked her if she would please check on the side.  There was a small kerfluffle between the cashiers at that point in time, One said there was no ticket for it, Ours had to show her where it was.  FINALLY - the okra came out. It was hot and ok.   I will not come back to Hanks. When it comes to service they're not on the ball.

I'm not a fan of Down Town St. Petersburg. It confuses me, however this was a friend's birthday party so I said I'd come. That and the Black Honkey's were playing, and she's said such good things about them...    Given that it was a Friday Night, I was lucky enough to find parking right on Central Avenue and made my way to the venue. I had no idea they butted right up against Janus Landing.  The location is spacious, high vaulted ceilings, and the tables and couches lend for a comfortable feeling.   The bathroom (Women's) had the BEST sinks! I loved the color of them and the shape. The stalls were all large and well maintained and the only Graffiti I saw had a good message it read "Be kinder than you have to be" it is a personal mantra of mine  - and no, I didn't leave it.  Drinks.. Well I had one, it was a smallish size one of rum(Well) and diet and it ran me $6.00. So I think that's a touch expensive, but I would certainly come back. The band was good! I had to leave earlier than I expected, but Yeah, I'd come back again!

Brand new, recently opened in Trinity, Florida.    First watch always provides a good product. I took my mom to lunch to look at the new stores and to have lunch after I'd returned from vacation.  She'd never been to a first watch so it was perfect.   We started our meal with the Million Dollar Bacon, which is my absolute favorite, perfectly crispy, with just a bit of chew. I can't go there and not get it.  For lunch we both decided to have the cup of soup and 1/2 the ham and guyere cheese sammie.    We both had left overs, but the food was delicious. The soup (Vegetable) was hearty and so tasty, and the sandwich was very satisfying.  The service was wonderful too, but confusing. Our waiter changed 3 or 4 times.

Wasn't aware this was a location until I passed it while I was looking for a place to eat while taking my CEU's.  It didn't look busy so I stopped in.  I asked for a table for one and was directed to the bar, I was not given another option.   I ordered the Chicken Salad croissant, and waited.. and waited.. people were sat after me, and got their orders before me. When the bartender asked me how things were, I said I didn't know, I'd not gotten my food... It'd been over 30 minutes at this point.    When the food did come out, at 35 minutes, it was ok, nothing amazing but I ate it and paid for it without complaint.  Its usually my favorite but it seems they may have changed the recipe.

Why can't I give .5 stars?Man I wish I could give a 3.5 stars. -sigh- BB&B's are all alike. They're HUGE stores with So much stuff. I came specifically to get new sheets since our old Modal sheets are showing age. SAD... too because Modal is such nice fabric.  This means I get to walk though and find everything I never knew existed! Including a wine glass that takes a WHOLE bottle of wine, Lego style storm trooper alarm clocks and who knows what else.   The sheets are -expensive-, hell ALL their sheets are expensive. And if I liked hotel style sheets, read cotton thread count sheets, they have a great selection, but the Modal are the ones I was seeking, and the king sheets are $80 for a set. This doesn't include extra pillow cases. Thank goodness I don't need others.   Added those to the cart, and a few other things that will become Christmas gifts and ... my total was MUCH more than I wanted to pay, but I did. Thank goodness for the 20% off one item. That always makes things much more palatable.

We enjoyed dinner out with our friends.  But there's nothing much you can say about this chain that would surprise anyone. It's Red Lobster, they have the absolute best cheddar bay biscuits, but other than that, it's "sea food".  It really is nothing special.   I had one of their Hurricane drinks and it didn't even taste like it had any alcohol at all.  They do tend to run some decent specials, like their 2 for $25 or their 4 courses for $15.99.

It pains me to write this, it really does. But for the most part, the store is quite lovely. It's mostly clean. Mostly neat, and the employees are happy to help. And then we get to talk about the 2 sore points of the store.  1. the Bakery. I wanted a loaf of bread sliced. Usually that's met with a "Sure, did you want that thin or regular sliced?"  But here, it was met by a "Isn't there one already out there?"   Since I'd heard the associate tell the other customer before me that there was one out there sliced, I looked, and when she snapped at me for that, I looked -again-. "Nope." and handed her the bread. Clearly, I was interrupting her standing at the counter. I'm not sure what she was doing, but ... *shrug* Rather than ask if I wanted it thin, she said "That'll be regular, right?"  "Sure."  When the slicing of the bread was done, she handed it back to me. "Have a good day." No inquiry of "Did you need anything else" nothing other than a cursory ending.   and perhaps the worst:  2 Produce.   Much of produce is nice, it's neat, but they have these Packaged tomatoes and some peppers. I'm not sure how old they are, or even why they're like this, but someone is not doing their job. Many of the pre-packaged items were mold ridden. When I noticed this, I asked a stocker if there was a produce Manager around. Apparently they were at some Award's meeting or some such, so the stock clerk called for someone to help me.  A young man came out and I showed him what I found.  There was no apology only a .. "Oh.. well, let me pull those." and he did, Which is good, but I wonder how they got that way in the first part. I know now that I won't use this store for fresh produce in the future, because I can't trust them for good turn over.  Check out was smooth and friendly, they even called for more cashiers when there were more than 3 people in line.

The husbeast and I waited too long for a friend to get in touch with us, so we missed our brunch window, so we had to go to an early dinner, but WHERE? All the places we usually go to were bustling at 3 in the afternoon, so we decided to spin the roulette wheel and choose someplace new.   I have driven past the Thirsty Marlin many a time and proposed the idea to the Husbeastie so a plan was set into motion. We made our way there, no traffic in our way, and when we arrived on this balmy Sunday afternoon, 80*F at the end of December, the place as all but dead. A few patrons were inside and one couple was outside, so we opted to sit outside on the patio. It was lovely, except for the all too bright sun. An umbrella would have been perfect. The table was set up for it, but none existed.   The waitress came out in short order and took our drink order and asked us if we wanted to place an app order. Given that we'd never been there before we asked for suggestions. She tossed a few our way, and Conch Fritters stuck. They were a bit on the over done side when they arrived, and the peices of conch that I could tell were there, were hard to eat, overly chewy, but the fritters themselves were tasty, as was the spicy mayo sauce served with.   We ordered our mains, The husband getting a bacon double cheese burger, served with fries and slaw, and I opted for a club salad with chicken, dressing on the side. I know, not something you'd expect one to order from a fish place, but oh well.   The burger came out looking and smelling delicious, and given the way the man inhaled it, it must have been amazing. The bacon looked -fantastic- and the fries looked WOW.. just as perfectly tasty.  My salad was odd. It was served in a taco shell bowl, a mound of older lettuce, with 2 large rings of green pepper, an egg cut in half. 2 cherry tomatoes, a handful of cheese, a handful of bacon bits, and 2 rings of cucumbers, all topped with 4 well seasoned chicken strips. It was fairly deconstructed. I had to eat it layer by layer.  But yes, the lettuce was old, peices were wilted and bruised, and had that OLD taste to them. I was rather disappointed in it, but ate 1/3 of it. Seriously, it was almost a whole head of ice burg.   During this time another couple came in with their dog and sat on the patio with us, Our waitress came out and served them, but never once refilled our drinks, My husband's iced tea ran dry and mine came perilously close.  We did order the Key Lime pie, and it was decadent. I'd go again just for the Key Lime Pie, but also know exactly where to get that from, so maybe I'll just go if people I know are going. It wasn't really worth repeating a trip.

I dislike when I have to down-grade a review, but tonight I have to.   Tonight the husbeast and I went to Bob Evans because I was craving Soup. I've been Ill for about a month and after a lady's day out, the soup sounded soothing.  We arrived, we waited a few minutes and we were seated. .... and then we waited, and waited.. FINALLY about 8 minutes after being seated, our waitress cheerfully apologised for the wait - Even though she never acknowledged us after taking the order from the table behind us - she could have let us know she'd be right with us, but NO. nothing, no eye contact at all.  When she finally did come over, we placed everything at one time.   We placed drink orders: Iced unsweet tea, ice water and coffee, Apps of Twisted cheese, and mains of Soup and salad (veg beef) and soup (veg beef) and burger.   Our meal came out as follows: The appetizer. Which was good, but with nothing to drink it was very thick and cloying. We then noticed that one of our setups had jelly stains on it and the knife was dirty.  When the waitress came back to the table behind us, she took care of them, DIDN'T check on us.. so I raised my voice and asked her if we could have our drinks.. "Oh yes, I'm sorry.." We heard a lot of I'm sorry tonight.   When she came back with the drinks, no ice water was had, I pointed out the stained napkin and dirty knife "Oh my, I'm sorry about that too.." she came back with both the new set up and ice water.    "Your soup and salad is up, I think we're just waiting on your fries..  I'll go check." I'm not kidding when I say I timed her. It was another 7 minutes when she came back.  The soups, which were identical orders were NOT identical soups. One was rife with meat and veg, the other was mostly broth and veg not so much beef. There were NO soup spoons, no saucers under the soups, no crackers.   The salad was the last thing to come out and it was right.   I'm not sure if our waitress was new, but when I was asked how the food/service was when I checked out, I said that the food was ok, but the service was not. I didn't receive an apology or anything, just sympathetic eyes and a nod.  REALLY??

I like the theater. I especially like the theater when I love the subject matter and the people in the show.  Last night, I went to the Jobsite theater's production of Silence! The musical.  Yep, it's what you think it is. It's Silence of the Lambs set to music. It's brilliant!   The Jaeb theater is where it was hosted and Other than it being at tables, it really was fantastic. The show, the music and of course the acting, especially that of the antagonists, Buffalo Bill and Hannibal Lechter were so well done.  It's on for a few more days (until 11/15/15) so if you an, I suggest that you go see Silence!

Why only a 2? Apple doesn't focus on Customer Service. If I'm dropping $5K on a new laptop, I would prefer not to have to hunt down the ellusive blue shirt who really can't be bothered to actually HELP.  It's a good thing we new what we wanted, knew what else we needed, else we'd be adrift on the see of people, made to wait on line like so many others, because they need help. We weren't greeted. We weren't even acknowledged.  Frankly, if I liked windows I'd have just gone and gotten a Dell, but Apple is virus resistant and thus, we spend on them.   Still, their lack of customer concer/care annoys me.

The husbeastie and I were hungry. We were out to run errands and needed lunch, Westshore pizza looked like the right choice.  They have a lunch special for 2 slices and a drink for $6.00, which is a fair deal when you consider the size or their slices.   I got a spinach, tomato and ricotta and a cheese slice while the husbeastie got 2 meat lovers slices.   While they warmed, we got our fountain drinks and took a seat.  It was a busy Sunday afternoon, so our seats were limited to one jacked up table at the back, or a tiny corner seat, or outside. We chose the tiny corner seat, and waited patiently.   The pizza came out, and the Hubby liked his, but I felt mine was barely ok. The crust was fine, but the toppings were barely melted it seemed. It felt like they'd been in the case for a VERY LONG while. They certainly didnt taste fresh.  In any case I didn't eat but 1/3rd of each pie.  I wont go back.

Needed to pop in and grab some decongestant before we hit the road for Tampa, and this was on the way. It was Valentine's day and there was one cashier on. While standing on line - 4 deep at this point, she finally called for help, by the time the help arrived, the line was 8 people deep.  Frankly, they seem either understaffed or don't really care about how their customer service is perceived.   Over all, CVS has everything, except tobacco, and can be found quite reasonably.

Summer time and the living is easy, Nothing beats a good scoop of ice cream on a hot June evening.   The kids that work here probably would rather be doing something else, and I can't say I blame them, but they do a good job. always appear friendly and neat.    Admittedly, this is an indulgence, as $10 for 2 ice cream cones is a tad bit expensive, but the flavours are usually good, and they'll give you a free sample if it's a flavour you're unsure of.

Had lunch with my niece one afternoon. She got a chicken burger and I opted for their Philly cheese steak.   The food was good, the service was Ok.  It wasn't a particularly memorable visit. We got refills when we needed, The food was hot and fresh when it came to the table. We ate what we wanted and left happily full.

Food truck.   It was located outside of DeBine Brewery so we got ourselves some chips and a quesedilla.  They actually have REALLY god food. The quacamole was quite tasty and the quesadillas were freshly made and you get three in a serving, which for the price is a good deal. The taste of it was absolutely delicious. I'd certainly eat from them again.

Stopped into the celtic shop looking for a present for my Beau. His birthday was coming up and I was looking for something unique.   The shop is off the beaten path, near Alfresco's diner, and has a nice selection of Irish themed gift ware.   I wound up finding a journal for my beau, a wolf and celtic knotwork done on the cover and the back. It was at a reasonable price too.

I've lived in this area 96% of my life and this was my first visit to Anderson park. I'm LOVING the water front! It's gorgeous.    From the little picnic tables and grills that dot the lake front just off the boat launch, to the large sweeping areas that allow you to enjoy the waterfront on swinging benches, this is a park that is for those who wish to be active or peaceful.     The park was a lot bigger than I thought, when We drove over a bridge that was apparently a drive way, and over to a 2nd area of the park for another large expanse of play space and walking areas.   The park is well maintained and quite nice to visit. I know I'll come back.

They have almost everything you could want when it comes to crafting. I went on this trip for some tracing and transfer paper. I was happy to find that they had both and a coupon that I could use for my purchase.   I asked an associate where things where and both times I talked with them they were friendly and kind.    Even found a kindness rock! (OK, I found it back in October, but they do show up here frequently, I'm told.)

Stopped here after an afternoon in Sarasota with the husbeastie. The only stipend about eating is that we should eat someplace we've never been before.   Since he's working in Down Town St. Pete, He eats in the city a lot, so we decided to drive to the fringe Luckie B's.  It's a nice enough place, looks like it should be smoky and have peanut shells on the floor, but it isn't either one of those things.   We were seated and perused the menu, placing an order for the Fried Green Tomatoes as an appetizer. When they came, they were pretty dang Amazing. Lightly battered with a lot of flavor. Truth be told, I was full when the entree came.   The entrees were hugely portioned, the sauces were plentiful and the sides were tasty.  I had the brisket and I swear the serving must have been at least a half pound. The meat was super tasty. I chose the macaroni and cheese which is spicy if you're unprepared for it, and the green beens which were very tasty.  The hubs had the half rack and the brisket and he too was quite pleased, though he didn't like the cole slaw.  Over all, the prices were reasonable and the service was friendly and efficient. We'd come back if we were in town.

It's Covid season, the store was one of a few that was open in WireGrass, so we ventured forth.  There were a few people inside, most not wearing masks. I didn't see associates wearing masks, either.   The bathroom was neat, clean and well stocked, but the store was still stuck in March. There were decorations for March 17th and Easter up for sale. The fashions were for Spring and not yet summer.  I understand why, but it was so very odd, like stepping into a weird time warp.   We didn't speak to any associates, no help was offered.

Stopped in for lunch one afternoon. I'd honestly not been to a Boston Market since I worked for Capital One in Tampa.   I placed my order for their 1/4 chicken white, got the upsell of the garlic herb sauce (Do this, it's amazing), got sides of soup and green beans and enjoyed myself a lovely meal.   The dining room was in need of a little attention, but the food hit my belly just right as I watched the storm spill outside.

Our first time trying Puerto Rican food and we were not disappointed.   The eatery is lovely, the staff was quite friendly and warm. The air is heavily scented with what can't be described as anything other than Abuela's home Cooking. It smells mouth watering good.   The menu is large and thankfully it had pictures as there were things I didn't know what they were, and the menu photo looked good so I took that as my guide. As long as it wasn't too spicy, I could eat it.   The Food is delicious, the flavor is in every bite. I ordered the skirt steak with a chimichuri sauce and it was amazing. My guy got something with plantains and though I don't usually like plantains, they were tasty too, what I did find was that, on average, for the value, they seem to have smaller portion sizes vs other eateries in area.   Would I go back? Yes. the food is very good.

My father in law got to choose the place since it was Father's day. The first choice was a new place in Brandon, but it, being Portillo's, was BUSY, so we opted for a place to get Phó, and it wasn't busy at all.    Pho Viet, was nice, and we were seated quickly our drink orders taken right away, by 2 different waiters.   Once we looked over the menu, we placed orders for starters, the fresh spring rolls with peanut sauce and edamame.  While we waited, because it wasn't crowded, I heard their microwave go off twice.. Yep, microwave. That made me sad.  I know they're used but it also tells me that something isn't quite fresh.   When the apps were delivered, the spring rolls were large, but to me the peanut sauce was VERY peanut butter-y and almost fermented, it really didn't taste right.  The edamame... well they were most certainly what was being microwaved. the salting on them was uneven and some were cold.   Our meals were decent, the husband got the hot/spicy Pho, and my father got the combo bowl. Me i got the grilled vermicelli bowl, with pork and grilled shrimp.  For the husbeast he found that it had too much oil in it and later suffered gastric distress because of it.  The father in law ate every bite. Me? I found that the grilled pork was quite dry and tasteless, but the grilled shrimp was tasty.   It was ok, but I don't know that I'd come back.

Stopped here for lunch with my Niece after being out Christmas shopping.  This is a sister eatery to the Joeys in the Southgate plaza, so I  wasn't surprised to see that the place was absolutely packed with people, only 2 tables were open so my niece and I took the two top and a host brought us the menus.   It wasn't a long wait before out waitress came over and took our order. We wanted diet cokes and shared a ham & cheese calzone. I knew the size of their calzones so this was the smartest idea for us.  It was about 15 minutes of a wait while they cooked the order, but it came out perfectly golden brown, brushed with garlic butter.  It was so stuffed with cheese and ham that some of it hadn't warmed to piping hot through completely, but that was fine, it was warm enough.   It was crispy and piping hot at the edges and tasted like Heaven.  We even had some left over for my mom to have a snack.   All total, with a bit of a little bigger than normal tip due to the holiday, we paid under $20, for lunch for the 2 of us.  Service was fantastic, You can bet that we'll come back.

The beau wanted to show me one of his favorite places where he used to hang out in St. Pete. The traffic was down the street for parking as the lot was filled. The small over flow waiting area outside was full but inside, we were able to sit down, so that was nice.    The wait, about 30 - 40 mins, was TOTALLY Worth it.  We were seated in the main building along the wall so we could watch the buzz of the eatery. Buzz it did, this place was a well oiled machine.  My guy placed his order for 2 eggs, Bacon and toast with a blue berry pancake, I got an omlette with grits.   I was NOT prepared for the pancake, no one warned me it was the size of a hubcap. It was huge! It was also delicious.  The prices were amazing, as was the food, the service and everything else.  I wish this was closer because I would eat every meal here.

I don't need a reason to love this store. They're much like a Ross or Tj Maxx, but with out the clothes and Beauty items.  I can come here to find awesome Halloween stuff, or other seasonal things, Cool food to try, and neat coffee cups. I found Smashmallow plushie toys on my last visit and since those are a collectible for a friend, I scooped up three of them.   in the time of covid they've been trying with arrows on the floor (People don't really comply) Masks and social distancing. And of course they have their people cleaning the carts which is awesome.

Lovely newish BE! We stopped since we were down that way making a drop for a friend.  The place was super clean and the staff was friendly.  They were (At the time) Enforcing social distancing and not seating everyone together. Staff was wearing masks.   We were sat and our waitress came over and took our order, She was friendly and efficient. We both placed our orders and our food came out quickly. I got myself the Pot Roast, because Bob Evans knows how to make pot roast. I was not disappointed.   One thing you can count on at BE is fast and friendly staff, and we were not disappointed. If we're back in the area, We'll stop in.

Our feline's litter box quit working, so we needed a replacement. Those mechanical ones are expensive, let me tell you! We stopped here on a whim to see if we could find one that worked for us.   Given that we were looking for a specific type, we found JUST what we were looking for, but there really are only .. 4 or so to choose from, and be warned these kind of litter boxes run from $125-$210 depending on the options you need/want.

Hard to find, It wasn't clearly marked, but once inside, I was pleased! The lobby bar was neatly stocked, the restrooms were clean and well appointed.   The theatre itself is intimate. Cozy even. And as another poster pointed out, the way it's set up, if you need a potty break, just wait for the break.. otherwise you are pretty much up on the stage with the actors and invading their space.   We truly enjoyed the show we saw - a WIT IMPROV production - which was a fundraiser for our friend Billy Edwards. The best part of the night was Scott & Billy getting down to their underwear and walking blindfolded through a minefield of mouse traps all for the laughs of those who watched. Truly a bunch of masochistic souls - who do anything for a laugh!

Visited here on a date night with my husband. We'd spun the wheel of Yelp after visiting Sunken Gardens.   The inside of the place is So unique.  It was really neat to read that the decor is from locations that have previously existed.  I wonder if the location is haunted.   Their Grouper bites are amazing. I don't like fish and I like these.  The food was good. I had a hamburger and it was quite tasty.  The service was good too. Our drinks never ran dry.

Stopped in before going to the Fresh Market for food shopping.   The place wasn't terribly busy, so I got myself the muffaletta and soup, both of which were quite tasty. You get yourself 1/4 of a sandwich, and while that doesn't sound like a lot, it's quite sufficient. The soup was Irish Potato but it was over shadowed by the smoky bacon flavor.   The ice cream at the end of the meal is always a favorite.   I don't get down here that often, but I'm glad i got a chance to visit .

This is only for the Cafe...  Went in to get a Chai tea, my newest addiction. The husband was over at Tiger direct, so I popped in to get something cool and refreshing.  The gentleman before me had a bit of a complicated (read large) food order, so I patiently waited my turn.  When it came time, I stepped up, placed my order for my large iced chai, skin, no water, light ice.  The barista made NO eye contact, didn't smile and basically looked as if she were being put upon. I get it. It's hard to make a drink that you pour out of two containers and don't even have to heat up. But a little friendliness goes a long way. *shrug*   I've been a barista. I know the order could have been a lot worse. I could have ordered a double tall half calf mochalatte over ice, with double cream. But it was relatively simple.  When dealing with the world, suck it up and smile.

Decided to try a new local eatery for our Anniversary.  When we arrived, they weren't busy at all. There was one other couple in the dining room, and they turned out to be the owners of the place (Which is really cool because that lead to a lot of info being shared and a nice chat).  Our waitress, Gina, is the owner's daughter. She was warm and friendly and very good at her job. We started our meal with a Cappuccino and a frosty Sam Adams which was perfect as we looked out over lake Tarpon inlet.  The fresh bread and Pesto (It's the best-o) is amazing, the pesto is absolutely DELICIOUS and made in house.  We ordered their Brussel Sprout starter as well, and we were NOT disappointed, ZOMG I could eat that EVERY dang day.  It was crispy, full of flavor and I need it in my life, and so do you.  It is also keto friendly.  Get you some.   For mains, My husbeast ordered the house made lasagne and I got the Duroc maple glazed pork chops. We were warned that the chops had a longer cooking time, and I assured the owner that this was fine. We'd wait without a problem. They were only too happy to let us know about their experience (Previous owners of a pizzeria in Oldsmar that was really popular as well as another venture so they're familiar with food) and that the family is in the kitchen and much of the staff.  They are passionate about food and it shows. This place is amazing and I really hope it stays.   Our food came out and we were thrilled. The lasagna came in a cast iron skillet and my HUGE 14oz double chop and sides (mixed veg and mashed sweet potato) Were served on a cutting board, beautiful presentations!  But it wasn't until we tasted the food that we knew what we were in for.   Guys, You all know that I'm all about what a place is like for service, and this place has that.  BUT THE FOOD!! ZOMG ! The food here is incredible, and I mean that. The pork was tender and so flavorful, The maple and garlic glaze gave it kind of an Asian influence, but OMG so So SO good! The lasagne was tender and so full fo cheese and meat sauce.    Neither of us could finish it. We both left with enough for another meal.  We didn't have enough space for dessert but their big thing is Creme brulee and Tiramisu, so you know that I'll be back.   I look forward to being a regular here.  Grand opening is this coming weekend May 16-20th, I'm told that they'll be doing give aways and what have you, so make sure you come out and see what they have.  This place is going to be a go to for my family, make your reservations accordingly!

I don't know what they're putting on the chicken as a seasoning, but it's AMAZING. I'm addicted. I've literally, and this is no exaggeration, eaten there 5 days in a row.   The husbeast and I popped in here on my suggestion because I knew they'd recently opened, and though we're familiar with Greek cuisine living in Tarpon, we're less familiar with Schwarma and the like.  Inside, it smelled SO good. There was one other patron, ahead of us and the cook and the counter clerk, all masked, in the time of Covid, this was wonderful to see.   When it came time to order, I ordered the Chicken Shwarma, the husbeast ordered the beef, we opted for the platters the first time, and soda, we were not disappointed. The long grain rice was beautifully seasoned, the meat was deliciously flavoured, the salad was light and delicious as well. Their taziki was heavily garlicky which I find amazingly tasty!  Since that first visit, we've tried their fries - SO GOOD, and wraps too, with tahini, and I can say we're fans. It's become my go to when I want something from a take away shop. One of my visits afforded me the chicken shwarma platter with some pickled veg that were so GOOD. I need to know what they were and where I can get them. I NEED to have them regularly in my life.   Suffice to say, I Love this shop, I'm a fan, and I will be back, frequently. Their prices are reasonable, the food is good, reasonably healthy/clean and the service has always been friendly, masked and polite.

On a whim, we opted to go to the butchery and pick up steaks to grill for the evening meal. While we were there, we looked at all the fresh meats they had ready, including the seasoned breasts of chicken, the sausages and the kebabs. Everything looked so tasty.   We opted to pick up 2 steaks and 3 breasts of chicken, two cajun and one garlic. On the grill these thick breasts turned out delicious as did the two steaks. We were really happy with our purchases.   The store carries more than just meat though. There is honey, there are specialty items and so much more. Treat yourself by stopping in, you'll be happy you did.

New in Tarpon Springs, Ihop is a nice addition to our Eating Establishments.   They opened during Covid, so for the visit, they were at 50% capacity and not seating every table. Since then the Govenor has opened up the state to phase 3 and they can be full, but the staff is still wearing masks, and that makes me happy.   The eatery is clean and neat, the staff is friendly. Each time, I've been sat in the same booth and that makes me giggle a bit, but I digress, the bathrooms are also neat. I've not seen this place be messy, which is good.   The food, it sometimes takes a bit of time.  The first time, our order was out quick. My 2nd visit, I watched 3 tables that ordered after us get their food before us, which lets me know our order got skipped or not put in, but that's Ok, sometimes stuff happens.   When the food came out, it was good.  I always get the same thing, the beef tips, with egg or the dinner which comes with corn and mashed potatoes. The food is always tasty. My guy got a fajita omelette and I don't think I've ever seen that much cheese with eggs. I had a bite, it was good. YUM.   We will come back, we enjoy breakfast for dinner and Ihop is our favorite place to get that. So Yes, We'll frequent this establishment, no doubt about that.

One of the larger Publixes, Publii? In the area for sure. I stopped in the day before Thanksgiving and the store was hopping. The parking lot was a manageable nightmare but the staff was friendly and smiling.   I had to pick my Niece up a birthday cake and the Bakery staff was as helpful as can be. They had the perfect little cake right up front, in the perfect assortment of colors. I just had them remove the Thanksgiving pik and put a birthday one in and it was golden.   No one seemed rushed or hurried except the other patrons. Every employee seemed content and willing to get you what you needed. It was an exemplary Publix Experience.

Stopped in for lunch with mom on a Wednesday afternoon, just as the skies opened up and the rain came down.  The pick two combo of soup and a sandwich was the perfect thing to make the wet afternoon go by.  With their new pasta entrees and their flavourful soups/salads, you can really eat well for under $10.00.    Be sure to use your Panera's card to earn loyalty points which are good towards food rewards.

When they were located in their old building, I never visited, but now that they're located in the strip mall, I stopped in after having lunch just a few stores away.   I stepped inside with my beau and was pleasantly surprised, I expected just a head shop, but it was so much more.  Yes, they have all the things you need if you partake of the 'Devil's lettuce" including some AWESOME glass, but they also have some amazing gift ware.   I found some beautiful clothing, some great soap, a few little tchotchkies as well as CBD cigarettes, Cloves and incense.  Our associate, I don't remember his name but he was a really knowledgable guy, friendly as hell and he's the reason I'll be back.

After Kitting the Husbeast out for the Yelpies, it was time to choose a place for dinner. As I was beginning to play Spin the Yelp, the husbeast spoke up and mentioned Massimo's, how his former boss spoke so highly of it, and that he'd like to go. So I pulled it up on Yelp, checked it out and gave him the times it was open.. It was until 11, and given that the clock had JUST struck 9, we were fine on time.   When we arrived, the parking lot near Massimo's was not terribly full, unlike that around another eatery in the same lot. From the outside, the location is quite non-desscript, but when you open the door, the inside surprises you. The dark woods, the wall mounted waterfalls, the wall of wine at the back. It's all quite warm and welcoming.   We did not have a reservation, but given that there were only 4 tables with patrons, and the late hour, we were seated and our waitress Julie came over to see to us almost immediately.  She covered the specials, Lamb, grouper, a clam chowder and something with lobster and then let us peruse the menus for a few moments while she went to get us our still water.   When she returned, I asked for a bit of clarification on the lamb, which she readily gave me, as well as she expounded on the grouper for the husbeast. When that little detail was out of the way, we placed our orders. We opted to start with the Wild Mushroom strudel, and the husband also thought he'd add to that a cup (really a small bowl) of the clam chowder.  We also placed our orders for the mains at this time, mine being the lamb, and of course the Grouper for the husbeastie.  When the strudel arrived, it came topped with a parmesan sauce, which smelled heavenly. The two, two inch slices were the perfect starter to the meal we were about to eat, and the soup, the husband said, was delectable; rich and cream with a lot of clams.  While we were enjoying our starters, Julie came out with fresh bread and scented butter. Yes, this is not ordinary butter, no! But butter made with black olive, garlic and balsamic vinegar.  The result was so very savory and yum!  Our main courses came out and we were rightfully impressed! The grouper was light and flaky, topped with a pumpkinseed crust and a slightly sweet/tart sauce on the side. A side of veggies (spring carrots, asparagus, bok choy & a lone beet), and some decadent mashed potatoes were the accompaniments.  Watching the husband eat, it was clear that he truly enjoyed the meal.  The lamb was presented beautifully! Four lollipop chops were lightly battered and fried, served atop the same vegetable assortment with a mint basil puree and a Greek yogurt sauce.  The lamb was perfectly cooked, the fried texture of the batter added a delicious crispness and contrasted wonderfully with the earthy-ness of the beet. I could not get enough, heck! I didn't even share a bite of the lamb with the husband!  And the beet! I wish there had been more, there's nothing quite like fresh roasted beets. SO YUM!  Needless to say, we cleared our plates, and yes, dessert was had! Tiramisu that was both velvety and luxurious on the tongue, and absolutely decadent.   While we were finishing, Massimo came out and thanked us for dining, I thought that was a nice touch. The service was impeccable, we wanted for nothing. Our glasses never went below 1/2 empty. There was never a dirty fork or plate on the table. Truly this is a one of a kind establishment.   The husband liked it more than I like Berns. How's that for a recommendation?  Yes, we will be back!

3.5, but I can't do that so...  Stopped here to see my friend who was visiting from out of state.   They are currently still having staff wear masks. Not sure about the patrons. I was wearing mine just in case.   The lobby is large, spacious, with nice seating groupings. There's a large eating area for the (I'm guessing) Breakfast buffet.   The rooms are large and comfortable.  I'd stay if I needed to.

I'd only ever been to this Columbia location once.  And while this is the original, it is far from the best.   The decor is lovely and the location is spacious, but that is where the similarities end to the others I've been to.  We were set in the 2nd room, a table of 4 against the wall. Our waiter was an older gentleman who... was inattentive and rude. He would reach across me, no "Excuse me" no "Pardon" just - REACH- and deposit what ever it was he needed to do.   We ordered the Sangria, and in other locations, this was made at our table. Here, it was delivered by someone who was not our waiter, who had another pitcher on the tray, where he had all the fixings to make it at their table side, but ours, ours was already pre-made.  I was kind of disappointed.  Our food was delicious.  The salads, both the 1905 and the Tomato were delicious. All the mains were delivered promptly and tasted amazing, all but the yucca on the plate. At first I thought it was potato, but it was flavourless and gummy.. All in all it was fare that was fair at best. I will go to other locations in the future.

This was just a pop in/pop out little trip but I can honestly say that It was lacking?   Ok, so I arrived at 8:30 pm on a Sunday to the Southwest gate, this meant most things were closed except the Hudson's Booksellers. I was -hoping- that the shop that sold beignets would be available because who can make a trip to New Orleans without getting a beignet even if you don't step foot on Bourbon street.   But I digress. The airport seemed small, clean and efficient, but lacking in personality and services.

Met friends from out of state here to enjoy the evening and hopefully catch the sunset.  I hadn't even been aware we had a Frenchy's outpost close by!  Totally a tourist destination with a lot of outdoor seating and live music, it was a nice place to visit.  I'm NOT a fan of much seafood, so I got myself their pulled pork tacos without cilantro, and they accomodated that request. I was happily surprised that the food was good. The service was excellent.   I would totally come back.

I came to sears to look for a Tool Storage container, because I trust Craftsman tools. Why am I looking for one? Well, I have a lot of makeup and One of these would be perfect.  We found them amid all the sales, but not a single sales associate to be found, save at the cashwrap, and a long line. So there was NO ONE around to answer the question we had.    The question?  The one we were looking at, and primed to buy was RIGHT THERE, but looking at the description, it would consist of 2 pieces, the one on display was 3 pieces high. But the sign said -AS DISPLAYED- they had it in both black and red, identically displayed. We ended up leaving without purchasing our $400 unit, finding it at another place, one that was bigger, and a better value.

New Starbucks in Tarpon, Previously down by Publix, it's now in the walmart parking lot, where the KFC used to be.  The location is clean and bright, but way too loud on the inside. The older location was dark and intimate, this location is very open.   The counter is reversed so you order on the right and pick up on the left, the baristas were friendly and warm, they got our simple order correct, on this past Saturday night.   I like the place, even if I'm not the biggest fan of the over roasted coffee.
We love the ability to use the Ap and go to ANY of the local Tommy's Express car washes. We have never had an issue. It's great to be able to have a clean car when ever we want.

I swear I heard angels singing when I entered.   It was heaven. It reminded me of Pearl arts from my teen years.  They Literally have Everything you need to Paint, draw, sculpt, sew (its a small section) leather work (also small) etc.   I love the selection, there is -so much- that I want to play with, to try, to experiment with. It's just so much WOW.  I know I'll be back.

New KFC in the Holiday area. Really happy that they've opened and they are serving our neighborhood.   As we are in the Pandemic world currently, all things are going through the drive through, and the lobby is only partially opened up.  That being said, the drive through was really fast! They were exceptionally quick and friendly.   I ordered their $29.00 family fill up and it fed the three large adults that I have for 2 days.  I would order this again in a heart beat.
Drive through order was perfectly sufficient. There was no one in line so the wait was in order. There was nothing remarkable. The service was fine, friendly, fast.

10:08pm Wednesday Generally I don't like giving low reviews, but this one is for the service.  When I walked into Applebee's, there was no one at the host/ess stand. I waited, and I over heard a conversation about "How a family was supposed to get their friend out, since he was in a wheel chair." I stood there, shifting weight foot to foot, for four minutes, FINALLY I was seated, after being asked if I wanted to sit at a high top or a booth.   I looked at the time and noticed that 10:12 when I was sat.  I was given no silver, my table had no set up on it, but the guy who sat me asked me what I wanted to drink and assured me that my server would be with me soon.  I even saw him chase after who I think was supposed to be my server, as she headed out to the patio section, to let her know she had a table.   Time passed, as a single diner, it's boring, I got my tea but did not drink. At 10:23 a gentleman approached and asked me if he could help, I did ask why it took 9 minutes for a server to approach. To his credit he apologized and then told me that there were only 2 people on tonight - the place was rather busy, so under staffing seems like an issue to me, and he asked if I would like to speak to a manager. At this point I wasn't hungry but more irritated, Seriously, 2 wait persons for a place on a busy night is .. silly. I told him That I wasn't going to order that I was going to leave, and I did.   You only handicap your wait staff and provide bad service when you under staff.

A friend blessed me with a trip to St. Petersburg's MOFA, and I am so thankful she did!   We came on a Friday afternoon, no one was there besides the docents and one or 2 other small groups.  A lovely docent named Susan, who's worked there for 8 years walked with me and chatted with me about the art works I was looking at.   She challenged my 30 year repressed art school learning and I am happy to say that my brain is good at pulling up old info. That education resurfaced and I remembered how much I love art!   I want to go back now with my mom because there is an American Quilting expo (September/October 2021)

FOAM GLOW Edition  I came to the Florida State Fair Grounds to run/walk the Foam Glow 5K. We were told Parking would be $6 bucks, but when I arrived it was $10.  I was also told that I would not need to be at the front gate, but I needed to exit and go to the Orient Road entrance. So I did.   When I got there, they told me I was at the wrong entrance.  Um.. But your front gate folks told me I needed to go here. I guess communication got fouled up. I was there ultra early, I was arriving about the time that the workers were.. but they let me park with the workers behind the scenes, this made it a lot easier to get out at the end of the night.   Inside, the sky opened up with our usual torrential rain, but that didn't stop us, because once the foam started pumping, the music did too.. And when it got dark, we began to do the course. One thing I noticed about the course was that there were a lot of cheats and cut thrus that were too easy for folks to use. Me, I was there for personal reasons.. but lots of folks didn't have the same compunction and took them.  I guess if you're there to do a 5K, you should be there to do it.   That being said, the course could have been lit better.

Five star service, Five star view.   My husband's company - Malwarebytes, new to the Clearwater area - decided they needed to have a Christmas Party, and this was where they opted to do a low key affair on Monday evening.   It started out with drinks at sunset on the patio. I was glad I brought my coat, because that wind was bitter, but watching the sun settle into the ocean was splendid as I sipped on my blue Hawaiian, as our waitstaff of 4 attended to our every need.
