The fire columns interested every one, and when I put my hand on the cage, the sound of caution and then amazement when I didn't burn myself made the geeks all take notice, I'm sure we'll see a new design coming soon.   Once we were all seated, after about 10 minutes of musical chairs, and everyone jockeying for position near the various heads of the company, more drinks were offered, different wines and mixed cocktails. I asked about the wines and they were all dry, when I wrinkled my nose, I was offered a sweeter choice, a Reisling, without hesitation. SCORE!  There were chosen menus on our tables, we could choose a Soup or Salad: Mushroom Barley Soup, White Chili - Made with Alligator, Lady Moon Butter Lettuce or Little Gem Ceaser Salad.  The husband got the Mushroom Soup, and though it was flavourful, it was missing something. That Something was salt.  I ordered the white chilii, and it was missing NOTHING. It was delicious.  Our Mains were a choice of Black grouper with kale and clams, Naked bird Chicken - a stuffed chicken breast, or a petit Center cut filet. The husband had the fish, and he said it was delicious. He thought that it was served on corn, but I knew better, it was over an orzo. I chose the Filet, and OMG! That was one tasty steak. Perfectly seasoned and cooked!  The desserts were second to none! We had our choices of Vanilla bean Creme Brulee, Chocolate Cheese cake or Seasonal Sorbet - which turned out to be Key Lime. The husband chose the Keylime, since he likes all things tart, and he only ate about 1/2 of it. I chose the Creme Brulee, and I could have eaten more, it was DELICIOUS. Seriously  it was one of the best Creme brulees I've ever tasted. The vanilla bean was so thick in it you could see the flecks through out the dessert.   Through this, the service was the epitome of perfection. Nary an issue with drinks, your glass never went dry, if you were drinking alcohol, a new drink was always at hand. Yes, an unlimited bar.. how very nice! This is what i would call a first class meal at a first class dining establishment.

I like shopping at Ross, but this Ross.. I don't even know what to say.   There was precious little in the way of organization of sizes, the store was an absolute mess. I know, it's just after Christmas, so that might account for some of it, but LORDY! Spend some of your valuable time out on the floor getting it spruced up.   I did buy a dress and a shirt for $30, so I can't truly complain, but really... this place was a disaster, especially in their check out area.

Having been to a recent Yelp event, I just had to return. My husband and I are fans of Vietnamese food, so I had to share with him my newest discovery (Thanks Brett!)  The restaurant was a busy place on Thursday evening, with most of the tables filled, and that made me smile. That means they're doing well!  We stepped up to the counter and placed our orders.  My husband ordered the beef Phò and I ordered their beef terriyaki bowl - something I'd yet to try.   We sat at an unoccupied table and waited - not very long - for our food to come up. Their Phò base is REALLY good, very flavourful and as the husband said, better than many of the other places around.  For me, I thought the bowl meal was just right, although I left a lot of rice behind -damn lo carb diet!!! *fist shake*  Drinks were delicious, their iced jasmine tea is yummy and the green mint lemonade is beyond description. I only regret it does not have refills, else I would drink them out of everything they had. It is -that- good.   If you're in the area, stop over near Burlington and pop in, Say HI to the hard working crew there and patronize this little shop. You won't regret it!

I went to Georgie's alibi with 50 of my closest friends for an event called "Pinellas Coffee time". We get together once a week and hang out, this time it was here. Color me surprised to find out that the bar had food! I knew they had some Awesome drinks, but I had no idea about the food!  First let me tell you to try one of their signature martinis. I had the S'mores and the Russel's Chambord Dream, which were a BO/GO - Don't miss this special. OMG, let me tell you these were decadent! The best one.. The Russel's, was to die for! It was an orgasm in my mouth. One sip and I was hooked. I wish I had ordered it first, then I could have had two.  The other was good, but this was AH....Mazing!  And the food..their menu was extensive, but I opted for Tator Tots smothered with chili, cheese and sour cream Who could go wrong? It really was amazing. And all of that for less than $15? You can bet I left my waiter a hell of a tip.   The service was amazing, the drag show was good. It left me wishing we could have our PCT here every week!

I arrived at the Sand Pearl for the Husband's Christmas Party, which was held at their Resturaunt, and was pleasantly surprised. Everything was valet, but as long as I had the ticket validated, that was no problem.   Walking into the foyer, I was greeted with a sand sculpture of Santa and his elves. This was such a beautiful work of art.  There were games in the lobby - chess and checkers. and very comfortable couches. The decor was absolutely the epitome of Florida casual meets oppulence.   With the Christmas decor done, it is a sight to behold, especially since it looks like christmas on the inside, but outside, you can't be sure, since it LOOKS like summer, but the air bites like winter.   I can't wait to do a staycation here!

Dual drive thrus make it easy to get a Half/half tea when the person in the other lane is apparently ordering 1 of everything off the menu. Mine was a quick in and out trip and It took less than 3 minutes to order and get my tea.   I am sad though. Large Iced teas no longer are $1.00. Le sigh.

Loved this Royal St staple.   Smelled divine when we entered, like freshly baked brownies. We sat for a bit until we decided what we wanted to order. We both opted for their tea blends.  My friend wanted their fruit tea and I opted for their citrus Jasmine... Both were deliciously refreshing, and we split one of their fresh baked scones. Just the perfect amount of sweet.  I wish these were in Florida, because the service and the coffee/tea is so much better than the $Bux

The International Mall. A great destination if you have cash to burn.   it reminds me of the AlaMoana mall in Hawaii, only completely closed in and no Koi.  It has 2 of my favorite stores, LUSH and Sephora, and that's what keeps me coming back.   I really am not one for big named products, so I don't care about the Vera Bradley, Coach, or even the Neiman Marcus. The stores that get me coming back are the unique ones: Art of Shaving & Bettie Paige Clothing.

I love Wawa. They're always so clean, their gas pumps are plentiful and they make coffee for you in the barista style! What's not to love?   You want a sandwich? They'll make you one. You like pretzels? They have them. Do you like snacks? They have a plethora of them to choose from. There's so much to pick from at a WaWa.

I've been to other Longhorn locations and have never been truly impressed, but tonight was different. This location is apparently run with an efficient hand and a good manager.    We arrived around 8:30 pm and it wasn't busy at all, this was good, because we got seated very quickly.  Once seated, our waitress came over and took our drink orders, since I ordered coffee, and they had to brew some fresh, it took a little while longer, but fresh coffee made me not mind at all.   We ordered our starter of Pretzel sticks with beer cheese and honey mustard & bacon bacon dipping sauce.  These were -so- good! The cheese sauce was decadent. Our mains were a burger and Napa Grilled Chicken which is essentially a grilled chicken breast with artichoke hearts, sun dried tomatoes and portobello mushrooms in a light white wine sauce.  They were quite tasty, especially with the sides of a salad, asparagus & Brussels sprouts au gratin, finally a way to get me to eat those little cabbages.    I will admit, we had a small issue with our meal, my plate had a hair on it. I brought it to the waitress' attention, and she quickly removed the plate, had it remade and since my husband had eaten his meal in the interim, had the manager remove the cost of my meal, this was not expected, but it was greatly appreciated.      The service was excellent. We would most certainly come back again!

Brand new, they just opened on Monday, and so far they seem to be doing well. I heard about them last weekend when I'd visited the Pub. so I was excited to be able to see what they were all about.   We were seated almost immediately, though the floor was wet and I, quite literally slipped into my booth.  The Buc's game was playing over head, and it was loud on the inside but the tables were comfortable.  We placed our orders: Appetizer of the baked chicken wings and both of us ordered the knife and fork cobb salad, dressing on the side.   When the wings came out, the were surprisingly small, but topped with a pesto sauce, the were undeniably delicious. NEED MORE OF THE PESTO!  Our salads were different, seemingly a bit deconstructed,but delicious none the less. The cornbread croutons were the bomb, and the avocado was tops (and I don't generally LIKE avocado)  Our waitress was on the ball with getting us drink refills, only having to refill so often because there was so much ice in the glass.   Overall, we have a very positive first impression, I know that when I'm at I-Mall, I will stop back in.

This is a starbucks inside of a Target. The locations Perfect! It's got great service and of course, they make ALL the drinks just like you like them.   I always get a Medium hot chai latte, made with skim, with extra chai, which is always no cost. I LOVE it.

I stopped into Tiaga because a friend of mine was Dj'ing an event for the PLUSH club of Tampa Bay. DJ Chef Zulu was in the house for Partygras 2015 and the music he was spinning was HOT.   Everyone was dressed to thrill and the beads (And drinks) were being tossed back. The venue allowed us to have the top floor dance floor, and the patio for our event, and we filled it. I can tell you that It was my first Club Plush, and it was an interesting experience.   The biggest detractor for Tiaga? Parking.

I'm not sure why this particular Walgreens was the only one to have the Elf Villainess line, but they did. I tried every Walgreens from here to Palm Harbor and either they claimed to not have it or they don't get that particular shipment in until closer to Xmas. WHAT EVER. According to this Walgreens, they should all have it. *shrug* Not my issue. This location had it. I got what I wanted. Service was quick and I was in and out in no time.

Stopped in here on the recommendation of my mom, she frequents the place monthly and it was close, so I was able to get there easily while visiting her.   When I walked in there were 2 ladies waiting, and me.  All the techs were busy, I waited about 30 minutes. I was given a bottle of water during my wait which was nice.  One of the ladies waiting before me, didn't want to wait any longer so she left.   I was given to Miko, who had an appointment booked for 2:30, I was seated with her at 2:pm to get my nails colored, but first she had to remove the previous dip polish job. That alone took 25 Minutes.  Lucky for me her appointment cancelled.   Miko is exceedingly proficient at her job, She took her time and made sure my nails were both shaped to a shape I liked, and chose a color for me that would be better than the one I chose.   All in all, it took about 1.5 hours but my nails look good. The gel polish I chose is sparkly and bright, the nails are well shaped and even in color, they're a glitter and that can be hard to achieve. She took her time with me and I'm very pleased with the results!

Met here tonight with our geek squad. A party of 10, we had reservations for 7pm. I arrived first, about 15 minutes early and would have been seated immediately. I let the hostess know that this wasn't necessary, I'd wait until others of my party arrived first, once that happened, we could sit and the others could find us.    When we were sat, there was a large pair of tables set against a banquet, this made for a box, and the box made for a sound reflector, so it amplified all the noise in the room, making an already loud situation LOUDER.   When the whole party was sat, Ashley was prompt and efficient, and very, very wonderfully attentive, LOVED her!  We were all surprised at how large the appetizers were, my husbeast and I ordered the firecracker shrimp and we were pleased at the amount and the flavour of what we received. It was both spicy and REALLY Good.   The husbeast had the gumbo and he was very happy with how that came out. It was a cup serving that was steaming hot and tasty.   The table ordered lots of different items, but we ordered the stuffed fillet and the fried grouper. Sadly here's where the night didn't meet my expectations.  When my stuffed fillet came out, I'd ordered med rare, what I got was pretty much blue.  The veg and the garlic potatoes were delicious, but the shrimp tasted off-ish (to me) and the steak was really under done.  It took a bit of a while to get Ashley back to the table - we weren't her only group and that's understandable, but she took it back to the kitchen and made sure that I had something to eat while the others finished their meals - more veg and potatoes, a really nice touch.   The husband enjoyed his fried grouper, I can tell you he liked it a lot as his plate was cleaned by the time I looked over to ask him what he thought.   All in all, I found Ozona blue to be crowded and Loud but the food was tasty.  The service was personable and efficient. If you have a group, make reservations, as I heard one group of ladies in the bathroom say they waited 1.5 hours for a table.

Clean, well organized and a friendly staff, make this a nice place to shop.    You'd think that on the Monday after Black Friday that they'd be low on their stock, but no, they were pretty flush.   I actually had to return something I'd purchased over the weekend, something I adored, but sadly they didn't have the -exact same- one. I didn't have my receipt either. But there was no fuss, they let me trade it evenly for a different one, in a different color, no questions asked. I'm rather pleased with them.    The next time I'm in Port Richey and need to do a little shopping, I'll be there.

This is my favorite place for Cuban Food.   I didn't know that they'd close early on Sunday, so when I walked in and -all- the family was there, it was kind of nice, everyone was welcoming us and thanking us for dining.     We sat and ordered quickly. They've changed the menu, it used to be fold out thing, now it's a single sheet, double sided item.  But I've been here before so I knew what I wanted and I placed my order for the roast pork with yellow rice and black beans. My date ordered the fajita chicken with yellow rice and fried plantains.  Let me be the first to tell you my date is from Scotland, he's never had a plantain before, and so this was something new to his palate. He LOVED it. He loved the spice on the chicken and he liked the yellow rice.  My pork was done to perfection and everything was done with love.   As we left, our bellies full, the family wished us a happy Sunday.  It felt very warm!

I -love- what they've done with the old Waterworks area. This used to be a derelict part of the river front and now it's a blossoming, booming beacon! The Tampa Waterworks park is lushly landscaped, has a great children's play area, complete with a splash park for the wee ones to get soaked in.   The Rotary pavilion is there as well, allowing for concerts or even weddings to take place under cover in case of rain. If you happen to have a 4 legged friend, bring them along! There's a lovely gated park just for Fido too!

This is a hotel eatery.   The whole place has been remodeled since I was here last year and it's absolutely gorgeous. However, with the bar just out front, the traffic pattern is really wonky.   Since I was staying in the hotel for a convention, this was the easiest place to grab our food, however the prices were a bit exaggerated. I don't do buffet eating most of the time so I had to order off the Ala-cart menu and found that coffee and oatmeal for $9 was a bit out of line.  That being said, the service is incredible.   We had a bad go of things our first visit: We came in as they were transitioning from breakfast to lunch and tried to order off the breakfast menu. I wanted a specialty omelet and my date, the Belgium waffles. While we waited what seemed a long time, our waitress finally came out and told us that the waffle iron had been turned off and they had no waffles to be given out, could he order something else. Ok, that's fine but why wait 15 minutes to tell us.    While he was perusing the menu once more, my food came out. My omelet was missing the ham, had spinach on it and when I got to the center, uncooked egg whites came rolling out. That about turned my stomach.  I get it, things happen and when it does, the management takes care of things. And take care of things they did.   I can not fault them at all for their response!   Sherri the manager came over to make sure that my date's order was placed and then she found out my issue and apologized profusely. She asked me if I wanted something new, I opted for the Lunch menu on this go round. I ordered a spring Mozzerella salad, and my date the pancakes. In the end, both of these came out perfect and we were told it was on the house. Like I said they took care of it promptly and without complaint. The service was AMAZING.   On my stay, I visited two more times: Once I had their french style chicken with gouda mashed potatoes and spring vegies. This was just a tasty baked chicken. And I tried their tail-gate buffet. It was alright if you weren't aware most of the things were Sysco frozen offerings.  Certainly not worth the $20 price tag.   TL:DR?  Service is amazing, Prices are too high for this area.

When I'm craving BBQ, there is usually only one name on my lips, and that's LUPTON'S. Why? Because it's a buffet and because it's GOOD.  There is almost nothing better than the way they do their ribs. Sometimes their sides are ..meh.. but if there's cabbage on the menu, I am a -happy- girl.   This is an excellent place to go after Faire or any time I'm on that end of town.  And don't forget, your Tea is free with your meal!

I want to give this a higher rating because the food was DAMN good.    Right on the water at the start of the Sponge Docks, ShrimpWrecked is a new addition to the area.  I'd just come back from the hospital - yay foot injury, and I was hungry. So we opted to get food here. First issue, parking is confusing. But once we figured it out, it was easy.   We made our way to the back of the bar area, to sit out side, because it was a lovely day to be outside and nearly sunset, the perfect time to be on the water.  The hostess sat us and we were given menus. Once that was given, our WAIT-ress, came over and asked us for our drink orders, we placed them, and they came over quickly.. I was ready to order my app, but in a quick second she was GONE.   We waited... we waited... we waited.  In 10 or so minutes she came back and asked if we wanted to place our orders with the preface that there was a 20-30 minute wait in the kitchen. She just wanted us to know. No worries. We placed our order for a soup and salad, an App of the buffalo shrimp, the coconut shrimp and the crawfish platter.   And she was off.   Around us, I noticed that other people weren't having the wait times we were, or the others in our section. One table was especially techy about the waitress, I'm not sure specifically about what the issue was, but they had the manager come over and I did over hear them talking about how the waitress wasn't around.  Our drinks went empty.  Finally our salad and soup came out. We enjoyed them.   And we waited some more. The live music was awesome. I'm not sure who was playing on Sunday afternoon, but he was really REALLY good.   When the food was delivered, it was hot and fresh. The coconut shrim was as good as the other people have claimed. The buffalo shrimp was hot and spicy, there could have been more celery offered with it.  The crawfish were.. interesting, more like fried clams than crawfish, but what do i know? I've never eaten them before.   We waited again.. I asked for a refill on our drinks from another waitress.. I asked for a box, when I asked for our box, I had to ask for our check AFTER she dropped the box off. I'm not sure if Lola was having an off day or what, but she certainly brought down my rating due to the lack of service we were having.

Headed into Tarpon proper for a nice afternoon lunch on their Tiki deck to enjoy the lovely weather.  It was the first visit to this local icon and while I wasn't daunted by the lack of "proper" parking, I was by some of the menu prices.  The food was good, the service a little slow, but over all, it was a nice experience.  The scenery made up for it all. The warm breeze, the slowly rolling storm front that has yet to break..   The attire is flip flops and shorts, comfortable and causal, don't worry if you're wearing a bathing suit, you'll fit right in.

I'm from Tarpon, so to me if it's not from there, it's not really Greek.   To be honest, their food was tasty. The Gyro was a bit heavy on the lamb, but I'm not complaining. Their greek fries were to DIE for. So good.  The menu wasn't terribly expensive and I have to wodner, looking at the pastries, are they from Helas?

Found this little place when i checked YELP to see what was in the local area. I'm glad I popped on by. It was a beautiful Saturday morning and the outside tables were busy so the husbeast and I opted to sit at one of the large communal tables inside after we placed our breakfast orders.   Inside, it's decorated in a fun, ecclectic way, that speaks to different cultures. Mexican Dia de los Muertos skulls are around as is other iconic statuary. There's a warm and homey feeling that just exudes friendlyness and the locals seem to like the place.    The food too, speaks of the love the people have for what's offered. I had an omelet with ham and cheese and some of their home fries, the husband had one of their burritos, all the food was delicious and well made. everything tasted fresh! And let me tell you about their coffee! It was AMAZING!

Drive thru in the newly refurbished Wendy's.   Things went very quickly, the service was exceedingly polite, if a bit rushed.  I wanted to ask for sour cream for my chili, but the guy on the headset was hard to get his attention when he wasn't looking at you.  The food was good, hot and fresh, especially the fries. And that matters!

Visited here the other day,  Stopped to get food after the Doctor's visit, after finding out that the husband was indeed sick. So we opted to get him some hot soup and me a burger.    Their food is consistently mediocre, not AAHHHMAZING and certainly not terrible, but they do offer something I've not seen anywhere else, Bacon Mac & cheese balls! Now those were tasty!  The soup was good, the burger, well, I take them apart and just eat the protein and veg. So it really would behoove me to order it that way ratehr than waste the bread, perhaps one day i'll do that.   The waitress we had was excellent though. She was always on hand getting us what we needed!

The husbeastie now works in Ybor, so he's checking things out on 7th. He mistakenly thought this was a place like we'd seen back in GA that made your ice cream with Nitrogen.  When we arrived, Snobachi was packed, the line was moving though, so we picked up a menu, hopped in line and waited a few minutes to place our order.   The husband chose a vanilla base with strawberries and strawberry syrup. I got vanilla base with coffee, caramel syrup and chocolate chips. We were told the wait was about 10 minutes and they were right. It was fun to watch them make the 2 different ice creams. It was even more fun watching them roll it up from the frozen tablets and put it all together .  So, what's it taste like? REALLY GOOD!  Super sweet, very creamy and rich. I might try one of their custom flavours next time. And trust me, there will be a next time. ;)

Since the Florida weather didn't want to cooperate while the Scot was in town for most of the time, we FINALLY got a beautiful day to go to the beach.  The plan was to go to Clearwater, but apparently Spring Break had already begun, and parking   was proving to be a nightmare.  No worries! I've been in Florida forever, I have a few tricks up my sleeve, and so we went over the next bridge, and low and behold sand key park was there, with hardly anyone there.  Parking was cheap $5 flat rate for the whole day, and it was plentiful. The beach was wide and sparsely populated as we made our way out to the shoreline. The tide was rolling in quickly so we only spent an hour - well the tide and pale Scottish skin that is. In that time, we spotted a dolphin in the waves, a live baby conch, many children and couples playing in the surf, and we were buzzed by a low flying plane. It was a great place, far better than the commercialized Clearwater Beach.

They know my husbeast by face, since he used to work around the corner. They know his order by heart and he doesn't even have to open his mouth. Me? I'm a different story. But What I order never changes, Give me my Chicken Satay and my Chang Mai fried rice and I'm a happy girl.   Portions are generous, service is quick and they have Coconut custard and sticky rice, It's similar to haupia and just as tasty. I love this place.

Smaller format Target, but one of the cleanest target's Ive ever been in.  Everything was in it's place and I was VERY surprised by the Furniture/housewares section. It felt more like an IKEA than Target by its very design.   They had exactly what I was looking for, and they even had it in a multi pack, which my usual Target did not. So that was surprising.  Their Movie's department threw me a little bit, with their NEW MOVIES not being on an endcap but rather in a waist high bin. So very different. I have to think this is a test store and that's ok.  I liked it.

Since mom and I were on Clearwater beach trying to find a funny t-shirt for an event, I thought it would only be right to do lunch down there.  We walked down the North beach drag and stumbled across Clear Sky Cafe with it's Large beach chair and dolphin out front, and the nice dining patio. It looked inviting so we went inside.   The sign said "Wait for waitress to seat you" so we did. The bartender was busy with her clients, all 3 of them, that she never once looked up.  It was about 4 minutes before a waitress walked by and delivered food to a table and started to walk past again without even acknowledging us when I asked if there was a hostess.  She looked surprised and said "Sure, sit where ever you like." So I took mom to one of the small booths inside and we sat down.   We were handed the menus but no setups, and given a few minutes to look them over.  When V-ron came to attend us, she asked us our drink order and came back promptly. Then we placed our order for the Soup and sandwich combo, both of us getting the French Onion soup and the pressed Cuban sandwich. The food was absolutely delectable. The service from this point on was great. V-Ron (Veronica) was sweet and attentive. We would certainly come back.

Stopped here with my girls while visiting the Mall.   At first we thought we lucked out as or waitress was awesome and friendly, but then we noticed that the service was incredibly slow.. I mean sloths are faster.   When I asked for coffee it had to be brewed, and I understand that. But it really shouldn't take nearly 30 minutes to get the cup.  Refills took so much longer for my table mates.  I had ordered the loaded fries for the table but they didn't come out ahead of time, they came out with my soup - which was my main and they were cold. No one at many, thankfully they were taken off the bill.   Over all, FRIENDLY but very slow service. Food that is sub par.

Stopped in Sioux City today for lunch. We showed up just before/after (Not really sure) of the lunch rush. I can only tell you this because the gal behind the hostess stand seemed really frazzled.  She asked us where we wanted to be seated, and I told her it was ok, wherever she wanted to seat us.  We were sat at a table and then waited 5-10 minutes for the waiter to come.   The waiter was pleasant enough, just slow. in truth that was the hallmark of the service. it was slow, our glasses went empty for a good while before they were refilled but the food was tasty. The main complaint was that they didnt have the Ap I wanted. Other than that, our ribs and steaks were done as we wanted them.

Do you like bath bombs? Do you like homemade soaps? If you do? GetaGuru is the place for you. Their bombs and soaps are all handmade, each is heavily scented with natural oils and smells -so- good.  Stop in, spend your money in a local merchant and help the local community!

I came in looking for a lap desk for my lap top computer. In a store the size of Staples, I thought there might be a selection. Sadly there wasn't. There was One. ONE in the whole store.    The store itself was...  It was rather depressing to walk into.

Came here for a date night with my Beau. Our goal was to have dinner before the belly dance show.   The menu was an experience, we started with coffee martinis that were made to perfection. Our first course was the pumpkin soup which we both loved. Our second was the meat and cheese pies. I think I fell in love over those meat pies. They we're so delectable.    Our main course was the steak, I don't remember what name of it was, but the spicing, the peppers and meat were all an amazing flavor combo on the palate.    The service was attentive, friendly and efficient. We capped our meal off with two espressos and a tiramisu. If I'm going to be critical I will say I was disappointed ninnthe dessert. It was mostly flavorless. But the coffee was delicious.

I Thought that I'd stumbled into a  PDQ by the way the counter and drink station was set up, because they were nearly identical - and quite probably the same format of place (I think they're owned by the same company)  After perusing the menu, we placed our orders, the husbeast chose a double bacon cheeseburger meal and I ordered their Wow Phillycheese steak meal with onion rings. I will say that we were upsold (good job) on the combo, and since we would have ordered the sides and a drink this was a good bet.   The staff was busy making sure that the dining area was clean and the floor was being mopped, despite this it was still sticky. (happens)  Our food came out in about 8 minutes or so, which is pretty fast for "fast food", we both found it good. The rings were definitely the highlight of my meal, with their thin but crispy breading.  My sandwich bread however wasn't toasted as much as it could have been and didn't stand up well to the cheese sauce. (again, happens.) But the meat, veggies and cheese made for a tasty Philly cheese steak. By the way the husbeast consumed his bacon cheese burger, I have to think it was really good.

9:30 at night, Down town Tampa, and you're hungry. You don't know anything in the area, so you go with the name you know.   The food was delicious, the food was out quick and the service was both friendly and fast. They closed at 10:00 on the dot so while we were there just past the tick of the clock, they didn't kick us out. They let us stay until we were ready to go.   The food is good.

After pricing a camera at several different places, we wandered into HH Greg because I'd never been to one.  We found the same camera there for the same price, but what we ended up with was a bundle.  Not only did I get the camera, but I also got a bag, 2 lenses, the charger a strap, memory card & necessary cables.  Quite a better deal than the other places were offering!   The 3 year Replacement plan for $150, though I bought it, was a bit steep. I bought it because I KNOW I'm going to need it.   We also considered buying a bed, after losing the weight we both have, our bed doesn't fit us as comfortably as it used to. Sadly the bed we were interested in was discontinued. They were more than willing to cut us a deal on the floor model. More than 1/2 the sticker cost, but it was just a queen, and we want a king. *SAD*  We're going to keep an eye out, because these kind of beds are really nice. Hopefully something similar will come back in stock and they'll be available again.

I was meeting a friend for coffee, I left the choice up to him. We didn't want a starbucks so he found this place. It's right off Mandalay, not far from the Sand Pearl resort. I'd forgotten that this is a peak week for tourists, so the first thing to note is that parking was difficult to say the least.   The coffee was good, though. It's a custom bean to them, and honestly, it was well done, not over roasted. We did have to wait for it, and that's OK. We sat at the tables out side and watched the people pass by. And boy was there a lot to watch! Tourists are so much fun! The seats outside were nicely kept, the tables were comfortably seated under an awning, and since the weather was perfect, there was no need for an umbrella or heater. Good thing, since neither was visible.   Prices were the same if not a few cents less than S*Bucks. If I'm ever in the area again, I'll be back.

Needed to get new flurescent bulbs for the garage and a new shower head... wasn't prepared for the plethora of choices for either. LORDY!  Who knew there were -so many- different 48" types of light bulbs. We ended up getting two different wattages so we could change out the laundry room too.   Regarding the showerhead: I wanted the $225 multi-head shower bar, but the husbeast said no. We did end up getting shower head within the head.. by Moën, I can't wait til we install it!  The store is very clean and neat with very impressive employees who know where -everything- is.

A unique shop that sells specialty dessert items across from the Movie theaters in Countryside mall, Le Macaron is a sweet stop.   Gluten free, the treats are delicious, fresh and very colorful. They're also not cheap. $13(with tax) for 6 of the half dollar sized "cookies".  But they are light and tasty, and just the right size for you to pop in your mouth or enjoy with a capuccino.   They also sell some of the prettiest chocolates I've ever laid eyes on. Hand painted, custom flavored confections that would put a smile on anyone's face if they got them for a holiday gift.

Simply Delicious!  From their quaint decor to their off the beaten path menu, you'll find something that you like at Sandwich on Main.   I tried their Muffalittle, while my friend had the tomato bisque and a cheese sandwich. Both of the sandwiches were to die for. I've not had such a good Muffaletta sandwich since I came back from the big easy! And the soup was tasty too!  The only issue I really had was the service, as it was kind of spotty. *shrug*  It was a festival weekend, so I can give a pass on that one.   The inside tables each have the neatest little terrarium on them... check them out when you eat inside. Don't ask for ice, as there is none, they're not "big" enough for an ice maker, or so I was told.

This is the smallest Sweet Tomatoes I've been in. It's floor plan leaves a lot to be desired, but tonight the salads were fresh and the food was all tasty.  I noticed that the Ceasar salad seemed to have been just made and I could taste the lemon juice in the dressing (YUM!) Using a coupon (They come out in your Email on Thursdays if you're a club Veg Member) we saved a few bucks and had ourselves a light and tasty dinner tonight. Soup and deliciously crisp veggies, and .. those OMG! yum gluten free Coconut Muffins. PLEASE don't take those away. I love them!

I needed to ship my phone back to T-mobile. I had a pre-addressed label on the package and all I needed to do was drop it off at the UPS store.  I walked in, handed it to the girl behind the counter. She made sure that I had my receipt so that I could prove that it went back on time.   Excellent customer service.

Found myself adrift this afternoon, when the plans I'd had changed. Instead of letting this get me down, I made it into an Yelp-ortunity! I'm only vaguely aware of the south Tampa area, so I decided I'd play Yelp Roulette and let the spinner choose where I was going to eat.   The first place (read closest) was Pinkys. Sadly, they were closed.  So I headed down to MacDill and saw Byblos right around the corner. I like Middle Eastern food, there was parking, so SCORE! Lunch would be had.   There were very little patrons at noon on a Monday, but I imagine during the weekend this place is hopping like mad! I was shown to my seat, given a menu and a few minutes to decide what I wanted.  It was pretty easy, I love labneh, which is a dip made with a kefir goat cheese and herbs, tangy and delicious.  And I was in the mood for a salad, so that's exactly what I ordered.   It was delivered quickly, the food was extremely fresh.  The salad, $7.95, was little more than romaine lettuce, cucumbers, shaved carrots and tomatoes, but it was very tasty. Not sure it was worth the cost, *shrug*, but I didn't want to add meat to it and bring the cost to double.  As for the dip! It was amazing, I've not tasted labneh in a long while, so this made my tastebuds dance! And the pita the served with it was chewy and just the perfect texture.   I used my Yelp check in, so I received 2 free pieces of bakalava as my dessert!  The service was excellent. Zuzannah was very knowledgeable, friendly and happy to show me around the location. She was very proud of the party room! And she even showed me the attached store, which sells oils and spices as well as a few food items that they sell at the location.   The decor is -gorgeous-! Reds and golds everywhere, Rich fabrics and stunning portraits on the walls, it's a place I could get lost in for hours (if I had them!) Every saturday night, they have a live Dancer, who will perform for you. Hookah is also available if you partake!   I know that I'll be back!

I've lived in Tarpon Springs for the last 4 years. I was born in Greece (Fun fact!) and I keep hearing that I need to try the Limani.  It is a hole in the wall, but they are known to have the best tasting gyro and souvlaki.  I've kind of been ambivalent about it this whole time.. until today. They're RIGHT!  Today I took mom down to the docks to try something new. We decided to go to The Limani, and lo and behold, the stories are true. Spit roasted Gyro and fresh, cooked to order souvlaki are absolutely delicious, especially when paired with the rich tatziki sauce, decadent with cucumber and garlic it is certainly hard to beat.   The outside seating and water views make this place a winner in my book. Today was a perfectly mild afternoon so the breeze and the seagulls (Sea bullies) made for a lovely time to chat with mom and make acquaintences with 2 visitors from Chicago.  Will I be back? You can bet that I will be. I'm a convert!

Formerly LeeRoy Selmon's, and honestly not a lot has changed.   The place has cleaned up, put carpeting down, and taken the football crap off the walls, but for the most part, its still a sports bar/grill.  Our server was a delight, worked hard to make sure everyone in his section was happy and pleased. Our food was delicious though. We ordered the pub chips - basically a potato or two, thin cut and deep fried, with basalamic vinegar, bacon and bleu cheese dressing. The husband had wings and I had the steak rice bowl. Everything came out quick and was very tasty.

Having visited during a Yelp event (Yelp's French Halloween), I knew I needed to go back, so when a friend came back into town, I figured this would be the perfect spot to enjoy dinner and conversation with him.  I was right!  I made a reservation on line, drove the distance and arrived a few minutes before my scheduled time. My friend was a bit challenged by the traffic on the interstate - but it was a Friday in Down Town Tampa, so go figure. However, once he arrived, we were sat at a lovely table in the back of the place, and given our menus. Our waitress explained the specials - that aren't on the menus and we were given time to peruse our selections.   When she came back, we made our decisions, me the waygu beef burger with the truffle oil fries and my friend the table side scallops with the ragout of vegetables and a citrus air.  Fresh bread and butter was delivered to the table while we waited for our food.  When it was delivered, we were certainly NOT disappointed at all. The fries were hot and crispy, perfectly seasoned. The burger was juicy and flavourful, absolutely tender and delicious. My friend's scallops were seared to perfection, and the "air" which was a delicate foam added just a hint of citrus-y flavour to the seafood which elevated the essence of the scallops perfectly.  Once we'd eaten our fill of our mains, our waitress offered dessert and since i KNOW Piquant is perfect for that course, we heartily agreed! We chose a dessert, who's name I couldn't hope to pronounce, but the item that was delivered to the table was no less a work of art in chocolate and sugar. It was absolutely decadent. The coffees that we ordered too were perfection.   I will most certainly come back to Piquant, it will be my South Tampa location of choice!

Out of season Haunt, attended due to HauntCon, GREAT show guys! Loved the 4 different haunts. Horror High was my favorite, followed by the First part of the 2nd house, Though I'm not sure of the name of it.  The Zombie was pretty cool and the Fairy Tale still has a lot of work to be done, but their haunt actors, the queue actors all committed and you could tell that they loved what they were doing. LOVED talking to Jinx and the Sliders, they really made the experience wonderful.   The attention to detail on the inside of the houses was Amazing. A few things that stood out were, the Spirit in the library, she was Spot on and her makeup, lighting and motion were all absolutely astounding.  The lead in the Zombie house, She was exactly what you needed her to be. Commanding and imposing, and a redhead! Nothing better than a woman in her full power.   The Funeral parlor's peeling wall paper, and crashed in roof with the tree. Very believable.   This house has a Lot of potential and I hope they continue to bring screams and laughter to the Nashville area. SCREAM ON!

The drive through is always polite, they always say it's "my Pleasure", and are always super efficient.  Yesterday. when I went through, on my way to Sarasota, I ordered an 8pc nugget meal with an extra fry and med coke for mom. What I ended up getting was 2 meals at no additional cost.   It was a nice treat. I was kind of floored by this, honestly, because I didn't pay for it and I didn't discover the mistake until I was down the road a ways, so Thank you for treating my mom to the nuggets.   Only issue with this is, the drive through feeds into itself, when the line backs up  and those who've paid can't get out. So a faulty design.

The Centro Ybor garage is close to all the west end clubs, directly across from Centro Ybor - but 2 blocks down and across the rail road tracks.  It's always well lit, clean and dependable. Most nights, you can park for up to 3 hours for a buck, unless there's something special going on and then you have to pay that fixed rate.    The biggest thing to watch out for is the tight corners when you enter. The way people tend to back up without looking and of course drunk pedestrians who really don't care if they become speed bumps.

We had a different destination in mind tonight. The husbeast and I wanted to go to the new PF Chang's but with an Hour and a half wait, there was NO WAY that was going to happen.  And since I was hell bent on a new place to try, enter Grimaldi's Pizzeria.  Entering, the air was heavily scented in garlic, and that made my tummy rumble with delight. We were ushered to our seat, and were told that our waitress would be right with us, and she was. The menu was explained to us, and it was pretty simple. Everything on the pizzas and calzones was alacart, and portion sizes were generally large, so after ordering a white sangria (Not the best I've had) we settled in to a Caprese Salad and a Large Pizza with Pepperoni and fresh garlic.  The Caprese salad was served quite quickly, with large slabs of fresh tomato, huge leaves of crisp basil and thick slices of mozzarella cheese. So amazingly delicious.  The pizza was cooked in a coal fire oven, a traditional New York thin crust pizza that was crispy, oily and absolutely decadent when bitten into.  There really is nothing like warm oil that drips down your chin while you laugh with your significant other.   Prices weren't terrible, they even tempted us with dessert, as they were having a great special of 3 for $10.  Unfortunately there was just no room, we were full. We will certainly be back to eat here again.

New Eatery in Palm Harbor area, Located in the Fountains Shopping center.  I wasn't sure what to expect, but it was a Friday night, a bit late so we decided to try it.  The menu was posted in the window and I noticed that the had a LOT of sushi selection  - The husbeastie was pleased, and there were other options which made me happy.   Inside the place was very pretty.  The decor was very well done and we were lead to a small booth so that we could peruse the menu.  We ordered our drinks - Iced tea and green tea, which were served quickly.  We started our meal with Goyza and then placed our order for our mains. I opted for the Tempura Chicken - Which came with 6 pieces of chicken, 5 peices of veggies, a salad, soup and rice. The plate had a LOT of food with it and it was tasty. It was some of the lightest tempura I've ever eaten.   The husbeastie had a sushi platter that had 6 pieces of sashimi, a California roll as well as soup and salad. By the way he ate it, I'd say it was good.   The prices were a touch high.. but over all the value was ok.  We'd come back again.

It's a nice Ross, not as ... unorganized as some.  They have a decent selection of clothing, some nice home goods. I can usually find something unusual where ever I go. And this one wasn't any different there.  I ended up walking away with a new dress, some pretty lingerie and of course some jeans. I absolutely love Ross.

It was a roll the dice day, and I wanted some place I've not been before... The pointer landed on Johnny Grits. It was close to home, and that made things Easy.  We made the short drive to Klosterman and to Johnny Grits.   It wasn't terribly busy, and with food this good, I'm Surprised. They're hidden, perhaps that's why, but what ever the reason, the word needs to get out. Granted most days they're only open until 2, but on Thrusday  - Saturday they're open until 8. Get there!  We were seated immediately, and noticed that the place was Clean and fairly large. The staff was happy and did a lot of work to keep busy. No one was idle or just hanging around. Something you see at places that just don't care.   Our Waitress, Renee, was AWESOME. She really seemed to care if we came back in the future. We asked what was good, and she mentioned the Shrimp and Grits.. She RAVED about it. Said that once you had it, you'd come back, you'd crave it.  Well, that sold the Husbeast, and he ordered it with the andoullie sausage.  Me, I went for the chicken and waffles with 100% maple syrup.  Once the order was placed and our coffees were on the table, we didn't wait terribly long.   The food was Beautiful when it was presented.   My chicken was golden brown and the waffle was light and fluffy.. absolutely delightful. It came to life in my mouth. THe husbeast nodded.. he said to me "Yep, She was right,I'm going to crave this.." and so now I'm going to have to go there on Tuesdays when the shrimp and grits is $2 off!    Go and find this little gem, You won't be wasting your time.

One of the bigger stand alone Starbucks I've been in.  Very clean, very neat, and of course, it smelled DELICIOUS. YAY coffee!  Service was good, quick and full of smiles and kindness. Only one small problem, they were out of toilet paper in the women's restroom. I mentioned it and it was taken care of after my vanilla latte was made.

Date night with a friend. It was late 11:30 and Appleby's was Swamped, so we opted to come here. When we were waiting to be seated, I saw the host actually check his watch, wait a moment or two before coming to seat us. He made a point to tell us that the place closed in half an hour, and then proceeded to rush us through our order.    The food was Ok. My salad was tasty, but my date's food as "just Ok". All in all it wasn't a spectacular event, it was JUST ok.

I came here to see my friend perform a Mind Reading act. I'd never been and I'm sad that it wasn't even on my radar until then.. Inside it's dark and moody, but it has a really cool vibe. The lanterns are all different, they have high and low tops, and even outdoor seating. Menus on the table with the note at the top, "Order pub style, at the bar." pretty cool.   There's a heck of a range of food options too! I chose the Goat Tacos and they were delicious. They also had a Raspberry frambrois which was perfectly sweet and sour. Writing this, my mouth waters at the memory.   The show was amazing and Frank was absolutely a show stopper. I will come back!

The husbeast and I wanted to try someplace new for dinner, so we went to what used to be "Pauls" and now it's Gusto D' Amore, a pizza joint with a bar and other food. Stepping in, we thought maybe it was karaoke night, because we heard someone singing pretty flatly. But no, this was the evening's entertainment.  There was an Honest to God Lounge singer, complete with smarmy leisure suit and keyboard. He was singing all our "favorites" from the 60's and 70's but not doing them justice. he wasn't on key , pathetically flat and lacked enthusiasm. I can't blame him for the latter, as no one seemed to care he was there.   The interior of the place was inviting, the food smelled good, so we looked over the menu and placed an order for a starter of Garlic Cheese bread and marinara sauce.  Our main would be a large "Special" Pie ( Peperoni, Sausage, Onions, Mushrooms and green peppers - anchovies by request)    The bread was tasty, but odd, because it appeared there was Mozz & American cheese? There was some garlic, but not a lot of it to flavor the bread, but it was crispy where it counted and the Marinara sauce was tasty.   The pizza was a different story though. The toppings were tasty and fresh. The peperoni was sparse as was the sausage and mushroom but the onions and green peppers were plentiful. And the crust was.. well it was not the worst I've ever had, but it was like cardboard. It was thick and had a flavor almost like a saltine without the light/flakiness.    The service was OK. Our waiter, Hunter was brand new and though he felt like he was stumbling over everything, he really wasn't. He was polite and helpful and very sweet.  We'll come back, to try something OTHER than the pizza, and pray the entertainment ISN'T the same lounge singer.

Needed to stop for gas on my way home from the CYME Event. The WaWa was $0.02 more expensive than the station down the road, but with it being at the cross roads of 301 & MLK that is understandable.   The station was neat and clean and well lit, which is important when you're 2 women traveling alone.  The pumps worked efficiently and then we went inside to get coffee. They have easy kiosks to order at, and once the order is placed, you wait.. It doesn't take long for your order to come up either.  Then you pay at the front check out.   Their bathrooms are clean too!

My niece's hair was fading, she needed a new color to put in her once gorgeous blonde hair.    I'm a sucker for that girl so we went to Sallys and she showed me what she needed.  They also had a red, so since it was buy one, get one 50% off, we got her one and myself one that will become my color conditioner to keep my hair it's vibrant shade.  The store's employees were kind and friendly, happy to answer any questions we had.  The store was well stocked and clean looking.

Late night and I've got to grab something on the way home from HOS, sonic is a great stop. With lots and lots of choices for drink combinations. I made the mistake of asking for "Diet" and was told that they have more than 50 options. WOW!  I generally order a Foot long coney with tots and a diet coke. it's a reasonable order for under $10. The service is fine, never rushed or hurried, Sometimes it's slow but on a Saturday night, that's what I've come to expect.

Came here to sing Karaoke with friends. Nice destination, relatively clean if a bit smoky. It's certainly not as smokey as other locations I've been to.  A friend of mine got a beer, and he was given a token for another beer, he wasn't sure what it meant so he had to ask.. :)   Loved it, Would certainly come back.

Wow! This is my final review for 2014, and this brings my tally to 765, I can hardly believe that, and I'm ending the year on a high note!  I decided that lunch today was going to be at a place that I've heard people talk about, so after finding out that it was only minutes away from Tj Maxx, I headed to the local and walked right in. There was no line, only one lovely young lady writing "Happy New Year" on the To-Go sacks as she welcomed me to the store.   She asked if I knew what I wanted, or if I needed a few minutes. It was my first visit, so I said it would be a moment as familiarized myself with the menu.  First thing I notice is that their menu is similar to Five Guys, but their quality is STEPS above. I Ordered what I would normally get, a burger, with provolone, bacon, grilled onion & grilled mushroom, lettuce & A1 sauce on the side, an order of fries (Which is 1/2 pound of real potato) and a fountain drink.   I was given a number, shown where the fountain was and made my way to a seat.  They use real silverware, plastic glasses and real plates. Their teas were good, a choice actual brewed Jasmine tea as well as green and another. that I don't recall, but the Jasmine was Delicious!  When the burger was delivered, it looked fantasitc, it was cooked perfectly and so were the fries.  A few minutes into my meal, the Manager came over to see how I was, he asked how I found out about the place, I told him Yelp, and he called the Owner over, who happened to be visiting!  The owner was happy that it was working in his favour. He said that he found that most Yelpers were more discriminating than usual food critics. ;) As an elite, I think that's true, that and we give our true opinion, it's not bought and paid for.   I'll certainly come back to this place!

Homemade ice cream is always yummy on a warm spring day. And they always have some of the best flavors out there.  Hand made waffle cones, dipped key lime pops, frozen bananas on sticks make for decadent treats. The main drawback is the line. There is -always- a line for this shop, and even with 3 people dishing out the goodness, it still seems to take forever.  ***a note to those with nut allergies. Make them aware, so they can change their scoops.  ***

Geek God KEVIN SMITH came to town and we got seats.  I was stoked because This is something that the Husband and I could do together! They weren't going to seat until 7, but we arrived at 6:45 and we were seated right away, with AMAZING seats 3 rows from the stage and dang near dead center.    The wait staff was very attentive, they made sure that if we wanted to order something, it was placed, they made sure that if we needed drinks, we got them. Water? Sure thing. Over all the experience was Awesome. And Kevin Smith? In the first 10 minutes of his show, I was CRYING with laughter. The whole night was pretty damned good.

Panera's near Busch Garden is close to work so I can stop in and grab a bite on the way to HOS. It's a good thing too, since I often want something that tastes good and makes me happy.   I find that I prefer their take 2 option vs other fast food. And when I want something made special: ie take off onions or dressing on the side, they're happy to make that accommodation. And they do it without argument.

I stopped in here on the way to somewhere to get my usual, a half & half iced tea.  They got the order right, but I miss the days of $1.00 iced teas.  Nothing exceptional about the service.. it was just ok.

A stop on the Legendary Haunt tour after we visited Eastern State Penn.    Nice and warm with a very friendly vibe. The Cash Bar was utilized by many.   The bathrooms were neat and tidy and the front room was packed by locals. We were in the back room as clips from Terror behind the Walls played in a loop on a wall.

Stopped in to get the beau's phone glass fixed. Didn't take into account that their store would be busy unlike on a monday when most folks would be at work.   We signed in, told that they would text us when they were ready for us and hied off down the plaza for breakfast.  We never received a Text for our appointment, but we did receive a "Your appointment has been cancelled" text.

This is NOT one of my favorite TJ Maxx Stores.    It's nice, don't get me wrong, but they're no where nearly as neat, as organized or as up to date as others in the region.  Their make up, hair care and sundry items is no where near the stock that others have.   The store does have a nice jewelry counter, and i've bought a few costume pieces from them, those make me happy. Finding that one sparkly item that really makes you shine, THAT's a good thing.   I'll come back to see what new things come one, but only every so often.

I was happy to find this Ulta on North Dale Mabry. I'd not been in and was in need of getting new shampoo. Thankfully they carried just what I needed.   These kind of stores are bad for me, because I end up spending too much money there. And this occasion wasn't any different. 3 lipsticks and my shampoo and I was ready to go.   Over all, the store is well stocked, and the service was good.

The food at CB is always good. And it's always fun introducing someone new to "Country" style food.  The only draw back to this experience was that we were in the side dining room, and at the end of the evening, they were hell bent on moving around all the chairs over the stone floor, making an ungodly racket.  It drove me to a horrid headache.

DO NOT GO HERE ON BLACK FRIDAY!  What a nightmare! I had no idea they did the 50% off everything. If I had, I would have saved myself the trouble!    Over all, the prices were pretty damned good, but the store was a nightmare mess. Everyone, and I mean EVERYONE was tearing things apart. The line was a mile long (But it moved quick) and there was almost nothing that I wanted for gifts.  Though I did find myself a nice woolen Pea Coat for a decent price.

The husbeast and I were running on fumes. We;d gotten up early, not eaten and dropped his car off for some much needed work (oil change, tires, et all) and had plans to see the new Mad Max movie at the Veteran's 24 theatre, but now our tummies were growling.    What to do, What to do..   And there it was, sitting where Perkins used to be. Mission Barbecue. So we made a U turn and walked in. The people greeted us with warmth, and since it was our first visit, they explained everything to us without hesitation. the cashier even offered samples of the meat products before we ordered! That was awesome.   Both of us ordered off their Meat Market menu, choosing to make it a combo, by getting a side and a drink with it. We also donated $2 to the Wounded warrior project and got a re-usable cup. If we bring it back in, they'll give us a buck off the next visit.   The food we ordered was pulled pork with green beans and then Pulled pork with brisket (moist-they asked what we wanted) and coleslaw.  The meats were divine. The brisket was perhaps some of the best I've ever eaten. The pulled pork was flavourful too! Their sauces.. 6 of them in total- are a sweeping variety and there are 2 that I like. The Kc Twang and I forget what the other one was. LOL.    One thing that I -really- like about this place is that they have a notice on the door that every day at noon, they ask that every one stands and observes the singing of the National Anthem.  We were there to witness that, and it made my heart swell with patriotic pride to see every person stand, every hand over their hearts and yes, people sang our National anthem.  A moment of unity, it was nice.   They are heavily militiary and that's great! I noticed that the men behind counter, where they were chopping meat, were standing at attention, waiting for orders. I LOVE that they support the Wounded Warrior project. I hope that all the monies donated to the project via them goes directly there.   We will certainly be back.

Last night, I ventured out to The Pub, Tampa Bay because my friends in the Black Velvet Band were playing.  The last time I'd been here, was at a Yelp Event.   I'm glad I came back!  The service was excellent and the food was good. Their Scotch Eggs and the goat cheese dip were both tasty as hell, and of course the Cider was cold and refreshing.    But it was the music that really had me happy. The Irish bodhran drummers and fiddlers all kept perfect time and of course the bawdy toasts were both amusing and sometimes almost blush worthy... ALMOST.  They made me crave Ren Faire .. Spring is coming, I know.

The absolutely best thing about the Holiday Family Restaurant? It's less than a mile from my front door.    The 2nd best thing? The food is great! Some times the service is iffy, kind of like to day, where the waitress was abrupt, we didn't get our bread for the table (which is OK, since I'm on a low carb diet) and she just didn't seem to want to be there, but the food.. is always really damned good.   The prices are REALLY good as well, especially for what you get. It's very much a "Local's" place, where they DO know your name when you come in if you've been more than three times. So stop in and sit a spell. You'll be glad you came.

Large Publix supporting the Moon Lake area.   Located off of SR 52, it's easy in and out with ample parking. The staff is quite friendly and doesn't hesitate to answer questions.   Clean and neat, they were open until 10 the eve of Christmas Eve and it seemed that the store was a ghost town. We came in and got what we needed and a few items more.   Checking out was a breeze. If I'm in the area, I'll certainly stop in.

The last time I was in Ybor this was a different place, now it's a BWW and I can't say it's for the better, but... Bww has good wings, even if their service is mediocre.   We had a large group so we camped out in their "sports room" The TV's were SO loud that it as nigh impossible to hear each other speak. I ended up asking that the volume be turned down because -seriously- WTF.   We had two waiters, one was efficient and fine the other, perhaps a newer guy? was a bit scattered and clearly not very good at his job.  He forgot to get drink orders, he didn't get refills often and when asked for the bill, he didn't get it, I had to ask twice.  Honestly, I prefer a different location of BWW and probalby won't be back.

My friend and fellow Yelper, Lindsey has always spoken highly of this store so the husbeastie and I decided to check it out. I didn't know what to expect, so...   When we walked in, the first thing I noticed was that it smelled like a Pier One.  I love that smell, It smells like imported wood and cloth, like things from other locations around the wood, and that's good.   We started looking around at the decor items and noticed a picture of White llamas with a black llama in the middle, I desperately wanted that picture. Why? I cant even explain but it spoke to me.  I did pick up prayer flags for my massage room.   They had their Halloween things out and some things I'd not seen: Like Jelly Belly Disney Villain series, a lot of Jack Skellington items and the like.  THey had coffee samples at the back and their food selection was quite amazing. I saw hot sauces I'd never seen before! I even got to pick myself up an English Honey Comb chocolate bar for myself. YUM.   Their glass ware section was lovely, though the iridescent glass made me afraid to touch it as it was extremely delicate and not durable.    When it was time to check out, the cashiers were having a conversation amongst themselves, and too busy to look up, so we stood there for a few minutes whilst they chatted. That was perhaps the most annoying part of the trip.  I get it, they're human, it happens, but they need to be aware of what's going on and the people who are in line are their clients.    When we did check out, I was asked if I was a member, I was not, I was asked if I wanted to sign up. Membership is free, so I gave her the information and saved 15% immediately, which was very nice.   Will we come back? Yes.

The Bay Area Renaissance Festival has been one of my go-to events since I was a young thing. The first time I attended it I was but a tender 16 years old. Fast forward a half a lifetime and i still go every year.   It's true, I used to work the event, but ever since Howl-O-Scream came along, I had to choose between them, October wins out.    What can I say about an event that offers you multiple venues of entertainment including such favorites as the Demzarrah Gypsies, The Badwy boys, The Tortuga twins, Emrys Fleet; rat catcher, Washing Well Wenches, and many others.  There are rides offered to people of all ages, games of skill and shopping galore! It truly is something to behold.   Each weekend is a themed weekend and holds something unique. This weekend was Fiesta weekend as well as Easter. To celebrate this, they held a Latino Market in Piper's Valley, which focused on the products and foods of the Latin Culture.  They held a taco and burrito eating contest which was sponsored by Chipolte.   For Easter, there was an Easter egg hunt in the children's realm, where the Easter bunny was going to appear (I saw him!) and would pose for photos. And there was also King Henry's brunch. For an additional $15.00 in addition to your admission (if you think about individual food costs, this is a BARGAIN!) you got an all you can eat buffet of an amazing array of food specifically catered to this event. It included: Pasta salad, fruit salad, roasted root vegetables, ham, fried chicken, quiche, mac & cheese, scrambled eggs, biscuits & gravy, as well as things I can't remember.  There were desserts galore! Red Velvet cup cakes, eclairs, 7 layer bars.. the list goes on. All in all, it was well worth the price, as we didn't have to eat later in the day. Oh, and I forgot to mention. If you were over 21, you got 2 mimosas! They were AMAZING!  While I didn't wait for the pub sing, the end of the day came early for me, about 4pm after joining in with the International Wenches Guild 21 in a wenching. Nothing could have made my day better.   This event is by far one of the highlights of my year!

It had been a beautiful sunny day, so what better thing to do than to take my visitor to the closest beach to the house.   We drove to Fred Howard, but sadly, what had been a sunny day suddenly became cloaked in a deep sea fog, and you couldn't see much of anything.   For a flat $5 fee, we were able to park and enjoy the beach for the full 20 minutes we stayed there, (we passed the parking pass along to someone who was confused by the pay meter) and marveled at how clean and neat the space was.

I used to come to Pit Boss ages ago. It was my Dad's favorite place in the world. Since I was craving MEAT, I took my mom out for food. When we got there, the scent of roasting meat over whelmed us  (in a good way) and we made our way inside to the almost empty dining room.  We were told by the waitress (Who was eating her own lunch ) to sit where ever we liked, so we did.   Mom ordered the Pitboss special - a pulled pork sandwich, 2 sides and a drink ($8.99) and I ordered a full pound of ribs dinner (+2 sides and bread) with an iced tea.  We didn't need any appetizers and we reminisced while we waited for the food.   When it came, the serving sizes were pretty large. Mom and I both ended up taking things home. I adore their potato salad, but their green beans were pretty weak.  Their ribs were amazing.

Stopped in on a quiet afternoon, no one was there but the staff when we walked in.  They were very courteous and friendly. We were seated and given the menus to peruse.  A few minutes later, our waitress came to take our drink orders, I ordered a coke and the husbeast ordered a diet.   When she returned, the husbeast ordered a cup of their chili and a big boy burger with frisch's sauce and fries. I ordered a coney, no onions and chili cheese fries.  The food didn't take any time to get to us at all, it was ready very quickly, the chili arrived first and the hubby kept asking what was missing,  I had to tell him it was the beans.   The mains that arrived were delicious, my hot dog was in a casing so it had that wonderful, crisp SNAP that is so satisfying, and the chili cheese fries were so good, that chili was rich and unctious.  The husbeast really enjoyed his big burger. He almost couldn't finish his meal which is highly unusual for him

I've had better, I've had worse.  When we sat at the booth, we noticed that the bread plates were not clean. They were smeared with -something-.  When this was pointed out to our server, she apologized and took them away, but never returned with new, clean ones.   We ordered starters of French Onion soup, and while it was the classic recipe, it was lacking -something-.  The vegetables on my plate were so very over done, and the steak, while it was cooked to medium rare, it just wasn't flavorful.   The husband's burger was good, he said. He said that it was perfect and to his liking.

Stopped here before we went to the CYME event.  It is located right across the street from the CQ location.  Easy in, easy out off the road, so that was nice.    We placed our order and then walked inside to get our drink from the coke 100 machine and sat down to avoid the super 'skeeters.  Our food came out quickly but I noticed that my order was not correct. *sigh* I asked that there be no cilantro, since it tastes like soap to me.  However, there was cilantro through out my main dinner. The sides were great though, the rice and the beans had great flavour.   All in all, It was a good visit and I am a fan of the brand.

One of the smoothest TSA visits I've had at TIA. They were prompt, organized and friendly. Which you usually can't say about the TSA.  They seemed to be happy to be there and very eager to help everyone through as quickly as possible.

Stopped in for lunch one afternoon and I was blown away.   First of all, it smells like heaven when you walk inside. Garlic and tomatoes, so much YUM!  I was seated immediately, and my order was taken.  I perused the menu and opted for a calzone. I really had no idea what I was getting into.  The calzone was HUGE. I mean REALLY huge.  I ordered a Ham and cheese calzone. it took maybe 20 minutes to make. When it came out, it was piping hot, fragrant with garlic butter and looked to be half the size of a large crust. Like I said, huge.   And it was stuffed! When I cut into it, it ooze all the good stuff out. It was tasty too. But I could only eat 1/4 of it So most of it went home to the husbeastie who got to eat that for the next day or two.   I'll be back.

The beau likes muscle cars. I can't blame him, I like them too.   He asked me to stop at Exotic Motorcars so he could look at a few they have on the lot as a possible replacement vehicle in the near future.   It was hotter than blazes on this afternoon, and we spent a few minutes unmolested on the lot looking over a few nice looking cars.  The doors were locked, they had some body damage, but they were mostly recent years and the papers said they had low milage.   When we hit the main lot, we were approached by one of the sales men, he asked what we were looking for, the beau said basically just looking, dreaming, but still gave him a little info, and the gentleman showed us to a few nice things on the lot.     After a while, he left and went back inside and we continued to peruse the vehicles, they had a few classics on the lot as well as some really exotic vehicles, that looked absolutely gorgeous, but not what we wanted.   My guy did see one that he had an interest in, so we went inside where we saw the REALLY high end vehicles.   We got the car fax without issue, the price and milage on the car and even the keys to see what the car sounded like. We did not take a test drive.  Our salesperson was friendly and gregarious, never pushy.   Wether or not we come back to actually purchase the vehicle, this is a used car lot. It is exactly what you would expect. The cars are varied and may be here a day or a lot longer.

Popped in here and the Palms for a fund raiser for a friend of mine. Peabody's catered the event and provided some delicious wings and burgers for us. I'm happy to report that we raised $2500 for our friend.   Thanks Peabodys & the Palms.

I always walk by this shop and have never wandered in. Today I changed that. I was honestly surprised to see that when you walk in, they're carrying "upscale" home goods. And by home goods, I mean bath and body lotions. They're not a product I'm familiar with, so I can't attest to what the quality is.   Inside the store, they have a lot of quality merchandise. Some lovely collections of antiques, that are MOSTLY priced reasonably.  Some were a bit outrageous, but for the most part, things were decently. I saw a gorgeous tea set that was $48.00 for all the pieces, and a stunning collection of cobalt glass. Each room is laid out in an easy to figure out way, so you can find what you need without too much help.

Came for the Queen of the Night competition, the place was PACKED.  People were rowdy, they didn't want to listen to the judges when they said move back, move over and give them space.  The place is small, but the lay out is good. The entertainment was excellent. For most of these being unseasoned Queens, all I can say is Tampa has a lot of talent. I was really impressed with those who traveled from Orlando and Ft. Meyers too!   The sound System and light show seem to be damned good, so I'm guessing on a not so crowded night, Liquid might be enjoyable. But standing in one place, being jostled around by a backpack wearing 20 something, not my idea of fun.

My father in law was in town so we all met up down here for dinner and to celebrate my husband's birthday a few days early.  We were seated and shared an appetizer of humus which was absolutely decadent. Some of the Humus that I've ever had.   I'm not sure where they get their bread, but it had the fluffiest, most light and delicious interior, it was addictive. I could have eaten a full loaf myself, and that isn't an exaggeration.   For dinner the husband had the meatloaf special, which he said tasted amazing. I had the chicken breast which were absolutely delicious. They were flavored perfectly and cooked just right. Everything was wonderful.   Our service was fantastic and attentive, I'm sorry I didn't get her name but she was awesome!

This afternoon, while in Safety Harbor running errands, I decided to spin Yelp and come up with a new destination for lunch. Whistle Stop is where it landed.  I've been here before, But I guess I never wrote it up, My bad..  With the sky heavy with rain, I went in and sat on the porch near the rail, the service was Immediate: What did I want to drink? (Unsweet Iced tea) did I have any questions? I was still perusing the menu.  While the waitress went away to get my drink, I took a moment to look at the over the menu and never got past the Small Plates menu. They have Buffalo Cauliflower & Fancy Fried Green Tomatoes!  So that's what I got.   It came out Super quick, The breading on the Cauliflower was thicker than I'd have liked but they were delicious! As for the Fried Green Tomatoes, I'm used to a sauce of some kind served with mine, and these came with none. They were tasty, but there wasn't enough of the goat cheese to make the up grade in price.   I ended up passing my Fried Green Tomatoes on to a lovely couple who asked me about them. I'd only eaten two and asked them if they'd like them, they said they would. When I'd finished the cauliflower, I ordered dessert, they didn't have my first choice, but they did have Key Lime pie. It may not have been pretty, but it tasted great!

Everyone gives the TSA Hell, but You know what? If you do what they ask, if you get the things out of your bag and onto the belt as you're supposed to, and you actually just smile it goes a lot faster.   I sometimes get to get patted down due to my underwires, but other than that, I don't usually have an issue. They're pretty efficient.

Popped in today to find my husband a suit Jacket for a wedding he's going to in San Fran. I was happy to find that the suit jackets were on sale for $59. We also found dress shirts for $12.40 and a great tie for under $15.00.  With their prompting, I down loaded the Macy's ap, and got an additional 20% off my purchase.

Grabbed a quick dinner with my husband. Nothing amazing, but the food is always quick, the service is always good, and they always make sure that your glass is full of your drink.  Prices are reasonable, and that's probably what's the best about it.

I had a craving, so I opted to pop into one of my pre-diet favorites, Tijuana Flats.   They've re-vamped the inside, new paint a bit of a different look on the hot bar, but over all it's still the same.. The food is still tasty, made to order and served quickly.  The girls who take your order come around and do refills on the sodas too.    Since the last time I was in, they've expanded their dessert menu.  The food was tasty, the service was quick, If I could eat here more than once a year, I'd be back sooner than later.

Friday evening birthday celebration with friends. We had a party of eight and our table was up front and in the center of things.  Our waitress (I didn't get her name) was attentive and very knowledgble of EVERYTHING. Any question we had, she didn't hesitate to answer anything.   I was happy to have checked in on my YELP ap because I scored a free Appetizer (or sushi roll value of $14 or less) so I chose the Chicken Satay. It was well done and the cabbage salad beneath was amazing. The dressing was complex and very, very tasty, though the chicken was thicker than I'm used to having for Satay cuts.   My entree was their pork loin, served with bok choy and mashed potatoes, and a sauce. I'd asked for the sauce on the side which they were very happy to do.  The bok choy was light and flavourful, the potatoes were a bit on the thick side but very tasty and the pork was seasoned perfectly. There was more than enough for me to eat on for the meal and to take home.   It was a lovely location but sadly a bit too loud for our table set up. I wasn't able to comiserate with everyone, and that's on us - since we chose to sit the way we did. But all in all it was an excellent experience.
