I -finally- got to enjoy Ulele on my own (well, with the Husbeastie, that is)! I was pleased to be able to visit on a sunny afternoon, so that I could sit outside and enjoy the sun and breeze, and watch the river.   The service was delightful, our glasses never went empty, and the husband was excited to get to try some of the hand crafted beer that they make on sight.. he opted for the honeymoon beer, flavoured with local strawberries. He said he didn't taste the fruityness of it, but that it was tasty none the less.   We started our meal with the chicken lollipops and they were just as flavourful as I remember them being. A hint of spice in the sauce that made them sing on the tongue. The slaw that they nested on was made of apples, cabbage and other thinly sliced vegetables, which added to the crunch and made it heavenly!  Our mains were very diversive: I chose the steak and since it was lunch it was only $15 for an 8 oz portion, atop a large mound cheddar mashed potatoes and the vegetable of the day (grilled asparagus) and a garnish of popcorn (I admit, I was confused) The meat was absolutely delicious, tender and grilled to perfection. The seasoning was so good! The potatoes were decadent, buttery and cheesy and NOM! I was slightly disappointed in the serving of the asparagus as I was given three thin spears, and Asparagus is one of my favorite veggies. (sad)  The husband ordered a Chicken corn salad with a lime jalapeno dressing. The corn was straight off the cob, and apparently had been grilled right on it as well. The chicken was juicy and tender, and the dressing was the right amount of tart, but there was very little jalapeno kiss.  He devoured it any way.. loved it.  While we were dining, we noticed the couple next to us getting dessert, a mounded serving of something, we asked the waiter what it was: Candied Duck Maple bacon fried ice cream. That got us wondering.. and so we decided to try it. Our serving was truly epic, it was HUGE, and surrounded by a moat of cream Anglaise. It was DELICIOUS. I admit the flavor of the duck bacon in the ice cream was a bit of a surprise, but it was a welcome one. We did not lick the bowl clean, like the people next to us, but we came close. Oh boy did we come close.   Oh and as for the pop corn garnish: Apparently the local indian tribe are the ones that figured out that if you add heat to dried corn kernels, you get pop corn. That explains -everything-!

Really nice Marshall's out in the Trinity area of New Port Richey. Clean and well maintained, even if their Loss Prevention people are a bit over zealous. I found myself being shadowed even though the only thing i was guilty of was opening a light package to make sure the product was inside. It wasn't. I found the missing product in the bin and placed it INSIDE the package it'd been removed from.    They have a huge selection of gift items, a lot of nifty little nick knacks, and what have yous. I like the store, but some of their personell are just a bit out of line.

I could have SWORN I wrote a review for this theatre long ago. I guess not.  *shrug* So I get to write one now. I really didn't think it'd been that long since I'd been to Vets 24 theatres, I guess it has.   My beau and I stopped here to see a movie, Suspira. We're both fans of horror and suspense and this had a good review. It was a remake and that's fine. I won't give anything away, but this was such a 1970's Art house, foreign horror movie. It was good, but not like you're used to. Go see it.   Anyway, we were in one of the smaller theatres, they still had the leather recliners and that made the experience SO much better than the old time  theater seats which were ok (and still in many AMC's in the area). The Concession's area is nice and clean and the employees are quite warm and friendly.   The restrooms on the lower number side was large and clean, easily accessible to everyone.   This is one of the better theaters in Tampa Bay

I've come here twice now. Once for a manicure and once for a pedicure. The manicure was awesome, but the pedicure.. that was a bit.. lacking.   The manicure was quick and professional. but the pedicure, the gentleman didn't speak much english, according to their sign, water or soda is to be offered, and it wasn't. I have tiny toenails, one nail wasn't even polished.  I have another salon.. and they manage to polish them all.. So .. what can I say?

On my way home from getting my hair done, I stopped in VidaCann, as this was where one of my Budtender's at another place said he shopped.   The shop is small, non descript on the outside, with ample parking.  They have curbside pick up labled well and a spot just for that.  Inside, it's clean and neat, and smells of really nice flower.  They took my card and made a profile for me and then let me inside.   My Lady Budtender, with the crown royal mask was awesome. She answered all my questions, let me know about her favorites and pointed me to a few strains I might like due to my own needs. They have a fantastic first time buyer discount of $55 of, so I was able to buy a bit more than I expected.   I purchased Some RSO (Haven't tried it yet), Alaska from their Isreali partner and the King Dosi, all vapes, and I'm incredibly happy. Alaska is as I was told it would be, a nice Sativa dominant hybrid and the King Dosi is a lovely indica. I can't wait to try the RSO, but haven't ventured to that just yet.   I know I'll be back, but I only get to tampa infrequently since the days of Covid are upon us.

I LOVE book stores, I especially love old book stores or used book stores. I'd never been here and this was a place my beau wanted to share with me, I'm so glad he did.   The Wilson's book store is an absolute delight. They have a large Games/Comics section, a lovely New Age/Metaphisical selection and a great mystery selection, so I was a happy camper. I also found a kindness rock tucked in on her shelves!   I know that I'll be back, because i'm a hard core librophile and I liked her ghosts.

I knew it was in St. Pete, and I love the glass itself, so I took myself to see the collection. I was NOT upset by this turn of events.  It was on a Friday during the afternoon, so it wasn't busy, and I didn't have to share much of my time with anyone else.   The pieces and the lighting are all fantastic. I loved how the pieces were set up and the stories they told.  The large display in the one room was simply so beautifully staged that it was breathtaking.  I spent an hour just taking photos of my own.   The video of the process and watching them create the pieces was pretty Amazing. I LOVED that.   I totally would come back and visit the collection once more.

We stopped here after having driven home from Orlando.  We were hungry. The place looked good.   Once we were seated, it took a little while for the waitress to come and get our drink orders and even when we placed them, then edited them to add another drink, she didn't get it correct, and it took three times as long to get that 2nd drink.  When she was asked about it, she actually snapped at me "It's coming." in a sharp tone.    The food was good, really tasty. We ordered fajitas for two, adding in the shrimp. They were well proportioned on the meat but skimpy on the veggies, which was kinda sad as those are usually the cheapest ingredient.  Ah well.   The best thing on the meal was the Cilantro Ranch creama you get with your tortillas! That stuff was delicious.   Will I return? Probably not. I mean the food was good, but the service was either really harried or sniping at each other in front of the patrons.  My boyfriend caught the brunt of two wait persons grousing at each other at the bar while he waited for me to come out of the rest rooms. That's just not something you do in front of paying customers.

Nice little state park that is located just off of US 19 that has access to hiking trails and walking paths. During the season of Covid, the kayak/canoe rental is not operational. There is a lot to do here: Birdwatching, hiking, Boating, fishing, picknicking and wildlife watching.   There is no net fishing and no scuba diving.

In my travels, I often shop (No! You don't say!) and Target is one of my favorite shops to stop at.  This Target is located at the corner of 275 & Dale Mabry amid a lot of annoying traffic construction, which makes it difficult to get into and sometimes out of.  That being said, the store itself is rather nice. It's a mid format, meaning NOT a super Target but a store that has a cold goods and some fresh foods. It has a good clothing and hardware, as well as pharmacy and everything else.   They have a large selection of everything you'd expect at a target. I love their covered parking too!

I was excited to try Sacred Floats. I've heard about it in passing, so when a friend of mine got a couple's float through Groupon and invited me to come with, I jumped at the chance.   I'm acquainted with things in the Woo range, and this is most certainly there. The comfortable space of the reception area/sales floor is made more so by the warm energy of the varied crystals and jewelry up for sale. The small oxygen bar sits off to the side of the baroque red plush sofa.  Once we signed in, we were shown the bathroom/shower and instructed that when it was time, we'd come in and shower without soap. make sure to remove all oils on our skin. Then we'd go back to the individual pods, insert ear plugs and get in, closing the doors behind us.  Seemed easy.   We were shown the pods, these were rectangular, about 4.5' high, the same width, and 6'long, draped with a mandala. A little table to hold your personal items and a little box that holds the individually packaged earplug sets.  In one corner of the room was an infrared sauna that had jaunty lights - this is their sauna and light therapy offering.  Our host left and we proceeded to follow his directions, each of us careful to take a towel with us - One thing to note, the floors just outside of the shower, though there is an anti-slip pad, just beyond that, is very slippery, watch your step.   We each chose our pods and began our journeys. Here's what you need to know: The pods are filled with a water/Epsom salt /hydrogen peroxide solution. Some people may have issues with it, so keep this in mind please.  The water is comfortable upon getting in, it feels just above skin temperature, and as you settle in, you lose the difference between air and water. The air around you is close and warm as you slow your breathing and settle, letting yourself relax.  It is dark.. completely dark.  If you are claustrophobic, this might not work.  And with ear plugs in, all you have to focus on is your thoughts, your breath and your heartbeat.  It is very womb like.   My friend M, she said she fell asleep. I did not, but I did relax greatly. My body seemed to lengthen, to stretch. My shoulder which has been aching for a dog's age is feeling much better than it has. I did not have a spiritual experience, but I did have very clear thoughts.   When our time was up, our host came in and knocked on our pods and we got out slowly.  Keep in mind, you're covered with salt infused water, you will see this as soon as you hit the air.. since my friend was taking her shower first, the salt began to dry on me, which meant it began to itch.  Be thorough in rinsing your skin, don't forget your ears, you'll find salt in the oddest places.  If you want to, bring conditioner, soap and shampoo is provided (and they smell really nice!)   All in all a really nice experience, I would do this again in a heartbeat.

I only found this spot because I was early to my hair appointment. I'm glad I was, because, dear lord their bowls are AMAZING. They are the perfect refresher on a hot Florida summer day.    Their service has always been wonderful, and the swing is a great place to take Social Media photos and tag your friends.   I'n going to visit here again soon, I just need another bowl!

I came to Dysfunctional Grace Arts to take a class on making horns. I left with an appreciation for all their neat things.   They have skulls, jewlery, taxidermy and everything in between. Do you need a dental chair for your haunted house? Perhaps you need a Skeleton for your medical practice. Or maybe you're making a unique piece of art and you need something that you just don't know yet. You'll find it here.  The shop has a flair to it that will give some people the creeps. Me? I could live here. I really do need to come back.

What a great addition to the Oldsmar area! LePeep is a stand out!   My guys and I went there the other day for brunch, and what we saw and experienced made sure that we will be repeat visitors.   It's covid season, every person needs to wear a mask, every table is equipped with hand sanitizer, the menus are disposable, the staff keeps social distance from your table and they also wear a mask.   The menu was nicely laid out, it's the first eatery ice seen to offer breakfast appetizers. The churro french toast sounded amazing. Each of us opted for something different. There was an eggs benedict, a Spicy Hamburger and finally the avocado toast.   Each entree was about $10.00, give or take. The serving sizes were large but not grandiose, I was full but not stuffed. Each plate came with "something extra"  wether it was spiced apples, fruit salad or a jalapeno pepper.  You most definitely got value for your money spent.

I stopped in here with my niece, we had gone on a girls day out and ended up in Spring Hill.  Both of us were hungry so Rocco's was a natural stop.   Upon entering, I swear both of our stomachs growled in unison, we both felt our mouths watering, it smelled THAT good.  We were sat, and our waitress took our drink orders, both of us went for Diet Pepsi.   We placed a simple order, a Large Cheese Pizza.  ($12, is very reasonable for a large pizza)  I watched it be made, put in the oven and taken out, it came out in less than 10 minutes and was delivered to our table piping hot and delicious.   It was REALLY good pizza.  If I lived close by, I'd come agian and again.

For a Target, this store left me a bit cold. I was looking for art to put up on the walls at my Mom's house and we opted to go to this location... What a bad decision. Apparently this is the redheaded step child of the chain as they had less than no selection.   We will not be returning to pick up anything else.  *shrug*  It is clean, it is a nice store, but they are not stocked. They are apparently not a super target, but a mid chain.

I don't think I've ever had a service state a time window and actually show up at the start of that window.   Theses guys did. They were masked, they were thorough and they were very professional.  They took care of snaking my drains and repairing a broken out door faucet and their price was reasonable to me.    I would totally have them out again and recommend them without hesitation.

Unassuming location off of US 19 in New Port Richey. The in/out efficacy isn't the best because the lot is small in front and in back it expands, but a lot of folks don't like to use it.    Inside, the waiting area is currently set up for Covid, so seats are 6 feet apart, no more than 4 people are aloud to wait inside after checking in. Once you're called back, the room is smallish, but there has to be more since the space is large around them.  It is done all in dark wood and the bud tenders, there seemed to be six of them, are enthusiastic and friendly.   Everyone working is actually working together so feel free to ask a question. If your budtender doesn't have the answer, someone else in the room does.  They're happy to help you out, to sign you up for their loyalty program and get your first time visit discount.    The merchandise is good quality (What do I know? I'm new to this.) the prices seem to be about average and I left happy.   I know I'll be back.

WOW! Talk about a warehouse store. This was a nice stop after being down at the beach. My Paramour needed to pick up his currents and I agreed to go along for the ride.    I was impressed with the selection of items. They literally have -everything- comic related. They even have comics! A huge selection of collectibles and even a small selection of coloring books that weren't over in the "kids" section.   It was a fun visit, I'd do it again!

Went to PH in Dunedin on a fluke. Id driven by it so many times and had no idea that it finally opened.   There was no wait to be seated when we came in, which was late on a Sunday evening.  The place smelled SO GOOD.  We got to sit near the dessert case and that just had me drooling.   My Guy got himself the Salmon Risotto and I got the 6oz Fillet, with sides of fried corn fritters and Brussel Sprouts. Let me just say that those sprouts HAUNT me, they were So good. I will order them ALL the time.  The steak was nicely seasoned, with a heap of garlic butter on top. The corn cakes were sweet and tasty.   The Salmon Risotto was delicious. He ate All the fish and some of the risotto due to muscle building.    We ended up bringing home a cookie and a Chocolate Peanut butter Mousse pie home which was to die for.  I will come back. The service was wonderful, the food was delicious and the scenery was Great.  This is an awesome new place to visit with friends.

My nails desperately needed being done, I'd just visited Curv Exchange next door and wandered into Wanderlust Nail Spa.  Immediately, I was asked to sit down, and the Owner took a moment out of the manicure she was currently doing (with permission) to set my nails to soak with remover.   I watched her do the other woman's nails and was quite impressed. She did a matte nude coffin nail that was to die for. When she got to me, she was super friendly and really personable. We picked out a color I liked, A rich sparkly blue, and she set to work.   She's really good at what she does, my nails look fantastic! I can tell you that I'll be back to have them done again.

This is one of the only places I know that I can count on to get Clove cigars. They are reasonably priced, and right behind the cash register. They have several varieties of flavours, whether it's menthol, lights, vanilla, cherry or even your standard Blacks, you can find your Clove's here.   They also have an impressive walk in cigar humidor, different hookahs and other smoking periphenalia. Stop by and give this place some love.

Here's to making memories.   My beau took me here before I left for my trip to Scotland, unfortunately on that journey, my phone decided to die. I mean literally give up the ghost, never to be resurected.. I'm sad too, because on that trip I had the most delightful dessert, and now I don't have the picture I took.  Ah well..   Anyway, On both visits, I've enjoyed their "Breakfast all day" sandwich, 2 eggs, cheddar and bacon (Or sausage), on a croissant with coleslaw.  It's so, so, SO good!  I've also ordered latte's both flavoured and unflavoured, and the barista is really good, she even didn't over heat the coffee which takes skill, too many scald the milk.   This will be my favoured brunch spot with Mr.P from now on.
Stopped for a quick pick up of Nuggets and tea, brought some home to the hubs as well.  Double drive through, with absolutely no issues what so ever.

I stopped here on the day Hurricane Michael was blowing through.  It was a lovely rainy afternoon and I thought I should go see how the water was being affected. I'm odd like that.   I've been near this beach park more times than not, but I've never actually gotten out to see what it's like.  I was pleasantly surprised. It's quite large, a big area for boats is available so you can put in and get out of the water.    There are multiple areas for picnicking and swimming.  There's even an old Spanish well and a Florida Indian Mound.  Lots of history here along with beautiful river views.  A perfect place to walk around and see what's there. Even on a rainy afternoon.

The husbeast had never been to a Culvers and since this one was on our way, We stopped in.  We both opted for a double butter burger with bacon, our sides were different, He wanted crinkle fries and I wanted cheese curds. The best of both worlds...   The food was good, the service to the table was pretty awesome. Honestly, I love that everything is fresh and people seem happy in the store. There doesn't seem to be a down face in the joint.  And yes, HE ate every scrap of food given. Me, I don't ahve that appetite, but both of us left with full bellies.  He even tried the cheese curds and deemed them better than his fries!  ( They're my favorite!)

I visited here because an orginazation I belong to was having a get together. It was a bright, but chilly autumn afternoon, and the park was full of people. We had shelter #9, and the view was absolutely gorgeous.   We took full advantage of the amenities the park had to offer: The picnic tables, the parking, the grills and the restrooms.  Our kids had fun at the swings and in the large fields.    This is an absolute treasure to the town of Safety Harbor, Fl. I'm glad I've been introduced, I'll certainly be coming back.

I should NEVER be allowed in a Dollar Tree again.   Let me tell you a story. LONG ago, I used to get $10 to spend at Dollar tree, this was when I was worried about bouncing checks and lived paycheck to Pay check. and that $10 brought me so much joy, because I could buy myself and anyone else I needed to, a great little surprise, or I could get an eyeliner or lipstick, etc...  Those days are gone, but the feeling of Euphoria I get when I walk into a Dollar Tree hasn't diminished. I STILL like to bargain shop and I LOVE a great deal. So today, when I saw this new Dollar ttree on Alt 19, and I knew I needed a few things for my up coming trip, I decided to stop.   This store is a stand alone and it's LARGE. I think it was a family dollar before, because it has LOTS of space inside. It has the usual suspects, the housewares, the cards, the stationary, etc but it also had a lot of name brand things: Clearquil, Excedrin, Vicks Vapo-rub, And this really made me happy.  The quality of the items in the Dollar tree has really gone up.   Today, I went in, expecting to spend $20. I ended up spending $$43. Ah well..   And that's why I shouldn't be allowed in a Dollar tree any more.

I've lived in the area forever, and B-21 has been a staple that I've never gone into until recently. COLOR ME IMPRESSED.   The store is HUGE.  I mean REALLY Large, and it doesn't smell like liquor stores usually do. It was clean, the folks working there were very helpful, although they didn't carry the vodka I wanted. They did have a glorious selection of every other type of liquor.   I'm not a wine drinker but there was a nice selection here, along with other spirits and snacks. You can bet that i'll be back at another time.

Do you quilt? Do you know someone who does? Have them come here. This is one beautiful store, filled with quality fabric, filled with wonderful associates and some of the most state of the art quitling machines I've ever seen   When I was there, we saw a group from the Villages visiting, apparently they were part of a shop hop and going all over the state visiting many different shops. Pretty cool concept.   This store had some of the most beautiful fabric I've ever seen, especially the ombre rainbow up front under the register.    The staff is very accommodating, their store has custom ceilings and lighting to make your shoping experience that much better.

My Home Town theme park. What's not to love? You've got a world class zoo, you've got excellent song and dance show. You've got killer rides like Sheikra, Cheetah Hunt and Montu.. All of this and then you've got the special events that they have all year round: Musica Latina, Bands, Brews and BBQ, Summer Nights & Kinetics and of course Howl-O-Scream.  There's nothing like this park in the world. I LOVE IT!

Arrived here about 2 hours before my flight. It was around 1 pm on Sunday afternoon.  I took one of the last seats available. I noticed the woman next to me was sitting there with a menu but nothing else. She said she'd been there for 10 minutes already and wondered if she should go to the bar to order. She tried. She was told by a very curt female wait person that she'd be right there.   I start timing.. 10 minutes later and there's still nothing.  An older, heavier set guy comes out of the back and starts telling people to do things.  Again, the girl next to me goes to the bar to try to order, the guy over hears and tells one of his staff to go and take the order... and notes I don't have a menu, he tells the barstaff to give me one. A patron ends up giving me one.   The guy comes over and offers us the apology that it's shift change and foot ball and apparently everything goes to hell right about then.  Just then, the waiter who doesn't even smile or even look interested in taking our order does just that. First hers, then mine. The food comes out in less than 2 minutes - which is why it's a 2 star vs a 1, because the food was super fast and good.   We waited - after we were finished - for our checks too... and waited, when it finally came I aid my bill with 2 twenties, my total a little over $22. the waiter asked if I wanted change. YES. Nothing here deserves a nearly 100% tip.   TLDR: Slow, unenthusiastic, unfriendly service.  Good food. The fries were amazing with cheese sauce.

I visited a friend here today, and was quite happy with the set up.  Their 2 bedroom apartment is fairly large, with 2 bathrooms and a large living area and kitchen. I understand that the rent is ok too.   Me? I'm not a hive person, so I won't live in one,but I'll be honest, they're pretty nice.

Stopped at the McDonalds to picked up a happy meal with a coke no ice. I asked for no toy, and was upgraded in my drink. Which was pretty awesome if you ask me.   The food was served quickly and the order was accurate.
My Beau got his Mustang tinted here, and he is thrilled with it! They did a great job with the windows and did it all in one day.

Nice little smoke shop across from La Quinta in St. Pete.  People said they've had trouble with the staff, but my experience was wholly different. They were friendly and warm, the only time I ever saw anyone be rude was when the clerk had to turn someone away because they forgot their ID and that guest tried to cajole the clerk into letting them stay. Considering that might cost her BIG MONEY, it's understandable that she didn't cave.   They have a nice selection of glass, a nice selection of hand blown and a good selection of kava as well as other things. I picked up a Halloween Hand blown pipe to try out. I was quite happy with my purchases.

If you like Live Music, if you like bars in general, then the Bras Mug might be the perfect venue for you.  A large floor with sparse tables allow for plenty of room to socialize and even dance f that's your thing, while others may find themselves more comfortable hanging back and slinging back drinks.   The accoustics are great, allowing you to hear all the nuances of the music, whether it be death metal or scream-o. In any case, what ever band you hear here is going to be enjoyable to you.   They have a nice, outside patio where you can chill and still hear the music and be able to have a conversation, and have your ears stop ringing. (grin) But the main draw back to me is that smoking is allowed inside. Yes, it's ventilated, but that doesn't stop you from going home smelling like stale smoke.

A friend of mine came into town from Wisconsin.  He didn't ask my input on his hotel reservation, so when He told me where he was staying, I immediately YELPed the Hotel to see what the reviews looked like and my eyes went big. Oh this wasn't good. But I hoped for the best.   Sadly, my best wasn't good enough.   Yes, they've recently done some renovation, but a coat of (poorly slapped on paint) and (misplaced) Memo board in the room do not justify the $55 a night room rate.  The bed is on rolling casters with a Good Will bed cover complete with cigarette hole, but don't worry, the pattern is so damned distracting you won't notice it.    There are 2 lights in the room, one above the door, it's bright and glaring. The other is a standing lamp, over by the wall, close to the bed, but not NEAR the bed. The lamp shade is caked with dust.  There is an old THRIFTed wing back chair that I wouldn't sit in, and the desk has a rickety/rockety chair that looks like it may fall apart at any minute.   The black out curtain has.. it's tie back SEWN to it so it wont be lost. The TV gets 5 channels poorly.  The bathroom has sub par soaps and watered down shampoo, thread bare towels and a bath tub that looks like it hasn't been cleaned in YEARS.  The shower head is set... so low that I'd have to be 5'2 to use it.  I honest was waiting for someone to come in and kill me while I was in there. At least the toilet was clean.   I would ---NOT--- recommend this place to any one or stay here in the future.

Good Food, Great friends and Bingo for Charity, what could be better? Not a lot.   Hamburger Mary's is a good place to hang out if you enjoy Drag Queens, an openly LBGTQ environment and good food. Make sure you try one of the ultra juicy hamburgers, the macaroni balls and of course S'mores for dessert.

The place looks GORGEOUS since the renovation!  I was in the mood for something, but i couldn't put my finger on it.. So  we went for italian and I was able to get my Chicken Bryan. I LOVE that.  We also indulged in a bit of calamari and some delightful peach sangria. GOD was that food good!

The Garden District of NOLA is difficult enough to drive around in, but this Chase bank made it even more difficult with it's convoluted enterance for the drive through. We literally had someone else do the same thing we did, which is go in the wrong enterance , have to pull out and go in the right one. Oy!

On my way home from St. Petersburg, I needed to get gas. I was on E and my car was crying, so I pulled into WaWa because I like how nice and clean they are.  The pumps were nice and neat, the music was at a nice level and the gas was reasonably priced. I was in and out in moments.

Car buying can be a hassle, especially if you're not quite sure what you want or need.   The guys and gals at Toyota are wonderful, especially Mr. Hayes!  My husband and I visited Sun Toyota on Wednesday before Irma hit and we spoke with Pat, looked at a few vehicles and said we'd look around at a few other dealerships and make a decision.   Irma ran us out of town.  When we came back, my husband opted to buy another vehicle, but we decided to replace my car as well.  Pat was AWESOME. We tested a highlander and I was sold.  On Sunday we wrote up the contract and I left with the 3rd new vehicle I've ever had.   The people are friendly, the dealership is clean and over all, I'd do business with them again.

It's a neat & clean Dollar Tree.   I like this one, almost as much as I like the one in Tarpon Springs.   They keep it fairly well organized, they make sure that everything is properly categoried and what have you. It's usually a very nice experience.

I waited too long to eat, I wanted food but not McDonalds. So I drove thru this Arbys. I loke their sandwiches and as usual, this is pretty tasty. The fries were fresh and hot, the sandwich was filled with meat and the diet pepsi was ... well diet pepsi. blerg.

I had been looking for a reason to try Roy's for a while.  And given that tonight was my Husband's birthday, what better reason?  I made a reservation on line, noted anyone in our party's food allergy (we had one with a shellfish allergy) and any important event - the birthday, and got prepared to be WOWed.    We picked up our old girlfriend and arrived on time, it took them just a moment to get our table ready and we were sat.  It was a very nice touch to notice the confetti around the candle on the table, and on the inside of each menu was a "Happy Birthday" note for my husband. I thought that was really sweet!  The service was EXCEPTIONAL! Our waitress, Nicki (?) was very attentive. She took time to explain the cuisine, wrote down the spice on the edmame, and made sure that our iced teas never ran dry.  When we placed our orders she made sure we knew how they were cooked, and if we wanted sauces, etc.    The food... here is where I can't give them more than a 3 star rating.  My husband ordered the Spicy Combination Hot Pot. for $36, the portion size was small, it was not spicy at all and the lobster tail was terribly tough.  My mac nut crusted Mahi tasted... not at all fresh. It wasn't bad, but it was lacking in the usual delicate flavor in favor of a very "fishy" flavor - the whole reason I don't usually eat fish.    We declined dessert, since I'd brought along something to celebrate the birthday with, however, as I mentioned before, the service was incredible, and since we'd ordered cauppucino's for the whole table, our waitress brought a plate with fresh fruit, a scoop of ice cream and 2 flourless chocolate cakes on it, all with "Happy Birthday" scripted on it.  It was both thoughtful and delicious.  The tab for the three of us, 2 apps, 3 mains and 3 cups of coffee turned out to be $145.00 --- Not a terrible price, but for what we got, It could have been better.

Right down the street from all the antique shops you'll find the Tarpon Tavern. Lots of High top tables, a lovely out door seating section, they have a great selection of beers and wines on tap.   The food they offer is a varied selection of delighful choices. My salad was excellent and my husband's burger looked juicy and flavorful!

It's that time of year again, time to celebrate the anniversary of when the Husbeast and I said our vows.  Bern's is where we choose to celebrate this momentous event because the food is beyond par and the service is absolutely incredible.  Though they suggest that you make your reservations at least 72 hours out, I tried a short order reservation on Monday and was able to get a 6pm time slot for Wednesday.  We actually arrived a bit early and were seated at about 5:45 pm in the first of the dining rooms.    If you've never been to Bern's Steak House, the opening decor always reminds me of Disney's Haunted mansion, that kind of rich opulence, that one comes to expect from only the finest of establishments.  The tables are comfortably spaced and though each room can get crowded, they still maintain an air of intimacy.      Our waiter, an older man who's name I didn't catch, was quick to the table with our water and tea. He gave us a few minutes to peruse the menu, but we were pretty well decided before we got there. We were set on getting the 18 ounce, 2 inch thick Del Monaco, cooked medium rare.  We also wanted to make sure that we got ourselves the charcoal grilled sea scallops because they are to die for.  The sea scallops were fresh and tasty and each course that was brought to the table, the french onion soup, the fresh greens salad and the main course of steak, vegetables and onion straws was gastronomical perfection!  The bill arrived, and it's something to note, they AUTOMATICALLY add a tip of 12% onto the bill for the waitstaff, be sure to add additional to qualify for their impeccable service.   After dinner was settled up, we headed on up to the Henry Waugh dessert room where we each had a coffee, his Americano, mine was the Cafe con Leche ybor, which is a signature there, and is absolutely wonderful. We usually get the creme brule, but tonight we changed things up, we opted to get the sampler of the three molten cakes. They're small, cup cake sized, each served with a cannel of specially selected ice cream - though the cakes are small, with there being three of them, there's enough for two people.   They do NOT add the gratuity up in this room for the server, so please tip accordingly.   And because they knew it was our anniversary,we were presented with a small anniversary dessert, a little desert shell filled with decadent whipped cream and topped with chocolate chips and a candle, It was a lovely touch for the night.   You can not beat the service or the food.  The prices are high, but for two people, including dessert, but no wine, we didn't spend over $150.00, and for a special meal, that's a bargain in my book.

Lunch for one could be awkward, but only if you let it be. Seriously, I enjoy my down time, so when I get a chance, I like to eat alone.   I treated myself to lunch at Longhorn and enjoyed their 7 pepper steak salad, along with their half a loaf of bread with butter, and I was so stuffed by the end of the meal. Nope, I didn't finish the bread, but yes, I ate the steak and the veggies, because they were so delicious!

I've been coming to Ybor city since I was a young woman. I started coming out here when Tracks was a bar and the city really was hard and gritty.   It's nice to see the clean up it's gone through, how Centro Ybor has made it a great place to congregate, and more clubs and bars populate the strip up and down. Truly this is the place to come if you want to explore. There are comedy clubs, good places to eat and multi-screen cinema's to catch the newest releases.   There are pan handlers and bible thumpers that hang out in Ybor, so be on guard for those, but otherwise, enjoy the shopping, the dining and the dancing that can be found.

"WELCOME TO MOES"   That's the usual chant you hear walking in. Didn't get it when I came in this time, but hey, there are many reasons for that.  I noticed that their Queue line had been taken down, so the husbeast and i stepped up to the serving area and waited as the guy behind the counter made the lady before us's order.   I decided I wanted nachos, a new-ish menu item, I was asked if I wanted beans, and I did. I got black beans, and it, being the end of the day (About 8pm) They were having to truly scrape the bottom of the bean bin for them.  The rest of the ingredients looked and tasted fresh, but the beans? They could have opened a new thing of them.   Over all, taste and quality seemed on par with what I'm used to. I did like trying the new coke machine. They had diet raspberry coke. YUM!

Very nice place geared towards cyclists and everything they could ever want.  I'd never even noticed this shop until my beau pointed it out to me.  He'd recently taken me on a bike ride and the seat wasn't good for my "delicate parts" so the goal was to find a seat that better fit my form.   We found that there, a nicely padded wide seat, instead of a narrow thing that hurt any time I used it.   We also found: Trail bikes, road bikes and combo bikes, Beach cruisers with big fluffy tires and trikes for people who want more stability. There is clothing and accessories for every level of enthusiasm.   it's a really well rounded store.

First of all, the address is a bit misleading. If you go by the street count down, you THINK this is going to be down near Crispers & Starbucks, but NO! It's actually just behind Renaissance Realty, off of 5th in Safety Harbor.    Once you find the place though, you're not going to be disappointed. And this comes from me, someone who does not generally LIKE seafood.  We met up with some friends and found this little converted house and made a foursome for dinner.  Making with the appetizers, we had their bacon and cheese waffle fries and calamari for starters. I wasn't too keen on the fries as the cheese sauce was more like queso dip vs real cheese, but the calamari. OH MY GOD! tender, light and not a bit rubbery at all. Someone finally got it perfect!   Dinner for us came in the form of a Scallop plate for my friend's husband, Mahi Mahi for me, and our respective spouses got their specialties: the buckets, a flavorful blend of vegetables and broth with seafood added in. The husbeast opted for a half pound of Shrimp (I think he got more) and our dear friend got snow crab. There was enough food on our table to feed a small kingdom.  This leads us to dessert. We sampled both that were on the menu, the Rum Cake and the home made Key Lime pie. Both were fantastic and the portions were HUGE. I swear I am not kidding when I say they gave us almost a quarter of the key lime pie, and the rum cake HAD to have been soaked with a good ounce or two of quality dark rum.    I'll certainly go back, the Mahi Mahi was perfect!

Met a friend here for lunch. It was time to catch up as it had been far too long.   Let me say up front, I am NOT a sea food fan. We went here because it was close to both of us.  We were seated immediately and our Waitress was awesome. She was there immediately, and the place was nearly empty.   We started with the new crab cakes as an app, and while I don't usually eat them, they were tasty!  Our mains were the lobster boil- his choice. Mine was the shrimp. The lobster boil produced a big female lobster filled with Roe. And my friend was in heaven. he really enjoyed that extra treat. My shrimp were Amazing! They were done to perfection, though I could have done without the fries.   Will I come back? Not on my own, this is not my choice of place, but it might be fun with a group.

If you want to know where most of the 20 somethings in Town n' Country hang out - that aren't gang related, on a Monday night? I can tell you. They've brought their lap tops down to Star Bucks and are hanging out here near the movie theater.   The coffee was coffee, it wasn't any different than any of the other Starbucks I've been to. The chai was good, the service was quick since our order wasn't complicated. The conversation with my friend was really what I went for.

Free parking at the airport! All you have to do is wait for your loved one to signal that they've landed. Give them about 25 minutes from that time to pick up their luggage and then you can go get them. It's a pretty genius thing, really!

Since the husbeast now works in Ybor, he's getting a chance to experience the foods they have in the city.   On Black Friday, instead of visiting stores, he took me here to see one of his favorite places to get Tots.  We ordered at the bar, both of us getting an OOps beer (kinda tart, but very refreshing), I ordered tots with chili and he ordered tots with sour cream.   It was too loud inside the main dining room, so we opted to eat outside since the weather was wonderful.  We had our drinks and only waited about 10 minutes for the tots to be delivered. The chili was delicious! The tots were hot. Yep, I can see why people want to visit here.  The food is good, the beer is cold and the atmosphere is fun!

Pizza + an amazing local comedy troupe (Wit Improv)= an amazingly good time.  I didn't even know this Grimaldi ' s existed, the last I remembered,  this was a different store. I'm glad that it is now a great pizza place.   The waitstaff was very accommodating for our comedy show, I know it isn't what they were used to, but they did amazingly well. The service was great, the food was tasty, and the comedy was GOLD!  If you bring WIT Improv back, I know I'll be back!
I'm very much a fan of Ban Thai Restaurant. Their food is lively and fresh, their service is absolutely spot on.

The Location has moved. This one is NO MORE. The old store is in the process of being demolished and a New (and I mean BRAND SPANKING NEW store) has opened at the corner of Us 19 and SR 52. Drive through is still under construction, but the store was operable and the service was fine.

The original plan was to go to another eatery in the same plaza, but the wait time was 40 minutes and we were hungry. Given that we didn't want to wait that long, we decided to eat at Tijuana flats.   The service was prompt, the girls were very pleasant as they took care of the lobby, as they took care of our needs. The food was out fast, and was exactly what we ordered. we were quite pleased with everything.

I live in the area and figured I should try Fairway Pizza. I've seen them for ages, but have never stopped in.  The husbeast and I decided we wanted pizza...so we got it.   We started with a Ceasar Salad and fried Zuchini both came out very quickly and were HUGE portions for their price. They were tasty and neither were finished.  We also ordered one of their "everything" pizzas. You know the kind, topped with Pepperoni, Sausage, onions, peppers and something else that escapes me.  When it arrived it smelled nice, looked tasty so we dove in.   Mind you, we're on a low carb diet, so what we did was carve off the toppings and eat them, leaving the crust behind. - though admittedly I did eat one of the tops of the crust to see what it was like. All in all, its a solid pizza joint, just not my favorite.

Went here today with a new friend. We decided we wanted to go someplace that neither of us had ever been... and boy! Am I glad we did.   Their menu was fun to read, the music was great to listen to... And the FOOD! OH MY WORD! Both of us had the Shanghi Chicken Rice bowl.  I wasn't sure what to expect, but when it came out, I think I might have sighed with delight.  The fresh flavours danced on my tongue. The ginger soy dressing was just perfect and the rice and veg were crisp and delicious.   The building isn't much, the decor is straight out of Ikea, but once you get past that... ENJOY. You won't find much better.

Gerardo is an EXCELLENT photographer! He's got an eye for color and composition. He knows what he's doing and he really is very nice!  I've had the pleasure of speaking with him at a few events, but it was at the last event that he captured a great shot.  I'm really happy with how it turned out.   If you're looking for a photographer for any occasion, Gerardo is the person for you!

WOOT! My 750th review!!!  Visited with Rachel M and her family, (Thanks for the invite!) I was surprised at how long the line was! It was out the door and down the front of the building.   Disposable, but not Menus are available as you step into line, giving you plenty of time to read over what they have, so you don't hold up the line any further. They have a lot of choices on the menu from pork, chicken and beef. There are a lot of Sides too!  I opted for my hands down favorite at any BBQ joint, Pulled pork, which was served on a tray, lined with brown paper. The serving size is moderate. Not huge but certainly enough. Three sides for a dinner is generous, I chose the Potato salad, the Green beans and cole slaw. Everything was tasty! The only thing I would have preffered would have been is that the slaw wasn't confetti cut. I like the texture of cabbage, and when it's cut so tiny, you lose that and sadly, a lot of the flavour.   The biggest drawback is how loud it is inside. It's almost headache inducing. Everyone is talking and it's a big feedback loop if you're sensitive to sound. There is nothing to absorb the noise and it just bounces around.  When you try to order from the sweet shop, you can barely hear the girls behind the tall, tall glass.   Over all, I'd visit again, but I don't think I'd make the special trip, unless it was a Yelp event.

Dinner for the husbeast and myself on a Friday evening after his work can sometimes be a task. We feel like we've been there, done that. But tonight was different! I found a new little hole in the wall that looked promising, so without much hesitation, we popped into Anthony's and had ourselves a look-see.  The service was a tad slow, but that can be forgiven since the food was delicious. We started with a Caprese salad, and ordered our mains of Parmigiana Chicken with rotelle and a 16" House Special pizza.   While we waited for the food, another table's order came out. It was a pizza that was easily 3 feet across. HOLY COW! That's one of the largest pizza's I've ever seen. I had to take a picture because I don't think I would have beleived it if I'd not have seen it with my own eyes.   My Chicken Parm came out perfectly, nice and crispy cutlet with a good layer of sauce and cheese. The pasta side was ok, but I don't eat pasta so no harm/no foul.  The husband's pizza Smelled delicious! He said it was good! But he could only eat a couple of slices, so we had the rest boxerd up and he'll nom the rest of it over the weekend.

Stopped in on the final day of the Chalk fest. In the final few minutes before the closing of the store. And I grabbed the last Coconut Cuppy and One of the last vanillas.  They were quite tasty!  I was told that they'd been baked within the last 12 hours, because the store's owner was up until 3am that morning baking.. Business has been brisk due to the 3rd Friday and of course the Chalk festival.   I'd like to see what other flavours she has in the future.

It's not easy to get a reservation on the Saturday night before Valentine's day, but thanks to Open Table, Grille One Sixteen had the availability within 90 minutes of the time we really wanted, and a reservation was made.   The first thing our party of four noticed was that the place is not really easy to find off Dale Mabry, and the door leading inside is so well fitting that it is so easily missed that we walked right on by and around the front of the building towards the Korean eatery next door. WHOOPS.  Once inside, we waited about 10 minutes for our seating, and then were seated at the first 4 top in the place, about 20 feet from the front door, a great spot to people watch.  Our waitress, Jennifer, was pleasant and explained to us about the beef, how it's aged, how it's grass fed and no antibiotics. We were left alone to peruse the menu after our drinks were ordered and it was a good little wait until our waitress came back to take our orders.   My friends ordered an Old Fashioned Maple and a Moscow Mule, while my partner and I declined to order alcohol, favoring water and soda.  OUR drinks were up right away, my friends drinks didn't come until after the salad course.   What we ordered: We started with the Ahi Tuna app,  Seat 1: Pan Seared diver Scallops, Seat 2: Jamacian Sirloin, Seat 3: Mixed Grill and Seat 4: 16oz Bone in sirloin.   The Seared Ahi was brought out first, and there was just enough for each of us to have a piece.  $15.99 for this serving to me was a bit steep, but it tasted delicious.   The meals each came with a salad, 2 of us got Ceaser salads and the other two got the house salads.  Each was crisp and flavorful, but the general consensus was that the ceasar salad was the more tasty of the offerings, due to the parm cheese used. SUCH a deep, rich flavor.   Entree 1: The Pan Seared Diver Scallops were presented atop cheese grits and topped with a sweet corn sprinkling. 4 of them... The serving while appearing small was actually quite generous. The scallops were delicious and tender, with a buttery sensation on the tongue. The cheese grits were creamy, but not overly so. Decadent and so full of goodness. $33.00  Entree 2: The Jamaican Sirloin: It's important to note that on the website it's called a Kona Steak, on the menu we were showed, it was a Jamaican Sirloin, but the descriptions were the same.  Cooked Med Rare to perfection, served with root veg and garlic mashed potatoes. The guest said it was amazing.   Entree 3: The Mixed Grill offered up an orange ginger glazed salmon fillet and a few large walkers wood jumbo shrimp along with a few steamed veg, the husbeast also ordered a side of the mashed cauliflower - it was a VERY large side.  The seafood was tasty, if judging by the clean plate I saw next to me.   Entree 4: 16 oz Meyers Angus bone in Ribeye. Almost a tomahawk chop.. ALMOST, served with mashed cauliflower and roasted root veg.. My first steak was cooked Med Well, sadly I'd asked for Med Rare, so I had to send it back. By the time it came back, most of the people I was dining with were nearly finished.  I noticed that the cauliflower had an ... interesting.. taste, the husbeast commented on this as well, almost "animal-y" it wasn't bad, but ... different. And when I say animal-y, I mean it in the way goat cheese is animal-y.  Needless to say, I took 95% of my entree home.   Since tonight was "Valentine's Day Night" All entrees came with a free dessert, so each couple got to split a Molten Lava cake. A dense chocolate cake with a light citrus-y note to the flavour, with hand made whipped cream.  Our friends were set on the doughnuts, so those cakes didn't get eaten completely, we were more interested in the Doughnuts!!! 4 of them on a plate, Raspberry, Chocolate, White chocolate and caramel.. These were more like bignets, but they were heavenly, they just needed MORE whipped cream.   All in all a delicious night. Some small errors, but those will happen on a busy night like tonight. Nothing that cant be forgiven. I will say that the menu on line appears to be in need of updating, prices are currently off by a few bucks.

Our geek group met for the first time this year and this is where we chose to go.   The parking was confusing, a little worry because they're in the same lot as the Red Roof inn, I had to explain that they'd likely be considered the hotel's resturant so parking near the hotel would be fine. That seemed to alleviate the concern our party had.   Entering, the place was kinda dead, and that was fine. We had a reservation for our party of 6, and were seated immediately.  Our waiter, a very young man was attentive, but he would walk away while someone was speaking, he did that twice while we were trying to order appetizers. Not sure if he didn't hear the people or just wasn't paying attention.   We started our order with the Garlic Knots, The fried Ravioli and The Fried Provolone- very reminiscent of Greek Saganaki.  You'd never know we liked it by the look of the plates (They were practically licked clean - yes they were very good. My personal favorite was fried ravioli followed by the fried provolone)  Our table ordered a variety of dishes: A white pizza with black olives, An Italiano Calzone, Lasagne, Chicken Alfredo and 2 orders of Chicken Parmigiana.   The food came out quickly, the dishes were hot and the food was GOOD. Julio even came out to check on us and we found that very sweet. Every one asked us to come back and dine with them again.    Food: White pizza with black olives- The crust was good, but a touch dry. Not enough garlic.  Calzone: No ricotta? Unexpected but very tasty.  Lasagne: Tasty, big portion.  Chicken Alfredo: Smaller portion than expected, no salad. tasty.  Chicken parmigiana:Huge portion of chicken, Well made, great amount of cheese. needed more sauce on the pasta.   We'd certainly come back.

This place was chosen by a spin of the Yelp dial.   And OH MY WORD! I won the food lottery! #Hauntdaddy and I hopped in a lyft and made our way down town, and found this classy little joint on the corner.  When we arrived, we were told that they were on their small menu - salads and appetizers due to the time, 4:30 on Sunday. They'd have their full menu at 5, but we were fine with what we saw.   Everything we read, was mouthwatering, and it was HARD to make a decision. We finally opted for the Fried Green tomatoes, The steak Biscuits and the Bless Your Heart Salad. When everything was delivered, we took turns sharing bites of everything. NOTHING disappointed us. The flavours were So GOOD!  The steak and biscuits literally melted in your mouth. The fried green tomatoes were some of the best I've ever had, and the Salad was a roasted veggie salad that is bar none some of the finest I've ever tasted. The vinegrette dressing brought it all together.   When our mains were finished we HAD to look at the dessert menu, since they hadn't disappointed with the meal. Again, we couldn't make a decision so we opted for 2 desserts to share: The Bluberry crumble with coconut gelato and the Spice cake with pumpkin gelato. Both of them.. Oh man, that was the perfect ending to a great meal! If ever I'm back in Nashville, I'm coming back here.

I love bookstores, and B&N is no exception. I absolutely love getting lost in the stacks and racks of the books and magazines.   I miss Borders, so B&N is the alternate destination of choice. The cafe was clean, but it was having difficulties making any hot drinks save Tea. The restrooms were clean and well kept and stocked, always a plus.   I suppose what I miss most were the comfy chairs you used to be able to sit in, they were always inviting.  I will always support book stores because I prefer paper to e-books, so I had to make a small purchase.

...well that was less than inspiring. I went with friends and the Beau. It was a lovely, but COLD afternoon in Tampa, with a biting wind, and I'll be honest, I didn't know what to expect, but I certainly expected MORE.   When We arrived, we were lucky and found parking about a block away.  Having been to several events at the Red Rockstar bar, we knew that parking would be atrocious, so we tried next to the bakery and found a spot there.  I had hoped that we'd find some vendors of ephemera, not just food.  Sadly this was mostly a food truck rally.   Since we got there just after 2 pm, we got to see the Tampa bay Kendo club (I'm sure it's a different name, but that's what's in my head) do a demo from across the parking lot while we dodged cars pulling in at all angles, and we played with people's pooches.    The offerings of food were a few. At 2, the lines were 30 Minutes long and terribly unorganized, feeding into one another across the cement square area. There were a few smaller vendors like Hot Sauce, flaming fruit sauce and cheese cake in a jar that weren't as busy, but they too, were swamped because that's all you could get to.   The food vendors that I did notice were: Moca Loka, Pho Truck, Flip'n Tasty, Mmm BAP Korean Cuisine, Tongue Thai'd, and Kona Ice - why that truck was there I have no idea... It was 48* outside and no one was going to it. I felt kinda bad for them.   We left after 2 hours because of the cold. We didn't want to fight the crowd and honestly, there was nothing to do. There is -so- much room for improvement, and the space need to be MUCH larger for this event.   At least the company was good. I adore my friends!

I've been meaning to get into this place and finally the opportunity presented itself.  It's a great little natural foods place smack dab in Oldsmar. A lot of supplements, a fair selection of gluten free items and an ingredient replacement option area so you can continue to bake. They've got an awesome selection of fresh fruits and beggies from near by, which is great. And I was able to pick up my Holy Basil.

Stopped in with a friend after having $bucks down the street because it was Lunch time.  We bought the special. A slice and a soda for $3.00. Not a terrible price, the pizza was edible and the service was adequate. The place does look disheveled, not the neatest.

If you enjoy Authentic Chinese food, and like Yummy house, you'll LOVE Asian Pearl. The food is delicious and the service is both quick and very polite.  They are locate behind the former Tilted kilt in a small strip mall, which is mostly empty, but their store was full that night.   We ordered the salt & pepper calamari - which was absolutely delicious, the husband had the General Tso's and I had the beef and broccoli. The portions were so large that the husbeast had plenty for left overs for the weekend.

Safety Harbor's post office is just what a small town's post office should be. Quaint, quick and easily accessible. With plenty of street parking, a ton of post office boxes, they are right there when you need them.   There is only one small issue: Unlike many other post offices, they don't have an APC, (Anytime Postal Center) Which means you can't go ant any time, any hour and mail off your express packages, or get postage at 2:30 am, when that odd need arises.  Other wise, Thumbs up!

I almost forgot about this - it seems so long ago (And it kind of was.. ) At here before heading out to Ohio, the service was ok, and I was seated right before the great big fish tank, lovely view.   My food - eggs, bacon and potatoes, was edible, not terrible and honestly not very memorable.

I loved that they were pimping Howl-O-scream!  I really couldn't decide what I wanted on the menu, so I opted to get the Pretzels for an appetizer and my friend and I opted for burgers. When I ordered mine,  (cowboy burger) I asked for no onions, meaning the raw onions, it came to me without the fried onions, making it nothing but a bacon cheese burger, since I didn't get any of the bbq sauce on it. Oh well.  My friend had the bacon cheese burger. All was well with his.  It's a chain location. Nothing wrong with it, but .. it's not the cream of the crop.

Stopped here to pick up my brother who came in to surprise his family. The Truck stop part was well kept, even if the parking area for cars is a nightmare to navigate. Yes, it's a nightmare, because you have old people and young people who are impatient, and don't know how to drive. They don't look before backing up and they just do what ever they think they want to do, YOU be damned.   The trucking section of parking is very plentiful, I had to drive my lil blue over there to actually get my brother as his truck was parked facing the pumps. My car was dwarfed by the big 18 wheelers, I felt tiny in comparison, but all in all it was a positive experience.

I was hungry, and my mouth wanted a taste sensation that it'd not had in a while.  The husbeast was running late home from work, so I dialed in the "NearBy" application and lo & behold, Yelp did not fail me!  We ended up at Tacos Flacos & Cantina, which is located about 5 miles from our home, tucked away in a strip mall that also has an LA Fitness. When we pulled in, most of the parking lot was being re-surfaced, so parking was at a premium. Not a problem though, we found a close by location and walked right in.   It wasn't a busy night, and that was great! We were seated immediately and handed menus by one of the hosts. The menu's still read SALSA'S, which I found amusing.  There were a lot of choices, but we finally narrowed it down. Ian ordered some HUGE monstrosity of a burrito and I ordered pork tacos.   While we waited, they brought us fresh chips and salsa, which were still warm and very, very tasty.  When the food was delivered, neither of us could believe the size of the burrito. It was GINORMIOUS! Seriously this thing was the size of a serving platter.  My tacos came with a serving of refried beans,sour cream, salsa & green sauce.   I asked the hubby what he thought... he said that his burrito was damned good. That he'd come to expect that most Mexican food was pretty flavourless, that he always needed hot sauce, but he wasn't using any because this food was REALLY good.  My tacos were filled with pork, lots of burnt ends, lots of juicy, fatty bits, they were -stuffed- with meat. There was no cheese, so I did need to ask for some, and the staff was MORE than generous, bringing out a large cup full.  Other than that, once they were assembled, they were AMAZING!  The refried beans were DELICIOUS! It tasted like there was a hint of Cinnamon! All I can tell you, is that we both left with take aways and it made for a delicious lunch today!

Took Mom to lunch today, and when we arrived, it was hoppin. We were seated quite quickly despite the line at the door.  Our waitress was quite affable, her smile warm as she took our order.  Her service was quick and the food, all but the app, was delicious.  I exclude the app, because what we ordered, the tempura green beans, were not served as individual beans dipped in batter, but rather messy clumps that were doughy in some areas and hard to eat/share.   Our main courses were quite delicious. I had the chicken breast with bbq sauce and bacon & Cheese, with my sides being roasted zuchiini (SO GOOD!) and green beans. Mom had the soup and salad bar.  We even indulged in dessert and coffee.

YAY! They finally opened a Wawa just down the street from my home! No more traveling a few miles. I'm THRILLED!  This off set from a corner off of Us 19, in the turn lane heading to Alt 19. The funny thing about this location? There are already 3 other service stations there. A BP, A Racetrack and A Chevron, and by far, WaWa's prices were the lowest. Today's gas price $2.45.9 for Regular unleaded vs $2.59 at BP.  Their pumps are Clean and neat, they are well lit and right now offering Free coffee any size and any size soft drinks are $0.59 - I'm sure this is a grand opening special.

I got sent to Palm Harbor MRI for Xrays of my neck, shoulders, knees and toe after a recent car accident. The staff was friendly, outgoing and professional.  The office itself was quite nicely done up and clean.

After our teaser for our Fringe play, my cast and I were looking for something to do in Ybor on a moderately late (read that as 9:30 pm) Wednesday night.  Many of the dinner places we wanted to go, were closed, but we saw that the Brass Tap was open so we opted for it as it was a short walk and those in the cast wearing heels wouldnt have to walk too far.   It wasn't a busy night, but the TV's were blaring loudly, almost to the point of pain.  We sat at the bar as the waitress said she wasn't seating any more tables, the bar was fine with us.  We weren't looking to purchase alcohol but food, so we perused their dinner menu.  I chose the riblet skillet (it comes with a 5 cheese mac N cheese, though it didn't say in the description, it was topped with both jalapeno peppers and peppadews, and of course the riblet meat.) Others chose the nachos and chips and salsa to eat.   When my order came, the whole thing had a very petroleum smell too it.  The meat and top layer of the mac n cheese tasted like it'd been splashed with watered down lighter fluid, like maybe it'd been too close to the flame under a gas salamander.  It just didn't taste right. I ate the meat, I was hungry, but the M&C was just too .. meh to eat.   The service though was great at the bar.

I came here to pick my husband up who was enjoying a conversation with a friend. I went to get a Tea.  Sadly the tea I chose was really weak. Usually it's a bright PINK color, but the hibiscus tea was this very pale purple, sort of like the acai tea, with little to no flavour.  When I told one of the servers, she didn't have a clue about her product.  But she did go ahead and was going to brew a new pot. Sadly I didn't have time to wait.

Yes, Clearwater Beach is Beautiful! ! It's one of the most gorgeous beaches in all of florida. You can't deny it at all.   But there's construction going on, and parking is minimal. Hotels are charging you $20 to park in their lots, just to go to the beach! The beach is getting g crowded, especially since Spring Break is gearing ip. In a weeks time it's going to be impossible to get across the bridge to even get over to the beach!  So while I love this place, it's not the best out there.

So thrilled that I got to see their last show of the season!  I was able to attend an earlier walk through of a portion of their show with the lights up thanks to the Legendary Haunt Tour. The fact that I was able to go back later and actually see the whole thing LIVE? That made my entire trip.  Six haunts rolled into this one magnificent location that just becomes all that more omnious when the lights go out and the fog comes up. Since this was a dark show, the only light we had was that from an orange glow stick.  All my friends and myself did the whole experience, the tracking device (glow necklace) and the bloody X on our face. We only had an issue with the people behind us who were so freaked out they wanted to blunder through the event. We eventually let them pass ahead.   The intake is probably my favorite, that Cell block 12 that opens up into the rotunda was just amazing, it really did turn out well and creeptacular with the fog and roach characters that inhabit the place.  And getting to do the detour up to the 2nd floor to see where they've seen the banshee was pretty cool and really spectacular.  One house that doesn't work when the lights are off is the 4D house. the effects that rely on 3D glasses don't work when you can't see them.   All in all a solid haunt that's been running for 27! Years.  Keep doing what you're doing and the crowds will come back and see the show.

Out in the middle of no where. My gas gauge is WAY past E and I know I'm on fumes. I pull off the interstate and see that WaWa is 1.1 miles away. I headed off to find it, praying I'd get that far.   I did, I had to make a U-turn because it is off 301 and NOT on the corner. If you see Walgreens, make a Left turn!  Anyway, they were there, they were bright and when I filled my tank, gas was $1.69 a gallon, which is officially the lowest I've seen it.   Pumps were clean and tidy, the windshield stations were stocked and everything was neat. If it weren't that far out of the way, I'd visit more often.

After picking my brother up from the Flying J, (He's a trucker), we headed up to the next exit for lunch. BBQ is always a good choice, so we stopped into Sonny's and ordered food.   The service was good, even though getting the food from the kitchen seemed slow. I think that's because they actually had to make my brother's smoked chicken salad.  As usual, the pulled pork, garlic bread and broccoli were good and the fries were delicious.  Bebo said that the chicken salad was good, even if the smoky flavor was a bit.. odd.

Happy Birthday, Anna.   Yep, this was an Unofficial Yelp Event - a UYE, and a whole bunch of us showed up to celebrate one of the most loquacious of us all.  I don't live in South Tampa, so I'd never heard of Ciccio's, I'm not familiar with the name, but once I walked in I was hooked.   The atmosphere was welcoming and inviting. The live musician was pretty awesome too! He could really play and sounded like anyone he was covering.  Since we were doing a private party, we were in the private party space, The room was large, with enough table seating for 25-30 people. Though loud, it wasn't terribly obnoxious.  And since it was Sunday, there was the added perk of Happy Hour all day! Score!  Now lets talk about the food. Brunch on Sunday was pretty Amazing. They are apparently known for their sushi, but I don't play that game. After a careful perusal of their menu, I opted for their Gyro California wrap.  Made with lamb, feta, humus and other tasty ingredients it was served in a flour tortilla vs a pita, which was thin and crispy. And the taste combined was so good!  The others at the table opted for breakfast items.   And WOW.. let me tell you that If/when I come back, I will order the chocolate chip pancakes. They were AMAZINGLY delicious! Topped with strawberries and served with a side of perfectly wonderfully seasoned home fries.  Another person at the table ordered a bowl - With Basil scrambeled eggs and ricotta cheese. I'd never thought of combining those tastes, but now I'm a fan.   This place is a winner in my books.

A clean Walgreens store. Nothing out of the ordinary, save that on this day there were only 2 people working - as told to me by the cashier.  The girl at the register was bemoaning the fact that everyone else has called in.   You can not run a store with just two people, but the were doing an admirable job.

Stopped in for lunch on Christmas Eve.  A note on the door said they closed at 1:30 and the time that I arrived was 1:09. There was no rolling of the eyes, no gnashing of teeth that I was there 20 minutes before closing.   The place was clean, the service was amazing.  I ordered something new for me, the Spartan Skillet: Gyro meat, onions, tomatoes & feta cheese with hash browns topped with 2 eggs any style and a side of carbs ( i chose their 'Famous' pancakes.  When the food came out, it was both fast and tasty. I was quite pleased with what they offered. Only that there was no butter for the pancakes. The runner brought me 3 little packs of whipped butter, and when I asked for 2 more, she kind of tossed them on the table.   The pancakes were light and fluffy, as were the eggs. The flavours of the Spartan mingled nicely. Usually I don't like onions in my food, which is why I omit them from EVERYTHING. But when they're cooked, they're ok. Today they added just the right taste.   I would come back.

Leaning Tower of Pizza has been open FOREVER.  I remember going here when I was a kid.  My mom was out of town and my 16 year old Niece wanted some bonding time, so I took her there.  I was craving pizza, nd I knew they were good.   The two of us ordered our drinks, we had mozzerella sticks to start with and a pepperoni pizza. I think it was pretty telling that we both could only eat 2 slices and the Mozz stix.  The rest was taken home to be eaten later.   It was just as good as I remembered.

I stopped in here to pick up some school supplies for a teacher friend of mine. I wanted to get her some college ruled paper. WHY can't I find the 200 sheet pack that I used to get when I was in school? All I can seem to find are 120 or 175 sheets? WTH people? Where's the consistency? Where are the ream packs? NO BUENO!  THe store had some good deals on Sharpie markers and white board markers so I picked those up as well! My friend was very happy with what I provided her, and Staples helped make that possible.

Need a tarot deck? They've got it. Need incense? Check! Need crystals?  Yep! they're here.  Do you need to do a cleansing on your personal space? White sage is there, so are a bunch of other herbs to help.  Are you in need of a love spell? There are ones that are pre-made. Or you can buy a book that will teach you how to do it.  Herbs, books, stickers, bath bombs, EVERYTHING you could expect is here in this quaint little shop. They have readers too, that can help you figure out where you're going in life, if you need their guidance. There's a great energy about the place too, if you want to just go and feel rejuvinated. It's relaxing as all get out.  I have to say, it's one of my favorite New Age shops I've ever been to.

Why have I not heard about this store before? Take a Dollar Tree, add in a bit of higher end merchandise and you get the 5* below. Everything in the store is $5 or less, this includes the electronics, the coloring and crafts and the gift items.  There are clothing, hair and jewelry items - I'd guess it's geared to the teens, a place to pick up that last minute gift for your friends, when you don't have a lot of money. I can see this store doing REALLY well.

I was taken here tonight by a friend for a belated birthday dinner. I've driven by here for months and finally took the chance to eat here.   We placed our order for Black and Blu burger, Chicken Strips and the fries with cheese & Ale sauce. Everything came to the table quickly while we were catching up on my recent trip to Hawaii. The burger, even though I ordered the small one, was HUGE! The flavours were absolutely delicious and my friend's chicken strips were light, crispy and so juicy. They were probably the best chicken strips we've ever had.   The sauce for the fries tasted -to me- like potato cheese soup, I would gladly eat it by the bowl full, although the fries left something to be desired. The ones that came with her strips were old, a bit cold when they came to the table.   I'm only giving 4 stars because the bathroom was out of toilet paper and when we came in there was only one cashier behind the register at 6:30, still peak dinner time.

After a Yelp event, I was invited down to Rapp Brewing to hang out while others did their Fantasy Football team selection - I had no idea that it was 'Srs Bsns', but it apparently is!  The place is tucked back in a business park, off BryanDairy  Road, and you will miss it if you're not looking carefully, so I'm thankful for GPS.  I found it without too much trouble, and went inside. It's pretty spare, but I did like the menu board, where all the beer names are written in chalk. The listing is pretty extensive as well as comprehensive.    While I'm not a drinker, my friends are, so they indulged, and if (When) I got curious, they'd let me take sips. I found that the "Chocolate Peanut butter Stout" had a surprisingly delicious taste.  The Watermelon Pale - was ok, light but not watermelon-y at all to me.  The Gose was sharp, almost bitter, but would be really refreshing on a hot day.  There were a couple of other beers that they were drinking but I can't remember the names. One that I do remember, it was a hoppy one, I snffed it and it smelled.. well it was unflattering. However one of the guys at the table Really liked it! It's all about an educated pallet, I guess!  I am going to have to bring some folks here, because THEY like beer. they are interested in places like this! These are the little gems that we have tucked away, So thanks Anna for introducing me to it!

And I said, what about Breakfast at Tiffany's.. *la la la*  So sorry about the ear worm.. Now go and listen to the song, I'll be right here.    Back? Good.  This is a quaint little diner that's been in Palm Harbor/edge of Tarpon for as long as I can remember. Family owned, they offer a lot of different options, and every one of them is tasty.  Today, since we had to be up early for the nephew's 2nd birthday party, the Husbeastie and I decided we'd stop for breakfast. We didn't want to do the usual, or a chain, so we stopped here.    First things first, they greet you warmly and when you're sat, they place a bowl of mini sweet corn muffins on your table. They are So GOOD!  We took a few minutes to order, and in the end the Husband got Chicken and Waffles and I got a Chicago skillet.  The portion size for mine was huge: A large omlette style egg filled with canadian bacon, sausage and other meats topping fried potatoes and topped with delicious crumbled bacon and cheeses. There was -so- much food.

Found this place quite by accident.   My beau and I are always looking for new places to hike. The parking for this is located about a mile in off of Bramble wood off of Lutz lake fern road.  It's easy enough to get to.   There are a substantial amount of trails that are periodically maintained. But this is Natural Florida. So the terrain is uneven, some times overgrown and with the occasional *SURPRISE SWAMP* on your path.  If you're nimble enough you can make your way around it.   It's great to do these hikes as the weather cools, the height of summer is terrible. ;)

Since I live in Tarpon Springs, I find it almost mandatory that I try the different Greek cuisine out there.  Last Sunday, after my recital for belly dance class, I opted to visit here, because they advertise a belly dancer -starting- at 7:30 pm. As luck would have it, I knew this particular dancer and hoped to get to see her preform.   I got there shortly after the 7pm hour and found out she'd already danced and would not be doing any more shows that evening. This left me disappointed, because the sign clearly states STARTING at 7:30. *le sigh* That would be the big complaint I had.    Now onto the good stuff:  I was there with friends so the company was great.  I ordered their house made white sangria, it was happy hour so 2 nicely sized glasses of sangria (which was delicious by the by) was $7.00. Because we were ordering three entrees we were given a free order of saginaki or flaming cheese, which was absolutely decadent.   When the entrees came to the table, my friends' orders of Gyro and fries looked and smelled wonderful. Their meat mix tasted more of lamb than beef, and was fresh, not a lot of crusty bits from rotating on the spit all day. Clearly people order this all the time.   I ordered the spanokipita, and it was amazing and huge. Freshly made, the pie was ginormous and exceedingly delicious. SO GOOD!
