I would eat here again, but I would want them to make sure they got their signage fixed so they didn't disappoint their belly dance fans.

I enjoy FCU's for banking as they're always a lot more friendlier than national chains.   This location on Water's avenue is always busy.  They're located near a Tampa Health Center, so the parking lot is always a bit of a challenge, especially if you don't come in by the light. If you're using the drive through, you can often expect longer than normal wait times, even if you're the only person in line.

I've driven past this place hundreds of times, but never had the time to drop in. Since I was picking up a friend to go to the Screamagedeon yelp event, and my friend was picking up dinner, I suggested we go here. It was close to her place and I thought it might be reasonable. She agreed.   We arrived, the parking lot on one side was nearly empty, so we made the trek inside and were told to sit ourselves.  It was 6:00 pm on a Friday, so we knew the seats would fill soon and that happened pretty quickly. Once we were seated, our waitress brought us Placemats/menus and asked us our drink orders: Tea for me, Bud for my friend.   We perused the menu until we found something we both liked and waited a few minutes while our waitress handled the 5 new tables that came in. She was in for a busy night, let me just tell you.  They started to shuttle people over to the 2nd location across the drive way.   When she came over, I ordered the 2 meat combo platter with Brisket and chopped pork, sides were potato salad, mac & cheese with garlic bread.   My friend got the sampler platter which contained a rib, a chicken thigh, chopped pork and a slice of brisket, green beans, potato salad and a sweet corn muffin. It was an incredible amount of food.   We chatted aobut the nights events while we waited. The decor inside is dated, but homey. Rustic and neat, but the bathrooms are TINY and hot. There is a larger "Handicapped" Stall, but there are no bars for assistance, and the door is about 18" from the toilet bowl, that makes for a claustrophobic experience if you're tall.   THe food came out, and it was good. They offered us different sauces than were out on the table (Mild and regular) They brought us spicy and mustard. I have to say, hands down, the Mustard sauce was my favorite. Just the right amount of tang and flavour.  Their brisket was tender, with a thin layer of fat along the top. The pork was tasty, but there were a lot of burnt ends in mine, and those are hard for me to eat.   The potato salad was heavily mustard based but so damn good and the mac & cheese was standard fare.  But the "Garlic" bread didn't live up to expectations. It was grilled\charred bread, and that's fine, but there was no garlic flavor what so ever.   We both ate our meals with gusto and left saited and happy.   10/10 will be back.

Had a nice lunch with a friend.  The location is clean and the staff is friendly, but I find it disturbing when you go into the bathrooms and they're teaching you Italian in a loop. I mean, you hear a man's voice suddenly all around you, and you don't know him? At first you're like WHA???   Any way, I digress, 11:30 am, I meet my friend, we are seated and we have a lovely view of the kitchen - that's a good thing, we both enjoy watching the kitchen staff work. The Waiter - who is also the bartender is being run a bit ragged so we cut him some slack, but we place an order for a starter of Calamari - it's tasty, crisp and tender, not at all rubbery or over done.  I eat the rings, my friend can eat the tentacles. Our mains are placed a bit later, I get the take on the Wedge salad with bib lettuce and chicken, and my friend gets the Sausage and Potatoes,   All and all, the food is fast and the service is quick.. We're out within 45 minutes.

I remember when the mall opened, it was your typical mall, since then, it's truly expanded, adding a huge upscale food court outside, with The Cheesecake factory, a brand new Bahama Breeze and the like.  They've got everything you could want in a mall, from jewelry stores, to fashion stores, to boutiques for gifts to high end fashion, and everything in between. It really is a shopper's paradise.

How is it possible for you to lose the same luggage on the same trip?  On my way out to LA, I understand it, I really do. My first flight had a delay - something the airline didn't notify us of until 15 minutes before departure. But HEY! That's ok. We're not boarded yet. We're all still planeside, None of us could POSSIBLY have connections right?  There was a "sand storm" outside phoenix the previous night and the flight crew hadn't gotten in until the wee hours and so they hadn't gotten their prescribed rest. OK, I get that. HOWEVER, That's no excuse, the Airline had plenty of time to notify the passengers that this would be a delayed flight. They did not do so.   They tried, unsuccessfully to get another flight crew to man our flight, so they gave us cards and had us all call in to a "special number" and re-book our flights. When I finally got through, Someone picked up, said something and I was put back on hold, and eventually the line went dead.  I had to call in again! This time someone picked up quickly, was very brusque and informed me that I was already rebooked and going to Texas! This was the first thing I knew about it. (GREAT CUSTOMER SERVICE HERE!  /sarcasm)  When I got to the new flight - through no help from ANYONE on USAIR, I was assured that my bags would be transfered over to the new plane.  So you can imagine my chagrin when, at LAX I stood around waiting for the baggage to come off the carousel, and it didn't.  Mind you, I was in LA for a HUGE party that -REQUIRED- either black tie formal wear or Costumes. I had several thousand dollars worth of costumes in that bag.   Yeah.. the bag didn't get to me, it had gone to my original destination of Pheonix - except my destination was to be LAX.  Again, great job USair.    I had to rely on a friend for costumes that night, this made me VERY angry since I had costumes that I'd worked on for over a month in that bag.  It did arrive in 24 hours though so bully for that.   On the flight home: I checked into LAX 2 hours before my flight. I sat at the Counter for a good 8 minutes waiting for someone to take my bag. When the girl finally saw that i was waiting. She asked me if I was checking a bag. Yes.  Well it hadn't printed out anything. (I'm sorry, the big pink hard case is too big for over head bins) So she "unjammed" the kiosk and handed me my baggage slip. I didn't even look at it. (MY FAULT, I know)  So when I landed, I expected my bag to be on the carousel...  And .. it never came. So I went to US AIr baggage service and found out that my bag was now going to be in another city in Arizona. - It gets to travel more than I do! When Faoula checked on it, though.. It had not actually left LAX. So she was going to have it sent to me here in Florida, by way of Charleston (See, it sees more cities than I do)  and I should have it here today.  Really though, Totally unacceptable, the only person who was in anyway apologetic was Faoula, She was pleasant, She offered to refund me the bag handling charge, and she understood how angry I was. How can you lose the same bag on the same trip coming and going? I wonder if this merger was a smart thing? Did you can all the good employees and keep the inept ones?

"Better than Red Robin!" That's what the Husbeastie said, anyway.   We went looking for a new place to review and ended up here at Pearly's Beach eats inside of Countryside Mall on Sunday.  It's located just under the cinema so it's really easy to find.   They weren't busy, and that's perfectly fine for us, we walked up to the counter, perused the menu board and the small hand menus for a moment and placed our orders for the Big Kahuna burger (I think that's what it was called), the husbeastie got his just as described, with fries (an upcharge) and I got mine with no onions or sauce.   We sat and waited while the orders were made, and then it was brought to our table. The burgers were generous in size and toppings, the sides (Fries for him, fritos for me) were plentiful and tasty.  The burgers really were delicious, and fresh.  Will we come back? You bet. The service, what there was of it (ordering and them bringing it to the table) was excellent.

Stopped to get money out for my beau.    The bank is well landscaped and kept, and the walk up to the ATM is kept clear.  The ATM is a 2 unit so there is no wait if someone is using one.   The beau was done quickly and back in the car in less than 3 minutes.

I've been wanting to try Hofbrähaus for some while, but trying to get in has been a nightmare - or it was back when they first opened. However tonight, it was far easier. We had a large group of 10, and at first we were sat directly beneath the band, sadly, it was too loud for us to carry on conversations, so before we all gathered - we were still waiting on some of our party, we asked our Waitress Jamie-Marie, and she managed to get the private function room for us!  This made it MUCH easier for us to hear, to talk over business and in general enjoy our meal.  I've been to another location in Kentucky, and while I enjoy the style of eating, I found it a touch loud over all, but once we were moved, It was far more tolerable and Jamie Marie was VERY attentive.  The food was good, our drinks never went empty and we were all quite full by the time we left.   Thanks again, Jamie Marie for your help in making tonight memorable.

Just driving home from the Tampa airport, we stopped to put our feet in the warm waters of the gulf.  The sun was beautiful as it glimmered on the water and kissed on the skin like a hungry lover.  Man, the water was nice in comparison to the Pacific I'd just been visiting.  I am so glad to be home.

Last Sunday, while out and about with the husband, we were looking for a BBQ joint to eat at. Sadly, when we stumbled in on the Pig, they had already closed, by the scent of the air alone, we vowed to come back. Today was our lucky day!  Since we both had today off, the husbeast and I made our way back to picturesque Ozona and knocked on the door of this rustic eatery. There were a couple of noisy gents at the bar, and a few other diners at tables, so we sat ourselves in a booth and were promptly served by a friendly waitress.  Since we'd never been there before, we took a few minutes to place our order, but what we were presented with was MOUNDS of food.  We both ordered the BBQ plate, I chose the pulled pork (of course) and he got the brisket. Normally these are served with beans and slaw, but they let you sub out for most of their sides, He chose fries and I chose potato salad.  When they were delivered to the table, each was garnished with a deviled egg (YUM!) and a trio of heated sauces.   The pork was so tender and the beef was yummy, and while I like the vinegar based sauces, the husbeast wasn't so fond of them, he found them too runny to be of much good. What he DID like was the shaker of rub that was on the table - he liked it so much he asked if we could buy some. (We did). We ate our fill, my husband is a member of the clean plate club, but I'm afraid I am not, there will be some shame on my face for that, but while the food was delicious, I really did want to save some room for the Homemade banana pudding - or Southern creme bruele as the menu put it.   I'm glad I did, that stuff was fan-freaking-tastic.   We will be back, the service alone was amazing. The locals at the bar, well they were "colorful" and made a few.. mm off color jokes that everyone could hear, but I really can't hold that against the establishment.

Grand Opening day! I wasn't one of the lucky first 100 people, but I did show up and I got to try some of their Delicious food. Chris W. wasn't exaggerating. The food is good.  No, I didn't go inside, but instead I used the drive through - AWESOME IDEA FOLKS!   Going inside would have been a long wait. Going through the drive though, instead saved me a lot of time!   The menu is pretty simple and straight forward, the offer a few different styles of Chicken Salad, a handful of sides and drinks including Tea, Lemonade and Coca Cola products.  The food is made fresh, breads include: White, Wheat Berry or Croissant, - 2 of the breads can be toasted but the croissants can not.   I ordered the Fancy Nancy - a chicken salad with grapes, apples and pecans, so tasty, a side of pasta salad and a drink. My total was around $11.25 and the service was awesome.  I will certainly come back!

We were busy, but the husbeast needed to clean up his look.  Our idea was ... if there wasn't a long wait, then we would just go ahead and get his hair trimmed up.  Luckily we could walk right in and be seen.   There was -no- wait, the hairsylist took him right back and provided a much needed trim and shave to his head.  He looks much more presentable for his trip across the country at the end of the month.

While my usual Tribeca location was undergoing renovation, I had to stop into the Ybor location so I could see Mikey, my favorite stylist.  I won't see anyone else. Mikey is wonderful! He asked a few questions, and set to work. I'm in LOVE with what he did! it's FABULOUS and I keep getting compliments on the color.  You can bet I refer everyone to Tribeca and Mikey.

Lets hear it for the new summer time event, Sunset Celebration! Tampa's Lowry Park is an excellent  example of family friendly entertainment for ALL ages!  With the Sunset Celebration, You get excellent entertainment for your money! There are stilt walkers, tumble monkeys and hula-hoopers. There is live music and amazing magic, and that's not even including the delicious food to be had!  This happens Friday & Saturdays now thru August 8th.  Admission is free with your membership or $20.00 after 4pm

I love Ross stores. It is a challenge for me to find them where ever I go, to see the variety of merchandise everywhere. 85% of it is the same but regionally things are different   This store isn't the most organized, but it did have some things that the others in my local area did not. Including a few high low tees that I like.  Over all, I'd come back here on a day.

Love the new location, it's right near where my husbeastie works! Stopped in while in St pete for a short staycation and enjoyed a meal with the beau.   For a Saturday night, we were seated immediately, the service was amazing that the food was good. It is loud in the location, so if you're like me and have trouble with ambient sound, be aware of that, but other wise, go knowing the food will make you happy. I wish we'd saved room for dessert, it all looked AMAZING.   Ca't wait to go back!

I didn't even know this place existed, and then I had to kill some time before picking up a friend at the airport. Much to my chagrin, I decided to pop in and try their fare. The lady behind the counter offered me a couple of samples of the flavours and I settled on the Cafe and the rich Chocolate. Dear God! they were so good! Rich and creamy on the tongue with so much depth and flavour!  I also ordered an espresso, which was drawn perfectly. I will be back!

I don't/can't agree with their politics, but I'll be damned if their fries, service and nuggets don't make up for it sometimes.   Hungry, after my adjustment, I popped in and grabbed myself food. I ordered a number one, and it was a quick, and I do mean QUICK 2 minute trip through the drive through, with out errors. The cashier was both polite and efficient and the food was VERY hot. Nothing like hot waffle fries! So good.

Stopped into Danny's as our friend told us about a new Whisky bar here.   They've recently renovated and it shows. Yes they still smoke inside , so there's that, but the new TV's , the new floors, the new pool tables, all are great and add ambience to the local watering hole.   The food looks good too. The husbeastie and I ordered a shareable of Hand breaded Mozzarella sticks and those were HUGE and delicious.   The Whisky bar is still not open to folks yet, it's to the backside and still on the down low, but when it opens people are gonna love the Bear & Boar.

We walked into the foyer, and there was a horrid stench, a fetid odor of dying mop heads that had lingered too long in the mop buckets and had not been cleaned.  But the store it's self seems clean.  We sat down and were greeted by our waitress and told that she was training a new girl and that the new girl would be doing most of the work.  Honestly Nothing was wrong with the service, the food was delicious, but it was that damn smell upon entering. I did mention it to the girls and they let their manager know. As we exited we did notice that the stink seemed lessened, and that the pervasive odor of some tropical scent now was in place.

The husbeastie and I saw a write up on line and decided that sounded like the perfect place for his Birthday lunch.   We arrived a little after 1 on Sunday, the place had ample seating inside and out, and since the weather was absolutely gorgeous, we opted to take the tables outside.   Our waitress Delaney, was attentive and friendly and made sure we knew about the specials and the current holiday drink "Jingle Juice" which we both opted to try.  Their menu is ecclectic and funky with tacos that are unusual but cool and bowls that are HUGE but delicious.  We started our meal with cauliflower cakes, think crab cakes but none of the icky fishy flavor. It had the similar consistency and a nice light flavor, the lobster sauce was a nice compliment.  We had the Spicy Shrimp bowl and beef broccoli bowl, both were delicious and flavorful, but served in literal serving bowls. They were certainly tasty.  We also ordered a side of the Elote, which lived up to my expecation of being delicious. I will come back again, that's for sure.

Came into the store to pick up some fixings to make my mom some healing chicken soup. The store was clean and neat. It's a small format store like that one I usually go to, and the layout was similar, so it was easy to find everything I needed.   The employees were friendly, willing to help and asked if we needed anything. I don't know why the store is rated so lowly.

It's a Chili's. There's nothign different about this location than the one 5 miles down the street, or 55 miles away.  The food is the same, the service is usually decent. I like that they offer a low calorie option now.

Met my girls here for a Pre-Christmas get together tea party. I'd never been to the OE, so I set my GPS and let it take me to the location right in the heart of Tampa.    From the outside, the building is pretty Non-descript.  It's an older edifice in the middle of a split street across from University of Tampa. There's free parking down side streets or you can pay to park at the church. I found a free spot and made my way inside.  I had no idea I could enter off of the back street, so I walked all the way around to the front on Kennedy, which was fun, as I was dressed to the nines.   Inside, I was STUNNED. This place is huge. There's a gift shop, a book store, a Buddy Brew coffee and a champagne bar. WOW!  We waited a bit for our reservation and then were seated around the fountain in the atrium.  Lovely, really, but loud.  Especially when one party of young women decided that we all needed to hear what they were excited about. Seriously everyone in the eatery turned to look at them.   The tea menu and spirits menu was nicely appointed. I chose the silver leaf jasmine tea, and the regular tea service, as did my friends, though their tea choices were different.  Our waiter was polite and kind and when he brought the food, it was delightful. There were finger sandwiches of Peanut butter and jelly, Curry chicken salad, turkey . Scones with Clotted cream and jam and an assortment of pastries that were decadently delicious.   Our experience was excellent and we'd come back any time!

After a long drive towards home from Sarasota, I needed to stop some place before I made my way to a showing of RHPS.  I noticed that Chick-Fil-A was still open and I was happy.   I pulled in, the service was quick.. it was polite and efficient. I placed my order, the people at the window got it right and I was out of there in less than 5 minutes. The food was right - which is unusual for a drive thru.

I've watched this come in from the ground up, and I FINALLY got to experience it in full swing.   I was NOT disappointed!  We came here to usher a pair friends off to new phase of life. They'd be leaving Florida to go to the cold climes of Kentucky, so we reserved a place and met here on a Friday Evening.  The music was fabulous, the live piano, cello and vocals were pretty damned amazing.  The cellist, Rose is a character and a delight I adore her.  The wait staff was spot on, our dishes never lingered and the food was down right AMAZING.   I personally ordered the Brussel Sprouts and the grilled cheese... I was truly surprised at the flavours that danced on my tongue, they were bright and fresh. The Grilled Cheese is not ordinary by any means. It was more like a Caprese Salad on bread, and that, my friend is a delight. The sprouts were done with bacon and were utter perfection.   The drinks.. Lets talk about that: If you're a fan of Gin, go here.. They pour strong and they mix well. I had the Pina Colada and though it wasn't traditional it was delicious.  Our group had a great time and we decided we'd all return.    LOVE THIS PLACE .

We have a new buffet in town, Color me surprised.  It's near Country side mall so it should do well. Getting in and out may prove difficult, but once you figure it out, it's easy peasy.   We came to eat lunch on a Sunday, there was one cashier, the line was nearly out the door, the process was time consuming and slow.  The eatery wasn't that busy.   Once we were processed, we were told to sit anywhere, so we chose a table in the middle and sat. The hubby let me go up first.  I chose vegie soup which was meh (Very canned tomato flavour) the salad was tasty, and the other veg I chose was good. The fried chicken most certainly tasted of Peanut oil, but there were no peanut allergy warnings anywhere, this could be an issue if anyone has an allergy.   I went up for dessert and tried their chocolate pie and their banana pudding, the chocolate pie was delicious but the banana pudding didn't even set right, and when I tasted it, i knew why.. it was SALTY.  UGH.. What a way to ruin a dish.   The customer service was excellent.   I might come back if I'm VERY hungry and in the are.

Our first breakfast/brunch of the New Year, and the Husbeast is more on point with going to new places for Yelp than I am. You'd think he was reviewing and not me.  (He has a yelp account, he just doesn't yelp.)  This is a hole in the wall place, with 1950's furniture, and VERY reasonable prices.   Since we started on a protein only eating plan for the week, we had to be judicious in what we ordered, but I opted for the 2 eggs and 2 bacon, the Husbeast got himself the omelette with Ham and Swiss, no veg.   While the place was moderately busy, the service was quick, The coffee was hot and the food was damn tasty.  My eggs were fluffy, the bacon was deliciously salty and ZOMG I wanted more, but it was the perfect amount. I did get the home fries, but I only ate about 3 bites, because I really did need to try everything they were offering.  The omelette was Good too, just the right amount and of course the fruit cup had the best pineapple this side of Hawai'i.    Our total for coffee and 2 meals was under $18.  Will we be back? Yes.

This is a great little gift shop off the beaten path in Dunedin. They carry some fabulous art, some fashion, soap and lotions.  Their prices aren't cheap but they're totally worth it.  The service was kind and friendly and I would totally shop here again.

This store was amazingly clean, well organized and well stocked. The staff was exceedingly friendly and helpful. I was happy to shop and spend my gift card here.   Did I spend money too? YOU betcha!  I will certainly be back!

A walk back to the past with my beau. This is in his old neighborhood, so since we wanted pizza for an indulgent meal, we opted for ABC Pizza. I'm really glad we did, too.   It wasn't terribly busy, so we were seated and served by a lovely waitress. We placed an order for garlic bread, a Greek Salad and peperoni pizza. Everything was AMAZING.   The Garlic bread and the greek salad were more than enough for us, we really didn't need the pizza, but dutifully we ate it and it was good. We left with plenty for late night snacking.   Over all, we were very happy with our visit and would come back.

I'm being generous because they just opened, and I think they're going to fare better as time goes on, and they get the kinks worked out.   I witnessed a lot of front of house and back of house arguing over what's included with what is ordered. I saw blatant errors in what orders were out in. I saw slow service where guests came in, sat for 5 minutes without being asked a drink order so they got up and left. This kind of thing needs to be worked out sooner rather than later, else they're doomed.   Our orders were their Signature Steak skillet with veggies and salad. I had their brisket dinner plate.  We waited a very long time. They use a microwave a lot, I could hear it going off frequently.   When the food came it was presented beautifully. The Husbeastie said the meat was rather tough and chewy, and bland. No real flavor. He like the salad the best of all.   For me, the Cole slaw was good, the meat was tasty, had been seared on a grill top and smothered in a tasty BBQ sauce and served with room temperature canned baked beans.   The meat and toast were delicious, the beans were cold and obviously canned. Just meh.    I will check them out again in a few months and hopefully be able to re-do this review.

I'd heard that the had white gloves, and that's what I was looking for, so I had to go see. They did, so I bought them. In the process I saw that they're getting ready for Gasparilla, the pirate gear is out in full force.   However with that, comes cranky employees. Don't worry folks, I can assure you, people with carts really won't push through where you all are stocking. We're pretty good at gauging that kind of thing.   No need to snark at each other where the guest can hear you, that's not the way to endear yourselves to the public. Bonus when the guest calls you on it.

I stopped in for lunch since they have their 2 slices and a drink for $6 special. I ordered a slice of White and a slice of Pepperoni to go. Got my drink - only Pepsi? Yech. But the pizza was ready in just a few minutes.   When I took my first bite at home, it was barely warmed. It tasted OK, but still, if they're going to warm it up, it would have been much better to have it warmed all the way through.

My Mom was in a 4 car collision, and required transport to the hospital. She's a retired nurse and when given the choice, she chose North Bay.   The ER was very good in the care of my mom, they treated her quickly and efficiently, getting her a bed and medication to ease the pain she was in.    Through basic Xrays, they determined that she had a broken knee cap. This meant that she would need to be seen the next day and kept over night for observation.  Good.   She was taken up to the 3rd floor where she was promptly taken care of by a fantastic team of nurses. Each and every one of them was competent, compassionate and kind every day. I never had anyone treat my mother with disrespect or rudeness. She was comfortable and everything she asked for (bedside commode, water, help) was given with a smile.   The Nurses of 3N are amazing people.

After spending the afternoon down at the Dino world, we needed to eat, I played Yelp Roulette and landed on Smoking Aces, Just off I4, Across the street from StingRay Chevrolet.   It doesn't look like much. It's a small shack with a large area of barbed wire wrapping it's perimeter, so you're pretty safe there.   Entering, you're greeted and seated. What I didn't realize is that there was a lot of seating out back as well, I bet during peak season over the summer, that place is PACKED.   We were seated and our waitress was right over, she was very pleasant and warm, very friendly.  We chatted a bit about the sauces, about the appetizers and which we'd like more, all in all, we selected the onion rings.   When the onion rings came out, they were in a house made batter that reminded me of country fair onion rings, that were golden delicious and oh so tasty. I did the smart thing and only ate 2 while the husbeast polished off most of the plate.   When our food came I was surprized at the portions. I'd ordered the 3 meat combo with Ribs, Wings and Brisket.  I got just that, but where I was supposed to get only 3 wings, I ended up getting 5, the ribs were large and meaty and the brisket was so good and tender.   The hubby got a burger topped with bacon and cheese, having added them in.  Neither of us could finish our food, so we had extra for another meal later. I know that I'll be back again when I'm that area.

This was such a treasure to stumble upon a couple of weekends ago.  The Beau and I had just had a lovely date night down in St. Pete and were looking to extend it a bit longer.  The first night spot we had wanted to go to, looked WAY too busy so we had decided to just go home when I spied this on the road side.   We did a u-Turn and stopped in.  Inside was chill and relaxed, a totally nice atmosphere. The Kavatenders were cool. This was my first experience, so we let out tender lead the way. I was also able to purchase some of my favorite Delta-8 CBD Chewables there! I was so happy.   Once we had our drinks, we went out and listened to some Awesome Karaoke, while we played a couple of games of pool, and several times the others there invited us to share in the snacks that were provided. We were encouraged to join in, which was really awesome. The vibe there was one of inclusion.   I left a few of my kindness rocks behind, I hope others found them and they made them smile.

I've been coming to Tampa Rejuvenation for almost 2 years. I started out at their former location on Hillsboro ave and have followed over to where the are now on Linebaugh.    The staff has been ever evolving and ever changing. They're wonderful, every one of them.  I absolutely -hate- having to get used to new girls so frequently though.  You get close to certain techs and then -BOOM- they're gone.  Please stop playing roulette with your techs.   The place is small, but neat, the receptionists are warm and friendly. The techs are great and caring, and Doctor Lomboi is an awesome doctor.

One of my favorite places on Earth. Why?/it's Home. Growing up, we would come to this Area of Tarpon to see the Sponge Docks, to walk the cobble brick streets, to see the Yia Yias in their black dresses on their way to St. Nicholas' Orthodox Church.   Hellas is a favorite stop, but you can't forget the Limani or Dimitri's on the water for food. If you like antiques Main Street has them by the shop full and they are quality finds.   But most of all what this Area has is a small town flavor that's unique. The people are friendly, even though they hold the Epiphany on January 6 and people come from all over to see it. It is still a humble place and still my home town.

Very large park located in Dunedin. I came in off Michigan avenue, right near the ball field, and stayed to the Palm path and I know that I didn't see much of it.  I walked for about an hour and enjoyed my afternoon in sacred silence.   I like that the paths here are large and open, that there are some information plaques and that the city keeps the place well maintained (Though what's up with the Fern path?) and for the most part clear of trash. I took a bag with me and picked up along the way.   The diverse wild life is alive and well out in the woods, the birds are especially plentiful, I saw an eagle while I was out there as well as a few Hawks.  It was pretty awesome.

My guy took me here for a date night and I was rightly impressed. The food was AMAZING!  The atmosphere was relaxing and warm, almost comforting. It was just what you wanted. Cozy and charming.  I had their Pork Fried rice and the Goyza, both were DELICIOUS. The Goyza were fresh and tasty! They were perfection.  I ended up only being able to eat about 1/3rd of the rice, so I took it home only to eat it later in the evening.  This is on the Must return list.

I've driven by this place so many times and always wondered if they were open. The slat blinds are ALWAYS closed. After reading through Yelp reviews, I asked the Beau if he wanted to go there, and he was game.   We pulled up at about 12:30, and there was plenty of open seating. It was a bit warm inside - (it;s been chilly so either the heat was on or the ac just wasn't on so it was stuffy)  We chose where we wanted to sit and were handed menus a few minutes later.   We both ordered sweet tea and neither of us were disappointed, this was SOUTHERN STYLE sweet tea. It was good.  We were offered bread before our meals and it was FRESH, topped with rosemary, and still warm on the inside. SO TASTY!  I ordered the fried chicken, I was told to order 1/2 chicken - all white, with sides of black eyed peas and the fried green tomatoes, which is what I ordered. The beau ordered the Magnolia burger, neither of us was disappointed with what we got. My meal could have fed both of us without any issue. The breasts of the chicken were HUGE! THe wings were thick and TASTY. I ate the wings, and the breasts came home with me.   The black eyed peas were gone in a hot minute, they were -THAT- good, and the fried green tomatoes were some of the best I've ever eaten.  The beau had the burger, which was hand formed, and cooked to perfection.  He ordered his with fried okra and it was just right. It was also HUGE so he could not finish it.  Sadly we were too full to order the coconut cream pie that we wanted.   Would i come back?OH hell yes. IN a heart beat.

I've been using John Smith Plumbing since I can remember. My dad and he were friends and I went to school with the son, Jr.   I was disappointed that they were 4 hours late and there was no communication from them to let me know. My service appt was originally from 12-2, my actual service time was at 6pm.   As for the service, no problem. Quick and efficiently done.

Here for my CEU's, and it was the first time I've had a chance to be at this hotel. The training room was large and kept at a comfortable temperature.  This is usually the biggest issue when it comes to a training seminar and they were able to keep us all happy.   The restrooms were clean and well stocked, and in general the hotel had a clean and neat appearance. I greatly appreciated the free coffee in the lobby.

Nice, clean local smoke shop run by one sarcastic SOB.    There is a nice selection of product from glass, to electric, papers to Kratom. You can choose what ever you like and they're happy to help you out.

Wall Springs park has become my new favorite park of all times! This place is absolutely beautiful, jam packed with places to walk and things to visit and see.  The Playground is suitable for all children, I like that they have it divided for younger and older kids. The trails are great if you're into hiking and of course it's right off the Pinellas Trail so you can bike or what have you with ease.   The backstory behind Wall Springs park is pretty cool too. Apparently Mr Wall owned the place at the turn of the 1900's and had people come here to soothe the aches and pains in the mineral springs. People did that up until the 1950's and 60's. In 1988, the city of Palm Harbor bought it and began preserving it.   The Tower is especially wonderful as it is fully accessible with a wheelchair ramp for all three stories. in fact all their docks  are ramps so that everyone can enjoy the Florida natural view.   The parkinglot is exemplary, it's huge so there is no reason to fight over spaces, and both restrooms are clean and tidy.

What a great little cafe!   Tucked away in a strip mall on SR54, you'll find this little gem of a place nestled next to Beall's. It's got a unique flavour all it's own, that's lent from Greek roots and a chef with good taste.   Today I visited with my mom, so that we could go spend the Beall's cash I earned during Black Friday.  The service was awesome and quick. The food was delicious. I ordered a western Omelette and mom ordered a strawberry banana crepe. Both came out just as we asked and both were simply decadent.   I'll find time to come back in the near future.

I don't think I've been here since I was 8 or 9, when friends of mine were having a birthday party and it was here. Back then this was Brooker Creek Park, not to be confused with the preserve.   This park is HUGE. It has a gorgeous lakefront, which I've only ever seen in glimpses as I drove past to the shelter we always met at.  They have a huge playground, a dog park and lots of walking trails. The park is fantastic for doing what you need to be doing: Living life.   People come here to walk, run, bike ride, train, do fitness things and what have you. We have a rock painting group that has a shelter and during the cooler (heh) summer months we meet here and it's absolutely lovely.

With Auditions done, a few of us wanted to hang out until The Vault lit the lights in honor of Pride and the victims of the Orlando Mass Shooting.  We were hungry, so we looked down the street and spied Eddie & Sam's.  From Previous experience, we know this place to be hoppin! We've seen people here ALL the time, so we thought we'd chance it.  The prices were reasonable and the slices were huge. Heck, I mistakenly ordered 2 slices of white pizza, not aware of their size, but I was sorely wrong.. I barely got through one.. I ended up sharing the slices with the others.   The taste was good, and the way my friends ate at their slices, they absolutely LOVED it.  Would we come here again? You betcha!

We needed libations for the evening. Though we didn't find the Ciroc we were looking for, we did get some Grey Goose for $18.99 which is a decent price for a quality alcohol. Service was quick and efficient.

This is the economy parking at the Tampa International airport. It's approximately 1 mile from the actual terminal, but that's OK, because it's 1. Covered, 2. has a tram shuttle that runs ever 7-10 minutes to take you to your boarding area and 3. there are Many, many, MANY places to park.   The rate is a flat fee per day, so don't lose the ticket you were given when you pulled in. Always take a picture of where you parked so you don't lose your car - lord knows it happened to me and we saw it happen to a lady on our last trip. You -think- you parked on 2, but you REALLY parked on 3.  Always lock your car before you leave. And please, PLEASE remember to tip the driver, it's customary for a tip of $1 per bag. (I work on a tipped basis in another industry, trust me, you'll make his day)

The Todd is such a friendly place. Well lit, the parking lot is not a sketchy place. The inside of the store is bright and welcoming, the employees are always friendly and willing to help you with anything you might need.  They're able to let you see products, let you feel the sensations (yes, vibrations) of different toys with batteries. They're more than happy to let you see what the straps on certain items are like as well, there is no hesitation at all from them.  And you can't forget about the lube bar either! This is the best adult store in Tampa!  Oh! And I'd be remiss if I didn't mention the lingerie, shoes and stockings section. it's not just for dancers! They have something for everybody. If you want a costume at Halloween, if you want a corset for dress up or if you're looking for a wig, this is a place I would recommend you check out. Their prices are really good!

I stopped in to get some stamps that I'd seen during the Halloween season, spooky sillouhettes, and I was lucky that they still had them.  They had cookies and coffee out for the patrons as a gesture of warmth and kindness during this holiday season. (As nice as it is, I saw two people taking cookies without napkins and touching others in the process, and another woman sneezed near by. GROSS)  The clerks were cheerful and friendly and I bought 3 books of stamps for the holiday season. No issues.

New location of CSC out off of 54 in Trinity.  Lovely new building, plenty of seating.   Upon entering, my friend, who'd never been at a CSC location got to try several different types of chicken salad before deciding what she wanted to eat.   We both chose to get THE SCOOP and added a scoop so that we could try two different types of chicken salad and have their most delightful Chicken tortilla soup. SO GOOD!  The service was friendly and warm. I hope that this location thrives.

HUGE Macy's store at the King of Prussia Mall. A stand alone store that connects via pathway to the mall.  It's 3 stories of shopping paradise.  They even have a clearance outlet on their bottom floor.   I didn't encounter any employees while I was wandering through, but the store was transitioning from fall to winter and the heat was on and blazing inside - thankfully since it was miserably cold outside.  Unfortunately that makes it uncomfortable when you're wearing all your outside layers inside. *chuckles*   There was a lot of sales going on, a lot of LOOK AT ME kind of signage to grab your attention, and that's what its for. I however was a woman on a mission and didn't have time (or the luggage space) so I didn't have a chance to shop.

I'll be the first to admit that visiting Busch Gardens at night harkens back to the darkness in my soul and the "Dark Side of the Gardens, where shovels scrape along the ground and bushes startle in the shadows, but none of that happened.  What did happen was nothing short of magical.  I kind of knew what to expect, I'd gotten a few hints from friends working the event: 80 miles of lights - yes MILES of lights. Carolers, snow men and snow drifts, light shows and ice skating, and who could forget Jimmy Osmond, but what I wasn't expecting was how lovely it would all turn out to be.   Upon entering the park, your eyes are greeting with the most entrancing color scheme you'll ever see. Morocco at Christmas is simply stunning with it's purples and golds.  Each area you walk into is themed beautifully in all it's brightly lit glory for you to wonder at, and trust me, your inner 4 year old will gawp at it just like mine did, pointing at this and that with a smile -so- wide.   There are surprises around corners, lighting effects that change, music that is coordinated with lights so spectacularly that you will not believe it. And of course, there are the Angels!   Be sure that you check out the ice skating show that they've put on just for this event. It is spectacular. The little girl will steal your heart away.    The sing along train is by far one of the most fun ways to get around the park, it will lift your spirits as you chug from Stanleyville to "North Pole Station" Right outside Santa's house. When you do go to see the Big Man himself, don't forget to get your cookie from Mrs. Claus!  Ride Cheetah Hunt in the dark for a more spectacular ride. I swear! It felt like it was torqued up a few notches. It felt faster, it felt more intense in the dark. My 72 year old Mother, who'd never ridden it, fell in love with the beast!   All in all, this is going to become a New Holiday Tradition!   Well Done!

Color me surprised when driving down US19, I spied a familiar sign, but it SHOULDN'T have been there!  I was both amused and pleased to see The TODD now has a location on this side of the bay!  Known in the area as a very female positive, sex positive shop, the Todd is one of the most friendly adult shops you could ever hope to go into, and this location is no exception.  It is staffed by some young folks, but don't let that stop you from going in and checking out their merchandise.   They have a quality selection of hosiery, lingerie, shoes for the enthusiast. There is the usual collection of lubes, lotions and games for those that like to play them.  And we can't forget what the Todd is really about.. the toy collection! There is everything you could -ever- want there!  From bullets to butt plugs, dongs to strap-ons. They are your one stop adult shop.  They are well lit, well ventalated, no creepy corners for anyone to pop out at you from.  There are no video booths and no places you'll find people lurking.  The guys & gals that work there are helpful and approachable. Batteries are free with toy purchase and they have a lube bar so you can try before you buy.  ALWAYS a plus.

Please wear your mask, as we're in covid season. The dispensary is currently practicing social distancing so if there are more than 4 people in the lobby you'll be asked to wait out in your car. Be patient, your time will come.   Non-descript looking location in an older strip mall across from Ihop and Home Depot in Palm Harbor on Us 19. On the outside, it's nothing to look at. On the inside, the decor is warm and inviting. Once you have given your id, and they set up your profile and sign you up for their programs, they invite you back to their dispensary, its bright white and orange, it's lovely.   The tenders here are friendly, energetic and knowledgable. The product is mostly kept out of site except the few things that are out on display, things that are tangible so those of us who aren't in the know, get a little more knowledge. I felt comfortable asking, never talked down to.   Over all, I felt that MUV was a really nice experience. I will be back.

An Ybor City staple, New York, New York Pizza is a stop you have to make. I've been visiting Ybor for AGES and i'd avoided it forever until now.   The other night after a comedy show, I was hungry and needed food, so with the others in my party, we made our way down to NYNY and indulged in a slice each. I got the Grandmother's pizza, the toppings were a bit sparse, but the crust was good, especially when they heated it through in their big ovens.   I'd indulge again!

I paint rocks. It's my newest addiction. I was told that I'd be able to get my Santorini flats and other pebbles here for reasonable prices and people weren't wrong.   The Santorini flats are currently priced at $1.29 a pound and that's a pretty good deal, considering I bought 35 pounds of them for painting purposes.  I also picked up some pretty pink and green pebbles that will be made and passed out.   Service here was fantastic. As I said, I bought rocks, I had bagged in a grocery bag and was struggling to bring up to the counter. The owner himself carried it inside for me.  That's pretty dedicated to the service of your clientele.  I'll visit frequently!  Well as frequently as I go through my stones.

This store is DANGEROUS to me! Well, to my pocket book. They have so many good things!   I stopped in recently, and I walked out with far too many new tchotchkies. The new coffee cups will hold my paint brushes and be gifted to friends. The candles will be gifts that have dual purpose because the jars they're in are bowls or collectibles. They're just too cute.   I just can't get enough.

I stopped in with the Husbeastie because we wanted to try something new.   The order stations want a WHOLE lot of information before you ever place your order, I think that's a bit of a PITA. I don't want to have to give you my email address in order to order food. I don't want to have to have a password to your site. I think that's a bit invasive. I get it's for client retention, but hoops aren't what I want to jump through when I'm hungry.   We placed our order: Fresh spring rolls, I got the terriakai bowl, an the husbeast go some hot noodle bowl. Everything came out hot and fresh but the taste wasn't what i was expecting.  I swear the chicken in my bowl tasted like something from KFC. I really wasn't expecting fried chicken in the Terraikki bowl at all. Oh well.

My guy and I stopped in after dinner and a quick walk around the mostly tucked in down town.  We were happy we were able to procure a table and enjoyed the atmosphere.   We shared a dessert plate and had red wine together while just having a good evening together. This is a great spot for Down Town Main Street and a gem in the Tarpon Springs area.

We wanted brunch on Sunday, but didn't want to go to our usual joint, so the Beau and I went to Buon Giorno bagles, since it was in the same shopping plaza where our favorite diner is.    It was a little after 12 when we arrived and the shop was dead, they'd already had their rush and would be closing up early because they were running out of stock.  We ordered our food: Bacon, egg and cheese and a sausage, egg and cheese on everything bagles with coffee.   The food was made by a very pleasant young woman, and the bagles were absolutely delicious. We loved them.  We'll come here more frequently since they're closer and cheaper!

I hadn't been to Sunken Gardens since I was a kid, so coming here now, when I'm in my 50's is a nice nostalgic trip down memory lane. I came here on a date with my Hubby who'd never been.  Now we came in Fall so not much was in bloom, but it was still a lovely afternoon.   THe birds were a joy to see and I think there was even a small wedding while we were there.   This is a land mark, a gorgeous place to visit and keep in the heart of the city for years on end.

I've read the reviews and finally I decided to check Toula's trailside cafe out. It's in the neighborhood, so I don't know why it took so long.  Inside, it's not much to look at. it's bright but loud, yet it's VERY friendly. The waitresses are super warm and happy to have you there. You can tell there's a lot of regulars that visit.   We got our menu and took a few minutes to peruse, then we placed our orders. I got the Honey Almond Chicken salad, and my friend got himself the pressed cuban. Both of us opted for the potato salad.  We were both pleased with what we got to eat.  I will say that there was no crunch from the almonds in the chicken salad, but it was tasty other wise, and the potato salad was very good.   I'll come back to check out the strawberry nutella crepes. YUM~

Last night, after the Christmas Event (Don't get me started.. UGH) in Tarpon Springs, The husbeast and I were hungry. We didn't want our usual fare so we decided to try someplace new.  We rolled the bones and Yianni's is where we decided to go.   Yianni's is new-ish, clean and attractive with patio and back patio sitting areas right in front of the Sponge-o-Rama museum torward the first third of Dodecanese boulevard in Tarpon Springs, so it's not hard to miss. The metal tables and chairs out front can be chilly if it's been windy but after walking as we had (our parking last night was NOT prime) it was a welcome change.  There was one Waitress on at Yianni's last night, so service wasn't FAST, but it wasn't slow either, Yvonne was great. She was attentive and friendly. And when we placed our orders she listened and took care of everything.   The husband and I ordered the tzatziki and pita appetizer, and their Tzatziki game is strong.  It's good, cool and cream with just the right balance of cucumber and garlic. VERY NOM!  We had upgraded from the house salad to the Greek salad (With POTATO SALAD! this was on the menu for emphasis) and those came out first and were huge. I was pleased to see it wasn't the usual iceburg lettuce crap but Romaine, Feta (usually that's extra) a large dollop of potato salad, onions, tomato, olive, garbanzo bean and cucumber. It was a hearty salad, you almost didn't need a meal after this.   And when the meals came out, their portions for the platters were excellent. As you can see by the photos, you most certainly had left overs - ok I had left overs as did the husbeast. The Souvlaki was perfectly grilled, had a nice garlic mince and the potatoes were tasty too. I didn't eat the pita since I was already full of bread.  Their Gyro mix of lamb and beef was perfect! A bit more lamb than I'm used to, but I am -not- complaining, it was unctuous in the mouth, a very sexy combination.   Yes, I'd come back again. They offer coupons when you're walking in the afternoons down the Docks. Stop in and try Yianni's they're a

After a long evening at Busch Gardens, I wanted food, but not something gross or greasy, so I opted for Taco Bus. Their menu is pretty simple, you choose WHAT you want - as in style of food, be it taco, burrito, quesidilla etc and then you choose your meat, or perhaps a vegetarian option.   You place your order, and then you take a seat.... and wait.  The wait isn't terribly long and the food is deliciously fresh.   While they're currently open 24/7, as of 12/9/13 their hours are going to change. Keep this in mind.

Do you like teddy Bears? I do. Do you like making them? Well Build-a-Bear lets you do just that. And if you like fanbears, you can make one of those too! You can have a Wookie bear or a MLP bear (Pony?) and you can dress them in the cutest little outfits too! Prices can be expensive, but the cuteness is worth it. My favortie is the black dragon from "How to train your dragon"

I like checking out card shops. I love greeting cards and you just never know what you might find.    This little shop was much the same.. lots of cool cards and stationary and in the back a great collection of gifts. Some awesome deals on clearance too. Some of it was "out of season" but seasons come right around again, so I was able to pick up some Halloween gifts (Yes, I give Halloween gifts, don't you?) that will likely be given as birthday gifts. ;) for a really good price!

I stopped into McDivots for two main reasons, 1. they were close to work and 2. I wanted wings.  Nary a soul was there, the 4 people in attendance were all at the bar, so I did the same. I sat at one of the many chairs and was promptly handed a menu, and then a 2nd menu for the Happy Hour options.   The service was very quick, there were maybe 20 tv's in the place, all seeming to be tuned to a different station with some annoying sports program. I suppose I can't get upset by that, it is a sports bar, after all.   After perusing both menus, I opted for the Fried Pickles and the 1/4 pound chili dog sans onions. The fried pickles were wonderful, quite deliciously tart and tangy, the sauce was interesting, but the ranch dressing I ordered on the side was yum.  The chilli dog cane on a huge roll smothered with chili and cheese and a side of what appeared to be home made chips.  The dog its self was good, the chilli was mediocre at best, a bit on the sweet side, but certainly home made. The chips though.. they were stale. I ate one and didn't bother to have another.   The Barkeep never let my diet coke go empty, and when I asked for it to go, she did so very quickly.  I made a pit stop in the restroom to find their toilet just running, the float had gone bad, it was a simple, quick fix, so I took care of that for them.   I would come back to try their wings... maybe.

Far better selection than they had when they first opened! I'm glad I gave them a 2nd shot. One of the cleaner Ross' in the area too.. fairly well organised.   I went with a friend to take a look at the offerings and see if they had any options for a Christmas party, and lo and behold, I found exactly what I was looking for!    I ended up buying far more than I intended, but I'm certainly not upset that I did! I got basically a whole holiday wardrobe for less than $100.00.

Having been to another GG location, I had high expectations. Sadly I was disappointed.   I was part of a party of 10, celebrating a birthday. We arrived somewhat early, but the place was not busy, a smattering of people, but far from bustling at all.  We asked if it'd be possible that those of us who were there (including the person who made the reservation/Birthday girl) could be seated while we waited for the rest of the group. They agreed, as our area was ready for us.   We were seated, more than 50% of our party was there, and we placed our drink orders - beers on their Thirsty Thursday menu (basically a bogo offer) and a few of their specialty sodas and water all around. These took FOREVER to get, in fact one of the beers took far longer than the others to arrive, and had to be asked for 4 times, by 3 different people.  We ordered our apps too, those came out fast and were tasty.   When our party was assembled, we waited.. and waited... one of our party had to go get our waitress. She was no where to be found.  Basically our party of ten was set aside and forgotten about until one of us got her attention. When we placed our orders, she didn't even bother to give a bowl over view for those who'd never been there.. it was pretty much a crap show when it came to service.   The food was really tasty though, we were pretty happy with the quality of the ingredients, though many of the food containers were more than half empty. I understand when the place isn't busy, but it really just looks unappealing.   Drinks that were refillable, weren't unless we asked for it, Waters ran dry. So, It's not a statement on the food, but rather the lack of concern over the customer service. I'm -glad- that no automatic gratuity was added into our bill, as I don't think it warranted that kind of gratituity. 15% perhaps, but not nearly 20%  Will I come back? Only if the husbeast wants to.

Ok, ok, ok! You all know I like bargain shopping. There's no question about it.  I'm a sucker for saving(while spending) money.  But someone is going to have to keep me away from this store.  When we stepped inside after catching a movie, we were overwhelmed by the sheer mass of merchandise, not only that but how absolutely neat it was. The store is bright, clean and colorful.  The first thing I really took notice of was an end cap of Pez dispensers. There were so many! I not even talking about "vintage" styles or even slightly out of date ones. These were current issue. That was cool.  They really seem to have EVERYTHING. I saw: sports bras, t-shirts with witticisms, kitty ear headbands, basket balls, diaries, arts n crafts, bobble heads, cosmetics (PROfusion comes to mind), iPhone accessories, adult coloring books, school supplies and so much more!  I found things I wanted, a few small necessities and extravagances, but I didn't pay more than $35, because as the name implies everything is $5 or less.  Yeah, I'll be back.

I was craving wings. Like SERIOUSLY craving wings and nothing was working so we stopped into this plaza and noticed a new pizza shop. Pizza goes naturally with wings, and I was right.   The former Crisper's location wasn't busy, but the service was pretty awesome. Our waitress took our order - we ordered their special 20 wings and a large pie for $32, and we got some fried mushrooms. The Mushrooms came out 10 of them for about $8.00 a bit pricy, but they were tasty fried morsels of yumminess.   The wings came out and though we ordered Medium - they were pretty heated. The husbeast at 8 and I ate 4,  The pizza, they left it in a little long, I'm ok with that, i like my crust crispy, but the Owner was very apologetic, He offered to throw a new pie in for us. He didn't need to.   They are over priced for their location. Crispers didn't make it and if they want to, they're going to have to come down a bit to match.

One of the hardest to get to from US19, it's near the construction off of 19 near 60, but coming from the shopping center, it's all right.   I stopped in to get some diet cola and red bull for a drive down to St. Pete so I could work my magic on some folks. The place was clean and the staff was friendly, and gas prices were low.

I like Queens Pizza, I enjoy the food but today's service was.. confusing to say the least.   I came in around 7 pm this evening, it as just myself, no one else, and I was shown to a booth. I was given a menu and was told that my waitress would be with me in a moment. OK! There were a few families in the dining room, it was not a horribly busy evening, so when the waitress came to take my order, I gave it fairly simply: An order of their Homemade Spanokipita (Spinach and feta cheese wrapped in phylo dough & baked) and a Gyro no onions with the sauce on the side.  And an unsweetened iced tea.  Pretty simple and straight forward.  When the waitress comes back, she puts the menu down again (?) and 2 iced teas (I'm guessing for my invisible guest?)  As she makes a round, I point out that I've already placed my order, and that there is no one joining me, so I'm not sure why she gave me a 2nd tea.. With out an apology or an explanation, the tea and menu were taken away, and the waitress had a very confused look on her face, It probably matched mine.  The food came rather quickly. The Spinach & cheese pie was good, it could have used a bit of salt, but other than that, it was just what i wanted. But the Gyro. *sigh* this was a disappointment. I live in a Greek town, I am Greek by birth. When I order a Gyro, I generally expect meat that has been carved off of a spinning spit, that has been slow roasted all day, so there are roasted bits and crunchy bits. What I got was a pita, filled with 5 slices of pre-formed, poorly made, mostly chicken (or that's how it tasted) "gyro" meat. Meat that has never seen a spit or a Gyro roaster.  It was mediocre tasting at best.

It may have been a bit of a drive, but it really was worth it.  I decided to go to The Tartan Table because a friend recommended it to me.  She'd seen it in the Tampa Tribune.  I'm glad I took her cue as the moment I walked into the (outside) Non-descript shopping center, I was really happy.   The place is small 9-10 tables at most, it's decorated in a lovely fashion, with kilts and other Scottish paraphanelia.  It feels comfortable and homey and smells divine.   I'm not sure that the staff was expecting a busy Sunday, as there was one person waiting tables and one person cooking, so that made things a bit slow (hence 4 stars), but everything was worth waiting for.   We were served fresh made bread with real butter and our food was made to order, this is part of the reason for the wait. Nothing is pre-packaged or frozen. It's all made RIGHT THEN, so there's going to be some waiting.  When it was delivered to our table, my stomach literally growled.  I ordered the Shepard's Pie and the Husbeast ordered the Angus Burger.  Each of us was satisfied with our meal. The Shepard's pie was absolutely scrumptious. The brown gravy that the meat was cooked in was rich and tasty. The Angus burger was cooked to perfection, but was lacking the bacon that the husband ordered. All in all a small issue.   The service, for it being one waitress was attentive. I felt sorry for the girl as she had to juggle everyone, but she handled it nobly. She was running her butt off!   This is a place that I am sure I will return to in the future. I really am looking forward to trying the Scotch Eggs, and having my husband try the haggis!   This is my 300th review!

Took my father-in-law out to dinner since we were in Brandon. He suggested Allegria since he'd been there a few times in the past. He related that they make all their food from scratch, everything is made in house, so we agreed and he let us know where it was.  We arrived, and though we had no reservations, we were seated quickly, and our waiter came over almost immediately to take out drink orders and give us recommendations on the specials. Our app orders were places, and since I'm a fan of a Caprese salad, we started with that. The slices of tomato were huge, the basil was plentiful, the only thing that would have made it top notch would have been salt on the table so that I could have accented the flavor.  Dinner consisted of a pork dish - I couldn't begin to type out the name, but when it was served, it looked like a German Weinerschnitzel, topped with a basil tomato salad, that was SO good. The husband had a veal dish and these potatoes with bacon and cheese that were to die for and my Father in Law had a seafood dish that, well, me, I'm biased, I don't do sea food, it looked good.   All in all, the food was great, the service was fine and I would come back anytime I'm in Brandon.

This is right down from where I work, so I'm going to be a regular.   The food is quick and very tasty. The prices are reasonable. I love the fact that they have SO much out door seating so that every one with a pup can congregate outside.   Today, I ordered their soup and salad combo and was pleasantly pleased with both size and freshness of the plate.  For the $8 I spent I was well satisfied.  The others at work ordered Mushroom Chicken which was SO decadently delicious and a Waldorf chicken salad sandwich which was huge.   All in all, I'd say that they are worth a visit or 14.

So, since I had coupons, and I was visiting a friend who happens to live RIGHT BEHIND the place, we stopped in and ordered food before heading out to the Shallow Grave.   It was nice, I ordered the Bacon Cheese burger combo and used my coupon for a free shake. The service was amazingly quick and I even had a little chat with the Manager. he remembered me from the event. :)   There's a dinner rush, but there's a slump afterwards, and that's sad. The place is good, and the food is fast and fresh. More people should come here.

I remember when Good WIll was filled with cast offs, when you could find much needed costume pieces. I went to good will, looking for gloves, you know, the kind ladies used to wear. And I couldn't find a damned pair.  Not a single one was to be found in this place.   I did find a great pair of boots, though, so that makes up for the lack of gloves.

Well our Whole payche.. I mean Whole foods opened, and I finally got around to visiting. It's amazing what they did with the former bottom floor of Sears!   The store is nice, well laid out and has a good floor plan. The people who work there are friendly enough, kind and welcoming, but a lot of them WON'T move out of your way if they're in it. The isles are tight when you have a cart and people are just flippin' entitled.   Theres a fine selection of everything, I can't wait to explore the hot bar and the salads, but sadly, with a migraine, I wanted nothing to do with any of that today. I just had fun going up and down the isles, picking out things I thought would be good.   Lambec beers are plentiful, they had a decent selection of other items as well, but one thing they didn't have a grand selection of - and I was kind of disappointed in - was the lack of essential oils and what have you. I'm used to there being more of them.   The coffee bar was delightful, if slow.   i just wish the people who shopped there were nicer. I swear to dog, half of them have forgotten simple manners, the use of Excuse me, and Thank You. They don't bother to move, they don't bother to make eye contact. The entitlement was thick. *sad*

Since visiting the original location, we were tipped off about the newer/more posh location on Hillsboro avenue, so.. after an afternoon with screaming 2 year olds, the husbeastie and I made our way there and decided to have a late lunch before they closed.   As expected, there was a wait to be seated, so we gave our name to the gentleman at the door and had a seat. About 15 minutes later, perhaps less, we were escorted to a table near the window and immediately were accosted by the dim sum cart. We politely declined, much to the apparent dismay of the cart's owner.   We were there with a specific purpose, Salt & Pepper Calamari as well as the Yummy Chicken.  When our waitress appeared, she took our drink orders, then our food orders. We'd placed the calamari order as an appetizer, but it came out after the rest of the food was delivered.   Over all,the food was delicious - even if the calamiari tasted a bit "fishy", when it hasn't in the past. The chicken lettuce cups and the Yummy chicken were both fabulous. We will certainly come back when we're craving the more authentic Chinese food.

My first time in a Tropical Smoothie place, and while the decor was a bit run down, the service was great. I especially like that they give a nutritional breakdown on their foods if you're on a restricted diet.   The food we ordered was tasty. They offer Breakfast and lunch as well as smoothies all day, so it makes for an easy to grab kind of meal.

My favorite car wash shares the lot with the storage, so I think they're hand in hand kind of business partners.   The car wash is the kind where you put your quarters in and the time counts down. You provide all the labour. Which I'm fine with. It's what I prefer. Here for about $8 I'm able to do what I need to do to get my car as clean as I like it. Though I hate to say the "Spot free rinse" isn't as spot free as I'd like it to be.

This would have been higher if there hadn't have been a hair in my food.   Do you ever get curious about the name of a place? Sometimes it's just that simple for me. Carmel evokes rich, sensuous things for me. So I thought this might be what i found at Carmel Cafe & Wine bar.  I invited a friend along for the afternoon's foody adventure, and here is what we found.   Upon arriving, we noticed that the location was lovely! Outside the seating was plush and comfortable, with couches as well as tables. Inside, it was intimate and cozy with warm oranges and reds, very visually appealing.  We were given the choice to order old school or by the "newfangled" ipad.  I'm an old school girl and chose the menu.    Our waiter came over and helped us place our order, offering a few suggestions but in the end we opted for a few different things. A red pepper humus, the spinach artichoke dip, a margharita flat bread, a bowl of their tomato basil soup and a glass of white sangria.  When it all came to the table, everything looked delicious, that is until I reached for the flat bread, and noticed a long, dark hair across the slice. I checked my photos as well, because 1. I have red hair. 2. the waiter had short blonde hair, and my date, he has dark hair, but it's short.  I had to call a waitress over, since my waiter wasn't around, and point this out.  She came and took the food away. Our waiter came over and appoloized profusely. The flat bread was remade.   The food was good. The humus came with an olive tepenade which gave it a lovely texture and a bit of heat, nothing terrible, but very interesting on the tongue.   The spinach dip was amazing, and by far my favorite of the meal. The flat bread was good, but needed -something-. Salt had to do. The soup? Not good. It didn't get eaten. It was bitter, and .. I just can't put my finger on it.  The sangria was delicious.   We would come here again, because the service was good. The food was over priced.

Since my surgery, My body has been having odd cravings. VERY specific cravings. Today it was pepperoni pizza.  I figure it's my body's way of saying -try it.. see if you can eat it- and who am I to judge?  Instead of chain pizza, I decided I wanted to try this place I've driven by so many times, but never stopped in.  Convinced the husbeast that this is the place we should try. He agreed.   The moment we walked in, we were enveloped in the succulent scents of -good- Italian food.  We arrived as they were doing an employee turn over, so although our order was taken, it took some time for any of the food to come to us.   We were not offered any bread, so as I said.. it took some while for our Caprese (or as they call it Mozarella Fraisce) Salad to arrive.  When it did arrive, it was absolutely delicious.  The pizza, it was New York Style, so thin crust, rich, fresh sauce and lots of 'roni.  It was -very- good pizza.    All in all, the food was really good, even though the service was a bit slow-ish. I would CERTAINLY eat here again!

Had lunch here with an former beau before he set out for his next chapter.  Neither of us had ever eaten there, so we figured why not.   We were given the choice to eat inside or out, being it's summer in Florida, we opted for inside and chose a table at the back so we could talk. It wasn't very busy.   Our hostess was also our waitress and she was very knowledgable and friendly, she told us about the burger and beer special and gave us a few minutes to look at the menu.   He ended up getting a sandwich and I ordered the garlic parmesan wings, since they sounded very good.  I was not disappointed when the food was delivered. His sandwich was large and filled with good things and my wings were swimming in butter, lots of garlic and a ton of cheese. They made my mouth water and my tummy was really happy.   We ate and talked and had a great time.  I know I'll come back here in the ffuture

Lay-Z-Boy furniture is not for those who are not willing to put out the money for quality. If you want to do that, go to RTG. Here, you truly do get what you pay for. This is our 2nd purchase from this particular store, and they've always been quick and efficient.   We're going to be the proud owners of a new wide seat, low armed recliner rocker. I can't wait for it to be delivered!

A kitschy little place to grab a meal, it apparently has won a lot of awards in the local area.  We stopped for lunch, as the Scot needed to check out our idea of a 'Scottish' town - he thought it was quaint, , at about 2pm, and found that the patio was full but the inside was fairly empty.  Inside was dark, but it didn't remind me of a living room more like a librsry. We sat near a bookcase, it had a box, I snooped, now apparently I have a date at midnight with someone who will be wearing a red dress and heels.   The Food Was VERY good. I had the house salad and 1/2 of a chicken salad sandwich. The sandwich was a touch smoky, a touch spicy,  but it was so full of meat that it kept spilling out of my sandwich and onto my plate.  The Scot indulged in a burger with grilled onions and cheese with sweet potato fries. He said it was quite tasty. Given the chance I'd certainly come back, as the lunch menu is limited.

If you like to get things at a good price, and don't mind a revolving inventory, then you'll like shopping at Ollie's Bargain outlet.   Think of it like a BigLots, but on Steroids.  Seriously!  The products are similar, you can find just about everything there - from books and paper goods to housewares. There were rugs and bedding and even furniture being sold in the store. A small clothing section was found up front.   The only thing this store seemed to be missing was a frozen food section, but I wouldn't put that past them.   The prices were excellent, they claim up to 70% off retail, what I found was more to be 40-50% below the cost you'd pay at your local big box store, and it's for last season's merchandise, all of it was still good, nothing was out of date. Though I did find one book that was marked "unsaleable" I should have taken a picture of that (Dan Brown's DaVinci Code - I think).  The staff was incredibly polite and very friendly. I could see myself coming up to Hudson to visit this store from time to time. As it was I spent nearly $100 on things today, snagging some new Serta Pillows for the bed among my many treasures.

I found myself looking over their Halloween costume selection. I wasn't impressed with the generic items of "Sexy this or that.. " I mean really.. Sexy police officer is over done and how often do we need to see Pimp and ho done? It's been done to death. And for children, there is the requisite Elsa and Anna costumes. Of course there's the plethora of cheap wigs and colored accessories but NOTHING screams originality. And to me. Halloween is an original holiday.   But what got me is that when i went to check out - yes I found rainbow leg warmers for a clown costume - I waited 8 minutes while one transaction went thru. How slow can someone be? The other register was handling a return, but she didn't call anyone over when she finished. Seriously not the best service.

This was the place where we got together to say good bye to a good friend as he departed the state to start a new chapter in his life.   It was set up as a surprise for him, thinking that only he, his fiancee and another friend were going to be there, but alas, we had a handful of his closest join in the fun.   Being as he's a smoker we took over one side of the patio, comandeering both their large outside tables and took up residence.  There was a theme night that particular evening and many of the patrons and our waitress came bedecked in their best groovy 70's fashion. We had the distinct pleasure to be served by a beautifully done David Bowie/Ziggy Stardust.   They were busy, so the service was slow due to no fault of our waitress. We were also a large party, so it's to be expected.  Drinks were beer for most of the party save 2 of us, who drank Iced tea and water.  Guiness and Yuengling were the toast of the night.   The food was Irish Bar food, by that I mean Bangers and Mash, "Irish Nachos", Fish and Chips and another friend had the house chicken dish. The food all came out hot and fresh, even the Brie and fruit plate. The only thing that threw me was that was served with yellow mustard and it went with absolutely nothing else on the plate, given it was more sweet than savory.   We had a great time. The venue was awesome and the food was delicious. I will certainly be back.

Tucked on the side of 19, it's easy to over look Marley's. But tonight I decided to take the Husbeast there for dinner. We missed the first turn and had to take the 2nd turn around.. That can get harrowing, but trust me, it's worth it.   There weren't a lot of people in the place, only another couple at the bar, and the owner, who was doing clean up around the place.  We settled in and were given menus, which has some of the most fun names for a horror freak like me. ;)   We opted to start with Monster Knuckles, or as others would call them, garlic knots, and we were not disappointed! They were really tasty. What we didn't know is that we'd be given hand made tortilla chips and hand made queso dip. All was really flavourful and YUM!  The pizza that we ordered was a pepperoni with onion, mushroom, green pepper and bacon. It came with a tasty sauce, a thin crust and it was absolutely delicious. And to keep you occupied, to actually have you interact with your party, instead of being on your cellphones, they offer up a game to play, I thought this was worth the entire time. The game consisted of 20 squares. Each filled with - something-. This month it was a picture of a pun or situation, that you had to name. At the end of the month they'll draw a winner from the people who got the most right. I Hope we did well! It wasn't easy, but it was fun.  The owner, Alan and his wife run the place, They've been in business for 4 years and it's named after their grandson, who at 6 is still a lil monster (in a good way, he's got a lot of energy) It was nice to find out the background on the place.  I can guarantee that we'll be back. the place was really nice and welcoming.

I've been to Datz on a few occasions and I've always been quite happy. Once, When I showed up with the lovely Tiffany, we had the 2nd tier to our selves.    The food was delivered quite quickly, and served up by a friendly waitress. Granted all I ordered was a salad, so it's kind of hard to make that take a long time.. but I'm sure some could.
