Over all, I think Datz is a solid place. I'd go more if it were closer.

Grabbed lunch to go on the way to Ocala.   I rather like Panera, and happen to have one of the rewards card, and share the account with my mom. Sometimes there's nothing better than a bowl of soup and some salad.   Here, the service was quick and efficient. The food was, as always tasty. Nothing too far from the middle of the road.

Do you remember the Holiday Restaurant? Where it was? How recently it closed?  Well it just moved down the street.  The owners packed up and moved to the location at the corner of Alt 19 and Anclote blvd. A building that really hasn't seen a lot of luck for those who've been at this location before. I hope that these folks do better.   The family who runs this place have a lot of good ideas. The Father, the cook, is good! He makes his own bread -it's delicious.  They make all kinds of different specialties. Today he was debuting babaganoush!   There is Karaoke on Thursday evenings, a full bar and sports events are broadcast for everyone to see. Come down and enjoy their hospitality!

Kind of like an up scale 5 Guys. Only better.   They have some of the best fries.... It might be because I'm biased and LOVE krinkle cut fries.. but there you go.  I had a bacon cheese burger, and the bacon was really thick and crisp, yet fatty. SO GOOD.

I'd come to the area to go to my usual, but I decided to go to Pacific Thai instead.   Upon entering, I noticed the place was serene and quite lovely. I was seated and the menu was given and my drink order was taken.  I ordered my usual, Jasmine Hot tea.. it's my absolute favorite.   When the waitress returned, I placed my order for black pepper and Garlic chicken.  As I waited, she brought me soup and salad, both were very good, their soup wasn't just miso, no. It was a flavourful chicken and rice. And the ginger dressing on the salad was vibrant, it made the salad.   My entree was much larger than I expected, with a small amount of rice (thankfully) to the size of the veg and meat.  The tastes mingled pleasantly and I was pleased. Sadly I wasn't able to finish my serving so I asked for a box. To my delight, the waitress whisked it away and boxed it for me, all the while, another brought a plate of sugared puffs to me.. a dessert. WOW.   So for Tea and my food ($6.95) My total was just over $10. Not a bad deal at all. I really recommend them.

Smallcakes, a cupcakery, is pretty posh! Little pretty cupcakes are displayed on pretty two tier displays behind glass, and of course the offered homemade ice cream.   Today I came in and there was a young lady behind the counter, a gentleman came in before me, and he seemed confused that they didn't sell CAKES, just cupcakes.  She was quite patient with him and explained exactly what was offered. When he wasn't ready, he allowed her to serve me.   I chose a Carmel Crunch cupcake and took it to go. Let me tell you, when I get a chocolate cupcake, I generally expect it to be somewhat dry. NOT THIS CUPCAKE! It was perfection in a cupcake. I'm not exaggerating at all. Light, fluffy and moist. The icing was delicious and though the pretzel bits were stale (they'd likely gone that way since they'd been broken and out in the atmosphere all day) the cupcake was AMAZING.  I would come again.  The reason they get four stars? How can you sell these delicious things and not offer Coffee? Bottled drinks Don't cut it. PLEASE ... Please I beg you... offer coffee soon. it is the one improvement I can suggest.

We stopped here because we saw the sign for Food & beer/wine and though we used to have a membership to the wine of the month club (Thanks dad) we'd never actually been to the Keel & Curly Winery.  When we entered, no one was there to greet us, we didn't quite understand.  So when I finally could get the attention of the woman behind the wine counter doing a tasting, she acknowledged that we could sit anywhere.. our waitress would be with us momentairly.   There were 3-4 groups of people actively engaged: 1 large group of 6 people, one couple at a table, one couple at the bar, and another small group of 2 or three, but I think they worked there. All in all it didn't look busy.   The bar tender was getting flights ready for the couple at the table, when she handed them out, she literally slammed them on the table, no smile nothing. There was a look of avarice on her face, when the guy asked a question. It was then she shot us a look and said "I'll be right with you."     She then went to the kitchen got an order for the large table and passed it out to them.  We still were not addressed. She went back to the bar and chatted with those folks some, relaxing a bit.  By now more than 10 minutes have passed since we entered, we have read the menu over by 3 times.  Since this is the "Service" We see being offered, it's not something we want part of, and we left.   This was Thursday July 5th at approximately 3:30pm.

I'm not sure what I expected. We ate here right after they opened, and I remember it being a bit more "upscale" than it was last night.  Last night it seemed a bit "run down" a bit.. I don't know, low energy?  The food was ok, the flavours were good. The husband had a Dewey burger, which he said was really flavorful and juicy. But the fries were undercooked and under seasoned. I tried one and spit it right back out. Bleah.  I ordered the twisted southern chicken, which was a chicken breast, smothered with cheese, maple bacon corn and potaotes. I wasn't sure what to expect, but it came out all stacked together. The maple bacon corn took a bit of getting used to, but it was actually pretty good. I'm not the kind of person who eats their food all touching, so this was a challenge for me. I perceviered and got through it. I ate nearly all of it too!  We even tried dessert, a slice of the melt in your mouth pecan pie.  Needed more pecans, because really it was just the ooey gooey part in the center and few pecans on top. I was kind of dissapointed by it.

On no... An Ulta opened near me. You have NO Idea how dangerous this really is.  I'm an addict. If there was a Makup Annon. I'd be there with bells on.   The new store is clean, it's well stocked and staffed.  It has the typical things you'd expect from an Ulta: A drugstore makeup selection that houses your typical brands - Maybeline, Revlon and CoveGirl as well as NYX ( which has become a very popular brand as of late) Sally Hansen for nails and other lesser brands like the Kardashians and Flower by Drew Barrymore.  Then you have the Posh side which contains the high end, expensive brands like: Too Faced, Urban Decay, Bare Minerals, Lipstick Queen and so many more.  There's the brow bar, where you can get your brows done by a brow specialist for $20(ish) dollars, and of course there are other things too.  In the center of the store is the perfume collection, all high end designer name perfumes as well as your celebrity perfumes are represented. Mostly newer perfumes, but they have quite the smelltacular perfume collection.   And at the back of the store is the Nail section with your high end polishes, your hair care and your Hair Salon where they have the salon professional hair care and the Salon that is currently in operation.   I'm SO glad it's close, I'll be able to get what I need here rather than travel to NPR or down to Sephora in JC Penneys. WHEEE! There goes my paycheck.

I needed something to tame my bangs. the Icing is an accessory store that contains earrings, hair supplies and even makeup. Everything seems to have rhinestones or other flashy items to make it stand out - Bling for a better term.   They had a sale going on buy one, get one 50% off, not bad, not the best sale, but still, pretty good. They offer makeup as well, but I've not tried their stuff. Lots of brides maid things, and things for girls graduating or even the sweet 16.   If you need something to bling up your outfit.. come to the icing.

This is the first time I have visited the Salvatore Dali museum in St. Petersburg since it was re-done. Yes, I know, BAD FLORIDA LOCAL.   I was grateful to my Husband's company for providing the complementary admission, because we were apart of the special event, The Project 34 Hackathon at the Dali.  They hackers spent 34 hours coming up with new and unique ideas with the info/tech given to them.   Since we were part of the VIP's, we were given a Guided tour of Dali's most famous works, including the newest exhibit, Dali and DaVinci, which was particularly excellent.  I understand that many people find uncomfortable, but I find his work fascinating.   The museum itself is gorgeous, with it's dedication to the Golden Mean or Fibonacci spiral, it is, in itself a work of art. A single helix staircase, the panels of glass that are individual in size and shape, no two are alike. The gardens too.. are impressive. Be sure to wander through the hedge maze and be on the look out for a particularly illusive little brass thrush who perches someplace with a mustache on his beak.   This is a world class museum, dedicated to the fanciful, often odd and yet beautiful works of Salvitore Dali. Take your time, ask questions and learn, expand your mind.

So, It's been a busy few days, the husbeast is working on a deadline and I've been getting in gear for a trip to DC, and tonight meant I had been all day in Tampa visiting my favorite Salon (Tribeca on Kennedy, Say Hi to Mikey if you will) and I really wanted to see my husband for dinner, that meant challenging traffic over to the Pinellas side of the bay.   When I arrived at his company, he greeted me and we spun the wheel of yelp and landed on something he'd heard about, El Huarache Azteca, a place that claims to be Authentic Mexican.  He'd heard good things from friends and Yelp said 4 stars, so.. It was a go!    We arrived and the little hole in a wall place was packed. There were 3 four tops available, and one booth being cleaned up, but other than that, BUSY was the name of the game.  Two large TV's were broadcasting videos, a holiday awards music program off telemundo and the music flooded the place.   The menu was large, filled with familiar and unfamiliar things. I opted for the Nachos Azteca and my husband went for a chimi changa.  There was a large party at the table near us, and they were still waiting on their food, so I thought we might be waiting for a while, but we didn't. The food came out rather quickly.   The portions (Well mine) were HUGE. The Husbeasts were modest, with a chimichanaga and a small salad on the plate.  The flavors were good, though to me, even though I opted for no Jalapeño, the nachos were lacking something in flavor, a depth. The meat, the marinated pork was tasty, but there was just .. something.  THe husbeast said that his was good, and he was a member of the clean plate club, so there were no complaints.   The 2 of us with our meals and 2 cans of diet coke ate for under $20.   Will we be back? Yes.   Oh wow!  This is officially my 1475th review and my Goal for the year (After I passed 1450, that is)

On our trip to DC, the husbeast's shoes went kaput, and we needed to get him new kicks. He'd purchased his old shoes some 15+ years ago, so it was TIME to get new ones..   The store is clean, neat and well organized. Quite spacious in their floor layout, almost sparse. The first thing the Husbeast said was that it was very "WHITE", and it is, the tiles and walls are so white the light reflects and that leads to the airy feeling of the store.    Since we came in on the 2nd floor, and the men's department was on the first, we took the escalator down, giving us a chance to peruse just about everything, like I said, very well laid out.  The men's shoe department doesn't have a lot of selection, unlike women's shoes. Granted, it's men's shoes, they have 6 styles, with 7 different designers, but six staple designs, displayed in 5 diferent areas.   We did find exactly what we were looking for and the Husbeast tried on a pair of Ecco shoes. It was interesting, he even had to go down a size! All in all, after teaching him the difference between nice shoes and REALLY NICE shoes, he went with a good pair that the soles are sewn on and the associate was VERY helpful. We'll be back. I want to explore their makeup department!

Welcome to Moes!  New-ish store in a small complex off of Us 19. Not the easiest in/out, but the store is clean and tidy.   I always get a bowl, (I don't remember their name for it) because I'm not a huge fan of flour tortillas, and they made it to my requests.  I feel they were a bit skimpy on ingredients because the boss man was right there behind the counter training a new girl.  The meat scoop I got was only 3/4 their normal serving as were some of the veg.   They seem to do a brisk business and as such need more staff.

First review of 2017!  Found this place quite by accident. I was looking for a slice of pizza to tide me over, and since I was at the mall, I guessed this was going to be where I'd find it.  I FIGURED it'd be a place like Sabarro or some such, but imagine my surprise to find Rise Pies.   Fresh dough, fresh toppings and a quick toss into the 600 Degree stone, wood fire oven, the pizza was ready in less than 5 minutes.  It was deliciously tasty. There was, in my opinion, not enough cheese, but there was certainly a good amount. The basil and the sauce were delicious. All in all, I'd come back for some more!

I was hanging out with a friend and we were hungry. Since he's in a new apartment, he really isn't familiar with his area, YELP to the rescue. We looked at local eateries and Palm Riverside Pizzeria & Grill was only a mile from his home. BINGO!   Its a tiny place, kind of hidden at the side of the road and not really a place you'd look twice at, but you really should. It smelled like heaven when we entered. We took a moment to look at the menu wall, then placed our order for a white pizza with spinach and 10 wings.  THey're busy so you can expect to wait a little bit, but the pizza is worth it.  The food was Delicious and the wings were tasty!  This will become a regular when we're together.

We opted to go here instead of our original brunch decision since they had a line out the door. When we walked in, the owner was having a chat with someone over either a job interview or some such, but we were pretty much dismissed, until the person behind the counter asked if we were placing an order for here or to go.. Clearly their dining room isn't used very often.  We opted for here.   We sat down and waited for our Caprese salad, which was delicious, and then our Pizza. When it came out, the only thing I can say about it is that it could have been baked a tad longer but otherwise it was tasty. I enjoyed it.

A place to stop for Lunch after popping into Khols to pay a bill. I can always grab a bowl of soup and a quick sandwich and know that at least the meal is hearty and should be "Real" food, vs typical fast food.   Even though the parking lot was busy, I walked in and my order was taken quickly. I didn't wait more than 5 minutes for my soup and sandwich all together, and it was tasty and hearty. I do love their creamy tomatoe soup.

Popped into Walgreens to pick up an Arizona Iced tea, which was offered on their signage at 2 for $1.00. This was an easy buy. The store was ... well it's a bit dirty and the staff was a bit MEH in the terms of customer service, but all in all it was a decent visit and I got what I wanted without too much hassle.

Came here for a business Lunch. The Husband's business Lunch, i was just tagging along for the free food. It's been a while since I've visited Casa Tina, and It looks like they are in the midst of a renovation.   The salsa and chips is always Delicious. The food is always fresh and the service is most often with a smile.    I ordered the Enchilada Roja, or Enchilada's with red sauce, it was very tasty, but not at all spicy as the menu said it was - which is good because i was kind of afraid. The husband ordered the Burrito, which was HUGE, but tasty. Our friend, the one doing the business ordered civiche and black bean soup, he said it was delicious.   We even opted for dessert, I got flan and the others split an order of fried plantains ala mode. I wasn't thrilled with the flan, it lacked the caramel sauce it usually comes with, but the fried platains were plentiful and apparently VERY good.  Occasionally (I'm not sure of the timing) They do aerial shows! Catch these if you can, they're REALLY good.

Needed to get my fingerprints done for Florida Licensing, however I noticed that many of them were rejected. I don't know why and he didn't re-do them either. All I know is that I complied with the Florida regulations and got it done.  I have no idea what the picture looked like, because I was getting my purse.   Frankly, he didn't seem thrilled to do the work, but he was one of the few locations that the Health Department offered up.

We wanted to stop for dinner, the place I wanted to go, had run out of food and closed for the evening, so here was an alternative selection.   We popped in and noticed the 3 chicks behind the front desk weren't all that attentive. All young women were about bored with their job of rolling silver. One young girl yawned into her hand and went back to rolling the forks into the napkins. No hand sanitizer or anything. That was kind of gross.   The other two, once they said who we were to be seated with, had some kind of eye fight with either a busser or another waitperson, what ever that mess was, it was in front of a customer and NOT very welcome.  That really put a sour taste in my mouth. Their front end is NOT professional and not skilled.    We were set in Ariel's section, and she was a delight. Very friendly, very nice.  She showed us the different size bowls and gave us the directions of Meat first and then veg. Very different from the other places we went before, which allowed us to put veg in first.. Ah well, the husbeast didn't pay attention. Heheh.   The medium sized bowl was more than enough for me, the husbeast went large. We both ended with left overs. The food was good, quick and tasty. Will we come back? Probably NOT to that location. The waitstaff was fine, but the front end left an impression I'm not soon to forget.

Stopped into Waffle House after a work out with the beau because it was Late in the evening and they're a great place to get protein powered meals.  The Beau and I like doing that after we work out.   We both made sure to get our selves breakfast meals and sat at the end of the counter so we could talk quietly.  Our waitress was quite friendly and the food came up quickly.   Our meals were made correctly, the eggs with cheese were scrambled perfectly, the tomatoes looked good and fresh and the sausage was cooked right.   The meal was just what we needed before we headed home after our work out.

Great Service. I was pleased to find out I could get the lens on my Cell phone camera replaced and it wasn't an expensive repair. The guys were super friendly, they talked geek with the husbeast and even gave us a discount! I will come back when we need a cell phone or glass repaired! And I will reccomend them to folks in the future.

Stopped in after dance class yesterday, to catch up with a lovely fellow dancer. Haven't seen her in a year and she looks FABULOUS!  I ordered my chai latte and she got a peach green iced tea.   Both drinks were made with efficiency and a smile on the barista's face. It wasn't a busy day, so there were plenty of seats for us to grab and gab. We spent an hour sitting in the corner and chatting.  Have to say, one of the more comfortable S*bucks I've been in recently.

Since I was down in South Tampa, I might as well check out what the discount shopping scene was like. I spied a Marshall's I'd not yet been in, so I remedied that.   The store is clean, neat and some what organized. However not a single employe said hello, asked me if I needed anything or made eye contact.  Lucky for me, I'm a pretty much self sufficient shopper and can do it all on my own. I found what I wanted, needed and made my way to the registers.   I managed to find a few essential oils and other neat things, and checked out without a lot of fuss. All in all I spent just under $50 and walked out with my head held high.

Typical drive through, all American fare.   Don't go expecting gourmet burgers, don't go expecting really fast service. Do go if you want a step up over McD's or BK, because it is certainly that.  The "Steakburgers" are fresh made, and they do customize your order if you're like me and incredibly picky.

For date night, the beau and I decided to try this recent addition to the TnC area.   They are close by to his home so we made the 5 minute drive and pulled into the shopping center that I actually used to work in.    The eatery is clean, that's the first thing I noticed and it smells good. That was a huge plus. The pink color is bright and inviting as are the red rope stanchons that tell you where you should stand.   The menu boards are large and the menu is easily customizable, but the ingredients are not listed as to whats on each item (this is the only suggestion I'd make)  We ordered 2 tacos and a quesidilla, an aqua fresca and a coke. Our meal was $24 and we devoured every ounce of it.  It was SO fresh and so tasty.

I've always been a fan of the Mary's chain, but the Clearwater location wins HANDs down.    First, it's closer to me than the Ybor location. Second the place is open and roomy, not a cramped locale where the stage is an after thought.  Third, the service (Provided by Felicia Fox) was second to none! We wanted for nothing! She was attentive and very warm.  I will make sure I ask for her as a waitress -every- time.  The food was good, we started with fried Mac & Cheese, Not at all on my diet, but SO damned good. My friend had their Cheese burger with bacon and it turned out to be a 9 napkin hamburger! That's one juicy piece of beef!  I had the "Party at the Club" salad, and it was pretty damned good. My only complaint was the bacon.. it was tiny itty over cooked bits, rather than larger chunks.    I will be coming back with friends for their buffet on a Sunday, and certainly be back on a Friday night for a show when some of the most talented female impersonators in the area take their stage.

I visit here occasionally, but this is the first time that I've remember to Yelp it.  I was surprised to see that they've remodeled the inside, it looks really nice.  They also have these interactive tablets on the table: You can play games, you can pay your bill, you can even re-order your drinks, heck! You can even read the USA Today headlines.   The menu is also sort of new with new sandwiches, new salads and what have you being added.   I ordered my new favorite salad: The quesadilla salad. in essence a chicken salad with corn salsa & a 3 cheese quesadilla. It's very tasty.  And by checking in with 4 square (Yes I use it too) i was able to get a free order of chips & salsa.   The service was Ok. Not fast, not slow. And no one told me what the tablet was for or how to use it, I just figured it out on my own. It would have been nice if someone had shown me how to use it.  Over all, I'd come back.

I liked the Klosterman location, I had to check out the NPR One.   The staff was delightfully friendly, and very attentive. Our waitress was very courteous to my mother and myself.   My mom had just had oral surgery so she needed something soft, I suggested the Shrimp and grits. Mom was concerned they'd be blended, but the waitress assured her it was not. She even offered mom a fresh baked biscuit - something she didn't have to do.   Me, i ordered the Philly bacon and cheese burger, It was a bit more done than I wanted, but I was able to ask for a side salad as my side instead of fries, it all tasted delicious.   The service was quick and the food was delightful. We will return.

I needed a place that was half way between Tarpon Springs and Temple Terrace, so I spun the Yelp again and came up with Southern Fresh.  After reading the reviews, I was sold on this place as the perfect meeting place to hang with a dear friend I'd not seen in some months.   When I arrived, I was pleased to see the large southern oaks yawning out over the front porches, but sad that they weren't occupied, though this was no fault of SF's own... Florida is in the midst of a cold snap and people were driven inside!  The inside was quaint, painted in a gorgeous sage green and white trim.  The tables were comfortable and we were seated up front, giving us a view of the street out front.  The waitress gave us a rundown of the specials and a few minutes to look over the menu, when she came back, we placed our order.  My friend had the lunch special for the 3 pieces of fried chicken (Thigh, wing and leg), mashed potatoes and collard greens. I opted for the regular fried chicken meal (White) with green beans and mashed potatoes.  Since the fried chicken was prepared as needed it took a few minutes but the wait was worth the outcome.    WOW! talk about FRESH chicken. The wings and leg pieces were DELICIOUS. And the Breast.. It was absolutely the most tender, juicy breast I'd ever eaten. The breading was light and crispy. The sides were incredibly flavorful. I'd never had collard greens before, so I tasted my friends selection and MAN! These were -so-good.  The green beans were tasty, but lacked salt. Over all this was a really good meal and a great chance to hang out with my old friend. I will CERTAINLY be coming back!

I don't mind Walmart super centers. This is a smaller version of the one on SR 54 and larger than the one closer to me at Tarpon Road.   I stopped tonight to go through the clearance items. I always enjoy seeing what remains after the Christmas Vultures have picked through the day after. Tonight, I managed to score quite a bit of Hard Candy makeup for a decent price. This means my Neice's 15th Birthday present is already taken care of. SCORE.  The store itself is rather ... well.. Always in a state of being stocked. That's not to say it's stocked at all. There are always people with pallets, in the isles. They tend to be in the way and under foot. Generally, it's an annoyance, but they're polite and they move quickly to get out of your way if you're looking for something.   The electronics area is the biggest mess. The husbeastie likes to dig through the stuff there, so I leave that for him. Me, I used to like to go through their clothes, but not so much any more.

I needed food after being up so early and leaving home on an empty belly. I checked the handy dandy Yelp app and saw that PDQ was not far away so I motored the mile down the road and pulled in.    I got there JUST before the lunch rush, placed my order and got my salad JUST before the wave of people hit.  This place is EFFICIENT! I sat at the bar and watched how quickly they hammered out the orders. How fast they took care of everything.   One after the other, the orders of fresh french fries, of chicken tenders and sandwiches and salads came up, with virturally no wait at all. And the guy announcing it all - the manager I'm guessing, sounded like Don Pardo.   This is a fast, class act opperation.

Stopped in here for a late Sunday brunch, it was the first time for both of me & my beau.    This little cafe is tucked into the corner of this large strip mall and was very easy to find.  Once inside, we were seated and started looking at the 3 menus that were placed before me. YES, 3 menus. Their regular menu, the specials menu and the brunch menu.    The waitress came over and took our drinks order, we both needed coffee so that's what we got, and their coffee is Kawha coffee, which is SO DAMN Good, especially when it's hot and fresh.    I ordered one of their Western Omelettes and my beau ordered their 2, 2, 2, which is Eggs, Bacon and 2 pancakes.  We were not prepared for the amount of food that was delivered to us.  The Omelette came with a side of breakfast potatoes and a bread choice, I chose the english muffin.  It was well made, and tasted so good. I was unable to eat 1/2 of it.   The 222 was also made well, with the eggs scrambled and cheese added, the bacon was done right but the pancakes... can we chat a moment? These were HUGE, each was the size of a Dinner Plate and they didn't even need syrup. They were sweet and light and totally fluffy. SO tasty.  We shared a few bites but I think we left about 1/3 of them behind.    We will certainly be back.

I've eaten at other Smokey Bones locations, and the food is consistently good. The service is always good as well.  It looks as though they've gone though and done an over haul of interior and taken away the 'rustic' lodge look and given it an update to a more hipster vibe.  I love the sayings on the walls.  The one that caught my attention tonight was "A good dry rub enhances our meat.  STOP LAUGHING"   Tonight we ordered the fried pickles, a salad with pulled chicken and a sandwich for the husband with "kettle chips."  While the mains were ok, I have to say that while I expected that the pickle chips should be a bit crispy, they were more on the mushy side. As though they'd been pulled from the hot oil too soon.  The kettle chips too, were thick and un-crispy as well.

I have a fear of bridges. Something regarding a dream I had Ages ago that still hangs heavy in my mind. Anyway, any time I go over the Sunshine Skyway bridge I have to take the inside lane because this bridge is SO high.   It's an archetectural beauty that stands sentinental over the gulf. A beacon that says you are HERE in Tampa bay, Welcome home.

MAYBE I'm just a bit biased, but I think that the people who work there are the best in the industry.  They give it their all, from the start to the finish, you see people giving blood (Sometimes very literally) sweat and tears.    From the humble beginnings to the zombie extravaganza of last year, each new house that is rolled out, each new show and every performer is geared up to get YOU with a scare that will send a shiver down your spine and maybe some urine down your legs if you're the susceptible type.   Wicked sets, creepy music and eerie lighting all add to the ambeince that create this seasonal creature feature, every person who works the event from behind the scenes, to the ride operators to the scare actors themselves really do throw every thing they have into it to make it the best event it can be.  They truly do scare from the heart and deep into your soul, creating a lasting impression that makes you want to come back year after year.

I don't think I've seen a more disorganized location. Placed our order, the cashier, a young fellow, couldn't seem to get the order right. We waited, and waited, and waited ... and the people behind us all got their food, and when if finally came to their notice that my husband was still waiting for his food they said it would sill be a few more minutes.. At least the fries were fresh?

WOW..Trust your waitress when she tells you to order the Big Sexy. You won't regret it!  I digress, I'm getting ahead of myself.  We found out about this place by asking their property buddy, Imagine games.  Taking that suggestion, our foursome were seated at a high top and served drinks and a wonderful charchuterie plate.   We took a -LONG- time to go over the menu because some of the items were.. well.. odd.  I'm talking Brusell sprouts and pistachios. These aren't things you'd normally see, however they're things that go really well!   We asked our waitress for suggestions and she told us not to be daunted by the ingredients, that she assured us that the brussell sprouts weren't these huge hunks of green, but rather delectable slivers as our pallets would soon tell us. The ingredients included artichoke, pistachio as well as whole tomato slice, spinach, ricotta and a 4 cheese blend.  There is no "sauce" per se but a bit of olive oil and it -works-. This pie was amazing.   We also ordered a 2nd pie, the Michaelangelo: WF Tomato sauce, pepperoni, wf mozzarella, mushrooms, caramelized onions.  This is like your ordinary pepperoni pizza amped up and made SO much better. The caramelized onions make the flavour richer, deeper. The mushrooms ad an extra layer of unctiousness.   They were not cheap but reasonable. We were there at 4:30 on a Friday and the service was amazing. We all agree that we'll come back!

I'm a fan.   Particularly for their rewards card. Almost every fillup gives me something free, if I'm willing to go in to get it.  Inside, they have an awesome drink bar, that gives Chip Ice.. The best kind. They offer sandwiches and hot dogs. And of course all the little convience items ou could ever want. I really do like Thorntons for my gas choice.

A smaller format Marshals, didn't have a lot of what I was looking for, though they did have a few items I'd not seen at others.  I love digging through the make up to see if they have any of the high end stuff. Kat Von D, Borghese, Laura Mercer.. All these and more can be found at your local Marshalls, but this one didn't seem to have MUCH. I did however find a few natural oil and oil blends i've not found at others so I scooped those up as well as 5 pounds of Haribo gummi bears. YUM.

A nice apartment complex down in Oldsmar.  Off of Tampa road, it's pretty easy to get to. They have large sized apartments with nice lay outs, spacious rooms and cute kitchens.   I noticed though that for a gated community, the fact that the gate was broken was kind of a security issue for me.

After a lovely dinner and a bit of shopping  - yet before the movie we were going to see, the husbeastie decided he wanted something sweet.  I remembered I'd seen the Creperie in the food court so I hustled us that direction and showed him the wonderes I'd seen!  We chose their Nutella & Strawberry crepe with a scoop of Cookies & Creme gellato and watched the lovely girl make our sweet treat!  The food was decidedly fresh and very, very tasty. The only negative I have tlo say is that the gellato was a touch icy, as if it had been melted and re-frozen.   Other wise. Thumbs up!

Having never been inside a Hobby Lobby, I wasn't sure what to expect.  When I entered, i was FLOORED. This place was huge! There was a little bet of everything. From scrap booking, to kinttng, to wood working. From soap making to sewing and candy making. There really is something for everyone to do here.   Up front, there was wrapping paper that was marked as Christmas paper, but the colors were ambiguous that you could use them for every day, and the roll was ginormous, so I'll have paper for years to come.

I first saw this store in California, earlier this year. So I was really happy when I found one locally.   There's nothing more fun than finding candy that reminds you of your childhood! And talk about a variety! From candy buttons to wax lips and wax bottles, you really can find it all.  I found candy I'd not seen in - quite literally - more than half a lifetime!  And let's not even discuss the soda! I saw things like RANCH DRESSING flavoured soda. (Um...) and all manner of Ginger ale (except Vernor's, I might note) If you're looking for something unique, something you've never tried before and something that's NOT your usual cola, you'll find it here.   And if you're looking for an unusual gift, weather it be a bobble head toy, a Cardinal head mask or even a tin sign for your wall, you're likely to find it at Rocket Fizz!

What used to be the Old Schoolhouse is now New England's Ale house Grille.  I'm glad to see that it's open! Since we decided we wanted to try something new, this was the first choice!  I liked that it was all open seating, inside and out. That  you didn't have someone seating you in places where you might not want to sit.. I'm sure in time this will change but for tonight, it worked.  We chose to sit outside, the temperature wasn't too bad, and there weren't any bugs biting, so we watched the traffic go by as the evening progressed.    The menu is surprisingly large. Lots of options to choose from and not all of it is expected. I was pleasantly surprised to find that the offer a gourmet grilled cheese and a hearty bowl of Tomato soup!  There were lots of salad options as well as hearty burgers and nice entree choices.   Since I wanted something filling and the husbeastie wanted a burger, we decided to explore their menu.  We started the night with their onion straws.  They were lightly fried and served with a chipolte ranch sauce. Crispy and tasty! There was a nice serving size for two people.  For our Main courses the husbeastie chose the Chef Burger, which was a large 1/2 pound (I think) burger, with carmelized onions, cheese and bacon, a side of cole slaw and chips. He could opt for Fries for $1.00 more.  He ordered his burger med. Rare and when it came out, it was a very juicy burger.!  He said it was quite tasty. Very flavourful and the coleslaw was something really flavorful.  I chose the grilled chicken entree Which came with a dinner salad, a roll and one side.  It was served atop wilted spinach and topped with grilled fruit salsa. It ws absolutely delicious. The chicken was juicy and tender, the side was green beens, and they were seasoned deliciously.  All in all, the food was a good value and quite good.  Dessert, we opted to share their Apple Brown Betty. It came served in a small cast iron skillet. It was sweet and yummy, but there were two small issues. It should have come with a scoop of Ice cream and it could have been cooked a bit longer, as it was a touch doughy.   Over all, this place should go over well with the locals and travelers alike!

It's WALMART. It's a superstore, and honestly there's not much I can say about it.  Every one of them is similar. If I want a wrench, I can get a wrench. If I want a banana, I can get a banana.  I do find however that if you're looking for Plus sized clothing you're pretty much SOL. They've really made these departments smaller, almost to the point of being irrelevant. I don't get that. When more and more of your customer base is larger, why would you focus on Junior's clothing? Cute teen clothing isn't where the money is spent.  It's the mom's and grandmom's that are shopping. And they really don't want to wear the crappy JMS t-shirts and jeans you're carrying. UGH. I'm certain that the stores will be full tomorrow, as it's Grey Thursday. I'm not so sure I like this idea, after all, can't you let your workers have a day off for their families? This new policy kind of sucks.

I came here and had Xrays of my foot taken   The people were very very professional and friendly. I wasn't there for very long, My Orthapedist is in the same building and my results were sent to him right away, so I had very little turn around time.   I'd use them again in a moment.

I'd heard of this place but had never had the occasion to visit until a friend from out of state was visiting. We agreed to meet here as it was a central location.  Upon entering, the first thing I noticed was how good it smelled, like pizza with something else, and what ever it was, my tummy started to growl.  We took a table, started talking and ordered our first round of drinks. They ordered some of the local brews offered. I don't remember which one's, but this establishment's list is long. I ordered a cider.  We ordered the Guava Barbeque Mac n cheese and the shrimp and Mac and cheese, I wasn't sure what to expect but it was AMAZING. The BBQ, while s little sweet for me, had great flavor.   I will definitely be back there.

Great little chocolate shop in DTSP.    Loved that there were samples right in the cases, the espresso beans were delicious and the cookies were even better. Their Peanut Butter cookies are to die for.   I will most certainly return.  The look of surprise on the face of the clerk when 30 people showed up to help out was perhaps the best thing ever.

Need a liquor gift? This is the place to go!    One of the more comprehensive liquor stores in the area, they have a huge selection and a very helpful staff.  Their window decoration for bombay sapphire is something to be seen.. very Steam Punk inspired.

Stopped in to the New location of YoA. It's Airy, quite comfortable, but has the same issues with parking that the previous owners did in the same location. They cover this by having a lot across the street and one a block down. Just be aware that there is a house that has both feral cats and a raccoon behind the location.   We stopped in for brunch, something new they are offering, and we were a bit surprised. It was a brunch as in offering breakfast & lunch, not a buffet. That's ok, there were some interesting offerings on the menu!  The first thing we noticed is that (almost) everything had either bourbon or bacon in the ingredient list. YUMMY.  They were not offering the full menu either, but they were offering some fantastic drink specials on Bloody Marys, Mimosas and bellini's.   We placed our orders: The husbeast got the Cinnamon stack pancakes and I got the Fried chicken toast plate, and we waited while we sipped our drinks. I chose a peach bellini - ($6 all you can drink- I would NOT recommend it) and the hubster got himself a cider.    When the food came it was delivered on very pretty plate, but we were hungry and I forgot to take pics. I did take pictures AFTER we'd started eating. HEH.  Anyway, the hubs got three large, but thin pancakes layered with bacon and topped with fresh fruit and a bourbon sauce - though he requested the sauce on the side.  By the way he ate it, I can tell he liked it.   My food was good, the 3 large slices of french toast were fried, and served with 2 large chicken tenders (they called it southern style fried chicken, but lets be honest, it's chicken tenders) and maple syrup. The French toast was some of the best I've eaten. Because it was fried, it was not soggy, it was evenly done, and so good.   At the end of the meal, we opted to NOT get dessert, but we could have had a bacon plate (candied bacon to dip into chocolate) or cereal sushi, among a few other things. I'll try something next time.

I've had donuts from here once before and they were good.   The other night, after a celebratory dinner for the husbeastie, the beau and I went out and got a few donuts as a treat for all three of us.  We arrived just as the interior was being closed (10:00 pm), so we had to go to the drive up window.   Since we're not terribly familiar with their product, it took us a moment or three to choose what we wanted. We opted to go for their Cake donut selection, which was a REALLY good choice, and we added a Boston Cream donut   At the window, the girl behind the register was really friendly. The place looked amazingly clean, the donuts were OBVIOUSLY fresh, and as she got the donuts for us, she made a clarification on one of the donuts, and boxed them all up for us.   When we got them home, they were still WARM! The blueberry was my favorite. Though cake-y, it was still light and delicious, the glaze was delectable. All the donuts were like this. The husbeast loved the sour cream donut and the beau really thought the boston creme was fantastic, and I have to agree, the bite I took was just WOW.   I'm not going back to Dunkies again, this place wins!

Had a lovely lunch here with a friend of mine. I wasn't aware this location existed.   It was clean, the lines were populated well and filled with all the usual good things. Including my favorite, Pickled beets.   The people were friendly, the soups were good and they had Gluten friendly pumpkin muffins. Not as good as their Gluten Friendly Coconut muffins but they'll do.

Came here to have a lovely ladies day with my sister from another mister Lindsey. Our reservation was for 12:30, but we arrived a touch early. That was OK! We were seated right away and began to peruse the menu.   I've been a few times before on Yelp events but never at brunch. The menu was devine! We started with Southern caprese salad: fried green tomatoes, mozzarella and balsamic drizzle. It was heaven. Lindsey ordered the char grilled oysters and I actually ate one.  They weren't bad.  For our mains, I ordered a New Orleans staple, a Muffaletta sandwich. It was to die for. She ordered the crawfish hash and by the look of her clean plate it was excellent. I did notice that it was rife with a lot of the lil mud bugs and the color of the dish was fantastic.   Rest assured we'll be back.

I stopped into the Hooker Tea Company before a Yelp event, and boy was I impressed. The first thing I noticed, and even commented on was the heavenly scent. Man, did it smell GOOD.   Since it was mid morning, the husbeast and I wanted brunch, unfortunately they were out of the meat quiche that they were advertising, so I opted for the Chicken salad Croissant and he ordered the vegetable quiche, each of us ordering a hot tea to sip on.    The tea was fantastic! Their Jasmine Pearl is amazing.  The food... well the chicken salad croissant would probably have been better if it had been freshly made instead of sitting in a cold case. And the quiche took 20 minutes to be "Warmed up".  Either way, the food was tasty, the value was so/so.  I would still come back.

With as much time as I've spent recently in Down Town Tampa, you'd think I'd know the places to eat here. But alas, I don't. It took my beau to point out this little gem out to me.  7:45 pm on a Friday, Peak time for going out and Bamboozle is no different, it's crowded, and part of that is because Tampa Theater was running a David Bowie tribute (RIP Mr. Bowie), But since we were a small Party, we were sat quickly.   After a quick perusing of the menu, we settled on our drinks: Jasmine Tea for me and a Vietnamese Coffee (With condensed milk) for him, As hand rolled spring roll and 2 small bowls of Phò, 1 beef, 1 shrimp. We figured this would be quick and easy.  We were wrong on the quick part.   Seems that the drink took longer than expected since the coffee is basically a drip, and my tea was pretty much cold when it was served.   The spring roll $4.00 for one, was delicious, and their peanut sauce was better than any of the other I've tasted in the area. I mean, it was decadently good.   The small bowls of Phó were JUST the right size, they call it a sample, because the regular size is basically a trough. The broth was good, the noodles and veg were good and of course it was hot.  We got our bill early so we could pay it and not have to wait longer since they had a huge party come in while we were there.   Will I come back? Yes. the food was very good. I can't fault them on their speed because FRIDAY RUSH.

I'd tried to visit this location of P.F. Chang's since they opened but without much luck. So on Saturday, the bestie and I decided we were going to go catch a movie and do lunch. I went on line and made reservations through their website. EASY PEASY!  We arrived a few minutes early, and were asked to sit a moment while they cleared out table. We weren't waiting more than 5 minutes before we were taken to a table in the nicely appointed dining room.  The place really is lovely, clean lines and nice decor, it lends an air of elegance to the room.   The Manager came over after finding out that it was our first time there and delivered to us a $10 gift card, valid on our next visit, a survey to fill out about our experience that would give us a free app on the next visit. I'm not sure that they do this for everyone, but it was a nice treat to receive.  After a few moments our waitress, Tiana came over and took our drink orders, both of us ordered some of their steeped tea, I got the Orange spice blend and the bestie got the Green Citrus blend, both were deliciously flavoured and SMELLED amazing!  Once she came back with the cute little cast iron pots, we placed our orders for our meal.    They have this Prix Fixe offer where 2 can eat for $39.95, This includes Soup, App, Entree for each  and a dessert to share.  Since what we wanted to eat was on their special selection we went ahead and got it: We ordered the Thai Lettuce wraps as the appetizer, I got egg drop soup and my bestie the hot & sour. Our entrees were to be the Chicken with almond & cashew and hers was to be the Orange Shrimp.    Tiana was efficient, but she was green. It was her first day as a waitress, though she'd worked in other parts of the bistro before. When our soups came out, she delivered the egg drop to both of us.  When she realized the error, she brought out a Hot and spicy to correct it.     The chicken wraps smelled -so- good, but their flavour wasn't as promising. They honestly were mouth watering, but on the tongue there was something lacking. Don't get me wrong, they were tasty, but there was just something... not there.   Our entree's were delivered shortly there after. Both were amazingly delicious and fresh. That is until I found a blonde hair in mine. I'm a red head and my bestie has raven hair, so it wasn't ours.  We called the waitress over and she immediately flagged down the manager who profusely apologized and took my plate away. A new order was made and when it came out, i swear there was 2x the food.  I ended up sharing my bestie's plate and we took the other home.   The manager ended up taking off my entree from our bill, and that negated the prix fixe deal, but even with dessert, it all came out even in the wash.   I'd return. The staff was friendly, the food was good, and what ever error there was, they went out of their way to see that it was corrected.

I wanted to vote but I was going to be out of town on the day the votes were to be cast, so I opted for early voting.  I came out on the Wednesday before polls closed, I followed the signs to the CSA Recreation Center of Palm Harbor, and found that it is both easy to get in and out of. There's a thrift store on location, how neat is that.

I enjoy PDQ I love the fresh breaded tenders, the hand blended shakes and the coke machines.   The service is always fast and friendly and the food is always fresh and made to order. I wish there was a PDQ closer to me. (yes I know there is one in Clearwater but still too far.. )

Bookstores are great places for dates.   My Beau and I had just come from where I used to live (I wanted to show him my roots) and we ended up here for a Cup of coffee from Joe Mugs and looking at books, both of us are voracious readers.   We spent time perusing the stacks, where he found just what he was looking for and I rekindled my love for Mercedes Lackey and her fantasy series.   I love the way a bookstore smells and BAM is no different.   One thing that they have above the other retail sellers?  They take used books, including school books. YES! They're a new and used seller, how's that? They also have a huge selection of comics and the like.

Visiting Tiger Direct on Black Friday was an experience. There were more associates than I've ever seen on the floor. Given the day, It's easy to expect why.  There were some decent deals going on too.   The store isn't my cup of tea, but it is the Husbeasties play ground, so I let him go buck wild.  The customer service is always very good. 9 out of 10 times, they have what we're looking for, and we can usually find it in the first try, without help.  I'm glad this is close by and I don't have to wait to go to Atlanta to visit Frys.

We weren't aware you needed reservations when we arrived at 8:10 on Tuesday, but that was ok, the Hostess asked us to wait until a table opened up.  We waited about 10 minutes  and then were seated.   Our table was at the back, which allowed us to look at the artwork on the walls, and look at the whole place.  Over all, it's a lovely little place, a bit small, but the bar is really impressive.    The service wasn't hurried, Caleb, our Waiter, was attentive without hovering.  Our water glasses never went dry.  The FOOD! Lordy! The food was absolutely divine.  We started with the brie with pesto.  This was amazing.  Our entrees were the Seared Salmon with Spinach and a basalmic glaze, and the Angus NY Strip, both were cooked to perfection. The sides that came with each were perfectly seasoned and made out taste buds sing.   Lately, since we're both on a restricted diet, we wouldn't order dessert, but tonight, I just had to try the flourless chocolate cake.  I'm so glad we did! This was a little bit of heaven on a plate. Rich and thick, and served with a raspberry sauce... It was simply too much at the moment, so more than half came home with us.    I would recommend this place to anyone in the Tarpon area. Especially anyone looking for a nice little place to go on Date Night!

I really don't know where to begin. The theatre was.. abysmal. I'm serious. It's in the condition of being renovated but, it the way it looked made me feel as though I was going to be murdered at any moment.   I was there to catch the Midnight showing of RHPS, but after seeing the bored box office girl, and the way the doors were "CAUTION" taped off, I was actually second guessing it.   After taking my money for the ticket, the girl in the office, didn't speak into her mic but told me how to get to the auditorium... except I couldn't hear her, and I told her twice. Finally after rolling her eyes, she told me, using the mic this time, to go down the sidewalk, to just before plato's closet and go up the stairs. ... ok. Certainly not ADA compliant.   I went up the stairs.. and up the 2nd flight to where the theatre was in conversion to a church I'm guessing.  There were "Bathrooms" (I generally have bathrooms at home and restrooms out in public IDK) but they were one stall, and a big lounge area. it was just -odd-.  There was a beat up leather couch that was in the hall way out side where the 2 theatres were and the elevator, which had 2 or three bags of trash inside it was propped open. YES, there was an elevator, but it was not in use except to bring trash up and down.   The theatre itself was ok. The screen was nice and the chairs were comfortable if on the older side. Over all, except to see RHPS I don't see myself coming back to this theatre if I can help it.

Located in The Marq apartment complex, I was driving by and needed caffine to break a stupid headache. I parked and made my way in.    Its a lovely place, bright and filled with chairs. Their Barista was friendly and helpful. I ordered a my drink and waited not very long at all.. Within a few minutes my cappuccino was ready and I was out the door.   It was perfect, the temp, the amount of steamed milk and foam? All of it was JUST right. Ill be back.

I needed a root canal, so my dentist referred me to Dr. Liwen Tao.  I wasn't sure what I was in for, but Dr. Tao made me completely comfortable.   I opted for the use of Nitrous(laughing gas) because I have a HUGE fear of dentists, so that really helped, but the procedure only took about an hour to an hour an a half. There was very little pain. She explained every step as she did it. Her assistant was also very helpful and kind.   If I should have to have another in the future, this is where I would go.

I am -not- a Fourbucks fan. This is right down the way from where I work, so they're close and they're usually very good at what they do. I've never had bad service here, and they can run through a line very quickly, so I'm happy with that too.

As residents of Pinellas counties, we popped in after visiting the Pierce st. Market. It was just one of those things where we wanted to check out the Maker's lab. However because we don't have a current card, and the husbeast didn't want to sign up for one on their unsecured system. we hesitated.   What we did notice is that it's large, it is clean and it is fairly up to date. The staff is warm and welcoming and they don't throw out the homeless, which is good and bad, since the homeless tend to occupy the computers and utilize the ac during the hot days.

My husband needed surgery to have a hernia repaired.  We weren't sure what to expect, but the folks at the CountrySide Surgery center helped put us at ease.    Though the doctor was a bit late due to an Emergency surgery at the hospital across the street, but when he showed up, the ball got rolling. Everyone was exceedingly pleasant and professional. I was allowed to sit with him until he went back for the actual procedure.  True to their word, he was done in a little over 25 minutes. And my husband was awake and alert. We waited another 25 or so minutes for final instructions and then I went and got the car.  They even called the next day.

We were in the mall, waiting for a movie to start and wanted to grab a quick meal. We ordered one of their basic sandiwiches and it was darn near the best grilled cheese i've ever eaten.   They were fast and friendly and we had our food in less than 5 minutes! I'd certainly come back when i'm at West Shore mall

After a day at the beach, one of our family members asked us to join him for dinner, but left the destination up to us, figuring since we lived in Pinellas Co, we'd have the scoop.  I played Yelp roulette and landed on one place, but it was closed, so Roosterfish Grill was our 2nd location.   First impressions are everything and this parking lot was busy. Busy parking lot means popular destination.  It was early on Sunday evening, just 5:30 pm so Early bird as well, as seen by nearly every head inside was a shade of gray and I think we were one of three tables under 55.   Id never heard of the location, so I had no idea what to expect, the name said chicken/fish and that is more or less what the menu said too.  Our waitress, Carmen was very prompt, very friendly, absolutely wonderful.  My brother in law placed an order for the ahi appetizer and seemed to enjoy every bite.   When our mains came to the table: Popcorn shrimp platter, Fried Grouper and a NY Strip, we were surprised at the sizes of the portions. The grouper came with 3 fillets, the popcorn shrimp was huge. The NY Strip was large as well, 12 oz.   The sides were generous and well seasoned, I really liked the green beans and their garlic mashed potatoes.   I was disappointed in the steak and this takes one star away from what would have been a 4 star review, because the meat tasted more of propane than it did of meat. It lacked seasoning, not even salt & pepper. Other wise our dining experience was fine, the paper towel rolls above your head is kitsch and a bit off putting, but that's my issue.

I drove by here the other day when I was getting ready for my cruise. When we got back the Husbeast said he was hungry and I asked if he wanted to try something new.. He did, and so .. Burgerfi.   The place is relatively new, with seating indoor and outside.  Inside it's spartan with concrete floors and high ceilings - perfect for loud noises to carry and magnify as they were doing with the gaggle of kids on this day, and Outside it has a lovely patio with a few umbrella tables and few not. It's gated and quite nice.    We took a moment or three to look over the menu card, and waited in line as the singular (out of 4 cashiers) cashier took the order of the people in front of us - the other registers were going through a change of operators or weren't up. The manager made no eye contact with anyone.   Once it was our turn, our ordergirl was friendly and just full of happy vibes. The husbeast did a triple make your own with lots of stuff on his, me, I'm a classic type and went for a regular burger, burgerfi sauce on the side. We ordered a side of Cry-fries with urban sauce and 2 drinks. This came to just over $25.   We got our drinks and our table outside and enjoyed the lovely sunshine.   When it was our turn for food, the husbeast got our order and ... YES!! These burgers were delicious. I mean JUICY, well seasoned and cooked to perfection. The cry-fries (onion rings and fries together) were amazing. The rings have a slightly sweet but crispy batter and the fries were good. The urban sauce - parmesan with garlic aioli was tasty.   We will be back!

Stopped in one late morning with the beau and had a lovely breakfast/brunch.  The location is small, compact and quite quaint. I love the mural of the Train right behind the register.   We sat right up front and had really awesome service! The beau had eggs and hash while I had an omlette with hash browns. Both of us were hungry as we were both nearly members of the clean plate club.  The coffee was delicious as was the orange juice. The food was well done and absolutely tasty and filling.   We will most assuredly return.

Stopped in here with my Beau as a quasi anniversary celebration.  Our last time here was our Valentine's date, so we stopped in to celebrate Christmas.  They were open later, given that it was so close to the holiday.   Their espresso machine was down, but they make a fine cuppa on any level.  We hand picked out a few chocolates to share, and let me tell you, each one of them was an experiment in artistry, each one was hand painted and a different flavor.    The service was amazing, the tastes of each chocolate was unique, delicate and quite delectable. I will always come back to this place.   We also picked up a few specialty gifts: Imported candied oranges dipped in dark chocolate, a cup made of dark chocolate, filled with marshmallows, meant to make us hot chocolate.

The husbeastie's work Holiday gathering was held here on December 5th. We were in their private gathering room and that was actually quite lovely, if dark and somewhat loud.   I loved, absolutely loved the live Flamenco artist, he was truly gifted in his craft.  The Bartenders were fast in filling the drink orders and the wait staff was friendly and efficient making sure that the plates were cleared and the food was kept stocked.   The food! It was delicious. We were served in a buffet style, so I was quite pleased with what we had. Our appetizer or Cocktail hour course was cheeses, strawberries and some tasty meats.  An empanad and ceviche.   When the mains were served there was quite a selection, including Vegetarian and omnivour options. My favourite were the Prime rib skewers and the chicken.    I would certainly come again, they make fabulous sangria.

I tried their chicken terryaki, I can say that this is not a food court place I'll be trying again any time soon.   The rice was ... well it was rice, but it wasn't GOOD rice.  The chicken was soggy and just not good. The portion size was minimal and over all, this is not something I care to repeat.

A Michael's with a Bentley parked out front. Can't say it hasn't happened before, but I certainly didn't think it would happen in Caroll Wood. :)   Nice, clean shop, but the employes seemed harried. Management seemed cross the workers and in general not willing to help out those under their care.  I certainly would be reluctant to ask for a price check here. Ugh.

The husbeast and I were driving down to St. Pete to take care of something when we decided we were both hungry and needed to eat. We saw this little hole in the wall Cuban eatery and made our way inside. The first thing we noticed was how good it smelled. It literally made my mouth water.   We waited in a small line before we ordered from the slightly cafeteria style line. We both ordered the Black Beans & yellow rice, Ropa Vieja & plantains. I opted to get dessert, a chocolate cake filled with mousse. Bottled drinks completed the meal, together it was $25.89.   The food was hot, and oh so tasty! The meat was tender and well seasoned, the beans and rice fit the bill. The dessert was a little dry, but I'm certain that's because it was the last one of it's kind in the refrigerated case, not due to any other reason but that.   I would most certainly come back and eat here again, the food was a taste of heaven!

I finally got to go the Trulieve store, and though it's not easy to get to, the staff is friendly and welcoming.  I dislike that they play music loud enough to cover conversations with, but this may be more a me problem as the older I get, the harder it is to pick out conversations from the ambient sound.   They practice good social distancing, and have hand sanitizer around for you to use.  I was over all comfortable and happy with my experience.

After dinner tonight, I stopped by the outside of this yoga studio to check out their class list as they had little cards available. As I did, the door opened and Darcy opened up and asked me if I had questions.   She invited me in, and we spoke for a little bit. She too, is an LMT and it was NIRVANA inside. It smelled wonderful, the aroma of essential oils filling the air. The calming energy was palpable. And the class list was acceptable.   My body needs yoga, and their prices are on par with my Bellydance classes. Looks like I'll be venturing into the world of yoga soon. Namaste'

I came here because I'd never been. I'd been when it was a different place, and I'd liked it, so I decided to treat myself to a nice dinner.   I was seated in a nice little booth that was tucked up against the wall, this gave me a chance to look around and look at the decor. Much of it was lovely, with bamboo lighting and great paintings. It set the mood for a lovely island feel.   My Waiter, Fred, was very attentive, he'd not worked there very long,and answered honestly when I asked him what he'd tried on the menu. He gave me suggestions and I listened carefully, and went with NONE of them.   I ordered the Fried Green Tomatoes as a starter, they came with jerk Aioli, when they were delivered, they were crispy and hot, the flavour was delicious!  I ordered the steak as my main, and I have to admit I wasn't too thrilled with the seasoning they put on the meat or the veg. The redskin garlic potatoes were dry.  This was my least favorite part of the meal.   I was offered dessert and I chose to order the Coconut cake. I wasn't sure what I was expecting, but I'm GLAD I ordered it.     The cake itself was delivered with 2 scoops of vanilla icecream and a HUGE round of coconut cake smothered in toasted coconut. It was like heaven. I couldn't eat it all!  The ice cream though, it was icy .. not creamy. That was kind of meh, but the CAKE.. omg.. the cake! So good.   I did tell the waiter about the ice cream, just so it could be corrected for the next patron, I wasn't going to eat that anyway.   Overall, it was a good visit!

I've gone here a couple of times with my beau for Sunday breakfast.    We've learned to get here before 11:30 or face the church crowds.  Since we're a couple, it may be easier for us to get a seat over a 4+ top, but we've always been seated right away.   The place has a following among the older folks and the family set. The food is palatable. Our first visit, I got a 2nd helping of eggs, wasn't charged for it, and I didn't order it *shrug* I guess It was a mistake, but ok.  The 2nd time we visited we had very slow service and the food was bland and the coffee wasn't as fresh seeming.   Over all, the boyfriend and I don't really care for the place.  The food is ok, but not thrilling. You do get a lot for your money, but it's just not to our taste.

This was my first local escape room, and I'm happy to say that they are -excellent- and compare with the ones I've done in other states.  You can tell the detail that they've put into their story.   There's a lot of fun in their puzzles, there's a lot of detail in their story. A lot of fun interior design in their rooms.   My group chose this in a rather unconventional way.  I put out a call to people in the area for suggestions, this was the most popular. My friends had not done an escape room and I have done several in other areas.   We opted to have the private experience, so we booked the time slot for 3:30 pm on Saturday, for their reSEArch room. When we arrived, we signed in and did their "preview room" Our room Guide said he'd never seen the room solved so quickly. *shrugs* We were given 15 minutes, We solved it in 2.  The Room we chose is rated their hardest. I can tell you that it is NOT easy. Some of the clues should have been obvious to me, and looking back I'm slapping my forehead, but for a mostly first time group, I think we did admirably.   There are a lot of great touches that the team here have executed. I have to say that I can't wait for their next one to open, as I'm certainly going to come back and play!

We walked in on a Sunday afternoon. A few tables were busy, but a lot were open. Three or four waitresses were on duty, though I think one had just been cut as she told us to seat ourselves and someone would be with us soon.  Cue no one coming to us for a while and that same waitress asking the others if they'd seen to us, when they all said no, she sent one of the other girls over to us, this girl was very sweet, had lovely tattoos and was very efficient.   We placed our orders for Bacon Cheese burgers, one with a side of fries and the other with onion rings.  I got coke, the husbeast got unsweet iced tea.  The food came out quickly, and was tasty, cooked like we asked.    Over all, I'd say the place is ok.  I'd probably come back. I'm not sure if they're open during this Covid-19 outbreak, or if they're just doing take away, but I always try to support local business first over chains.

Used the drive through to get the beau and myself a pick me up. There was no line and we were able to order right away. I got a Pink Drink, and the beau got a Cafe mocha with 1/2 the amount of mocha.   The drinks were ready when we got at the window, they were efficient and friendly.

My Beau and I love coming here for the grouper nuggets. They're out favorite.    We love their fried fish and their sangria. The service is always good too! You can bet I'll be coming back quite frequently as love as I'm with my current guy.

We don't have a lot of stand alone, drive up coffee shops, so that alone makes WDE exciting. What doesn't make it exciting is the line you often have to wait in. But that's ok, they work through it quickly and the coffee is pretty good.   So far, I've stopped twice, I've had a hot and a cold latte and both times, the service and product have been excellent.

The husbeast wanted to show me his new work environs. He's down off 1st Ave in St. Pete, so he's got a great selection of places to eat!  While we were down there, he suggested we get lunch at this one place down the block. So we walked there, but there was a car on fire out side. Taking this as a sign, we made our way to Sushi Inc.   We were seated, our waitress took our drink order immediately and provided me with one of the best Cokes I've had in a long time.  The husbeast perused the Sushi menu and I looked at their other offerings. We both made our choices, He ordered a few rolls and I even ordered the Vegetarian roll. My main was the beef fried rice.   We both got a Miso Soup with the husbeast swears is the best he's ever had. It was very tasty. Their salad was good too, their ginger dressing was fresh.  The sushi came attractively plated and the fried rice came steaming hot. Everything was very good. I'd certainly come again.

One of the newest Publixs in the area and it's GORGEOUS. It looks a lot like the format they're using out in Orlando and it's SO useful. I wish all the stores would look like this.    The produce is so organized, they have everything SO neat. The wine is right near by too.  This store was busy, but they were the first one to have Toilet Paper that I saw. Color me Impressed.   The associates were friendly and helpful, we found exactly what we were looking for and were in and out in minutes.  I hope our publix gets a make over to look like this one!

Dual drive thru, they seemed to only have one person taking orders. I'd hear the one drive thru go off, that order was taken. Then Mine went off. Ok, I get being understaffed, but wasn't the reason you have dual drive thrus so that you could be faster, and get more people thru?  Ordered a happy meal and a frozen coke. Got exactly that, even got a larger coke without being up charged with my kids meal. Happy meals are perfect for me, I just don't need the toy. Food was fine, fries were meh, not hot and crispy.

I'm not sure what I was expecting. This place is usually Hopping and tonight it wasn't. This is our "comedy" club and what I walked into, was nothing more than a bar.   The outside is nice, a covered patio bar that plays foot ball, inside reeked of stale smoke and beer. No surprise.    The big surprise was seeing a sushi chef. I didn't expect that. The fish looked fresh, but as the husband said, He contemplated that, but he felt getting sushi here might be just one step up from getting gas station sushi.   We entered, No one but the sushi chef greeted us. There are no signs to say "Seat yourself" or anything. The one waitress seemed too engrossed in the TV to be bothered to acknowledge us.  When we did sit, she was still staring at the tv. The Sushi chef had to prompt her to give us menus.  It's a good thing that's all she did. Our waiter, turned out to be the indoor bartender. He was polite and friendly and he saved the visit from being 1 star.   I get that this is a LOCAL's place. A place when you go all the time because you feel comfortable, This wasn't the case in our situation. We thought the food was OK, we ordered the loaded fries - bacon and cheese sauce that was cheap - were ok, my garlic wings were good and the Black & bleu burger had too much bleu cheese on it, that the husbeast only ate half of it.  The service was just OK, but it was service. over all, it isn't something we'll be repeating.

The parking lot was full, so that usually bodes well for a place. But immediately upon entering, the sharp screech of a child greeted my ears, so when we were sat, we were sat in the bar/lounge area.   That was fine (for the most part) as it was quieter over all.   The bar wasn't terribly busy, but we still waited about 8 minutes until someone came by and told us they'd be right with us, first a woman and then a guy. The guy came back and took our drink orders and let us know that the bartender would be our Waitress.  She came back in a moment or so and took our order for apps and mains.   We ordered chips and homemade queso - with ground beef added for free, the home made (uh, more like shipped from Sysco) chicken pot pie and a bacon cheese burger.   Our chips and queso came out very quickly, and they added a -LOT- of ground beef to the dip. So much so that it almost over powered the cheese. Still, it had great flavor, the chips were fresh and the salsa was both spicy and tasty. When we were more than 1/2 way done, the bartender said she'd bring us more chips, we waved her off, we didn't really need more.   She also brought out my salad with the chips, and that's great, it was a fresh salad with romaine lettuce, cherry tomatoes, some shredded carrots and croutons. I don't remember asking for Ranch dressing, but that's what I got, and it was on the side, just like I like it.  It also came with a honey croissant ala Hops (YUM!)  We chatted and munched our way through this part of the meal, as the room seemed to grow colder and colder. We weren't the only ones to notice the temperature drop. The table behind me complained, asking them to bump it up. Apparently they keep it cold in the lounge because the main room gets REALLY hot if the ac in the lounge goes off.  It was -so- cold that there was condensation forming on the AC vent and dripping on me, on my seat and thigh. What fun.   Our mains came out and as I said, they advertise that their Chicken Pot Pie is homemade, but it's most certainly frozen and re-heated. This is not made in house, but its still tasty.  The cheese burger was large and topped well, though the fries were paltry and meh looking to my eyes.   Our waitress was attentive, but the temperature difference was too much. My hands were so cold they were aching. When we left we could tell how MUCH of a difference there was between the foyer and the bar area, a good 10-15 degrees. They really should put some effort into fixing that. It made it VERY uncomfortable to be in there for more than 15-20 minutes.

It's been DECADES since I've gone to a BK Lounge, but I was near by, and I was hungry for breakfast and a croissansanwich sounded perfect for breakfast.  I went through the drive though and placed my order for 2 ham and cheese croissant sandwiches and a coffee with 3 creams, no sugar.   The sandwiches were fine, microwaved, but fine.  The coffee was very good, but the cream was missing from the bag.  Over all, it was edible but I don't think I'd be going back to this particular location.

Bookstores are my heaven. I love love love them. I wish they were all over like they used to be, but alas between AMAZON and Kindle, they are slowly becoming passe.  Anyway, this B&N is gorgeous, a 2 story affair and it is lovely, spacious and just grand.   The people were friendly and warm, outgoing and polite, the store had plenty of places to sit,if you wanted to, and there was a Harry Potter event going on this night - gearing up for the script release me thinks.  Visit and enjoy. FEED YOUR MIND~

Our last stop at The Shops at Wiregrass was to grab dinner.  This is one of the larger Moe's locations we've ever been too. They even had a roped queue!  It was around 8:30 when we stopped and the line was about 6 people deep. Thankfully the line moved quickly as I was unable to stand for long (my knee was giving me issues) so I took a seat, and saved a table for my men while they placed our orders.   My husbeastie got the Joey bag o' donuts, while the beau and I both got steak quesidillas.    The food was made quickly and to order. It was satisfying and tasty.   The eatery itself was in need of some care.  I know they'd been busy, but their tables weren't cleaned off, they needed to empty their trash cans and clean up in general.  All in all it was a decent place to grab grub, when I'm there, but I wouldn't go out of my way to eat there.

Came here at my Beau's suggestion before Tampa Fringe.  It was in close walking distance and we had just enough time.   The eatery wasn't busy, it was perfectly comfortable during Cinco De Mayo, and my table was sat right away. We had a party of three.   We started off with an appetizer of the pretzels, which were tasty, the beer cheese was my favorite.   One of my party got their Burger of the day, which was spicy, I got a steak salad which had all sorts of good things chopped in, including egg, bleu cheese and candied walnuts. Would have been perfect, except the walnuts. I'll ask for those on the side in the future.  My beau got a black & Bleu burger and ate every last bite, so I'm guessing ti was good.   The service was fantastic. Our drinks never went empty and we were able to dine and pay without any problem, we were in and out on time to catch our show at the HCC location.

Curaleaf is my favorite dispensary. They are my go-to for my Medical Marijuana needs! On Wednesday you get double points, which helps you save money at later dates.   I've always experienced good service, very knowledgable bud tenders. The quality has always been very good as well. They were the first place I got to try the new edibles from!

Located behind Danny's Pub, the Boar and Buffalo is an upscale place to grab your favorite whisky or other high end cocktail.   Inside, its dark wood interior, barrel high tables and candle light sconces add an air of mystery to this not quite speak easy.  If you're looking for a good Espresso Martini, you can get one here. They're just amazing.
