I'd been to Bill Jackson's once before, to get myself some Vibram shoes, but that was YEARS ago.   I went recently, and for a store that was supposed to be limiting the amount of people inside, their parking lot was PACKED.  Finding parking was an actual challenge. But we did, and we went inside, We wore our masks, and saw a lot of Dick-nose folks while there.    I perused the clothing, shoes and what have you, while my mate talked to the pros about guns, since this is what we came for. They were limiting the amount of folks into those sections, and that's understandable.  The wait though, was long and my mate was not in the mood to be -that- patient.  So we left.   I did see there were lots of things that I would be interested in, but their sizes were limited.

The coconut rum is to die for!  I was not aware this place existed, even though the husbeast used to work less than a half mile from the TBRC.  I'm so glad we found it! When you walk inside, it smells so good!  We did the tasting and tour with our friends and found out that though we didn't enjoy a lot of the flavors, that the Coconut rum was decidedly our favorite, enough so that we bought a bottle and took it home with us.  They were very happy to let us know that beside rum, they're looking into distilling Vodka and a new beer very soon!   So if you're looking for something interesting to do, try the tasting tour at the TBRC and you might just find a new hobby too.

Stopped here for a farewell dinner for my husband by his co-workers, who's surprised him with an ambush.   We all met up at Ford's and were set at a long table against the bank of windows. We were a party of 6.    We ordered appetizers of onion rings and fried pickles, they were good. They came out without issue.   The service was friendly and pleasant, our varied orders came out quickly without much wait at all, which was nice, if it's not been for covid, it might have been a bit different.   We'd certainly come back

Stopped in while we were running errands, so we could grab food.    We always get the same thing, the pick 4, which is a good deal. I got the scrambled eggs, bacon, Strawberry crepe and hashbrowns. The food was quick and delicious.

I knew about this place when I was 16 and it wasn't yet a park.   I stopped here with my love to catch the sunset and maybe see if someone had left some painted rocks.  The tide was out, and we were one of three cars when we pulled in.  I decided to see what was going on down by the water side.   A guy was fishing, there were a lot of little crabs and I found a large painted rock down on the water's edge. I took some phots and then came up and decided to walk, because the park is not just that parking area, its all that edge water area.  There are benches, there are palm trees. It's really just a nice area along Dunedin's water front that make this such a plesant area to be in.

Tucked away in a partially defunct strip mall, between Pinch a Penny and an empty Winn Dixie, is Bj's Asian Fusion.  You can't miss it because of the blinding LED lights that surround the windows and door.  Once inside, it smells great and the place is very neat, a wall booth and tables w/chairs line one wall, the center is filled with tables and chairs and the other wall is filled with booths. Plenty of seating for everyone, and of course there is the ever popular take out. Mind you, this is not your everyday Asian take out.   The menu is THICK.. there is Chinese, Thai, Japanese and Sushi on the menu, and plenty to choose from, you can't possibly leave here with an empty belly. If you do, you must not have eaten for a week!   We started with an appetizer, this was a mistake, we had no idea how big the portions were, so... in the future we won't do this. We started with the Thai spring rolls, they were very fresh and very tasty, but their peanut sauce was a bit too sweet for me.  Since I ordered the hibachi dinner, I also got a salad and soup with my meal, I HAD NO IDEA there was going to be so much!  The won ton soup was DELICIOUS, the Salad was good, but there was way too much dressing (One of the reason for not 5 stars), the Hibachi style steak and shrimp was good, but the the steak was over cooked, to the point of being dry and tough.   The husbeast had one of the chef's specialties, the Dragon and Phoenix (?) The way he ate it, I can honestly say he LOVED it.    All in all it was absolutely delicious, we will certainly come back.

I've lived in this area of the County for 90% of my life and never knew this was here. I don't think it's been around all that long, honestly, but I could be wrong. ANYWAY.  Located off of Plathe road, this preserve is tucked off and hidden by the natural beauty of Florida scrub. The road that leads back to the preserve is dusty, but the left turn that I took led me to a park that had wandering trails through the Florida brush, over well constructed and planned out walk ways through the marsh and lakes, as well as an Eagle Scout's project of benches that provide plenty of seating.   There are plenty of opportunities to walk, run, hike, bike, play on the play ground, photograph the wild life or just BE.   Speaking of the playground: It's lovely, with a path all for the kids that tells them a story, a path to literacy, which in truth is very important in this state. There is also a Free little library here, so if you have books you'd like to share, bring one or 15 to leave or take one, they're there for you to have or give.   I'm so going back to the JEG preserve, to hide rocks or just to practice being present.  You should too.

I've been seeing Mikey since 2014, I figured it was time to update my review.   I'm STILL in love with everything he does for my hair.  He is the ONLY person I allow to cut or color my hair. He is not only my hair stylist but he is my friend. I adore him.   I used to be a signature red, but as of late, I've been more inclined to play with the color, slipping towards Pink and purple, and he's been making my hair look absolutely fabulous.   I look forward to every visit to the salon, because the staff is so friendly, So welcoming and of the highest calibre of stylists.   They just recently opened their 3rd location in Tampa! I'm so excited for them because I love it when my friends succeed!

Good coffee is hard to find.  And I do mean GOOD coffee, I don't mean the burnt swill from $Bux or even Dunkies.    I ordered a Vanilla Latte to go, and the Husbeast ordered a latte for there. THe difference was I was going to walk about the mall, and he was going to sit while I explored.  Both were made perfectly and deliciously.  The service was exceptional and the right size. I have to admit out baristo was attentive and friendly and made small talk because he seemed interested and craved the company. He was great to chat with.

I used to come to WestShore Plaza when I was working nearby, some decade ago. Back then the mall was nice if run down.  Once they put in International Mall, they've had to step up their game. And it appears they have.  With 4 large anchor stores, a nice food court and a movie theater, it's a nice location to visit. They even have a nice collection of places to eat on the outside like Maggiano's and PF Changs.

I stopped in on the way to The Vault of Souls to pick up a cup of Coffee and a sandwich for dinner later that night. I was THRILLED to see that not only did they have a selection of flavoured creamers, but they also offer pump chocolate, caramel and another flavor that I can't remember.  Their coffee bar was extensive.   I wish I could say the same for the pre-made sandwiches. I could chose from 3 subs that didn't have mayo, and since this was going to sit in my bag for a few hours, that was optimal. I did pick a Cuban and that was fine.   The clerks were awesome, bleeding through a line fast and with a smile, fast to say "Happy Halloween" to each and every person.

Met my friend here for a purchase of something I bought from her and Fox's was the designated spot, because it's iconic in the area.  It has plenty of parking, has plenty of light and allowed us to see each other easily.

My husband is home on vacation. He didn't want to go anyplace that we had to really travel to, so we opted to do things and go places we'd never been too, this works out well for me, right?  We made our hour plus drive from Tarpon Springs, found our way down the access road and pulled into the parking lot that was surprisingly more filled than I thought it would be. Seems other people had the idea to go to Dinosaur World two days after Christmas. The weather was perfect for the visit so we really lucked out.   You enter through the gift shop and pay for your tickets right before entering the main park. There are several replica dinosaurs right there, on display for you and your family to see, as well as 2 play grounds for different age groups, a lot of covered picnic tables and the entrance to a Dinosaur Museum which goes over history and relics they've found, and at the end a few anamatronic dinosaurs make a scene.   When you exit the museum, you walk down the pathway, past the two playgrounds, and the gem mine/geode shop to the dioramas they've set up.  This is obviously the life's work of someone, and while I may have gotten a few chuckles, the little ones around me seemed to love the park itself.   I personally loved the way they laid out everything in the swamp, they did a good job constructing pathways and scenes for you to enjoy, even noting when it might get a bit graphic.  If you come during late spring through Mid august, wear bug spray. I'd assume mosquitoes feast well there, and you'd be the food. Bring your camera, as there's a lot of places to take pictures and make memories.

Stopped here for lunch one afternoon.  Sent the Boyfriend in while I waited outside.    They were busy, most folks wore a mask, all good signs.  Our food was ready quickly and was done properly, which made us all happy.   The staff was excellent and the food tasted fresh and delicious. Will certainly come back for a philly cheese steak.

This is one of the biggest Publix' I've ever been too.   Formerly an Albertsons, the Publix store fits in just fine.  They've got EVERYTHING.    I came here on a Saturday afternoon to pick up a Fried Chicken dinner, and got the last one in the case, given the heat coming off the food, it hadn't been waiting long either.  I did a bit more shopping and even though the store is large, the layout is consumer friendly.   The store employees are friendly, as most Publix associates are.

We stopped in looking for a bite to eat. We weren't familiar with the chain, but thought we'd give them a chance. They were wearing masks (if improperly most of the time) but it took a few minutes for the cashier to turn around and notice my beau and I.   We placed our order: The double Angus with onion rings, and A chicken sandwich with onion rings, when the food came out, it was delivered to the table with a smile, we were asked if we needed anything, which I did, ranch for dipping, and we began to eat.   The food was good, it was nicely seasoned and tasty. The chicken, which is often the one that people get wrong was nice, juicy. I even forgot that there was avocado on it.  The beau liked his burger, said it tasted fresh.  The onion rings were nothing to write home about.
Stopped here with my 13 yr old niece.   Grounds are clean and neat. Restrooms were well stocked and kept neat.   An armed guard was on property.

The husbeast and I stopped in to Ferman Chevy to look at the Volt as a possible replacement for his totaled Prius.    The dealership is super clean, beautiful on the inside with some SUPER sharp Corvettes outside that made me do a double take. WOW.. they were AMAZING.  The receptionist asked what we needed, we told her, and they asked us to sit for a moment.  Within 15 or so seconds they had a sales rep for us, Dan.   Dan was incredibly knowledgeble, friendly and capable. We took a test drive and were all but sold on that Volt, it's a damned fine car. The only issue was the sport button as it appears my husbeast has a bit of a lead foot.   We left, with a bit of determination to decide which vehicle we were going to purchase, in the end, it wasn't the volt, but we would come back if we need to buy another car in the future.

My Hubs and I got the Monthly plan so that our cars are always spotless, at least on the outside. We rarely use the vacuums but they do Suck properly!  We like that they're open until 9pm so there isn't a reason to go early in the afternoon or morning. He can take his during the evening and I can take mine when ever I want.  We totally recommend the place.

I know people RAVE about the Fresh Market, and it's a fine place, I'm just spoiled with Sprouts.   The Fresh Market is small, crowded and some of the customers, on the day I visited were quite adjitated about something, so I didn't stay long.

So after having visited Ybor's location at the Yelp event, I made an appointment with my stylist to see him today.    As my appointment time rolled around, I walked into the location on Kennedy, it's not as posh, but that's Ok, the people were all friendly and well styled. I was invited to have my favorite beverage and sat down for my consult.     Mikey and I went over my color options, and we decided on doing the length first and then the roots, with a custom blend of color.  Once the color was applied, and trust me, he was so very thorough about the application, he let it set for a while.    Once it was time for the color to be rinsed, I was treated to the 2nd best head massage in town (Mine being the best!) as he shampooed the color out and then added the conditioner. I was -so- relaxed by the time it was over.   Mikey decided he needed to check the color, and we determined that it was perfect.    Then it was time for the cut. He truly works miracles. He is precise, he is dedicated to his art. He makes sure that it is -just- right.  In the end, I couldn't have been more happy with the result. You can be assured that I will travel back to Tribeca to see Mikey and have him do the cut and color next time. It was well worth the price!

Stopped in for a wash before I headed out of state on a trip. I purchased their $20 unlimited, Note to self, download the ap before the month runs out.   THe wash itself was pretty nice, the track is smooth as you're taken through the soap and brushes, and different color sprays as they hit your vehicle and take off the debris and road grime.   Once you're blown dry and unloaded, you're able to go over and use the vacuums that are under a covering. The first one I pulled up to was very weak, as if clogged, so I moved to another unit and had far better luck.   I'll be back.

I had been looking for new Asian Market when my friend told me about this location.   The store is large and even has a jewelry store and a home goods store located inside of it! So when I say they have an incredible selection, I'm not kidding.   Since my husband is a fan of Ramen, I was able to over indulge him for the Holidays and get him a ton of flavors I wasn't aware of. He was happy!   I will certainly come back here in the future!
